97c85c38-ee4d-4b1b-931d-d87e4b8ccc52: "That must have been Bokken. He sells potions. He lives out in the forest like a hermit, but he comes here every day. He knows every tree and bush in the area and how they can help you. The Stag Lord's gang wants him to work for them. He lacks the courage to fight those bandits, but he won't just walk away from us. He has a good heart, even if he grumbles a lot, especially recently."
309b2b61-cb2c-4690-90d0-889b6b675662: {n}He notices a fair-haired woman approach.{/n} "Dove! Why are you here? I told you to stay hidden!"
174f5476-4bca-49f0-860a-d176a3dd13c3: "It's all over — I saw it. I just needed to be sure you were all right..." {n}The woman looks at her husband tenderly, if with a hint of sorrow. Oleg mumbles something as he looks away, embarrassed.{/n} "My name is Svetlana. I'm sorry your arrival to our {g|Oleg's Trading Post}trading post{/g} turned out so... unwelcoming."
63fca25d-1c23-4adf-abdd-1406daca9ace: "Take that, you scoundrels!" {n}Oleg shakes his fist.{/n} "But now..." {n}He scratches his head and stares at the ground gloomily.{/n} "The girl got away, a plague on her. Now what are we to do?" {n}He sighs heavily.{/n} "If only I could send Svetlana somewhere safe and show those rats what's what!"
e9e58314-74c5-4e23-b690-b9bc162abb62: {n}Oleg waves his hand sullenly.{/n} "Who are they? They're the Stag Lord's gang, that's who! These lands teem with bandits like bedbugs in a beggar's hut, and you just stirred them up. They have a camp not far from here — I expect they'll return in full force in half a day, maybe less. The Stag Lord won't take an insult like this lightly, and his henchmen are more like demons than men..."
9c2a33ad-9649-4128-ab49-880e7ce3bd9e: {n}Oleg grunts.{/n} "So, what, I should start calling you 'Your Grace' and kneeling as you pass? I have some spare traps, some tar... and a box of alchemist's fire. I'd bet some of it could help in the battle."
ea32fd8c-d3a6-4b84-a5a2-2f444f4b0860: "Well, I appreciate your good intentions. I may not have the best manners, but Oleg Leveton is the last name you'll hear accused of being ungrateful! If we manage to defend this post, I'll reward you proper."
e3d6cf26-bd48-4d44-b2d4-36bdbae86446: "What do they want? Those bloodsuckers think they own this land — they come, take what they want, and steal the better part of our money every month as a toll for their leader. They even broke our gate so we couldn't try to hide anything from them. No one knows exactly how many there are. Sometimes only five or six come — sometimes, it's a whole gang. I'd have shown them what for long ago, if not for Svetlana."
3ec2401e-a9cf-4a58-b79f-84fc0495d1de: "For the Stag Lord and his cronies, of course! That Stag Lord fancies himself a king in these parts. He may have antlers for a crown, but all the troublemakers around here are happy to follow his orders as long as they're paid. So they charge an arm and a leg as 'taxes,' and they call their executions 'punishment for treason,' even those who never swore allegiance to the Stag Lord. They're killed fast, if they're lucky. If not..." {n}Oleg looks to Svetlana.{/n} "Dove, why don't you go start supper while we finish our talk?"
da1a43f0-b14f-4c2a-b049-099c6a9c394e: "I've no need to be protected from dark talk. I'm not some blind kitten, you know — I've seen what they do to people." {n}Svetlana lowers her head.{/n} "Most of the gang is made up of simple bandits, but there are a few monsters among the leadership, especially those close to the Stag Lord. Auchs and Dovan from Nisroch come to mind. They like to make a show of their tortures and executions. My husband and I... we saw the bodies."
fefcfdf3-4a58-47ff-8d4b-6351224368a0: "I'm afraid they'll come back while we're chatting away, but what's to be done...?" {n}Oleg mumbles.{/n}
b7824605-dedf-4fb4-8c31-3cc49be3be00: "Don't know what good trading will serve if those bloodsuckers come back and take everything... but all right, have a look."
f26ebfc4-bfe1-4f96-9f82-f551078d4df0: "Svetlana, go hide inside! We're going to go meet our guests."
1fdd819a-3c64-4af4-a6ae-c57cc456876b: {n}Oleg shifts uncomfortably.{/n} "Surely there are more important things to discuss... Well, all right. We also deal with the occasional huntsmen in the area. What does any of this matter? When those bandits come back, they'll either drain us dry or just kill us."
fd24759b-de47-4d63-b4f7-6f3b52f3d7cf: {n}Oleg seems to be even gloomier, and Svetlana sorrowful. Both of them look at you intently.{/n}
f2675c28-017f-4bc7-be34-5a4c23d70a56: "If we keep dallying, we'll end up talking WITH the attackers rather than about them. If they're even willing to talk..."
aaecfe2b-01cc-458d-9374-9f4f939421f1: "All right. Soon as you're finished, let us know. And don't leave the post — the bandits could return at any time."
51296a49-a2f7-42c1-8fb9-0196f0b77807: {n}Oleg and Svetlana are discussing something in low but impassioned whispers. You manage to make out the words 'Forget about it!' before they stop talking and turn to you.{/n}
273d3169-5be5-4e66-8164-304e6d090032: "But that could set the post on fire!" {n}Oleg shouts, surprised.{/n} "Well, maybe if we covered the walls with something to protect them... All right, yes. I think it could work — I'll even shoot the arrow myself. I used to be pretty good with a crossbow, back in my day."
3377e42a-39a0-4cb3-aeb5-17026b0fd1bd: "I beg you, be careful. And please don't let Oleg do anything too risky."
481c3dba-d808-473f-8958-da4e9eb9244c: "Fear not! I'll stand between you and this scum! You're under my protection!"
65110b39-2d6d-4caa-acbc-8f8abe292b60: {n}Amiri flexes her shoulders.{/n} "Finally, a fight. Was bored with all that talking."
36b43af3-b6d4-4355-a0a1-8c24969e7317: "Well, these aren't the heroics I was hoping to write about, but I guess even the greatest heroes had to start somewhere."
c1dfdaf8-bde4-444d-b269-f63cd3ed836c: "We have to hide Svetlana — please don't argue, Dove! Now, we also need to decide on a plan. Go ahead and look around — there may be some tools that can be used for the battle. There are some pretty solid traps around, some tar, and... a box of alchemist's fire, looks like."
666a9a61-f4c2-4e6a-bd8d-9be68fcc4ab5: {n}Oleg grunts.{/n} "Well, thanks, I guess. I might even be able to scrape some sort of reward together for you if we manage to defend the post."
6aecda09-fb13-4fc6-9c70-b148ee9a6db9: "I'll help you fight. I've got a box of alchemist's fire we can use. We could put it by the gate, then set it off with a burning arrow when those bandits get close. I'll even shoot the arrow myself. I used to be pretty good with a crossbow, back in my day."
65ac3237-1a83-4f66-84bf-f7189a6a01d9: "Are you sure? Well, it's your call. Here, take it."
b40e9c5a-4206-4d57-a2c0-8098e5873b5e: "Here, take it. But should you start throwing it into bandits, please, be careful. Don't set the post on fire."
cba6923f-830e-4a2c-bff9-b74bb1287242: "Hey, book kid! Want to hear a story about hunting a saber-toothed owlbear? That was a good hunt!"
1632d513-35d2-4780-b772-0bf375974b3d: "A saber-toothed owlbear? Hahaha! But Amiri, owlbears don't have teeth – they have beaks!"
235746cf-4f60-4353-98b1-cea505e51364: It was time to meet the real mistress of the Stolen Lands — the one who'd been pulling the strings to create and destroy kingdoms for ages now.
9d2b44fa-6b07-4c9c-9b4b-ed02bd8f5ee9: "I'm the local baron{mf||ess}. My lands aren't far from here."
3efb9226-1bf0-43e0-aaa4-b2621fe0353b: "Mind your tongue! I'm the local baron{mf||ess}. My lands aren't far from here."
843bdd90-0447-4f56-a46c-0717b1e83008: [Leave] "We're just travelers. We'll be on our way."
6099f599-b2bf-4d6d-9ffc-aad7da25ee0e: "Actually, I don't think I can help you."
ed0b995b-8c54-43f6-875c-bc8a777fa788: "From Numeria? You're pretty far from home."
7e99ac94-2a89-4158-844e-6c30c1af0b53: [Share food with the barbarians] "We're not here to fight. Let's share some bread and have a chat."
0c7c643f-9389-4785-9409-cd7f49a3b715: "Are you the only group of Numerians here?"
e1a758d2-51f2-45d7-960e-d60a8d85c072: "Have you found anything interesting in the area?"
c5c3c3f0-579a-49da-80c4-f6e31fb97a99: "Do you know anything about the situation at Varnhold?"
ba16badb-6bf7-4e3d-9e8a-66873bc22e64: {n}A small but well-armed group moves across the flatlands. Tattoos, leather and fur clothing, bone amulets at their belts — these are barbarians. 5d62aa58-472d-4ee7-8348-9bc76ae704e3: "What do you want? If you're looking for trouble, you might just have found it."
c4277098-b385-4fbc-8331-24c4d2b1e93a: "Hey!" {n}One of the barbarians shouts toward Amiri.{/n} "You're from the north, right? Which tribe?"
7e6af76a-4a59-4be4-85ad-547ea323cbb8: "Wait, isn't that the gal the Six Bears kicked out? Cause they were scared that if a woman touched a sword, their balls'd fall off?"
dac15a85-49cb-4634-8642-e17d98d49cf0: "Ha, ha... Just let bygones be bygones. I walk with {mf|him|her} now." {n}Amiri points at you.{/n}
daaa3016-f665-44ff-82b9-d0c93dd40f35: "Who're you, then? What do you want?"
ca371b5f-dc30-4817-aa46-d0965715efd7: "Best stay out of the way, little one, or we might step on you!"
bcf8cae3-a70f-4151-a685-6312cf11c71e: "Hey there, {mf|handsome|beauty}! What're you doing so far from the city? If you're not careful, you might get some calluses on those tender elven fingers!"
d38e0b0b-a499-4add-a25d-b81b3fc0e412: {n}The barbarian examines you closely.{/n} "So, you lead this group, then?"
d1ccbde8-eb37-4ac6-888b-300001f0059c: {n}The barbarians watch you sternly, their hands still on their weapons.{/n}
8213db03-35ec-41bd-9754-aceca0af2212: "Really? You don't seem much like one." {n}The barbarian stares at you incredulously.{/n} "Well, all right... Your Baronship, then, or whatever it is they call you."
31b9fd22-39a3-49cc-811a-9d657df2e75d: "You're the baron{mf||ess}? You? Bah ha ha! That's funny! And I'm Kevoth-Kul, the Black Sovereign of {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g}!"
d00d9ac6-995d-4147-860e-627e8f4a69a9: "Wait, really?" {n}The Kellid examines you closely.{/n} "Well, all right... Your Baronship, then, or whatever it is they call you."
2b4efd4e-cda7-406c-ae58-4f10fb760793: "We don't need your help-" {n}the Kellid starts, his voice grim, but he's interrupted when one of the barbarian women begins coughing uncontrollably.{/n}
f887cd61-1345-4b0e-8b12-7ad089f3aa82: "If you don't need it, just shut up so I can-" {n}The barbarian woman breaks into another short coughing fit, then spits on the ground — the phlegm is blue.{/n} "I'm not gonna die for your pride. 101406a1-51f4-4e25-a75f-3d3281991475: {n}The barbarian woman spits more blue phlegm to the ground, disappointed.{/n} "Why even open your mouth about it, then?"
bcb0e7c6-c924-4e08-87d9-4b9534b7621e: "I'm Nober. We're from {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g}, part of the {g|Tiger Lords}Tiger Lords{/g} tribe. We're just minding our own business here, not looking to pick a fight. We don't want any trouble, and we're not after anyone."
23983d10-876a-4ede-a3d0-81a5082ef4d8: "Not so far. The {g|Tiger Lords}Tiger Lords{/g} travel around a lot — from the {g|Worldwound}Worldwound{/g} to {g|Iobaria}Iobaria{/g}. Hell, these lands were once practically home to us — we used to clear them damned fey from the {g|Narlmarches}Narlmarches{/g} on a regular basis. Well, now we're here again. That's the nomad life, you see — never know where you'll find yourself tomorrow!"
00047d7f-3414-4e5e-9086-ace00e023265: {n}The barbarians sniff the food cautiously, then taste small pieces for poison. Once they're certain it's safe, they begin to eat. After swallowing some of the bread, Nober wipes his lips.{/n} "So you want a chat, huh? Sure, why not."
bee64f4d-7503-48f6-94ab-14a13773eb3f: {n}A barbarian woman steps forward, trying to control her heavy coughing.{/n} "That'd be welcome. I'm-" {n}The woman starts coughing again, then spits some blue phlegm on the ground.{/n} "I caught bluespit somewhere in the barrens. I can pay for the healing in gold."
b94a7aee-433e-4708-b4ff-0924af712e88: "You kidding? Of course not! Our main camp's over the hills there. If you're feeling gutsy, come pay us a visit!"
27bafb82-84ec-4428-855e-f7359f468a2c: "I wish! We've been searching the area for days now, but all we found was a cave with some grime-faced half-men. No ancient ruin, no treasures, not a damned thing!"
a8bbd490-0008-442a-8ecb-b9c4c10ed172: {n}The Kellid frowns.{/n} "No idea, really. Dugath just said we should search for caves and ancient ruins, and he'd tell us if it was what we were looking for. You ask me, we're just wasting time out here — but chieftain knows best."
62e16931-a227-4157-ac9e-111808d1ce7d: "An old cleric. He's seen a lot, he knows a lot, and it seems like he's the only one who has any idea what the hell we're looking for out here!"
7f1053c2-4930-43dd-80a8-4efa24617f97: "Ugh, I hate this question... Well, {g|Numeria}Numeria's{/g} a hard land made for hard people. Lots of the chunks just sit still and do nothing, and we mine them for adamantine. 58e37dcc-362d-418b-81cc-315d83d4047c: "The {g|Tiger Lords}Tiger Lords{/g} are an ancient and glorious tribe, one of the strongest in all {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g}. But now that the spirit of Armag's been reborn into the body of our new chieftain, you mark me — word of our heroic deeds will spread across {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g} once again!"
6db23a5b-a99d-4b30-b125-6e1293f7e23e: "Why would I? Bad enough it brings us so much trouble on its own, but it also attracts villains from all over {g|Avistan}Avistan{/g}, like flies to a steaming pile of shit! That {g|Technic League}Technic League{/g} alone... Ugh!"
381f13ee-9284-449f-ad3d-0c1d02e0596a: "{g|Varnhold}Varnhold{/g}? Never heard of it. Whatever's going on there, we got nothing to do with it."
6ae1d2cf-d7f7-4046-9775-cff63f020637: "Watch your tongue, barbarian! This is indeed the baron{mf||ess} of {kingdomname}. Show respect, or you will have to deal with me!"
7d5aa133-989e-4fba-8c28-ec94edbb7e54: "Look at that woman. I think she needs help," {n}Tristian whispers, pointing out one of the barbarians who looks to be quite ill.{/n}
3f3360ef-f3c1-4d64-96ec-ea11831e0b2e: "{g|Numeria}Numeria's{/g} also the birthplace of countless beautiful songs and heroic legends. I mean, most of them end with someone getting beheaded, impaled, chopped to pieces, or burned alive... but still, they're marvelous!"
528dd8ee-b06d-4964-b146-a0f899df4150: "Now those are what I call good assistants — dutiful, prompt, and aware of their own intellectual limitations. Why can't I ever get assistants like that? Maybe I should have pursued a career as a barbarian chieftain..."
dfc1055a-92a9-47c1-a976-da657fc9678e: "Eveld? Is that the character next to you?"
631e0b14-85d6-4c71-b064-0a042a0226f2: "You can't handle some row without me?"
e0ac643b-8cbe-4b5f-b8f9-b51f3d2a7ead: "You. Both of you. Figure this out someplace else."
8d2d4c72-1374-4b71-83fa-b32b13b2fac1: "I don't care who said what to whom. You're going to make peace now, right here in front of me."
3310512d-71dc-4577-bf19-0f5102f867f7: "Thank you for bringing this to my attention. I'll try to help her."
0c489d00-584a-4f64-8d42-494fd76b60d2: "I don't have time to deal with Valerie's behavior. Keeping peace on the streets is your responsibility."
f70455da-fac2-4b80-bea8-9e87ac8bac95: "I will talk to Valerie when I get a chance."
ef64a023-2b8e-4ead-bae1-1552d0a6bcc7: "Eveld, did you really write a pasquinade about Valerie?"
de577c34-2511-4a6c-9bc2-c3f4217d8957: {n}The captain's usually untroubled face is dark with rage.{/n} "{mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}! Please forgive me for distracting you from important matters, but you're the only one who can talk some sense into these hotheads!"
4da1222b-db5b-4e7b-827b-2a812df8b4e6: "They had an argument in the middle of the street! Yelled so much your subjects called the guards... but what can they do about Lady Valerie? Plus, Eveld hasn't done anything illegal... it's not like I can put them in jail!"
97381ea0-eed3-467e-bdb3-8fd5f1d1ec11: "{mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, Valerie is your companion, so she gets special treatment. She doesn't take orders from me, besides it would be wrong..." {n}The captain rubs his temple.{/n} "We fought together, protected the capital together... so what am I going to do now? Arrest her?"
b7de9295-a65f-4f2f-8dbf-c6883cb28aaf: {n}A short, rugged man in a sophisticated garment bows ceremoniously.{/n} "In my own person, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}! Eveld the Silver-Tongued, who once served as court bard at the best houses of {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}, and has now traded in his golden cage for the free winds of travel. But I digress..."
ef3ce511-aa36-492a-a6b4-5e2dec68b0e0: "This, so to speak, sweet lady insulted me, if you please, in front of my audience! Halted my performance and embarrassed me in front of the entire tavern! Would you please be so kind as to rein this lady in!"
77ac72e4-048b-4494-b999-a6847bb24e2d: {n}Valerie is apparently trying to control herself, but telltale red spots flare on her face.{/n} "I noticed that someone pinned a disgusting pasquinade next to the tavern entrance. Something about a bright bird who lost its feathers. That's... abominable insolence! Yes, I won't deny I'm guilty. I lost my temper, but who wouldn't have?"
e93adedf-3c0c-4dd3-a509-f1e9cd59c43f: {n}Eveld gasps with indignation.{/n} "Is that so? When I smothered this lady with exquisite compliments, I received only insults and jokes in return! When I came to her with gifts, begging her to become the muse for my greatest work – I was ridiculed and sent away like a snotty boy! And now, the moment I start to pursue my art away from this good lady, she seeks me out and says I'm guilty of spiteful slander! What shall I do? I'm but a slave to my inspiration, which is sent to me from above!" {n}Eveld smoothes down his hair and adds.{/n} "And while we're on the subject of my poetry, it's really not that bad..."
fe058bf1-06e2-43ff-b2a1-a38e58b69e51: {n}Valerie looks down, ashamed.{/n} "I humbly beg your forgiveness, {name}. I failed to control my temper and besmirched not only myself, but you as my leader." {n}The girl casts a burning glance at the man in sophisticated attire, standing beside her.{/n} "Unfortunately, I was provoked."
420ffc84-96fa-491d-ac57-ae701baa689b: {n}The man catches Valerie's glance and gasps with indignation.{/n} "Is that so?! So it's ah... Ah, forgive my manners, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}! Allow me to introduce myself — Eveld the Silver-Tongued, from {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}. It's a pity we meet under such circumstances, but..."
8ca1ecaf-04e1-4c0e-9697-b350c0b7c438: "Hell no, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}! If this rude dolt brought me here and since I'm already taking up your time, I need to make sure this lady is reined in. I need protection!"
3070b38c-efe1-4ae4-a174-93fed1710bfb: {n}Valerie's voice rings with rage.{/n} "I swear, another word from this lowly scribbler, and anything could happen!"
63145afe-b384-4cad-8b11-785da0578dc3: {n}Eveld opens his mouth but says nothing. Finally he starts enunciating words, one by one.{/n} "My only transgression is loyally serving my patroness, the beautiful {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g} who sends me inspiration, and never hiding from this world a single word that's born in my heart. But since my honesty and openness are so offensive to this good lady, then so be it – I apologize for insulting you, with all my heart!"
a908b445-ea90-425f-8bdc-e3e4856de0ed: {n}Valerie grows pale, and her lips tremble. Gathering her strength, she almost pushes the words from her mouth.{/n} "My deepest apologies, Eveld."
47a36675-448e-4b1c-8e2b-f0259421f39c: {n}Eveld turns to the girl with a triumphant look, about to say something, but stops when he sees her face.{/n} "I... I'm fully satisfied, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. I have no more complaints about Valerie."
81cb496e-7a5e-410b-8763-8c72f9543bfd: {n}Valerie purses her lips. She seems to want to reply to Eveld's monologue, but in the end she changes her mind and just nods.{/n}
63121ff6-fff9-463f-91d6-eda9ce6b4d31: "Your tongue befits your beauty, my sweet! Truly, what is a beautiful flower's bud worth, if it's worm-eaten and empty on the inside?"
1574f0dc-bf5e-43c3-8d60-3ce7a75b6f6e: {n}Valerie almost screams.{/n} "I'm not going to make peace with this... this... worthless paper-stainer! Let him spend his useless time insulting his other bootlickers!"
6e82ab69-c5dd-411e-841c-13e3b001d3aa: "Enough, both of you! First you scared everybody at the tavern, and now you're embarrassing yourselves in front of the {mf|baron|baroness|King|Queen}! 02b75542-99c1-41c6-b8f2-16662d5c3fca: "I... don't know what got into me, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. Forgive me this scene."
3cb12efe-509c-49fe-9bb5-ea02d608a404: "Please forgive me, {name}. Perhaps I should leave, to calm down and come to my senses."
0a765b14-a585-4036-af77-6b6aedab899f: "That's nice. You let some steam off, and worked some things out. At least now I can let you go, hoping you won't scare our good people any more!"
2584039d-328f-449b-b09b-a68bfdfffe67: "{mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, I'll go too, but... please keep an eye on Valerie. I don't know what demon has got into her, but she's not herself lately. ff78a046-ea37-4ccd-adde-5c4f7c5c7781: "Forgive me, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}! Of course! I promise – you won't hear about Valerie from me!"
7e3d1a93-84b4-45d6-afe4-3122db0b7eb2: "If I were you, I would talk to the Storyteller. One of my lads saw Valerie arguing with him. I have no idea how anyone can have a fight with such a harmless elf... but she did!" {n}The captain bows, finishing the conversation.{/n}
253739ee-e900-48bb-bde8-946c24843cc9: "Well, I wouldn't say that... the Valerie I used to know would never harm anyone without good reason. But the old Valerie seems to be gone. So I don't know what to expect from her."
d87f12cc-69e1-492a-bec2-dc940664afee: "She got defensive. Can't say a word to her. We've been careful around her, since she..." {n}The captain runs a finger across his face meaningfully.{/n} "I'm close to ordering my lads to keep an eye out for her in the streets, to make the common people's lives a little calmer."
7967eae1-9393-4d4f-9ba5-3ae72705c866: {n}Eveld clasps his hand to his chest ostentatiously.{/n} "Forgive me! Who would I be, if I stooped to such low attacks! I won't deny that the cautionary tale of this lady could inspire me..."
476cbf31-6a49-4be5-a11b-cf13bb15115e: "How can you listen to this featherbrain? Of course, in the face of justice he's ready to disown his own parents!"
0f2edfec-29d7-4134-b92b-06fb89c5af85: {n}The captain shakes his head sadly.{/n} "Don't even try, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. I'm afraid even {g|Abadar}Abadar{/g} couldn't get to the bottom of this ball of accusations."
d0ac925f-0b8f-4344-9604-830bb676f8e3: "...and if I'm allowed to continue, let me say what this pasquinade was devoted to: the sad position of the arts in these lands, forgive my frankness. Anyway, the good lady is unlikely to understand what allegory and poetic hyperbole are!"
86830e66-044d-4f96-b4ce-2cae47754584: "What do you find so strange about this place?"
23318719-6cea-48cd-9ca3-1343a3a6d1b9: "Cast your spells, and open the passage!"
6d31ebfc-6b4b-41ef-9228-a0af5de5fb3b: "Let's not touch the flower for now."
897ee024-7f5f-4e5d-b1c2-b0a570ccfa20: {n}The old wizard examines the flower, mumbling some spells. His face is a strange expression of surprise, admiration and incomprehension.{/n}
7aa4ed86-758f-495c-a966-42b2ec13563d: "I have seen a lot in my time, but this castle is the most incredible thing I have ever encountered. I understand more or less how it was created... But who could have done it? And the real question – why?"
392931a7-3acb-4216-9a06-ab0ec82c041a: "What an impossible place! If we survive this, we shall have to return here and examine everything carefully!"
72358f7d-74d9-4c80-9186-8144aade47b7: "This castle wasn't built as a dungeon. No, it was once an ordinary above-ground stone fortress. Someone spent dozens if not hundreds of years, sinking it slowly and carefully into the ground."
2c5ac8a8-5e07-4695-b0ed-2d7507391648: "Of course, the weight of the ground would have crushed it like an egg, which is why its wall had to be strengthened by magic. That is why these flowers are here. – To keep the entire dungeon from crumbling!"
870b294f-d83e-4d73-bf3f-0618d52ad4b7: {n}The wizard cracks his fingers.{/n} "As soon as the passage opens, everyone run inside. The walls are very unstable here!"
17f7b406-6dad-437d-ad0f-1857c851fc36: "But tell me, who could have spent so much resources, time, effort? And mask it to appear like an ordinary cyclops tomb? It would be cheaper to dig a real tomb!"
28582e12-1d08-4c93-a02a-5dd537727a23: "This place is incredible. I cannot even imagine what we might find at the bottom!"
8921f7ac-3a23-46be-be2d-06c699057aef: "However, that is not important now. We can contemplate the wonders of the magical arts once we are out of danger. For now the important thing is that I know how to clear the passage. I only hope I am skilled enough to keep the entire building from collapsing on our heads! Tell me when you are ready, and I will try to move the flower's roots and open that wall neatly."
f9094103-72dd-4e0f-8197-5ddfd9e7a6de: "You want to use this opportunity to find out why the gnomes left the First World – and how they might return. Right?"
61b6a2c8-fbf2-48a0-a174-5e82491a1302: "I don't know and I don't care. I'm not doing this."
39dfd8e6-d2ac-43e2-b4cb-e1093db8ee4f: "Do you know anything about these debates? Or are we completely in the dark here?"
0438448a-ac62-4607-8c70-21c4cdc1725b: "We can't pass up such an opportunity. I agree to participate."
964beb5e-fe03-460b-9cc3-cd126a4c2245: "I've heard about them. Strange entertainments, held on Golarion by fey lords from the First World. Strange tests with various unique rewards..."
5b0c73d2-bbb9-44d2-9b67-85705ba78fc0: "Keep your riddles to yourself. I'm not interested."
d4a2d915-5421-4e68-928d-0caf8a333f94: "Who do you think we should take as our third?"
be1d4cd2-4412-41e0-9d32-47a4760063a9: "Amazing. You managed to save your barony from an invasion of monsters from {g|First World}the First World{/g}. But you were not able to protect it from the attention of the First World's more powerful denizens. Believe it or not, but {kingdomname} has been chosen as the next location for the Inconsequent Debates!"
d3b073f9-bccf-4932-82e6-636b2c84c085:
"A curious phenomenon that isn't very well known. They say it's based on a bet made by the {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g}, the rulers of {g|First World}the First World{/g}, quite a long time ago. One day one of them sent a delegation of fey to {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g}. They announced where the competition would take place.
Don't let the name fool you, it's anything but debates. The contests begin as soon as they have enough participants."
da762970-5e51-45e1-bf45-7d5d808bfaa7: "The contests and the reward are different every time. Although 'every time' is a stretch — only three such occasions are known over thousands of years. Anyway, it's happened again! And this time the reward is a chance to ask any question whatsoever of the Host, the competition's mastermind. This creature, whoever it is, speaks on behalf of the {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g}. Do you see why we can't miss such a chance?"
2a95f9b8-0ecd-4a4f-9e37-bc3f1c0d9072: "But..." {n}Jubilost loses his usual confidence for a moment.{/n} "It's a chance to gain new unique knowledge! What could be more important? Anyway, I'm obviously talking to the wrong person. Waste your time playing at war and running around swamps if that's all you care about."
5b077422-e665-41e8-94d3-c692b3a248ed: "Nice to see our association has left a mark on you. Yes, of course! I'm none too happy that we'll have to play by the {g|Eldest}Eldest's{/g} rules. You know my opinion of the fey lords isn't very high. But if that's what the truth requires, then so be it. In the end, who would best know the answer to my question, if not the self-appointed deities of {g|First World}the First World{/g}?"
bcad88e3-23c6-414b-9be7-15f294ba8656: "Just think! We have an opportunity to ask a question of the Host — the messenger of the self-appointed deities of {g|First World}the First World{/g} — and demand an answer! The gnomes originally ventured from the First World, lost their immortality because of it, and received our curse in exchange. — the {g|Bleaching}Bleaching{/g}. No one has discovered the reasons for it — and none can stave off its consequences. But if we managed to win the competition..."
c175b454-c879-40f1-a0cb-55029a7f041c: "You never know what mad ideas the fey might have cooked up. I only know one condition: only teams of three are allowed to participate."
eb3975f2-fbb9-4c65-986b-8f95da0b4e79: "Considering that the fey are involved — absolutely. But if the chronicles are true, no one has died in any previous debate."
47a35210-aecc-4cd3-8497-e3a7d68a60d4: "Great! I'll mark the spot on the map where the competition will take place. The sooner we arrive there, the better. The fey lords won't wait forever!"
c8385683-019b-4ae2-a1d9-ed54f57bdfe5: "Your knowledge is — well, pleasantly surprising! It's true, the Inconsequent Debates are anything but debates. They say that the {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g} once made a bet. No one knows what it was, but sometimes one or another of them sends a delegation of fey to {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g}. Here they hold insane competitions for those who volunteer to enter, and present the winners with whimsical awards."
4a14c915-84d0-44c6-840a-7ed7afab1ed5: I think we should take Linzi. Something tells me fey are not likely to hold competitions in rope pulling or beer drinking. But the skills of a bard might come in handy. Besides, we should give the young lady a chance to channel some of that energy!"
b39d1bb4-23c7-40ae-8ade-0a617ac10cdb: "I insist that we take this chance. It's an opportunity to learn the secrets of the fey, and possibly alter the fate of an entire race."
467a1948-1b52-4070-9574-aad16cff2339: "Greetings, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}! As you know, I was born in Kyonin, the most wonderful land that has ever existed. 160c0027-836a-45ff-af3b-603981ee4fd1: "Good day to you, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}! And the day is truly good. I saw so many happy people and skillful entertainers on my way here. The {mf|barony|barony|kingdom|kingdom} is changing before our very eyes!"
219a795c-7d2a-4b38-b484-a1d9b06fa3a8: "It's a fine thing, to share in the joy and amusement. Look! This is my gift to you, {mf|baron|baroness|King|Queen}!"
3a3c0390-23a7-4fe2-86d2-c62ed5ed9381: [Leave the Six Bears' camp] "Wait, I need to do something else first."
b1922db9-2fbc-4be9-80f7-3c9298732f04: "They're waiting for us. Are you ready?"
6ea53b8d-852d-45ac-ab82-c8b00abe00fc: {n}Amiri fills her chest with air and exhales sharply.{/n} "Let's go!"
8ad724df-6a01-43e1-a579-8b355c410737: "You know, Ekun, when I gutted my family, I felt great, unparalleled pleasure. It was so wonderful... I wish I could feel that bliss again!"
106b7d13-b758-44c1-ab51-5618564cbb19: "Are you trying to insult me? I'm not listening. I won't give you the pleasure."
1fb509d9-43cc-45c4-8fd1-6b2f69b073ac: "I'm sorry, I don't like that. Let's stick to regular love play, ok?"
b51dff19-1ee5-41fa-9516-5caaa7197924: "Are you sure? I wouldn't want to hurt you..."
e3a6016c-55de-4252-9bd5-973c07928c54: "Be careful what you wish for. Next time you won't be able to sit!"
da83b9c8-7ea3-4308-87b6-865c8398b7a2: "I've never done that... But if you want to — let's try."

d16816d2-2ecc-4345-9d2e-8167fb5a4e43: "Armag was a coward and a piece of scum, unworthy of his name. He fled the battlefield, hid underground, and died like a filthy rat, groveling at my feet!"
7fd0f031-fe3f-4c79-84f9-a6116030ca31: "These seem like Tiger Lords affairs. What help would I be?"
55490ec1-e9b9-4258-bd64-f5eb55dc8db1: "Armag was a pathetic madman. He died in the tomb, unable to pass the trials!"
497415a6-2734-4b4c-bda7-c9df023bacdc: "Why are your quarrels my affair? Go back to Numeria and do whatever you like. Leave me out of your feud."
c1a24f28-1fff-46ea-ac6c-ac6f914b22bd: "All right, I'll take in any Tiger Lords who wish to leave their tribe and live on my lands — provided they swear an oath of fealty first."
f3f004f0-ebd4-4d4a-b28e-22ef031fa099: "There's no need to change chieftains. Let Armag remain your leader — he's a hero and a personal friend."
b9fc9b44-476a-4225-bb86-ab113c558ad1: "There's no need to change chieftains. Let Armag remain your leader — he's a hero and my sworn brother."
0dd903ce-5d2c-448a-90a7-92388db8d897: "Amiri fought Armag — she would have won, if not for the Sister's dirty tricks. She's worthy of being your leader."
68d8c323-3417-48e8-a6df-3581e39315b5: "Dugath is wise and valiant. He'll make a fine leader."
1d497d8c-27f6-4006-b3bd-cf83b4999814: "Gwart is young, but he's brave and smart. In time, he'll make a true chieftain."
3017e6cd-aadb-4eec-90db-e23fb019cf96: "I've changed my mind. You'll bring me nothing but trouble if you stay. Return to Numeria and deal with your problems yourselves."
55ad704e-5692-408d-aec9-859524effe5a: "You heard me — leave. If I find you in my lands again, you'll be greeted with fire and steel!"
9c5e33e4-b373-49fc-9d77-f560842eb417: {n}It's noisy at the tomb's exit — many {g|Tiger Lords}Tiger Lords{/g} tribesmen have gathered here. They're arguing and bickering, and the discussion is so heated that some participants have began punching their opposition or drawing weapons, while more level heads work to calm them down.{/n}
20ff762a-696e-48e9-bd5c-5dcb18a63b68: {n}The crowd is greatest around Armag. The deposed chieftain's escort holds their hands on their weapons, throwing nervous glances toward their tribesmen.{/n}
bb28eab4-20cd-40cc-8939-1cebda8fc046: {n}Amiri stands apart from the crowd, contemplating something intensely. Her arms are crossed over her chest, and she's biting her lip.{/n}
2a6730f1-4564-42d3-a229-14a15db1d7f5: {n}{d|Ashman}Dugath{/d} is here too. Noticing you, he stops speaking and gives you a warm smile.{/n}
6163deeb-d28e-41a5-967f-8d7c9de0cd24: {n}{d|Ashman}Dugath{/d} is here too. Noticing you, he turns away.{/n}
05dcc2f3-1dad-4b96-bf2a-ba870e84160d: {n}As you step forward, the crowd surrounds you. The {g|Tiger Lords}Tiger Lords{/g} bombard you with questions about the fate of their deposed chieftain.{/n}
564d65a1-7434-4fe6-90ae-5f74ecdbc84a: "It's good you're here. As you can see, the tribe's on the verge of collapse. Maybe you can help us work things out without resorting to fratricide."
3e36b120-a54b-4e48-b115-c7303976e482: {n}The barbarians all fall silent, stunned. A moment later, the arguing breaks out once more.{/n}
dd2720b3-4751-4109-bdc6-64a7a7d58d95: {n}Your words spur a new wave of controversy. As some barbarians cheer, others angrily defend their hero.{/n}
bb12745d-a5eb-4576-b33b-6a975337d404: {n}Your words cause a wave of outrage. For a while, the {g|Tiger Lords}Tiger Lords{/g} forget about their dispute and instead yell at you, demanding proof and accusing you of lying. However, it doesn't take long for them to begin arguing among themselves again.{/n}
0cff1d16-a3b5-4faa-a2f3-48db8dcc5da8: {n}{d|Gwart}Gwart{/d}, Dugath's apprentice, pushes his way to you through the crowd of arguing barbarians.{/n}
ec81c697-251e-4737-99a6-80442784bc9c: "It's a tribal council of sorts. Once word spread about the location of Armag's tomb, elders and other influential tribesmen hurried to come here. Armag's actions have split the tribe in two — some call him a hero, while others consider him a criminal."
51a9a348-b874-4c29-bbbb-8047d9a770cf: "Your army forced us to retreat. You defeated our chieftain in an honest fight. What's more, you've achieved what no one before you could — you delved into Armag's tomb and proved yourself worthy to enter his resting chamber! And if that weren't enough, the land where the tomb is located is yours, or soon to be yours. Everything hinges upon your decision."
73e74c4c-6507-4616-b6d8-2a4f8fd983f8: {n}Your words just add fuel to the fire. Some barbarians cheer, others demand proof, and some just stare at you, stunned, unable to believe the fall of their hero.{/n}
66c18333-5eaf-4a14-90db-c948faf55e06: "Our elders, clerics, bards, and strongest fighters have gathered here... Everyone important enough to have a voice in the matters of our tribe. And as you can hear, they're more than happy to continue using those voices. With the fate of our tribe at stake, I can only pray that great {g|Gorum}Gorum{/g} holds his hand and allows us to resolve it without bloodshed!"
7927e77b-dded-4322-9e51-3b415a9eb9f9: "Armag's death failed to mend the wounds his life inflicted on the tribe. Quite the contrary, in fact."
9f532559-e9fe-449f-bf0f-4c69bfff96a9: "Those who curse Armag for sending his tribesmen to senseless deaths also won't tolerate those who praise him as a great chieftain."
0e87e15b-8f77-41e8-b6bc-4280494a7e91: "You're well within your rights, but please consider the wisdom of this decision. We live quite close to your lands, and most river kings would be eager to have us as their friends and allies."
05f26325-044a-4f21-bbb8-8af959f03098: {n}This time there is no yelling, no bickering. After a short, intense debate, one of the elders addresses you.{/n} "We gratefully accept your offer. With your permission, we'll settle here, keeping the peace of Armag's tomb as well as the peace of your borders."
f9c9dea4-fe2c-495e-a87b-27626a297830: "There is one more issue we must discuss. Who will lead the {g|Numeria}Numerian{/g} {g|Tiger Lords}Tiger Lords{/g}? While it may no longer be your concern, those who make their homes in your lands will need a leader. And this person will need to be respected by the tribe but also hold your trust. If you nominate an appropriate candidate, we'll heed your decision."
24dbd047-0956-4af9-9856-7dd78cbcd235: {n}The crowd breaks into shouting, both of agreement and of outrage. Raising the sacred sword, Armag steps forward. His gaze wanders over the crowd, finally rising to the skies.{/n} "Armag was wrong. He believed the witches' lies. He spilled the blood of his kin for no reason. But that's all in the past! Before the eyes of {g|Gorum}Gorum{/g}, on this sacred blade, Armag swears to devote his life to the tribe! To bring the tribe glory and riches, like in ancient times! No, better than ancient times!"
109269c9-df28-4582-a7e2-1eb866efe347: {n}The cleric nods with dignity and steps forward.{/n} "{g|Tiger Lords}Tiger Lords{/g}! We can't let this rivalry split our tribe. We're still brothers and sisters, and if trouble comes, we'll unite and fight it together. But for now, {g|Gorum}Gorum{/g} calls for us to go our separate ways for a while. Return to {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g}, choose a new chieftain, and lead the tribe to wealth and glory. We will remain here, by the tomb of our ancient leader. Farewell, brothers and sisters!"
e85e8843-8b28-4c8e-a3d1-298ce11016bf: {n}Amiri is surprised by your words, but the {g|Tiger Lords}Tiger Lords{/g} noisily express their approval. The crowd pushes her forward, practically carrying her on their shoulders, as everyone gathers around her, waiting for her to answer.{/n}
f0ca2667-2515-4395-b740-c1ce1e4113ce: {n}The cleric's lips tighten into a thin line. He shakes his head and answers in an ice-cold voice.{/n} "I appreciate the honor, but I cannot {d|c31 Ashman Hostile}accept{/d}. I'll be returning to {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g}."
4ccbeef1-9824-4541-9ecb-bfeaf1323b43: {n}Your suggestion opens a new wave of debates, but everyone soon calms down — no one can propose a better candidate for leader. Reluctantly, the {g|Tiger Lords}Tiger Lords{/g} finally agree with you. The young man steps forward.{/n} "Brothers and sisters, Your Grace... Thank you. I won't fail you."
389a66ec-4d95-4135-b607-b4eaedd875a1: "So be it. The gods bore witness — we were ready to extend you the hand of friendship." {n}Cursing under their breath and throwing angry glances your way, the barbarians leave.{/n}
53645241-953d-469e-88d5-2df0f154bcb7: {n}The last words of the chieftain's speech are drowned in the cheers of his supporters. His opponents turn and leave one by one. Armag approaches you and shakes your hand, to great applause.{/n} "The {g|Tiger Lords}Tiger Lords{/g} will roam this realm. If anyone dares violate its borders and head toward the capital, they'll first have to step over Armag's dead body!"
a3750044-fd03-4360-b56d-8cb088152abf: {n}The barbarians nod grimly as the cleric speaks. Once his speech is over, some of them remain, and the others bid farewell to their tribesmen as they leave. Dugath approaches you and shakes your hand.{/n} "That's how it goes, Baron{mf||ess}. Truth be told, when first we met, I was sure {g|Gorum}Gorum{/g} would eventually pit us against one another on the battlefield. I'm glad that was not the case. We'll roam this area, and if any enemies approach your borders, they'll have to deal with us first!"
8882b844-5e12-4f99-9796-c4237e9dc9ed: "{g|Tiger Lords}Tiger Lords{/g}! I'm, erm... I may not be from your tribe, but... Well, long story short, I just want to say, the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g} is a place where... Um, it's odd. Everyone who manages to survive here — they're exiles, but they're like family to each other. It's crap that your situation made you turn on each other, but here, in these lands, we all have a chance for a new start. Whatever your Armag did... Together, we'll find glory! Mark my words, I won't fail you!" {n}The barbarians greet Amiri's inconsistent speech with applause. Then the time for farewells comes — some Tiger Lords remain at the tomb with their new leader, while the rest begin their journey back to {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g}.{/n}
3bd192ab-5364-435f-a7ca-5d65428a62c5: {n}Amiri approaches you, seemingly still unable to wrap her head around what happened.{/n} "You amaze me! Could have given some warning, or something! It's all right, though, it's not like I can complain! Ha ha! But I hope you don't expect to get rid of me that easy. I guess I'll just have to figure out how to manage my time traveling with you alongside leading my new tribe. But I can do it, don't you doubt! The {g|Tiger Lords}Tiger Lords{/g} will roam this area near your borders. If some enemy drags his ass here, he'll regret ever being born!"
a5636dee-defd-46fe-b65c-27685948ee12: {n}The young cleric shakes your hand.{/n} "I thank you for giving us shelter. Our tribe will roam this area. If enemies come, have no doubt, we'll stop them!"
7ef36777-c928-417e-bc19-ed796fd9a827: {n}The barbarians listen to Gwart attentively but with little enthusiasm. After he finishes his speech, it's time for farewells — some {g|Tiger Lords}Tiger Lords{/g} remain near the tomb with their new leader, while the rest begin their journey back to {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g}.{/n}
fa6e342f-5ba0-438d-8cdd-6f9cff028333: {n}After the new chieftain finishes his speech, the time comes for farewells. Some barbarians exchange hugs and shake their tribesmen's hands with teary eyes, while others simply clench their fists and spit on the ground, muttering curses. Finally, those who decided to return to {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g} leave your lands, and the rest surround their leader.{/n}
5b268564-6dfa-461e-8081-295f26b71a9b: "Amazing, no?" {n}The elf looks at the crowd of barbarians with pretentious indifference.{/n}
78b8f840-07d9-439f-a920-9640efb99edd: "Chaos and a rift — how else could this story end? Armag may not have been the best chief, but in trying to overthrow him, you only kindled the flames of a feud."
1026cb33-3680-4ef8-adb4-748e9feb0555: "Friendship? This rabble has quite the high opinion of themselves. They're uncontrollable and unpredictable — not fit to be servants or allies."
c203b5d2-02df-460f-a103-ca513f6ff6d9: "A murderer who settles next to the family of his victim brings only chaos and grief. The {g|Tiger Lords}Tiger Lords{/g} have no place beside us. Do not change your mind, {name} — let them go."
b8ec71f7-7f94-4596-8c81-93dfc08e5d4c: "This is a chance to show mercy and vision, {name}. These people may be lost, but they can still be brought to the right path. Stop this rift in their tribe from forming — stop them from suffering further bloodshed."
f5df16b6-f576-4976-9545-fbaf0391c22b: {n}The cleric's lips tighten into a thin line. He shakes his head and answers in an ice-cold voice.{/n} "That won't happen. I despise what has become of this tribe."
ec567ef4-4de7-4f35-b0a9-a94473b92e19: "I say we'd better root them out. But if, for some reason, you don't want to do it, then give them a weak chief, or someone you can control. Otherwise, in ten or twenty years they'll return to your lands, to try their luck once more."
282898e1-faa9-4cfc-9dc3-52c66dccb273: "These people bring only chaos and death. The best solution would be to send them back home, and never let them look upon the borders of this land again."
314f3b0a-6d3b-472e-8eb1-614482546237: "This Lander Lebeda... He's a shady fellow! I wouldn't risk setting out on a crusade with him."
770c4748-c2d9-4d9a-96ea-922b107cf684: "You're just realizing that now?! I don't know what's more amazing — the fact that you see this about him right away, or the fact I can still be surprised by people's naivete..."
6bdca6f3-6f27-47f3-ac69-c1a190984f7f: "When an animal flees its own pack, it's been chased away. When a man sets out on his own, he's running only from himself…"
f082d916-7f7d-40ec-84bb-e3217f70c63d: "Ha. His vile intent was written in red upon his forehead. I've seen enough such adventurers in the courts of Kyonin. But I suppose this only makes it easier to use him for our benefit..."
2d14e372-648b-47aa-859d-acd450f12a67: "Elina, could you give me a bottle of wine?"
b06082d8-d76f-4191-8538-d8a06dad87d0: "Thank you for organizing such a wonderful party for Ekun!"
81ed1d96-554f-4b8a-95db-b150f124bc7f: [Leave] "Well, I'm going to go check in on some of the others!"
a9b2b486-c7cb-4fbb-a009-84b340b9b96c: "Are you answering your ruler's command with a question?"
7340d735-e8db-4c5e-8945-4f5fac716379: "I need a bottle of wine. Now, I'm going to count to three. One..."
040d3e26-f226-4696-8c72-3bca09fcc3d8: "I need a bottle for Ntavi. She's our guest — you can't refuse her food and drinks."
ac62c023-bab6-43db-8f55-7864e5bc2881: "What can I do for you, Your Grace?"
6877a006-7e95-46ee-ba82-3938d4e10fb2: "My pleasure, Your Grace! I am happy everything turned out this way as well... Besides, entertaining a man such as Ekundayo is a pleasure!" {n}The innkeeper giggles, covering her mouth with a handkerchief.{/n}
31fc0573-9915-408b-a092-d73f4872e362: "Don't bother with the bottle, Your Grace. I'll pour for you — just bring a glass!"
401a9c5d-3702-489c-aa14-4c4d92c893a6: {n}The innkeeper raises an eyebrow.{/n} "I have no idea why Your Grace invited this harpy... Of course, you know better, but still..."
a0929716-6913-4b38-ae5b-8c72bde11e6c: {n}The innkeeper makes a long face.{/n} "There, there, here you go, Your Grace..."
f185ea7f-973d-4e66-866f-b468d862b248: "It's a pity you couldn't find time to investigate my murder. Our primary piece of evidence — the wild boar's carcass in the Old Sycamore — was torn to pieces, either by local wildlife or starving peasants. Enneo the merchant managed to flee, as well. All the clues have been lost. Now we may as well forget about it."
74117b64-3022-42b9-9418-49fb950d4669: "It's a pity you couldn't find time to continue investigating my murder. I've learned that a group of travelers visited the bank of the {g|Thorn River}Thorn River{/g}, exactly where the boar appeared before the Old Sycamore. But now the travelers are gone. Enneo the merchant managed to flee, as well. All the clues are lost."
d5c7301f-cff4-4975-b6ff-cae4d8291707: "It's a pity you couldn't find time to visit Enneo the merchant. He managed to escape, and his possessions were stolen by some petty thieves. All the clues are lost now."
93a3cb79-ceb5-42d7-bfc5-d2097adeb4a9: "Why Linzee smell so bad – ugh, like flowers. Clean flowers. Stings eyes."
cf213ebf-3c3d-4492-a6d4-8b32dca43e39: "I will take that compliment in the spirit it was given. So thank you."
c124edad-1aca-4441-a73d-abac956b166e: "I don't like this whole Bloom Season! What if that scoundrel we saw in the First World wants to grow another flower?"
475e6592-bb48-472e-aac6-8b80b4d328ab: "I... don't think that is likely to happen. Creating a second Everblooming Flower would require far too much effort."
4cde1de8-5cb3-4a00-881c-03f61cea9981: "I agree. I prefer an honest fight — and I dislike the unknown. Enemies who stab you in the back, with the help of alien magic."
0d4e989f-57b0-4488-adba-158a866d598c: "It would be less amusing, the second time."
237958cc-c9be-45ae-9d7d-2ac90f922b02: "Right! Who tied a bell to my tail while I was asleep?!"
11e9a6d2-19df-435a-927f-322d4cc929f7: "You have the right view on life. Take whatever you can from it! Enjoy every moment! Perhaps sooner or later you, too, will be touched by Urgathoa's hand?"
2b599beb-5008-4d67-a879-2c59a724d79f: "Calistria save me from that sort of pleasure! Hey, all of you – you hear? If I die, burn my corpse and scatter the ashes! So that none of the undeads get me!"
17cb893d-c0ce-4b90-8920-e2feb542a5da: "There is a nick in my sword again. Where's my whetstone..."
7afc08c9-9e60-4e3d-bc5d-ea553816eac7: "Nooo, not that sound again, please! Look me in the eyes, noble Valerie. Are you prepared to murder your companion with your 'Shink! Shink! Shink!'?"
e54df55a-daf8-4269-93fc-25ac0c2c0e86: "Nooo, not that sound again, please! Look me in the eyes, noble Valerie. Are you prepared to murder your companion with your 'Shink! Shink! Shink!'?"
7570a0c1-03b2-4f21-ba22-19ca0a8acb04: "I wish to know more about the Black Marquis and his Protectorate."
eab476a3-9697-4564-8d67-3dce3a568e6c: {g|Relations5_1}[Choice effects]{/g} "Show him how strong our army is. They'd better not cross swords with us."
24e59afa-d46f-4c1a-b3c2-5760ec442202: {g|Relations5_2}[Choice effects]{/g} "Show him we're rich, and he'll conclude that they'll be better off as our friends."
41cb6412-504d-441b-b18a-6d061416227c: {g|Relations5_3}[Choice effects]{/g} "Deceive him. Convince him we're a backwards country with little to offer."
f6063082-1cdc-496d-8151-bec29d62358f: "I will leave this decision to you."
f5d8293e-7d8b-4003-a359-01131a886783: "{name}, we've arrested a strange man. He was making a map of our rivers and bays. Upon his capture, he shouted that he serves the Black Marquis, and was sent to create a map of the local trade routes. But pirates are full of guile, and this map might be used not for trade, but for raids. What are we going to do with him, being that he's admittedly serving another king?"
5f395075-c7d0-4d88-80f8-ef6b8eb91824: "{name}, we captured a suspicious man. He was making a map of our rivers, bays and backwaters. When he was placed under arrest, he admitted that he serves the Black Marquis. By his account, he was sent to create a map, in order to arrange trade with us. But I'd more likely believe that the pirates are preparing for a big raid."
c7de39f4-d7f8-40ef-9a67-d3695d2a15f9: "{mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}! I'm afraid I have bad news. Today by the river they caught a man making a map of rivers and bays in our lands. He said he was a scout for the Black Marquis, and was drawing a map to open a trade route with us. But everyone knows the greedy and deceptive nature of these pirates. It's more likely that they're preparing an attack against us."
a2579319-997a-42b4-8526-b7f6dbf857e2: "Once a {g|Cheliax}Chelish{/g} pirate named Morgan the White visited the village of Deadbridge to rest and replenish his supplies. He settled there and in time decided to build a whole pirate nation there! Those joined him began to collect duties from foreign ships, but they never touched the ships of the {g|River Kingdoms}River Kingdoms{/g}. Thus he gained the support and respect of his neighbors. That's how the Protectorate was created."
efc839cc-d23e-458c-a541-dcf00e186ca4: "It's a group of pirates calling themselves a country. It was created by a {g|Cheliax}Chelish{/g} bandit Morgan, the White Marquis. But he didn't rule for long. The Protectorate changed hands several times, until the Black Marquis took its helm – the most cunning and treacherous of the White Marquis' henchmen. There is only one law in this land – the law of the pirate. But these bandits don't touch the ships of the {g|River Kingdoms}River Kingdoms{/g}... at least, that's the official tale. But how far that agreement is respected – only the dead can say."
cad87eb1-2704-4d6a-b746-a8cbdfecb8e5: "It's a dangerous place. This dominion was founded by a pirate from {g|Cheliax}Cheliax{/g}. When he came across the village of Deadbridge, he saw an ideal camp for pirates and the capital of his future domain. Morgan called on many allies, and ordered that no ships be touched if they fly under the banners of the {g|River Kingdoms}River Kingdoms{/g} – and 'duties' from all other countries be collected. Now the pirate nation is ruled by the Black Marquis, and his subjects are, all of them, pirates and robbers."
4fcf3438-a2d0-4f3a-8c10-6151d00eaf14: "I'll show him the strength of our army. After the pirate sees our soldiers, he'll not likely recommend that his Black Marquis ever approach our shores."
aab09fe2-ce9c-4d8f-8177-437efd09a753: "Well, maybe it's better we have no business with them. Who knows how much blood there would be on their wares and gold?"
faf49c9c-99bd-4e96-9212-207d6e62da2a: "Great! When we show off our riches, and convince pirates to trade with us, not fight. I can't wait for an opportunity to chat with the first captains who bring us their goods!"
fb650192-397f-4690-bd0d-70225c1e36dc: "Hm.... You're probably right, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}! Your courage allows you to see their greed, whereas I, due to my humble nature, am too horrified by their cruelty to see anything beyond it. I do hope our riches tempt them to start trading with us."
3377b691-d7a5-4431-a4cf-dbf9ebc8b718: "Hm... Fine, I'll lead him past the pigsties and chicken houses, so he thinks it's our main avenue. Let's hope it works. Although acting has never been my strong suit."
2d927230-2b22-4a08-98a8-31185dfb0005: "Great! This pirate will doubly regret his mission, because there's nothing worthy waiting for him here!"
239a2ba8-0cce-46f7-8a9b-9577946add0d: "The prisoner awaits his fate. We could receive him as an honorable guest, showing off our riches and power. But it would only whet the pirate's appetite. Better to show him an empty corner where there's nothing to take. But only demonstration of military power would make these pirates forget the road to our lands. Everything else is a half-measure."
128a44dc-9341-41b2-9e2b-c475016f0815: "I do not recommend we try impressing him with military parades. Pirates are fearless and stupid, they're not afraid of a stronger opponent. It's better we receive him as a dear guest and convince that it would be beneficial to be friends with us. Or we could do the complete opposite, and pretend we're a poor backwards country, with no treasures or riches whatsoever! This would yield the best result!"
305d669b-c4c5-4f91-add2-15ea44613a3b: "The most important thing now is to appear strong and influential. If we demonstrate our military power, the pirates will be afraid to face us. Even better – we could show them our riches. Whether or not the story about trade routes is a tale, we can let the Black Marquis wonder if he'd be better off if he were our friend."
c38ad5a1-2e11-43a7-8545-f80d251a79b6: "Your {mf|grace|grace|highness|highness}! Thank you for finding time to visit this humble corner of your gods-blessed {mf|barony|barony|kingdom|kingdom}! How can I be of service?"
9dca56d1-5a0c-40ac-91bd-135a06eeafa0: "May the gods never abandon you in their mercy!"
0ac49d56-1523-437e-a6a8-2cf59dfd4067: "What a beautiful sky. I remember a similar sky in Hajoth Hakados, when Octavia and I hid on a roof, escaping from the Technic League's agents."
6b44ad89-6918-4272-bdbe-28f28592ec21: "What is this I hear – Regongar talking about beauty? I was hoping at least this one vice was alien to you! Well, now I guess you embody absolutely everything I hate!"
b2332beb-87ec-4727-82d9-3d3ef0166c88: "It's surprising to hear you speak of the beauty of the sky. You seem more like someone who kicks people for admiring the sky, not doing it yourself."
4b6b6fae-b76b-456e-9b91-109fb454dfb6: "You know what surprises me most about your stories? How — how did the Technic League let you escape so many times? If the resources and people they assigned to catching slaves were instead focused on guarding them in the first place, their problems would be solved..."
0ee6faaa-2578-4116-b0f1-277917df3d6c: "Ugh, what a stench… though I smelled a lot of crappy stuff in my time!"
0e3916e4-1d15-4aa1-b28f-07da8d3426c0: "It smells like someone taked a huge crap nearby! Couldn't we find a better place for camp?"
e510da5a-58f1-4714-95d2-4739a0bcc815: "Ha! Be grateful we're not in Abaddon, the native plane of daemons! According to what I've read, it smells of cinders, swamp gas, feces — and things far worse!"
16de1dc9-d8a5-4c6b-84bb-83a9fd862d11: "Seems like an animal died nearby… perhaps if we bury it, the smell will go away?"
412eac54-d5b7-4372-91cf-a72fc8cb817d: "In moments like this I regret not carrying a flask of perfume with me, like so many other paladins of Shelyn!"
fd35deba-462f-43bf-8183-eecce1cbaa57: "And I am once again grateful that fate has spared me such distractions..."
6a96f6cd-a98e-47cd-8d6a-107b0d6d5257: "There's no water, and nothing to start a fire. – It's all just dirt and smoke..."
3692664c-b877-451a-b807-5fc887d56f05: "Greetings!" {n}Mim's face shines with enthusiasm.{/n} "The trade in your {mf|barony|barony|kingdom|kingdom} is so lively that I'm literally overflowing with commissions! It's splendid! – The more interesting the challenge, the better!"
bf327eb4-896a-47d5-a3e2-60d8f63266a8: "Greetings. I've decided to take a break and spent some time traveling your lands, and I'm surprised how well things are going here in your {mf|barony|barony|kingdom|kingdom}! Trade is thriving, and I can easily acquire rare materials and gemstones for my jewelry. And there are so many talented people around! I left Restov to enjoy the peace and solitude of a simple country life, but I must admit — I've missed the company of other artists!"
916945ef-fa8b-4920-a439-05031b9ef08f: "Finally! I have labored long on a special present for you, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. Mim is the best, isn't she?"
5c8fbdf6-51ca-4a08-abfd-a90e345550e1: "You're from a noble family. I don't understand why you didn't simply return to your parents' castle, rather than wandering the forests, slaying all manner of monsters."
598ef0d5-0416-40e5-8c36-71640594cb7e: "It's hard to understand... Here in the Stolen Lands I can be what I am, not who people want to see. Most simply want a beautiful façade, never noticing the human behind it."
f1b7d0bc-ee55-438a-9ea3-8b9d3b5c8960: {n}The mirror comes alive under your touch. Its dark surface is lit by flashes of a battle that happened in this very room, an unknown age ago. A group of warriors in dark clothes are fighting a flock of gargoyles. There are clouds of sorcerous mist in the hallway behind their backs. Suddenly, it's pierced by a ray of light, and the familiar wizard appears on the battlefield, holding a magic lantern in his hand. He is swaying from pain, but looks angry and resolute.{/n}
889aede0-52d2-4e4f-ba18-829425617dd6: "We will all die here! Run!" {n}One of the soldiers screams. Without hesitation, the wizard pushes him right into the gargoyles' claws. As soon as the monsters are distracted with their victim, the wizard envelops the entire group in a spell, and kills them on the spot.{/n} "Get to the stairs! To the second floor!" {n}He lights the lantern, and the warriors swiftly retreat into the mist.{/n}
a88105c6-64b0-4ae6-b6ac-e5a411a61b50: {n}The vision fades. But then another room, and another wizard's reflection appears on the other side of the glass — the one you first spoke to. It nods to you and says quietly,{/n} "I remember... remember this fight... you are on the right path."
f9bbe302-a0ab-4b79-8edc-39750c92a30c: [Give her the mushrooms] "Here are your black rattlecaps."
94bb5796-fb74-4fb7-9803-789852e83ee2: "How can I help you, good woman?"
d2d77d0b-67aa-493c-bcf0-40ff3f925e20: [Give her the herbs] "Here are your herbs, three bundles of each."
a77f8012-f6c5-4bac-a50a-3cdf4538a50f: [Show the herb you've found at the swamp] "This seems to be an unusual herb. Can you tell me what it is?"
d872ab7f-f5dd-4ccc-853c-4308d2a13a65: [Attack] "My lands will be safer without you."
d002a55d-48ff-4cf2-afdf-30001316ee12: "As far as I've heard, a daughter of a human and a fey used to live here. Her name was Elga Verniex. Are you her?"
073ffdc5-b01d-406b-bf94-0e16e146409f: [Give her the letter] "A dryad named Tiressia remembers you and would be glad to see you again. She asked me to give you this letter."
5ffcfd91-f64a-4778-8598-88ca6a3833aa: "Take a look at these coins — we found them at the bottom of a well."
35ed29e4-53c7-47a0-91ec-61d79b52b281: [Tell her about the coins] "I've learned what happened to the village, slain the monster, and freed a cursed soul..."
5aebc4f9-7009-4752-98a1-e1e40c8db4cf: "Dorsy. He was the one who cursed Wilber and Callitropsia."
df888674-d4cb-446d-b938-487093e34d32: "Nyta. If she hadn't cast Dorsy aside, none of this would have happened."
1730a26d-bd97-45b3-899a-3ba17e5c88b3: "Wilber. He's been stalling with the decision for too long, and in the end everyone started hating him."
3e3af5c3-3541-4e84-ad89-0f378a09acec: "Callitropsia. She's put a spell on Nyta and has stolen her from Dorsy."
8434541c-bb21-4841-bb4b-06963a2cb3aa: "Why bring this all up again? That's not important anymore."
e0201cb7-a837-4fe3-a6aa-22906241fb1b: "Maybe something else has destroyed the village?"
102f698c-35c2-4685-933c-ec97813b6e56: "I'm looking for a lost child. Have you seen him by chance?"
6adb09ca-dbe7-4dc7-8633-6dcba12643b9: {n}The old woman smells the mushrooms and takes a small bite. She chews on it slowly for a moment, then grins, a gleam in her eye.{/n} "Hah! Strong! These will be good, all right!"
f9d4d4dd-eae1-4f5f-803d-0c223fdaddc3: "Well, now we're talking! Much better than poking around where you don't belong, nattering on like a fool... here, look!" {n}She pulls a black, oddly-wrinkled mushroom from a bag on her belt — it has an odd smell about it that makes your eyes tear up.{/n} "This — this is a black rattlecap. The sporepods inside — the best thing for the lungs — and the skin. Me, I use them for tea. They're rare, though, but they grow thickest at the {g|Mud Bowl}Mud Bowl{/g}, east of here. Get me... at least ten... yes, ten, then we'll talk!"
15cd0873-512b-420a-a245-e7bc81efe5a3: {n}The old woman claps her hands and grins, revealing a row of brown, uneven teeth.{/n} "There's a good {mf|boy|girl}! Did it take a lot of time to find them, eh? Give them here, I'll put them to a good use..."
1e645860-e1af-4346-aaab-f846977071b2: {n}She takes the herb between her bony fingers, sniffs it, then gives you an approving nod.{/n} "You've got a good eye! The herb is useful, but not by itself. Look here."
b37630a6-3bd8-4e70-bcb4-71d2cb2e6205: "So — what in damnation are you doing here?" {n}The old woman squints at you with disapproval. Her hair is a tangle of grey, and her wrinkled skin is an unusual shade of green. Both her eyebrows and ears taper to points.{/n}
5aebfcc0-678b-423a-a2c3-869292f720ee: "You have no business prowling around here..." {n}Her eyes narrow.{/n} "What are you — a thief? Bandit?" {n}She studies you, then hisses in her throat.{/n} "Hell take you if you're a tax collector."
8774b6e2-5dc5-4bdd-9118-09f68f1395b5: "You again? Hmph. I'd offer you tea, but I don't have any. How about a cup of deathcap tincture instead?" {n}She gives a splintered grin.{/n} "Best thing for health!"
ba321709-3022-4cff-8dc6-c04b2c36dcea: "Me, eh? I'm just a harmless old woman, hoping for some peace and quiet… the 'Old Beldame,' they call me, and that's fine — been called worse in my life. Why are you asking? What fool's errand brings you all the way out here?"
8dc10c22-e533-4ee9-beb3-f57b698f0469: {n}The old woman frowns.{/n} "The 'Old Beldame' they call me when they aren't calling me worse — hag, witch — accusing me of fornicating with demons, stealing children..." {n}She grunts.{/n} "Came here to be as far away from gossips like that, but wasn't far enough. There's you knocking at my door — and just recent, some other fool came — begged me to buy his soul, can you believe it? Hnh! Is it too much to ask for some peace and quiet..."
60425dc6-5b58-42a7-a18a-ae1715bfabdd: "A boy? What would I do with a brat, pickle him in a jar? That's rich!" {n}She gives a rattling laugh.{/n} "Where is it written if an old woman likes a little peace and quiet, she must be a child-stealing witch?"
b6799244-2141-42ab-aa4e-9845a7754348: "Just look at {mf|him|her} — {mf|he|she}'s got a question!" {n}Her lip curls in a sneer.{/n} "What makes you think I've any answers for one such as you, scrabbling at my door like a beggar? Have you done anything good for me recently? You've nothing for me, and you're nothing TO me!"
daa06c43-2cbd-4878-a1b6-c45f907977aa: "Who knows what could have snatched up a child?! Mayhap he's been eaten by goblins, or lured to the swamp by the wandering lights! Or maybe his poor, sobbing mother with all her false tears strangled him in his sleep, then put him to bed with a shovel somewhere deep in the forest and now looks for someone to mantle the blame? Go to her, squeeze answers from her, make HER tell where her whelp is, but don't be bothering me!"
8ed62eb3-aa5b-4378-9a1c-086bcb6a48f9: "See, I've never done any harm to anyone without a good reason. Others have tried to harm me... they regretted it afterwards, that's certain, but folk never learn. Ohh, what should I say... " {n}With a sour expression, the old woman waves her wrinkled greenish hand.{/n}
6c243f76-0473-4307-aefb-1d7c13e2d0c6: {n}She shows you three different herbs.{/n} "This one's mudleaf. That there is gloomberry. And that — that's the dizzyhead, one guess what it does. If you can find three bundles of each — bring them to me!"
bfa557d0-1102-4a71-809f-c69fe56b7ffe: {n}Elga opens the letter, runs her eyes over it, and her expression shifts... it could be either a smile or a grimace.{/n} "So, that's how it is... Well, what does it matter now..." {n}She gives a rattling sigh.{/n} "Oh, Tiressia... I should visit her someday... yes."
a4229048-865c-4806-8fb7-68daddc281de: "Ugh, foul evil that is!" {n}She spits on the floor.{/n} "I don't know which magic is that, but it has the feel of a curse — or something even something worse! Keep it away from me!"
288b2c2c-9551-47aa-a3cc-319a64291968: "I've no idea. Used to be a village here once — good folk, well-off but not so well-off to put on airs... they were at peace with the fey — even had festivals, celebrated with them... but that was long ago — six or seven dozen years, at least."
a21f73de-fc9d-4abe-af76-66e4d85895d3: "As for what ruined them — I don't know. Got a guess, though. In the darkest nights, strange sounds come from deep in the woods — crackling and moaning, as if a great tree is twisting its roots, rattling its branches like bones. There's something there... a creature that drove away folk and fey alike."
8e7a0cb6-3065-4af0-aff6-815d134c7083: {n}She listens to your tale, nodding her head.{/n} "So, that's how it all happened... A scary thing it is, this curse and all. It would seem just a tall tale... but here we are — the village is gone! So who's to blame, you think?"
a09573d3-acb8-4c35-9bf6-151b173b8cf7: "Maybe, maybe... But the hatred may be well-earned, or at least seemed to be! Put yourself in his boots, see it through his eyes — fey are dragging your beloved to the forest, her fool of a father helping them... the fellow must have truly believed he was saving her!"
520b5f84-69ca-4d54-a722-54869223ec1f: "The heart wants what it wants, right? A girl falls in love, then the passion fades — happens all the time. The worst thing is she's cursed her own father — that's wicked, true. But her love must have been fierce if it gave birth to such a burning hate!"
5fafb8b2-6817-4347-9a07-ddac1c049be1: "Yes, Wilber was always a coward. He didn't want to hurt anyone, but in so doing, he hurt everyone and got retribution from both sides — his daughter and her groom… But he wished well to everyone, right? It wasn't his hatred that fueled the curse..."
ddb9724b-41d7-4618-aa6b-856231385fc0: "Stolen, huh? A bride's not a sack of potatoes, she's got a mind of her own — she could decide for herself whom she liked more!" {n}She grunts.{/n} "And as for putting a spell on Nyta — I don't believe it. I've seen how people act under a love-binding spell... So, though I haven't seen this whole story with my own eyes, I still believe it was born from true love."
5144f2a5-1ba1-4f4d-92cc-4bed95b778de: "That's true. What's done can't be undone — those who were right and those who were wrong, all got more than they deserved... you may have lifted the curse, but it had done its work. No people will live here for a long time... except for ones such as me."
f5b5f316-3f41-4403-bd39-61ec1b972eb0: "So, what would you say now? Who is to blame?"
29047651-89e0-4a82-a438-99a2fa6ce367: "Now that's clever of you — you're sharper than I took you for. You're right, Dorsy wasn't a mage — why would his curse come true, and with such strength?" {n}She raises an eyebrow.{/n} "Turning a dryad queen into a monster is not a simple curse, like making neighbor's knees ache when he tells a lie." {n}She sniffs, and her voice drops.{/n} "'Sides, the air in these parts feels wrong, like... no, no, never mind, we should speak no more about it."
a0ec17a1-2bd1-4635-9536-7aff4d6ae33b: {n}She's shaking with indignation. She's a proud woman, you can tell that easily, and the fact she's breaking composure makes you sure she's telling the truth.{/n}
1aa9d180-494e-45eb-911f-112b8381c153: {n}Her answer rings with indignation, but you can't tell if it is genuine or not.{/n}
2c52a581-2999-478d-a179-967b101a29c5: {n}The old woman slowly smiles and shakes her head — now, more than ever, she reminds you of a fey of the forest. {/n}"It's not up to me — judging folk. Gods can judge — it's easy for them, for they know everything. The young folks can judge as well — it's even easier for them, for they know nothing. And I... I just keep it all in my memory."
78e48cf9-6b3e-4d0e-bc7a-949427747f9e: {n}After her new herbs are tucked away, she seems a bit more pleasant, even gives a gap-toothed smile.{/n} "That's a proper greeting — trading favors! Help me, and I help you... so what did you want to know, hm? Ask, I know the area, might be able to help you on your way. Or maybe you need some potions? Nothing cheap, but nothing you can't afford — and they do the trick, they do!"
492e946e-2c71-4f53-af2e-7cfaf74d21df: {n}The Old Beldame averts her eyes.{/n} "Might be me..." {n}She sighs.{/n} "...or might not. What's the difference… who would still remember that name..."
f7668ae7-eb3b-471e-833f-c8f852acca30: [Try to put a cog inside the mechanism]
b2bd0777-ef9e-4a7d-a62a-3c3d770348c5: {n}You have all three cogs, but you're not sure how to fit them into the mechanism. Maybe the arcane markings inside are a clue.{/n}
0728dbc8-7036-494e-80f7-557803314f96: {n}You rotate the cogs and hear a rumbling noise from the statue, followed by a loud click. The panel opens, revealing the treasure stored within.{/n}
f21d4d17-b8c2-40f3-8b36-165c28da712f: {n}The stone panel and the mechanism keeping it shut are both sturdy and effective. Neither lockpicking skills nor brute force enhanced with cursing are capable of opening it. It looks like you won't get this hidden treasure without a proper key.{/n}
2175f4e3-5c68-4ced-8bf7-60e15372ca8d: {n}Your intuition tells you this statue may be hiding something of value. After several hours searching, you discover a hidden panel with a niche above it. In the niche, a set of jagged grooves adorned with arcane symbols seems to be connected to something deeper inside the statue. It seems that access to {g|Torag}Torag's{/g} treasures will require the missing cogs.{/n}
8e936d5d-899a-4b41-b89b-4c51eaeb2143: {n}This is harder than you thought. It takes some effort to place cogs into and remove them from the mechanism. After several hours of failed attempts, you finally find the right combination, so all of the cogs can now rotate.{/n}
bbddc845-567e-4a5e-abf3-b04ef9f0f8e1: {n}Jubilost inspects the markings closely.{/n} "What have we here? Some sort of puzzle? Interesting, let me see... Ah! Those are alchemical symbols, just written in ancient dwarven script. This one is "tin," so this is where we place the white cog. That one's "iron" — red one goes there. And the golden cog in the remaining space. A riddle for children, I'd suppose. Dwarves are fond of such things."
7ac8e680-b6f6-44f8-9115-ed8662d38e59: {n}No matter how you fit it, the cog won't rotate. It seems you'll need all three of them to open the panel.{/n}
3b52d936-2f71-4ad8-8cbe-9aa43ecac1bf: {n}Unfortunately, no one in your party can decipher the meaning of the markings. The only option now is try all of the possible combinations.{/n}
b8556bdc-fefb-46dd-b3b1-c67e9a2c5150: {n}Ekun bows his head and whispers a short prayer before the statue.{/n}
496035b8-fe72-4d98-8b3c-7ff4657be7bc: {n}Unlike the timeworn watchtower, the statue of {g|Torag}Torag{/g} is in perfect condition. The dwarven god's face has a stern look, almost accusatory when combined with the surrounding devastation.{/n}
b2a9cebe-2fb6-4134-9883-90f86a2adbd5: {n}Dwarven artisans are famous for installing clever hidden mechanisms in their works. You discover a hidden panel with a niche above it. In the niche, a set of jagged grooves adorned with arcane symbols seems to be connected to something deeper inside the statue. It seems that access to {g|Torag}Torag's{/g} treasures will require the missing cogs.{/n}
d6d52567-de64-41f9-bc45-74035697055d: {n}Harrim gives the statue a long look, then spits on the ground without saying a word.{/n}
c9add0a5-a622-4d85-bc5f-eaec6b15dc7f: "What's the problem?" {n}Harrim grumbles as he snatches the cogs from you and places them inside the mechanism.{/n} "This one goes here, that one there... can't you see?"
b10cdd90-0877-4b75-9a71-7fe70de26c97: {n}The markings seem vaguely familiar. Raking through your memory, you realize these are well-known alchemical symbols, though in an ancient dwarven script. The symbol for "tin" seems to be designed for the white cog, representing tinsmiths. "Iron" must mean the red cog, for blacksmiths, while "gold" is for the gold cog and goldsmiths. Having placed all the cogs properly, you see they can now rotate.{/n}
3c08f0cc-cbe8-4e75-a4cc-08d586c918e0: {n}As you whisper words of prayer to your god, you feel your heart fill with the determination to never shrink from any obstacle.{/n}
503b7a54-aa27-47f8-a96a-6b80ebf8f875: "I'll spare you the trouble and just collect this 'tax' from Oleg for myself. You could try to stop me, I suppose... it might even be amusing. The Swordlords sent me to wipe out the filth around here anyway."
447d61a4-e2a5-4427-b2c8-d9083d09f05c: [Attack] "There's no need for words. To arms!"
754154f8-9da4-49a8-81c8-34480bb63e71: "I'm not interested in bloodshed, but I won't let you rob this man. Be on your way, and I'll let you go in peace."
f1cc0832-1d6d-4618-8f27-4794444fb5ac: [Attack] "My task is to clear this land of bandits. I'll start right now."
9e9e141b-3081-4997-bfe8-0f00d0eaad40: "In the name of the Stag Lord, the — haha! -'lawful' authority in {g|Stolen Lands}the Stolen Lands{/g}, we demand this week's tax! And some beer."
c9d18381-675b-4a34-91c9-af5d0a0b4701:
"You want to drink some of my blood, too? I'm sick of you — you're like locusts! You think you control everything around here just because you put up that painted rag of yours?! You come here, squeeze us dry, and come ag-"
{n}Oleg, a large man with a rough face, stops talking when he notices you.{/n} "Ah, you must be guests from {g|Restov}Restov{/g}!"
c4d6734d-ff1c-4257-8218-eb780ede2233: {n}Oleg clenches his fists tightly.{/n} "It seems guests from {g|Restov}Restov{/g} are even worse than the bandits around here. To the Pit with you, then! Take the money — just leave us be."
5360889d-f086-432b-9da2-232d62177965: {n}The woman looks you up and down.{/n} "Stranger, you sure are lucky we don't have more of our crew with us today. Go ahead and keep this fool's money. But you can be sure I'll tell the Stag Lord all about what happened here!"
9c8cc812-9b37-44a9-8a66-cf07476cbf3a: "Retreat! We're too few for a fight. Let's call for help from the camp!"
23bc0b83-cf78-4e0b-b733-d024679e4c79: "No way! Just means we can rob a few idiots instead of just one! To arms, everyone!"
c28c0e36-f91e-4bac-94eb-c608f0be8dd8: "Why would we leave when we've got easy pickings from {g|Restov}Restov{/g} before us? We'll rip out your guts and empty your pockets!"
abaf2007-549a-4f9f-8a77-be369d0802f4: {n}The woman smiles coldly.{/n} "All right, we'll leave. But what makes you think we won't just return with greater numbers?"
d292131b-a8e7-4505-8049-686758bc9e0d: "Quiet down, dimwit. Oleg, we're just here for the Stag Lord's tax. Hand over the money, and we'll be on our way."
7c82113c-3caa-4ceb-bc60-2aa9318b7757: "And where's that pretty wife of yours, Oleg? She should serve us dinner!"
5f4150ca-c7df-4d64-b5bd-9619589866ba: "Isn't it obvious? These thugs are robbing us honest settlers! They say they're taking some 'tax' for their leader, the Stag Lord." {n}Oleg spits.{/n} "But I didn't swear allegiance to any stag lords! I pay my taxes to Restov."
d8268d7b-dfed-4951-800f-4fe218df3296: "But {g|Restov}Restov{/g} is so far away, Oleg. And the Stag Lord is so close. And as for you..." {n}The young, dark-haired woman squints angrily at you.{/n} "Get out of here before it's too late. This is our land — we own it!"
08fddbf0-49c2-4b2f-9f02-9ea601b5af6e: "How amusing. I'm starting to enjoy your company."
c5813557-9f2e-4fce-bbdd-ac0c092990d6: "Our duty is to protect the {g|Oleg's Trading Post}trading post{/g}. Don't waste your breath on scum like this."
f141be5c-8d30-4c37-afac-a9efc5d9d0b5: "Let's trade. You give me things, and I'll give you money."
c9937e35-5941-4cd9-be90-22235d6c232a: {n}An unusual kobold stands before you, decorated with bits of trash from horns to tail. He's wearing a necklace of metal shards, patches of cloth and bones, and his wrists are covered with bracelets made of wire, bone, and splinters of wood.{/n}
