566c45d9-9f5f-4391-a710-527b2f8c3d67: "You bring woe, bring grief, bring suffering to those around you. Why? Does your goddess want this? Or is it just your own ambition talking, wrapped in the cloth of infallible faith?!"
a8a41904-224e-41a2-a498-55af8630ab50: "I've always been appalled by your fanaticism. I'm disgusted by the blunt stupidity that keeps you from seeing the person behind my beauty. And you know what? Now that I've lost this 'gift' of {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g}, this mask that prevented everyone from seeing the real me – now I'm finally free. And if anyone wants..."
f52d5c7d-956a-49db-ac0a-77d6a00c6c91: "Do I value art? No. Am I ready to serve it? No. Do I respect those who have brought so much trouble to me and the {mf|baron|baroness|King|Queen}? 608695ed-cd57-4be6-ae6e-d20cb01341b4: "Maybe I don't deserve forgiveness in the eyes of {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g}. Maybe fanatics like Sir Hegend would be happier to see me in the noose. 6629b400-c86e-40e6-89aa-23d59d2d35c6: "The divine trial is over. {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g} has made her decision."
642e73ed-b2ac-43f9-8b96-689dcec00446: "About what... how?" {n}Valerie touches her face.{/n} "The scar! It's... gone!"
85561a9f-2444-4980-8f13-d61dfbdb2428: {n}Hegend, white as a sheet, points at Valerie with a trembling hand.{/n} "But... but why?!"
ae437171-0d7f-4947-ae26-00e3d593db7d: {n}Laryen looks at Valerie sadly.{/n} "You are full of wrath and resentment towards {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g}, and these feelings will never allow you to return to her light. c0bec21a-38f0-4ebd-8ee2-7171af881f07: "NO!" {n}Hegend pulls out his weapon and shakes it in the air, rolling his blood-shot eyes.{/n} "The witch has deceived {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g}! Only I know the will of my goddess! Death to Valerie!"
bd652d2e-31c2-4bf7-a849-f180b0548bf3: "Valerie's expression proclaims her blame louder than any words! Can there be any further doubt about what happened to Sir Sinnet, whose only fault was to have faith in this woman's virtue?"
980fedf6-4de7-44be-bf3e-0289f0eaacc5: "You could free yourself – cleanse your soul and admit your fault – yet I don't hear you crying or begging for mercy. Tell me, Valerie, what drives you? Wicked pride or stony stubbornness?"
d38c3c45-158f-48b6-a0d4-887f80b11fb5: {n}Valerie squints and purses her lips. Her neck seems to be covered in sweat.{/n}
ff88e713-693b-4b25-aeb1-d14d991a9dda: {n}Valerie doesn't indicate that she heard you, but you see her shoulders relax.{/n}
fbede796-c5bb-45f4-8d86-6148a02c966e: "Hm... I have no reason to distrust you, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. So the disappearance of Fredero Sinnet is not on Valerie's conscience."
c9d6ee1a-0544-4156-a162-34b439bef26e: {n}Valerie finds a moment to swivel around and burn you with a furious look. Your barefaced lie didn't seem to please her.{/n}
74cee83a-dc4d-45df-a662-f12b900c51da: "Is that so? Then after this trial has ended, perhaps we shall discuss the consequences of such rashness!"
6d010e7f-6bb7-4f03-a11b-5c2b802ab1a5: "The {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen} was in {mf|his|her} right. Even {g|Shelyn}Shelyn's{/g} paladins must respect the laws of the lands they're in."

bd826cca-6f39-41a7-ab8f-52d6763c6105: "I can understand the desires of a young girl who wishes to soak up the world. It's only a pity that Valerie didn't find another way to express it, and fled from the Order like an errant child..."
f645136a-6153-422f-b0b6-cd3efe910df3: "This woman has the nerve to openly defy the servants of {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g}! Oh, is there no limit to your insolence, Valerie?"
5569e331-b9f9-4478-bc92-dcb2717b6861: "This may surprise you, but I agree with you. Once my blood cooled, I started to realize that my complaints about Valerie were a little... excessive."
f7c598d9-3213-418b-a0e6-7fadf9abcdf8: "And we did – only for you to come following in his footsteps!"
cc46c961-c9ea-44d5-a8ef-b618e7f2bd8d: "An unforgivable crime with no excuse – that's what I see in Valerie's actions."
36d987a8-773d-4a7c-b5db-3c674c3055ee: {n}Valerie closes her eyes in irritation and swallows heavily. You feel she is about to scream.{/n}
97671085-daa2-4a8f-b85d-c9f9081335cd: "But are the lives of those who guard the peace of Jamandi less important than the life of a Swordlord? You made a terrible mistake, my child."
7b104472-20fb-4032-a7d9-41130799fb26: "Really? Well we can hardly judge Valerie's actions if they only happened in the imaginations of slanderers..."

49eab897-b977-45e9-9d5f-4441f4e2053f: {n}Valerie's face is lit by a faint smile.{/n} "Truly. I forgot what hypocrites {g|Shelyn}Shelyn's{/g} servants are! You only care about one freedom of will – the one that serves your own interests!"
2831541c-cfb3-4127-b2f9-99820917d9f0: {n}The priest raises his arms apologetically.{/n} "We are just clarifying some nuances, {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}. Although I can't but notice your readiness to take part of the blame. Truly, Valerie has chosen a worthy ruler to serve..."

5dbd0b4a-795e-421c-b235-1f5ad519f0b6: "Insulting the goddess in her own temple! Death to Valerie!"
ba38fc09-b449-44f8-ad96-c1727a30afe9: "So much smugness in her words! So much pride!"
ebffac0d-47f2-4090-9a25-a80cdd1d843f: "I am sure Valerie's heart is filled with good. After all, her delightful appearance is but a reflection of a perfect soul, hidden away from prying eyes."
6eb05343-44dd-4434-8c93-013155d28a04: "Of course, {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}. We are judging Valerie only by her actions."
405eb0d8-31ad-4cd7-81d4-8176fe4c3366: "W-What? I'm s-sorry, I'm confused... I have no complaints about Valerie. None! Whatsoever! I have to go!"
6b846a4f-b51c-4b47-9445-560772ff29a5: "Ha! You can't scare me with your idle threats! All you've achieved, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, is confirming the rumors that are multiplying around your lands!"

4f235fca-2b84-4a72-b5bb-eb7483e3f107: "Do I have time to look around?"

f02621cf-dd78-4913-b26b-b9f8f87aeba0: [Attack] "Amusing screams — and I haven't even begun yet."
490345e1-cf5b-4764-92af-3faf41d0e68f: [Attack] "Filthy pests! I'll purge my lands of you!"

3d4d93f9-1ad8-4199-9d1d-e39a1b7ce16a: [Leave] "I respect the Goddess. Praise her, for I am sparing your pathetic lives."
7d0720ab-2125-434f-bacc-d7db60aaffae: [Leave] "You're an amusing lot. Don't be frightened — we're friends!"

9255fc57-16a7-48a6-b3b2-fe1b5b12320a: [Attack] "I don't believe you can ever become civilized citizens — and so there's no place for you in my barony. Abadar won't cry for you, and neither will I."

c943099c-b50b-4a4d-b679-e064c6049ca5: "You must now make a choice between justice and mercy. Don't fear the wrath of an evil goddess — it's not her who will judge you for this choice. This will stay between your soul and your own deity."
f2d68c56-7458-4708-a374-a5d142bdf1e4: "Ha! Yeah, now I'm scared! What will {g|Lamashtu}Lamashtu{/g} do? Send another owlbear for us to skin?"
3eb164f4-2d6a-4b0f-9648-e019b7ef7f75: "Ha-ha, these pests are funny. Let's fry them!"
9c793d94-a9cc-4e53-a558-83ac90602de5: "What are you waiting for? Kill these miscreants, and let's move on. I'm fed up with this garbage heap."
e8b4a4dc-0116-475d-9c3d-30cfd4a5ccf3: "Great! Pray to your goddess, you little rats! She can't help you anyway, ha ha ha ha!"
e29d344c-8c00-49fe-a657-340afbce6b2f: "{g|Lamashtu}Lamashtu{/g} or not, you will be responsible for anyone these vermin kill or maim. Do not press your luck — cleanse your lands of these monsters."
639fece4-5061-4566-a377-87951f4b1150: "I would have said it differently, but our thoughts were essentially the same." {n}A caustic smile touches Valerie's lips.{/n}
1cad0ba9-0c6d-46c6-be65-8482b04e7072: "Why do you always think about death?"
da635584-9133-4f6c-83ef-ff061f1206da: "Ha, Ekun, Ekun... How can I answer this question? I'm more surprised that none of you think about it much at all!"
a6e47720-e843-4a49-9ab2-edaba74dec34: "What is this place? Where is it?"
19f468fb-c0e4-493b-bd30-9aab3660886a: "I will go there as soon as I am able."
19be5e35-9438-417c-a39b-caf5b71a5236: "Your Grace! Allow me to congratulate you on receiving the title of baron{mf||ess}! I am confident that you will be able to bring order to these troubled lands."

4aca7af7-19ed-4638-be24-dc9bc1bf8f6f: {n}Jhod exhales loudly, catching his breath.{/n} "And now there is a new woe! Tristian and I believe the curse did not simply disperse of its own accord! 604440fc-76f0-46da-9886-4d41e5deeda8: "I would be happy to accompany you, but I would not expect to see anything new there at present."
aca77cb7-78e0-4721-8560-3117b00368c2: "There is a Bald Hilltop not far from here, to the north of the capital. Its crown is entirely barren of life. 5a9cbed4-7016-45b8-b0ac-880f311809fc: "And this wound will undoubtedly open again! Tristian and I felt something approaching... Something ominous. The curse will soon return to plague us once more – I swear by {g|Erastil}Erastil{/g}!"

d3300265-aeb3-4a46-97e1-8dddd8b75fe0: "In any case, we can't do anything right now anyway. Tristian and I have been to this hilltop. There's nothing there!"
44648bff-4317-4493-95d5-7df285e9fcd4: "I agree with Tristian! We have been to this hilltop. It's barren, but filled with a dense atmosphere of unease!"
91ed19b7-6fbc-4c5b-ae6e-0c57cde64487: "The curse will grow in strength, and we predict it will reach the peak of its strength in about one month. That's when we should visit the Bald Hilltop and resolve this issue."
20d40806-d737-4454-a566-c5d11aa7501d: "For now we can only wait. And prepare."
02931bcf-5fef-4cd1-a690-c24d7d30a1b7: "We beg your pardon, Your Grace, for intervening with you getting the grasp of your barony. I'm sure you have even more pressing matters at hand right now."
1d8a33de-6790-4d13-916c-5ff137be8925: "I don't understand you, I'm sorry. How can you live without faith at all?"
cb5736fe-8bf2-478c-8b3a-6851f294de4c: "You said yourself that everything in this world is pointless. Do you think faith is an exception?"
b7d4f354-0e9e-46ee-97f4-04cd2ec3b0cc: {g|Loyalty6_1}[Choice effects]{/g} "Throw the mercenaries out of the capital. They're making trouble, so they have to go."
6ee753c0-23cb-44e8-aecd-5f8e71539cb3: {g|Loyalty6_2}[Choice effects]{/g} [Pay 100 BP] "Finance more guards from the treasury. Make sure the merchants' guards don't fight with the common people."
f45b224b-d2d7-45cb-9373-ec4d6fa37613: {g|Loyalty6_3}[Choice effects]{/g} "Send our citizens the message that these mercenaries are under our protection."
7743fb7e-acfd-47eb-bcda-1b6313f92d99: "{name}, the situation has become rather fraught. A group of mercenaries arrived in our lands to seek a better future. They've banded together for safety. Some have been hired by our merchants as bodyguards."
0ccf2e00-c497-46bb-af30-18cb2874db03: "There's an issue that requires your attention. Tensions are rising between the locals and a group of mercenaries that came at the capital to earn an income. Some have been hired by wealthy merchants who can afford bodyguards."
2e213786-bff2-4bd7-9207-6b2bbbf95e58: "{name}, there is trouble in the city. A group of mercenaries arrived at the capital. The people don't seem to like them, so they've banded together for safety. d805d8ee-c3a9-43a3-9c90-4f136f710e5f: {n}Tristian's voice sounds sad.{/n} "You may be right. Not everyone is capable of living side by side in peace. Nevertheless, it's a shame if we never try to change things."
d0802d22-b90b-49f2-b804-a686758decff: "Whatever money we spend on new guards, it will be worth it, if it prevents any more blood from being spilled."
4b7fd308-5b87-4db8-8ddc-9b947632b7ef: {n}Shandra raises her eyebrow.{/n} "Where will this lead? Do you expect the peasants will appreciate it? They'll just find something new to hate tomorrow, and you'll be the one to blame. You can't afford to solve all their problems."
9075de2a-7e9a-4573-a7ba-cb3ae2d1fa50: "All right. In the future, I hope the two packs, the mercenaries' and yours, will merge into one. Powerful... invincible."
14706482-cc15-4780-a117-f16133f62629: "Very wise. Allow the merchants to do as they like, and their coin will fill your coffers."
0c75ef8c-4dce-4e45-8fab-73bb12b74b6d: "You lock your subjects in a cage with savage cutthroats. Very well, let the strong survive, and the weak perish."
d8d06cb3-e2f8-456f-9f1a-4e4d9aed002c: "I'll draw from the treasury to hire more guards and avoid provocation. In the future, I hope the two packs, the mercenaries' and yours, will merge into one. Powerful... invincible."
549161ce-1d5a-4056-8d2c-0f3f53e122ee: "Alas, their manners are low, and the locals are prejudiced against them. They fight more and more often. The peasants want us to banish the mercenaries from the city. The merchants expect us to protect them, regardless of the peasants' complaints."
2da72e70-5a95-40a9-9c43-79b9b8eec4be: "If you ask me, we mustn't surrender to hatred. This matter should be resolved peacefully. Draw from the treasury to finance more guards. 24fe47b8-6d19-4602-83d6-10bce272d659: "Of course, the citizens regard them as brutes and bruisers – stereotypes to which they gladly conform. The people call us to eject this mob from the city. However, this would be a mistake. Think how helpful the loyal merchants' troops will be, if ever the peasants riot."
950e7afa-a59b-4e67-806c-fb5046222258: "Turn a deaf ear to those who encourage you to expel the mercenaries. It won't make us popular among the people, but these mercenaries may prove useful. a9d9962f-9b79-48ca-a7fb-af264414540e: "Alas, the citizens despise these mercenaries. They insult them behind their backs, and spit where they step. fd8c9d1b-c079-42f4-af3a-34a171062dde: {g|Espionage6_1}[Choice effects]{/g} "Pass the information about the Gardeners to the leader of the Revolutionary Council of Galt."
76e040ee-8784-468e-8d80-a6fe53c7a04e: {g|Espionage6_2}[Choice effects]{/g} "Help the Order of Vengeance achieve their revenge."
f751c448-14b1-49a6-91e4-968e882f121b: "We're fighting someone else's war. We aren't Gralton. We aren't Litran. We have no stake in this fight. Let us escape it before we're stabbed in the back. Petitioning for peace is an option, though unreliable. Let's distract them first."
4dfda269-101d-45ce-9c1b-bcb17a9f322d: "Look, {name}, we've suddenly stumbled into the middle of a fight between Litran and Gralton. I don't know who might benefit from this, but it's surely not us. 340c47ed-e221-4b71-882e-462e422a9a65: "We are pulled deeper and deeper into Litran and Gralton's fight. This already drains our forces, and cannot end well. It's time we plan our escape from this situation – preferably something that casts us in a positive light. I can see two options."
727a369e-5b7b-4737-8554-e8c97261110e: "Very well. I'll send Goss all he'll need to know about the grey masks."
6b0c98a7-1dca-4ede-a41e-4118040aac27: "He'll be more than happy to bleed the Grey Gardeners a little. And we've all the information we'll need to begin bloodletting. The ignorant fool won't even stop to think why we shared our knowledge with him."
0d19e677-2ff0-4f3f-b03f-0a042f2ec8d7: "This inane war between the two countries was bound to happen eventually. At least we might profit from it. That will have to be good enough for now."
392c9dd4-9a52-44fb-a44a-5e005bf01139: "Litran will forget all about us, once the partisans seize {g|Galt}Galt's{/g} borderlands. The Grey Gardeners should never have crossed us."

c4ad9d41-d6e7-4e71-8ac6-14b7782d1d55: "That is most wise. I will send an ambassador to Litran. I do hope they won't decapitate him... No, no, they mustn't."
95ea2bcd-bfa3-4b44-a528-81da99c3ec9e: "We could convince the Grey Gardeners simply to forget about us. d037c71c-dede-4bd8-a7e9-02573dfa6e04: "Another enemy, also thirsty for the Gardeners' blood, is a secret society from Gralton – the Order of Vengeance. They would start harassing {g|Galt}Galt's{/g} borderland, which will occupy the Gardeners' full attention. I will enjoy seeing my enemies bleeding to death in a battle that I caused."
4403c990-4e8a-421f-ad67-236e8ab8f4d0: "The Grey Gardeners have a more attractive enemy than us – and they're nearer to hand as well! Of course I'm speaking of the Revolutionary Council of {g|Galt}Galt{/g}, headed by Goss. He fears that his government could be decapitated, in every meaning of the word. But if we give him something to sink his teeth into, he might decide to go after the Gardeners after all. However, I would avoid this course. If Goss prevails, he could become even worse than the Gardeners."
8b272da0-34d0-47bc-abad-84eeb35040e0: "Another way to distract Litran's attention is the Order of Vengeance, a secret society in Gralton. A shame that this mess will be taking place just next door."
61f70cd5-2b6b-4aa8-a29a-8b881b96cdd5: "You cannot deal with the Grey Gardeners, but death already stalks them closely. Korran Goss rules {g|Galt}Galt{/g}, and he is wary of the Gardeners. 8fcfca47-9d05-4bfb-b67b-625b4c49abad: "We have another option, but it leads us down a dangerous path. There is an Order of Vengeance in Gralton, wild avengers with deeply wounded hearts. They would return to {g|Galt}Galt{/g} to exact their vengeance, and the Gardeners would become too busy to bother with us. But blood will flow. And they'll remember what we've done!"
53b5f253-63d1-4fda-a777-8380dda3c238: "Did you really steal that sword from a giant?"
304f4eb2-9deb-43ec-98d8-657aeccbb092: "Does he know that the sword is broken?"
55621778-a93e-47fc-85ec-4d9f7ee56df3: "Remember that evil spirit who haunted the Six Bears? The one we drove away? Well… Don't think I'm crazy! But he visited me in a dream."
46686d9f-6a89-4d5f-986a-912a85a266af: "Says, I'm a thief, because I stole his sword. Remember? — That big one, Armag broke it! Also... Says he has all my tribe as hostages. All of them, Nilak too! Says, they will be dead, if I don't return the sword!"
c41f122d-725a-4091-8a1b-b4c40ecbd738: "Well... Oh, no need to lie now. I found it! I lied to everyone I took it in battle — but that giant was dead for a long time! How could I know he would want his old piece of iron back?"
fd97134b-bf46-4c86-80ba-c35a6bc834b1: "He knows. I saved the hilt. The ghost tells me to forge a new blade. He even said how to do it. There's a whole ritual!"
c87f41e3-db83-4acc-b3d2-8cec9676b0a8: "He said — first I have to fix the sword, and then he will tell me where my tribe is."
c0700750-fc69-4242-a65d-9d60849e9272: "I understand. The repair will cost a lot. I never held no such amount in my hands. But... Nilak..." {n}The barbarian shakes her head in grief.{/n}
a865d011-2ff6-4e63-a77d-badac061ecd9: "I'd like to take a look at your wares."
486f895a-3a48-4648-a679-a71281741559: "You have many goods from Kyonin. Have you been there?"

da8ea86f-b837-4817-b2c4-51c6e5426d6b: {n}Enneo bows with his usual courtesy.{/n} "Welcome again, Your Grace."
afb4c676-2ce0-4af0-b04a-752d30093d27: "I prefer to travel the wild and sparsely-populated corners of the continent. 89373fcc-14ad-4540-b16b-35e0419fb8dd: {n}Enneo shrugs.{/n} "I was born in {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g} — in {g|Greengold}Greengold{/g}, a port on the shore of Lake Encarthan, and the only place in the elven homeland where others are allowed entrance. a932e653-a8c4-4c75-8e73-105add2be66e: "Kassil Aldori is an amazing creature. I talked to him the other day... I was surprised to discover that we had so much in common."
42279c01-d206-4fc1-9d14-224d627c18a7: "Well, at least someone enjoys the company of that buttoned-up Swordlord. I also tried talking to him not long ago – but fell asleep after the third 'Aldori, Aldori, Aldori'."

4d798f14-8005-4e2a-b84e-5b225f4d768e: "No one beats me. I always survive. Always."
acd2ceeb-2883-4af4-8827-3b01788f9b8f: "I got really scared when I saw you fall. Please try to be more careful next time!"

adce6697-2db1-46d5-b9cc-58d853a74b86: "I'm dying... I knew this expedition was doomed... Oh, {g|Groetus}Groetus{/g}, my vision darkens..."
9ede8042-ed25-4b67-8cb0-da12a89e005b: "That's impossible!" {n}The dwarf lifts his head and inspects his body carefully, then tries to move his hands and feet.{/n} "It... it seems you might be right."
4d699408-73d0-4fe7-a2a2-ed4663794c73: "You're wrong... Who would know better than I the severity of my own wounds...? I can feel the last drops of vital force leaving me..."
88703c8e-fd79-479a-a914-d04a33b268b0: "How rude — speaking to a dying man that way! Look, I can't even move!" {n}The dwarf moves his hands then looks at them, baffled.{/n} "It can't be... But I'm gravely wounded! I can't even stand on my own two feet... Watch!"
6e86af55-80f9-4b3b-bf4a-ebd0a976761f: "I can't hear you... I'm being taken away... into the darkness..."
06a99263-bf16-4a1f-a92a-c956bb704675: {n}Tartuccio gives the dwarf a swift kick.{/n} "Up, you faker! Just look at him — dying, he says! What a buffoon! Come on, get up now, or I'll tap-dance on your corpse!"
876c9735-a57a-45f7-97f1-eaa9b61c9db5: {n}The dwarf grunts as he regains his feet and warily looks down at his bloodstained armor.{/n} "It... it seems I will live. I suppose I must postpone meeting my god... Not for long, I'm sure. But while we remain in this transient world — Harrim is at your service."
2680a8de-1f56-4365-9186-c51a3137ab67: {n}The dwarf's wounds, shallow as they are, begin to heal, but he seems not to notice as he keeps whispering.{/n} "Too late... Forgive me... Oblivion is calling..."
8c8e69d3-755a-45da-8293-52a308d009f0: "What brought you to your faith in Sarenrae? Let me guess. You committed a terrible atrocity! And now you're atoning for it. Am I right?"
3818d765-4a33-498b-bd12-5f538d9399e0: "I was just looking at the world. There is such evil in it, and too little mercy. Is it not enough to simply want to change it for the better?"
3092b9af-009d-47f3-9ee3-0456b6a21dd8: "A talking bird right in the middle of a mysteriously empty settlement. Are you behind what happened here?"
8c06f783-9c26-480c-816f-426df5c42ca6: "They were thieves and looters — a threat to the peaceful peasants. What if they had come across another village?"
9d303f97-f08a-468f-bbb7-58b414abb20e: "They have broken the law and were punished for it."
ee1cb4af-049d-4fb9-97aa-2b91e5642f5a: "That's not true. Agai still has a chance for a fresh start."
ba75dae9-c1ec-45d4-9006-b25c8e68e6db: "I don't care where they go or what happens to them."
7ab54bae-b30c-466c-bf5c-6acd57acb89f: "That's exactly why I let them go — so they could suffer a while longer before the wilderness takes them."
d351fd66-ac28-4f0f-9549-15fa3200ee0a: "My name is {name}. Now tell me who you are."
1ba88910-1e86-49cd-9f3d-cdc92266e91f: "I'm guessing you're new to these parts if you still don't know who I am! Why don't you take to the air and ask around?"
d8cdfcc6-6782-4be2-99bb-9a1ae44cf642: [Leave] "Last thing I need is to introduce myself to a filthy crow."
8f0cb095-ffa7-4b4e-a949-7ddcc8311a61: "What do you know about the vanishing of Varnhold?"
934f61e2-f4f5-45f1-870b-e9cc3e9cf103: "I'm not from Varnhold, but I will find out what happened here."
2ec6e907-7647-4615-af3a-6ad2797ffe48: [Ignore the question] "My, my, a talking crow! Now if you said anything worth hearing, that'd be impressive indeed."
f6faaf89-7455-439b-844a-fba19462c9dd: "I am {name}, the baron{mf||ess} of the neighboring realm! Insult me again, insolent crow, and you'll regret it!"
e5f49dc4-a402-4956-bdbf-f9828bc9b190: "Put it out of your mind. It's just an insolent bird!"
739cbde8-3f30-4540-857f-5d7b2bcfd426: {n}You notice a huge black bird sitting still on a high fence by the exit, as if waiting for you. It's a raven — glistening black, and one of the largest ravens you've even seen. As you approach, it tilts its head and affixes you with a beady black eye.{/n}
bf37265d-43a3-4dc0-8e7d-56dcba6c133b: {n}As you are about to leave, you hear a cracked voice.{/n} "Hypocrrrite!"
39dae46a-0d8f-4965-80af-4c60fa0ef287: {n}As you are about to leave, you hear a cracked voice.{/n} "Butcherrr."
5870bbf8-7db3-4fc7-a13c-dca4c44a06db: "What have these miserrrable fools done that they must pay with theirrr lives?" {n}The raven gives a ragged caw, then tilts its head and looks at you, unblinking.{/n} "Who are you to decide the fate of those whom you do not rule? Why did the victims deserrrve to die?"
53e6b137-4227-4629-a1b8-6c127bc417ff: "What's the point of your false pity forrr these fools who you allowed to live?" {n}The raven gives a sharp caw, almost a bark.{/n} With no shelter, no family, and no homeland, always on the run... all you did is prolong their sufferrrring... and take pride in your..." {n}The raven gives another sharp caw, almost sneering.{/n} "...'chivalry'."
c5bf0094-5e9c-434a-a1c7-e4515bf260b5: "Miserrrable hyprocrrrites. You seek to justify yourrr actions?" {n}The raven gives a series of caws, as if laughing.{/n} "There is no justification, no, no, no."
77d55d22-e7f9-4bd3-95d2-bbc2bf1714fb: "Worrrms wriggling in the mud. Nothing concerns you but yourrrselves. You deserve contempt, nothing morrre."
e8c5e78a-0eeb-4bf7-82e2-77a116be7fe4: "The delight you take in your prrride! At least you are honest, although in the end, you're just like the rest of your decrrrepit race, {race}."
1fddc860-c294-4c2a-b9c3-e7913dc3bf03:
{n}Your aim is true, and the stone hits the bird's skull with a sharp crack. The raven falls from its perch with a shriek.
Just before it strikes the ground, it clumsily rights itself, and, cawing and losing feathers, takes flight.{/n}
50fcf92c-1f46-4b3e-afad-bbc09978b8c6: {n}The stone misses the raven. With rattling caws, the raven takes to the air and flies away. In moments, it is nothing more than a speck in the sky, then it is gone.{/n}
d626f57e-92a6-44b1-8605-9606e743a635: {n}The raven regards you for a moment. Finally, it flaps its wings and without a sound, takes flight. Moments later, it is nothing more than a speck in the sky, then it is gone.{/n}
f1c93da0-9b3b-42f6-8594-b17a24e96813: {n}The raven ignores the question, only echoing its last word.{/n} "Butcherrr."
cdd29826-ec73-4f1d-a20b-0e1ae80286fb: {n}The raven ignores the question, only echoing its last word.{/n} "Hypocrrrite."
41bf34e3-f1f9-4e8a-b410-8e25efab031b: "Why are you herrre? Are you one of the thieves that lived in this miserrrable settlement?"
2caafbf0-82f0-405c-9a60-467a1acecbc8: "Liarrr. This settlement was full of thieves — they paid for their crrrimes. Now only a single one rrremains — you. Who arrre you?"
d2f6c685-e0de-4de6-b3f0-af92951edab7: "Only that the people of this dusty village were thieves. Thieves and bandits who didn't rrrespect the law and didn't know their place. Inferior beings don't dare touch that which belongs to their masterrrs. Who arrre you?"
e3d7e954-cc56-49b4-b0d7-66eed2c3425e: "You?" {n}The raven gives a short, barking caw.{/n} "What arrrogance! What pride! You, thrall? Do not follow one crime with anotherrr… you will sufferrr the same fate. Who arrre you?"
ad3d723f-2c13-4e49-94f9-770f63d6baab: {n}The raven bristles, its wings fluttering.{/n} "You would do well to heed my worrrds, thrall — as would all of you of the lesserrr races! You will swallow your worrrds when the time comes, and the time comes for you all!"
c70ee351-79be-4b3f-bbf8-861030d2fc63: {n}Tristian follows the bird with a look of anxiety and determination. He seems so absorbed in his thoughts that he forgets everything else in the world.{/n}
438fbb71-9111-4c8e-a75c-5d6af6907659: {n}Tristian turns back, surprised, and smiles faintly, seeing you.{/n} "Not the most pleasant omen, right?" {n}He squeezes your fingers lightly and releases them.{/n}
8e862f95-728c-4f22-a92f-c69389ba391c: {n}Tristian shrugs.{/n} "I'm afraid that raven is more than just a bird."
e2fb6304-8568-4b28-a3a3-4bd99c825392: "Let's go. Let's not waste any more time."
f0a672d8-4433-4b9b-88c2-fe6e493fb1c0: "Look! Fat tasty featherbag! Hit it with stone!"
f0d8cb5c-3ad4-4669-8f4f-1585e05e1929: "It can talk! Maybe it's a wizard turned into a raven? Or a charmed prince? Oh, don't pay attention to me. – I've just never seen anything like it..."
891389ec-fc09-4024-9bd9-7dbb1dac7b0f: "Goblins seem as if they would do better to worship Rovagug. You adore destruction and smash everything you can. So why do you and your tribe follow the Mother of Monsters instead?"
babc0726-b615-4f16-b042-9c4650b8d608: "We like breaking others stuff. Things we built — too good to break. And Lamashtu gives tribe hardy babies — hardy enough to survive in their cages!"
ec026a86-5289-467b-8404-1150f31ca70c: "I thought I saw someone. Heh, I've been free for a long time, but I still see an assassin in every shadow!"
888660c6-74b3-4656-8be4-58a5dfdd06d4: We pointed out the cheating to the judges.
cc2d73c9-7c79-4f28-b779-9c5fa3bbb78a: We quietly warned the bard that we would shut him up if he kept interfering.
37526106-a720-453f-98db-69aa5e3c24f5: We snuck up on the bard, stabbed him in the back, and disappeared.
bfd7e98c-0ccb-4a9c-ae63-665c7a1840ab: {mf|He|She} regaled them with tales of our victories over the Stag Lord, the trolls, Vordakai, and Armag.
6217d1ef-2915-4ba0-986b-371393924e12: In response to Annamede's story, {mf||s}he recounted how we dealt with Tartuccio, another one of Irovetti's spies.
8e5b6b56-a283-4674-bcc5-089d85a3f3cc: {mf|He|She} told the story of the time the baron{mf||ess} was made an honorary goblin.
a1229df7-3717-4302-8dbb-be4e4ec1b820: {mf|He|She} described how the baron{mf||ess} had managed to make kobolds and mites worship {mf|his|her} gloves as relics.
b7a60f10-d323-43bd-b7a0-809bc74cc0a0: {mf|He|She} wove an interesting — but entirely fictional! — tale for the audience.
1de816a4-889c-408a-b8f5-1a8a9de1327b:
The tournament continued with a boasting contest. The first participant, a man from Daggermark, stepped up to the podium and told a raunchy story about {g|SillyHint Halfling}him{/g} sneaking into a temple of {g|Calistria}Calistria{/g} and seducing all the priestesses — including the high priestess — in a single night. The crowd was particularly amused by the suggestive glances he kept casting toward one of the guests from Tymon. She simply smiled mysteriously in response.
The second participant was a guest from Gralton, who told a completely implausible tale about his travels across other planes, where he battled {g|SillyHint Undead}undead{/g} hordes and defeated a bloodcurdling {g|SillyHint Monstr}monster{/g}. He was an average storyteller at best — he'd be lucky to get a C for that story at the {g|Academy of Grand Arts}Academy{/g} — but the listeners were inexplicably elated. Suspicious, we took a closer look at the crowd, and... Of course! We spotted a bard using some tricks of the trade (and likely a little magic) to aid the Gralton man's performance!
d163b048-de2c-4096-b21d-c9eba3b4dbcc: After finishing his story, the guest from Gralton stepped down from the podium to a very loud — and completely undeserved — ovation.
5f5e1f86-58ef-4884-b1cb-b50022fef132: The judges were reluctant to believe us, but the cheating was easy to spot once you knew to look for it. Once they'd concluded we were right, the guest from Gralton was disqualified and forced to leave the podium in disgrace.
632ceb55-6094-49ef-92b0-5e92d1529f48: It was just a waste of time, though — the judges completely ignored the cheating, and in the time we took trying to convince them, the participant from Gralton finished his story and stepped down from the podium to audience applause.
feac257d-0d41-4c20-9caa-26b2d09acad2: The bard got the message and quickly disappeared. Without the bard's support, the guest from Gralton immediately lost the audience's approval. As he grew more nervous, he began mumbling and stumbling over his words, and he eventually left the podium among jeers and whistles.
60a02afe-d3d5-4d57-8dde-665f7fa245c6: We tried threatening the bard, but he wasn't born yesterday — he started yelling and crying, calling to the guards, to Irovetti, and to all the gods for help. While we were managing that, the participant from Gralton finished his lying without interruption and stepped down from the podium to undeserved applause — and we were disqualified for trying to interfere with an opponent's performance. The indignity of it all!
8cd9decc-69b2-4e8b-8e30-44dd72356d59: The bard collapsed to the ground, choking on his own blood. By the time the crowd noticed, we were long gone. Needless to say, the audience's impression of the Gralton participant's performance was ruined.
5535c37b-ae33-4e9f-b4e6-c420992317b1: The bard collapsed to the ground, choking on his own blood. The audience's impression of the Gralton participant's performance was ruined, for all the good it did us — someone in the crowd spotted our attack and screamed bloody murder, and guards descended on us from seemingly nowhere. It looked like we were in trouble.
c09508fa-4104-44d4-acb2-94bf636d7a55:
Then it was {g|Pitax}Pitax's{/g} turn. The kingdom's honor was represented by Annamede Belavarah — a sweet-voiced singer whose smile could win over the most withered of hearts. Oh, Annamede... But while her voice was smoother than silk, her words stung like arrows!
With a soft smile, Annamede told everyone how she'd spent months in our kingdom learning our secrets and instigating a riot! Of course, the honest trade of the bard and the shady dealings of the spy often go hand in hand, but... Oh, Annamede, who could've expected such an ugly blow from such a lovely lady?
b99beb3f-b122-4300-9f79-103963d042cb: It wasn't easy getting the crowd excited for this story. They were all glorious feats, of course, but that was the problem — the audience had already heard them time and time again! {Name} used all the eloquence {mf||s}he could bring to bear to breathe new life into these old stories.
f82d6d18-2c5a-4e9c-8a3b-44b3b2d5401f: While not exactly a "glorious feat," the story certainly had great material for jokes. The audience likes laughing at simpletons, and {Name} did all {mf||s}he could to have them rolling in the aisles.
0c98d9f1-e358-4c16-8f4f-29a8f2a6ab74: Looking meaningfully at Annamede, {Name} spoke of the sad fate that befell the last of Irovetti's spies... and what may be in store for any other spies we might come across!
5be37eb8-7e72-435b-8ea4-eff21c2db044: {Name} took a deep breath and began lying enthusiastically. {mf|He|She} started with us supposedly setting off to the snowy woods of {g|Irrisen}Irrisen{/g} in search of the missing queen of witches, Baba Yaga, which led us to another planet entirely, interfering in a war between dragons. We then went through a portal to another world, one full of previously unseen technologies, where we hunted down Baba Yaga's son, an insane monk who had her trapped in a nesting doll... The audience listened on with rapt attention, their mouths hanging open.
7e95b1f5-cef1-426c-be76-962111e56de4: The audience hung on {mf|his|her} every word, sometimes laughing uncontrollably, sometimes holding their breath to avoid missing anything. {Name} finally brought the story to an end, and the viewers gave {mf|him|her} a standing ovation as {mf||s}he left the podium.
82206404-98a8-4771-b769-c59f5a5c25a9: {Name} used all the eloquence {mf||s}he could bring to bear, but the audience barely paid any attention, giving {mf|him|her} little more than polite applause as {mf||s}he left the podium.
cc41f07b-3d81-4504-91f0-62c42489d715: The woman from Tymon, a priestess of {g|Calistria}Calistria{/g}, went last. She told stories of her love affairs in faraway countries and on other planes, casually mentioning an unpleasant disease she'd contracted over her journeys that took her a long time to get rid of — hearing that, the participant from Daggermark paled and grabbed at his belt, bringing roaring laughter from the rest of the audience.
39496abf-74d3-4d03-8adf-bbc7aa6eb8bc: And finally, the judges announced the winner — {Name}! {mf|He|She} walked up to the podium to thunderous applause and took another bow.
393294a2-9d3f-492d-9ccc-cf1499910c4d: And finally, the judges announced the winner — Annamede Belavarah! The beautiful singer walked up to the podium to take another bow, casting a vicious glare our way. I was once again amazed by how deceptive appearances can be.
79a1ab09-a96b-4bf1-9776-7a2df13e2e25: When Annamede finished and left the stage, it was our turn to perform. And what feats did our participant decide to tell in their performance?
efe0277f-8fb7-4828-9c7d-aa59152340b7: She described — in surprising and exceptionally critical detail — how much the citizens of our young state suffered under the atrocities of the troll assaults and the magic plague. She never stooped to actual lies, but she made it sound as though our {mf|king|queen} — baron{mf||ess} at the time — was simply drinking and debauching while {mf|his|her} subjects struggled. She made our crusade against Vordakai look like a cunning conquest of {g|Varnhold}Varnhold{/g}, and the war with the {g|Tiger Lords}Tiger Lords{/g} was characterized as an irresponsible venture. Talk about cruel and unfair!
ff00d507-da81-4fd6-aa2d-628f040c8d4e: "Magic is such a strange thing… If you don't keep an eye on your spells, the next day you may find yourself without any!"
16fd4ca8-2e80-421f-bcc4-cb58565b904c: "Magic is like armor and weapons: if you don't look after it, it will eventually fail you!"
6d1cb9f1-9076-4bbc-8026-ec06d9d51e22: "Trust me, it becomes a habit in no time! Preparing your spells will be routine before you know it!"
bab0d277-3d29-45c6-90ad-226d13797984: "Magic is a bizarre and mysterious thing. It comes to its adepts in such strange and unusual ways…"
e389ffb1-8bcb-4fd8-86cb-25b6386d7811: "Magic, bodily strength, even faith demand constant dedication. The moment you turn your back on them, they falter. It's true of all that exists in this world."
5f937414-49dd-4482-9ebf-a1f2af8ead3b: "You know, before sleep I like to recall verses from my favorite songs. It's like a little ritual, and very soothing!"
52dab33c-efc7-477b-a143-afcbb2699ed6: "I never expected you to take up studying the magical arts... But you're making progress!"
3998872d-eb7b-45e7-9810-56a6d36f2117: "I never expected you to take up studying the magical arts... But you're making progress!"
74ab2f84-a483-4d8d-a063-2d9ff9a9a9db: "If only I didn't have to use it so often..."
90e33eed-56be-4e9e-b7f0-a5bd247b0e96: "We're out here like a piece of bread, cast aside by a careless traveler — with a flock of birds circling overhead."
fdf91527-2495-4ef0-bcde-ad244b9c1810: "It's good to see reasonable companions in this party. Some of us simply cannot understand reason."
b2014094-53fc-49ab-82c3-15a88ad73d6c: "After our expedition is over – why don't you come to Absalom with me? Our medics will flood us with gold, for the privilege of studying such a unique undead specimen!"
7c540027-c07f-433c-95e8-a399cabe94a0: "A flattering proposition, but I think I'll decline. Although if you want to supply your medics with an undead specimen so badly, I could certainly make one of you!"
c3e9e038-9ac2-40cb-96f3-05bbb6f1e5f5: "I made some valuable acquaintances at the reception in Restov. Maegar Varn I remember well. Truly a lion of a man!"
bb14de18-f431-4b15-9f09-f9d0a6f3dd6f: "Of course, he doesn't hold a candle to our own leader. Intuition tells me he will rise no higher than a provincial baron. But he has his charms!"
3fb527c6-b72b-49f3-bc40-258440e8928b: (draft) We guard these ruins and we will punish evil human looters
ec1884b6-3781-4070-afb3-cd9874b7fce4: "I see you understand these matters better than I. Solve the problem yourself."
90b4c9d5-99bc-408d-982c-14946dc19cf4: "{mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, I am happy to report that recruitment continues. Our ranks swell with more and more fine soldiers. However, we now face another problem – there aren't enough officers. We shouldn't look for them among the common citizens: command requires certain skills and knowledge."
3ecabf96-b327-40df-bc3e-9995d7f5fb45: "I recommend you recruit officers from among the {g|Swordlords}Swordlords{/g}. They are experienced warriors and skillful leaders, capable of strategic thinking and inspiring the sort of courage that will survive the harsh realities of the battlefield."
ca848280-d823-491d-bd04-a65cafffdf81: "Well, {name}, it's me again. Our army is growing. We got more soldiers. But not enough commanders. And there aren't no clever ones among the recruits. Without good command, you know, you can't run an army."
adf88a2a-85f7-4034-bb33-b3555866b44a: "In some armies the officers are wizards or shamans. They might be brainy, but they don't know a damn thing about soldiers. But when I was in {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}, I seen those... you know... {g|Swordlords}Swordlords{/g}, right! They look skinny, but they know their weapons, and soldiers look up to them. I think we should hire them to be commanders in our army – they'll definitely have the troops' respect."
6669f522-ccff-4c8f-bddb-0e69f7d62fad: "Listen, {name}. Remember about recruitment? Well, I did that, we have the numbers. But there's no one to command them." {n}Regongar spits through his fangs.{/n} "We need to find someone these dimwits will fear and obey. Me alone is not enough."
d899a11e-62f5-4577-86ae-3f43536ca241: "You know who we should make commanders? Not those boneheads from {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}, who dance around with their pig-stickers. No, we should hire spellcasters instead! Our regular bonebreaker troops won't whisper a word against a wizard. They're too afraid of getting lightning thrown in their face. And just imagine what terror they'll bring to the battlefield. Not like those {g|Swordlords}Swordlords{/g} – {g|Choral}Choral{/g} mopped the floor with them!"
d373da7a-33df-449e-8e06-00b519ddbf4a: {n}Kassil nods.{/n} "I will make the necessary arrangements immediately."
bcc1052d-0665-4ed5-9a85-0fa2c77cfdd2: {n}Amiri hums contentedly.{/n} "Right. Fine, I'll go tell the others what you said."
7e3793c1-a261-4dbf-ba67-6d9077afcfa6: {n}Regongar sneers scornfully.{/n} "What, you too? {g|Swordlords}Swordlords{/g}, no shit... even the peasants aren't afraid of them – what soldier will respect them?"
17f9792d-8a7f-43a2-89c9-a7cf2b30d12c: "But... how should a spellcaster, who has sat all his life in a lab, be expected to take up command?" {n}Kassil shakes his head.{/n} "I… I'm surprised by this decision."
c4cdb0a2-dc42-40cc-8cf5-cc1fdf6f72ea: {n}Amiri looks insulted.{/n} "Wha-a-at? These skinny dudes in robes will boss my guys around? You kidding me, {name}?! What will I do with them?!" {n}Amiri spits on the floor furiously.{/n}
44b780be-ea28-4197-b9c6-84392d30c620: "Great! A couple of fried troublemakers, and the rest of your soldiers will toe the line."

cdc7a42a-6ead-43b1-8964-2a93f6401c6b: "Today the assembly of merchants decided that the city would hold a feast in your honor! It's so lovely when your name is associated with joy and wealth. It means, your pack is flourishing, and they know who they should thank for it."

1c28f87e-191f-4027-a6ac-676dace4f552: "It's a shame. They were ambitious and strong. But they never feared you, so they would have caused trouble anyway."
32078ac0-1390-4bc9-ba74-abb457cad297: "The priests will gladly take the responsibility. This is merciful and wise. Thank you!"
18e653f3-de0e-4c90-ac03-2a2157396573: "I'm surprised at how willingly you share credit with these prudes. But it's your decision, of course."
7466d63d-5398-428c-9f16-d02f14d817d3: "It is merciful and just. Let me pass your message to the general."
c53532eb-2681-4dbf-8bc8-e958094c9d2d: "I agree. Why waste such daring and strong fellows? They may serve your pack!"
de59785f-8943-41c9-ae4c-6ec5352b0dde: "Let's send them off to the temple for schooling. Priests will help their heads clear by hard labor and a word of wisdom."
49598229-0372-47cb-b4b5-83bfb0d175fc: "I will dispatch them to your army. Their fault must be washed off with enemies' blood. They're destined by fate to induce rage of their comrades."

fda4ec0c-cf61-43c1-81af-e60818d76840: "Now that we're done with the rebels, I'd like to ask you to receive one more visitor. It's the leader of merchants of your kingdom."

f3f0117a-d744-4cbc-be2f-3c8302b42c8c: {n}A solid halfling with graying hair bows to you politely and wipes off the excessive sweat.{/n} "Greetings, Your Highness! d5eafb90-35b0-4e8e-9df0-1fae537f696f: "It's a very wise demand! The educated youth may come in handy, especially now that the trade in the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g} is flourishing!"
c6a2255a-92b3-41fe-87e9-0a39dc7b39b7: "You have a fine taste! My colleagues and I will do our best to surprise you with a decent gift!"
b56d94f4-0e15-481f-8f0d-98865fdb863b: "Believe me, Your Highness! We will spare no expense for the most luxurious monument possible! It will make rulers of other kingdoms jealous!"
5caa1cc1-b106-41a1-8478-7cdb6d15f2fc: "Don't forget to pay well to your servants, not only to your ruler!" {n}Tristian stops, looks at you apologetically and smiles.{/n}
1dede5e8-f777-4de4-ac6f-5e823235d1bd: "Remember who you owe your abundant life in the capital to, without having to hide from robbers in the bushes." {n}The merchant nods hastily. Tsanna looks up and down at him, like a cook checking out a fresh steak that goes straight into cauldron.{/n}
59902776-3de8-4faa-a771-51f2b914cb71: "Your Highness, the instigators of the riot have been arrested. You will have to determine their fate. If you're asking yourself whether you should make a grand gesture and pardon them, the answer is no. They're as dangerous as a hound that tasted blood."
b0dda7b5-4621-45f7-b6b7-0fbee0792145: "It's questionable. They'll keep spreading their dissidence among soldiers. The army mutiny is going to turn out much, much worse. I'll send my agents for surveillance."
eb0f3911-622d-4615-9406-f7773ad27f8a: "Your gentle heart will get you in trouble. The only lesson they'll learn, is that starting a riot doesn't carry a penalty. The next riot will gather even more followers. Those who got scared of the punishment last time, will certainly join the next riot."
e20c9d49-cb5a-47e7-b945-1da83cc98846: "Hang the troublemakers. It's your best option. It'll teach peasants a proper lesson. Just the idea of a riot makes the kingdom unreliable."
28db7f7e-51b6-44ee-98f0-442b1703fb9e: "Now that we're done with the unpleasant task, I'd like to ask you to receive an important visitor. He's the leader of merchants of your kingdom."
6eef4895-5fa7-4f8a-97f6-70c1d3143178: "I'm happy my advice came in handy, your Highness. You managed to tame the natural urge to take populist measures, and carefully considered your policy in a pragmatic manner. It was very insightful of you as a ruler!"
c74d4b4a-a1da-4f0e-bd85-307afeed8664: "The riot will start again unless you punish them. In Brevoy, they usually hang the rebels or exile them to army service. Considering that we don't want a military riot, I'm sure the rascals belong with the scaffold."
d82b9b8c-777d-465b-bde4-f46460f4c058: "Finally good news, Your Grace! {d|Varn}Maegar Varn{/d}, the ruler of {g|Varnhold}Varnhold{/g}, has sent aid! Together with goods came a messenger with {g|VarnHelp}a letter for you{/g}. Here, please, take it!"
a763ff66-5d57-4721-a06c-d36d17ef69df: "Wagon trains from {g|Varnhold}Varnhold{/g} have arrived in the capital. {d|Varn}Maegar Varn{/d} sends you his regards and asks you to accept the humble aid that he hopes will last you through these tough times. 1dcb0771-5633-407e-9485-5b42d805cb14: "I am Muan, a merchant of {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}. I thought I'd seek fortune in the new baronies – but so far I've met only danger and loss. be587aec-f349-427c-af18-63f7e559e9b0: "Have a look. But please be quick. I'm trying to get away from here quick."
058b0ee6-26d1-4aed-b817-377aae0e508f: {n}The merchant turns pale and reaches for his weapon.{/n} "Don't you even try it! I'll kill you right where you stand!"
c5b20bb8-9d61-4392-8946-8967abfb0809: "Enough! Put your weapons away. No one is killing anyone. Forgive my companion, sir!"
b3bbe7c8-660e-42fa-b2b1-570f0bb7045a: "A fair reproach. Let me introduce myself: Maegar Varn, baron of these lands. I've been called here to help – specifically, to dispose of those monsters that are troubling you."
2a7a33fb-42b7-4bbd-b9d8-88927d2cd34e: "You're the ba – ! Oh, me and my big mouth! Well, Your Grace, blessings on you and your subjects. I shall hurry home and never set foot in the Stolen Lands again!"

602a44e5-b32e-4b58-9ce9-552ec98d7a54: "No, though I thank you very kindly. But I will try my luck somewhere far away from the Stolen Lands. This place is..." {n}The merchant waves his hand in the air vaguely.{/n} "...not good. Like it's cursed or something."

7a8679db-3bb4-4616-9ee7-a7bc4aa7c839: "Very well, good-bye then. Personally I'm in no mood for trade. {Name}, Cephal, if you need anything, go ahead and buy it, but be quick about it. There's a battle in the air!"

d19cfc03-216c-4e49-84dd-b4437eb76e62: "If there's some real danger here, we should stay and remove it."

0e89ea11-bae2-4286-8417-4727c853a4e8: "Oh, an experiment, then? With us as the subjects? A delightful idea, I can't wait! Well then, I bid you all a good night, my valiant — if suicidal — companions! See you all in the morning, if we're lucky!"

75cc0209-ed5e-473e-83e4-ef3a10d36654: {n}Jubilost sniffs.{/n} "Camping? Here? Brilliant idea! What does it matter that these hunters had the same idea? Of course, they're missing now. Or worse. Probably worse."
e79762eb-adfe-416f-b6d8-61f62e9fc343: {n}The lack of obvious causes or dangers makes the deserted campsite seem even more suspicious. You choose to leave before whatever fate befell the hunters can befall you as well.{/n}

32ea2a39-82bf-43e0-beff-c770bca0e5df: {n}This shimmering is definitely a magical effect of some sort. Judging by its aura, someone may have been trying to cross the borders between the worlds.{/n}
dffd5766-d5ff-44e9-95b8-9760884bff9f: {n}It's all common hunter's supplies: a flint, some clothes, a box of salt. Oddly, there's only one backpack here, though there are three bedrolls and three mugs.{/n}
4982d847-f60b-43d0-8c2f-9051652ad3d4: {n}Several possible explanations come to mind, both natural and magical. None of them are cause for immediate concern, but it would be best to remain alert.{/n}
37a1c4f2-be75-4622-bb7a-c26eff6acec4: {n}Suddenly, you hear screaming coming from the east.{/n}
86f530c5-ae53-41ef-b61d-f91211605458: {n}It appears as though they suddenly changed their minds and left.{/n}
4c7830cd-3c6b-4125-afad-c6a4c52073fa: {n}There's no sign of a fight. It doesn't look like the hunters were abducted or scared away, either.{/n}
40629266-d87f-4eaa-bc7b-9bb270e8b574: {n}After exploring for a while, you begin to understand what's wrong here. 8a1ddb31-e981-4e8f-b454-dbfa6c4f91f9: {n}Ekun sniffs the mugs, then shakes his head.{/n} "Not a menace."
4a4dda74-657f-45ee-8f60-78f076b469e5: "Have you taken care of Varnhold's defenses?"
b7527f91-2b9d-4858-a643-2e3d5b5e63be: "Do you remember anything from when your soul was imprisoned?"
eb0edf5a-eebf-455f-8e37-5cc748057409: "In your room, I discovered a letter containing threats. Is there something you'd like to discuss with me?"

7db15f75-6384-4612-bacb-5576302a3fb1: "I'm thinking about offering you an official position. In what way could you help me govern the country?"
807cc288-d3ba-42f3-b39c-51849e982d77: "Remind me, what did you ask me to do?"
7f3d3740-1a0c-43c8-8e7c-3546db07058b: {n}When he sees you, Maegar gives you a polite bow.{/n} "Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}! Welcome back. How can I serve you?"

53b38f59-9c3e-4338-b4f1-68eca297328a: "The people have already reconstructed the fort walls, even started digging a moat around the town and organizing patrols. 552ee337-5e1d-457b-8dc7-f6cdca08b973: "Excellent, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}, everything is excellent. Sure, when everyone returned home, they were a bit uncomfortable. d7971b88-9702-4fa7-8c0f-c228f7adc72c: {n}Maegar hesitates a moment, then finally says,{/n} "You saved us all, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}, and I'll never be able to thank you enough for that. ec27d847-1bfd-413c-ba0a-bd74e7239339: {n}Maegar freezes.{/n} "I'm... n-not sure, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}." {n}The man frowns.{/n} "It was... dark. Almost no space..." {n}He closes his eyes and gulps.{/n} "If... if you don't mind, I'd rather not recall any more."
445fd10e-3532-4a92-ac9c-19193707b073: {n}Maegar looks around the hall, squinting.{/n} "It's impressive. Still, sometimes I just miss the open spaces of {g|Dunsward}Dunsward{/g}."
ade08162-40d0-4e2d-b442-caed8622e19e: "To be blunt, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}, who cares? Maybe she's angry back in {g|Restov}Restov{/g}, or crying her head off, or even celebrating. Matters not — the issue's already been settled between the two of us."
0db462a4-cc51-44f1-9e06-4fe192590647: {n}Maegar's face darkens.{/n} "I didn't want you to know about that. Wanted to spare you from any further worries... I began receiving letters like that one since about when I sent you trading goods."
8e4c2c8f-6283-4108-a020-378e3784b75f: "Once, my men even interrogated the trader who delivered the mail, but nothing came of it. I have some assumptions of who's behind it, but as long as I have no proof, I don't want to accuse anyone."
222ed2c3-d6fe-49a6-bd4d-3ef75ed497b7: {n}Maegar shakes his head.{/n} "Sometimes it's hard, other times — less so. But overall it's nothing special. The chests in the treasury are fine, all the records are in order, and as for all the pressing issues, I can simply address them to you."
14f95517-17f4-4ec0-9402-f48d8a0fb090: {n}Maegar gives you a crooked smile, and shakes his head.{/n} "Eh, no, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}. I've been there before, and it seemed my advices didn't do much good. You should find someone else to help you."
c4951382-e673-41bd-b841-980893c76f49: "I can't say ruling a barony used to give me much joy — there are far more enjoyable pursuits. a6980a35-01a9-46e4-b5a0-ed89a002cd66: "To help me learn the fate of my people, who were down in that mysterious dungeon when Varnhold fell under Vordakai's spell. Cephal and I went down some of the way with them, but then had to hurry back to Varnhold, and I still don't know what happened."
71cf27a7-2e7f-4d35-882a-bae89d5919c3: "What will happen if Nyrissa's servants notice you?"
975aae05-143f-4027-922f-0ba16fcd5d09: "I have to go. Grave dangers won't wait!"
fab30759-adb9-409f-9013-b87f64f3a824: "What are these strange books you're selling?"

74601401-900b-4e43-a446-c33aac69ef13: "Are you aware that fairies are reborn sooner or later after they're killed? When we meet again, there's no way I'm giving you a discount! Or I just won't meet you at all. Your loss!"
6a3bc8e1-ed36-4b1f-983b-6c5ccb686a5c: "Hello again. How are things? I hope you are exhausted and desperate?"
8c4abb3b-284a-48e9-bd1d-ee112fd75547: "The best market in {g|First World}the First World{/g} — and I'm not lying, not even a little bit. 64d7aee5-e17c-4379-a7fd-b54426d07037: "I'm ready for the final battle. Let us march!"

efe283cc-58fa-4521-a774-e660ab40049a: "How do you know so much? Who are you, Storyteller?"
615ebb21-7e8a-4d4d-a983-8fdd30d12177: {n}The blind old man bows to you gracefully, as if he hadn't just stepped out of battle a moment ago.{/n} "I'm glad you're all right, Your Highness."
7e33bf76-ac67-483d-9a8f-6e42c9533556: "Alas, we are short of time. You must act quickly to save your kingdom and yourself from the Worlds Merger — that's what we've named the catastrophe that's befallen us. There are two obstacles that may stand in your way. First — your advisors and subjects are now in various regions across the kingdom, and almost all are under attack by shadows. The power of any land lies in the brave souls that inhabit it. Save them, and you will save yourself."
3b1b55b2-4504-4113-94ed-3d4441987be8: "I think you'll be interested to know that the portal you used to enter the House at the Edge of Time has come to life again. Your remaining comrades, including the nereid Evindra, passed through it and brought me news about your feats in the {g|First World}First World{/g}. We've been eagerly awaiting your return, but meanwhile we've met the {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g} and the affliction he's sent."
a6308d3c-7eba-4d6c-9332-bda65263b601: "The nature of curses is mysterious, Your Highness. I know many stories about them, with happy and unhappy endings, and I can propose the following: to overcome a curse you must harness it. The {g|LanternKing}Lantern King{/g} would have you perish with your kingdom — and he has made real that imaginary bond between the land and its ruler, which poets and bards like to talk about so much. But this means that by protecting the kingdom from the Worlds Merger, you will also protect yourself. I think this is the first thing that must be done."
ba2f9062-eaad-45f3-8e8a-ed073bf869f3: "I sense you have about twenty days. That is as long as your kingdom can {d|c61 Kingdom Normal}withstand{/d} the onslaught of the {g|First World}First World{/g}. Believe me, this is a generous amount of time, considering the affliction we face."
b848fbcf-419d-49f6-b028-9f7f38e922d7: "I feel you have about fifteen days, no more. The pressure of {g|First World}the First World{/g} is imminent. I fear neither you nor {d|c61 Kingdom Poor}your kingdom{/d} can stand much longer."
9156399a-911d-45d0-aee6-5c75abf3239e: "{g|First World}The First World{/g} is rapidly penetrating the very essence of this world, changing everything at its whim — and this process will soon become irreversible. As I mentioned, after the Worlds Merger everything went mad here, even time and the laws of nature. The greatest danger to you is that the borders of the world of dreams have been destroyed. The visions of the past have become real, and you cannot sleep any more. This is a part of the curse — and one of the most dangerous consequences of your connection to your kingdom."
c53e290d-7733-4398-8e7d-7ced9859e2cd: "Everyone has found it difficult, especially in the hours after the Worlds Merger began. Those who could keep their sanity and escape are now either hiding or surviving and helping others."
14af101d-eaad-444a-8e17-78c483d32dad: "Jhod Kavken gathered the remains of the capital guard and set off to {g|Oleg's Trading Post}Oleg's Trading Post{/g} – to help hold back the shadows that escaped from the cup."
74d7662f-732b-442f-a7da-bb2950bb7778: "Kesten {g|House Garess}Garess{/g}, with the remains of the capital guard, has taken up position near {g|Oleg's Trading Post}Oleg's Trading Post{/g}. The shadows of the Stag Lord's bandits that escaped the cup have gathered there, and someone must repel them."
972a8eab-c867-4478-9d6f-4a32e0e9857c: "Many shadows that escaped the Apology went to {g|Oleg's Trading Post}Oleg's Trading Post{/g}, creating chaos and destruction along their way. Jhod Kavken and Kesten {g|House Garess}Garess{/g} rallied the remains of the guard and struck out to protect our citizens."
b49e52f8-608c-4bdb-846e-8265faf6cb62: "Bartholomew Delgado was able to escape the capital, but then he was beset by shadows of trolls from {g|Trobold}Trobold{/g}. They, like all the others, appeared from the broken cup, and come to take revenge for ancient grievances. If Bartholomew is still alive, you should look for him somewhere in the old Trolls' Lair."
3f9795a6-38c8-42d5-9251-4a6654a5e7e6: "Tsanna went to {g|Lamashtu}Lamashtu's{/g} Shrine to honor her cruel goddess and seek protection for herself and her pack."
357ba3e3-fd3c-4b01-81b4-9a7e60562e43: "{d|c31 Maegar Saved}Maegar Varn{/d} must be preparing a final stand at {g|Varnhold}Varnhold{/g}. The city is in dire plight. — An army led by Vordakai's own shadow is besieging it."
e57b0721-914a-47fe-95b7-af144d26c423: "Your advisor {d|c31 Vordakai Hired}Maegar{/d} went to {g|Varnhold}Varnhold{/g}, but was beset by shadows. I know nothing more."
7ec4f179-cbd2-4910-8c0d-c6a29aef9d40: "Your neighbors from Brevoy received word of the woes besetting your kingdom, and went to the border. The Worlds Merger found them as they passed the Flintrock Grassland. They were waylaid by an army of shadows. I can only guess what is happening there now."
d8453315-03c8-409e-b523-1e07b4e31a58: "Some of the citizens we saved were captured the moment Irovetti's shadow emerged from the cup. They say he arrived as if to one of his glamorous receptions, gave a flowery speech and departed for {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g} to restore what he had lost. Your governor is probably having a hard time right now. I also heard that a beautiful nereid was captured by a shadow. – It would appear that Evindra is in the hands of her tormentor once more."
66af598f-4fe8-4cd5-95e6-69330efcf757: "Are you sure, Your Highness? You will have to fight the {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g} and all his servants with but a handful of comrades..."
e568c7b4-8199-42f9-9f5c-c505180f7a6f: "Are you sure, Your Highness? Will the forces you have assembled be enough to overcome the {g|LanternKing}Lantern King{/g} and the horde of shadows flooding the capital?"
a7612ff2-ea1b-428c-8fd3-63a960da34a1: "Of course, Your Highness. My powers are at your service."
d77f9cc2-a119-4cac-83a2-1d1cbdb9234c: "He is the {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g} of laughter, mischief, and transformation — the most unpredictable creature of the unpredictable {g|First World}First World{/g}. You will never guess what stands behind his actions. An evil prank might lead to a great good, and a virtuous gift to a terrible tragedy. As far as I can judge by the stories I've heard, the {g|LanternKing}Lantern King{/g} is not an evil creature. But each deity has its role in the structure of the world. Laughter, mischief and transformation is a strange and powerful mixture, and one can only guess how it will affect this fate or that."
d5dd4fd8-4357-4f92-bac9-e640856ef5ff: "I see you are ready. You will make history this day."
ce07db84-5651-4ccf-b7ec-091836f5f04b: "Of course. Tell me when you are ready."
10648e22-9aa0-44dd-a8df-442eae523437: "Very well, so be it! Our main forces will march now for the city, Your Highness, and I shall go with them. We will attempt to engage most of the Apology's shadows, and the {g|LanternKing}Lantern King's{/g} minions. Look for me in the city if you need rest! And... good luck!"
731983db-cbfd-407e-93ec-013e3c8344b5: "Of course you can always count on my help, and the help of your companions and fellow travelers."
91b417e8-2c5f-4f61-bc77-9922973c7fc6: "The warrior queen Bdaah sends regards to her ally, and is eager to take part in a battle with the {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g}."
22c1a4fa-3233-4c29-9b2e-019d4d4afd01: "Chief Sootscale and his kobolds have come to support their friend."
9144d8c1-16dc-44e0-afa9-f0e653ad1408: "The lizardfolk, who you freed from the power of Count Shimmerglow, have come to the capital and are ready to join your forces in the battle."
907c7609-ae9b-4fd1-b58e-c5434a4c1f22: "You managed to make friends among very different creatures – including goblins! Their delegation is ready to join your army."
e8b1c66d-68d2-4062-ba4d-485862247f69: "Although all your troubles come from {g|First World}the First World{/g}, some of its dwellers are on your side. Some fey have come and offered help in the battle to come."
dc85aa83-17c8-4f8f-bb1e-b0ea6b174492: "Sometimes help comes from unexpected places. A group of former — and not so former – bandits have joined the army."
33ebdc4e-fca7-44b2-9f97-1ddf3f5d9769: "{d|c41 Darven Nice}Darven{/d} from Brineheart has come to carry out his duty as an ally."
c737d70c-3411-42bb-abba-60c0b22b11c5: "The nymph Nyrissa, a most unexpected and awaited ally, is ready to share with you all the risks of the coming confrontation with the {g|LanternKing}Lantern King{/g}."
04fc467e-47f2-4886-aadc-491dcac2f6cc: "The army of {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g}, led by its governor, is ready for battle."
d05415fe-3bea-476a-bd24-6974bebb3b2e: "The {g|Swordlords}Aldori{/g} forces are here. Lady Jamandi and her most loyal officers will lead them in battle."
95dc3162-534c-4b2c-86b3-8cf622ac74bd: "Shandra Mervey and Lady {g|House Surtova}Surtova{/g} have brought soldiers from {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}."
6292ae10-9820-4357-b83a-2ed31bff5713: "We have unexpected news: none other than Lander {g|House Lebeda}Lebeda{/g} has come to our camp with his people. He is eager to help you in the upcoming battle. This might be an attempt to apologize..."
144ffa93-a2f2-486e-8ce3-bb0a7d03ef3f: "{g|Tiger Lords}Armag and his warriors{/g} are awaiting your signal to begin the attack."
2d054563-e5c1-490e-bc63-e2c315f2d935: "{g|Tiger Lords}Dugath and his warriors{/g} have come to support you."
c3bac2e3-09e3-4e50-b097-3f299f2c1858: "Tartuk sent us a few branded trolls to help."
22b4a6af-15ef-4f59-b41b-e82ab1bb2cab: "Hargulka and his trolls are ready to aid us in the coming battle."
28c49ad5-136d-456c-af4f-f626280d546c: "The capital guard have returned from the {g|Oleg's Trading Post}Trading Post{/g} and await your orders."
d0510396-40bd-49a2-afa1-2bb04e6134e3: "Second – while the Worlds Merger is tormenting the kingdom, you will not be able to rest and restore your spells in the normal way. This seems a special gift from the {g|LanternKing}Lantern King{/g} — to let you fight for your life, but make it so that fighting leads inevitably to exhaustion and death. But I can guard you from this for a short time. Come to me if you need rest. But be careful — this takes time, and time is not on your side."
b532d42e-1974-439e-a297-1f59bcbf1498: {n}The Storyteller pauses.{/n} "I... do not know. The crucial knowledge just appeared in my mind, as though someone whispered it into my ear. Yesterday, I had no idea I was capable of wielding such powerful magics or holding such vast knowledge, and look at me now."
752fbdee-843d-41e6-8273-f78297988c35: "One might assume this was due to the experience I acquired while living through my stories... but I doubt that idea. I even doubt now whether I am an elf, or somebody... perhaps something else. However, this mystery is not important just now. We will deal with it after we save your kingdom."
d24e72e2-ed71-49ff-a8dc-0daec6fc7dff: "Of course, Your Highness..." {n}The Storyteller stops abruptly and frowns.{/n} "I feel the presence of a new threat. What is happening?"
f02e4054-ce86-42f6-bcd0-cd394d734049: "Your Highness! I sense the {g|LanternKing}Lantern King's{/g} curse still lingers over you! The enemy has a sword to your throat, and with a single move can end your life. Yet he waits, for now, enjoying his performance. Beware, he will use the curse to his advantage, as soon as he senses danger. You should lift the effects of Lantern King's curse, by gathering your allies and restoring your kingdom, before you move to challenge him directly."
d44fb58d-b7bc-44fd-8246-795983967054: {g|Military5_1}[Choice effects]{/g} "You must immediately prohibit this home-made booze among our soldiers, and arrest any who brew it. We need fighters, not drunken murderers."
ad68ad4d-a25f-43f7-b9af-ed8e288af109: {g|Military5_2}[Choice effects]{/g} "I provide my soldiers with weapons and ask them to kill. How they do it is their business. I won't make anyone drink, but I'm not prohibiting these potions either."
75fe32f3-585b-4452-a419-ee64b27b82d0: {g|Military5_3}[Choice effects]{/g} "I like the idea of these potions. Let every soldier drink them if they really help. Whatever they lack in power, they'll make up for with this magic."
5836b028-3739-4bf5-b199-b2fcc6aa60f5: "What is the potion's effect? Is it dangerous?"
6b19a637-cae3-4fde-bd5c-b0fea2e95345: {n}Kassil seems to be lost.{/n} "{mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}! I need your opinion. I caught a new recruit brewing dangerous potions for himself and the other soldiers. These potions turn them into fierce fighters for a while, but they dangerously twist their minds."
4af8ca14-9c68-4dbf-b0b6-e7a6a137ac48: "Instead of training and drilling, these lazy fools are relying on their potions. Many have already tried it, and the others are surely curious. I've arrested the cooks, but the officers are of a different opinion! They believe the potions might be effective, though they're quite unpredictable."
303f7d7b-38c2-43eb-a058-f6a98b4ebc45: {n}Regongar has a strange look in his eyes, and his speech is confused.{/n} "Ah well, how you doing, your chieftesty? You know, I've seen a miracle! {g|Gorum}Gorum{/g} himself honored one of my commanders... with a gift! He turns pathetic weaklings to fierce spawn of the {g|Abyss}Abyss{/g}, able to defeat anyone with their bare hands! You know how?"
66668747-26ef-4eb7-901e-94e55fb7855b: {n}Amiri looks annoyed.{/n} "So, chief, it's about our soldiers. The pups are brewing magic potions of strength and bravery. It leaves no fear or doubt in their heads, just fury like the howling wind."
815c270b-15ca-4299-835c-a3f85224b9c7: {n}Regongar laughs out loudly.{/n} "Potions, he says! He got his fighters drunk! And they're not what you'd call fighters... All he's got is weaklings in his squad! But they all went like they were battle-crazy, fighting anyone who steps in their way! Pure gold, that's what this potion is."
22d82757-cb8a-48b4-ad80-a02038b5a61d: {n}Kassil opens his mouth to object, but stays silent. After a while, he nods.{/n} "I understand, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. Everyone is responsible for the power in their own hands. I will pass down the values of the {g|Swordlords}Swordlords{/g} to as many fighters as I can reach. Those who won't listen... Well, I feel sorry for them."
44eb3ae1-c882-4a9b-a255-b437ae6436a7: "I mean... Back in our tribe we used it some. But mostly it's for lazy bones and weaklings. A real fighter like me doesn't need that stuff. I wish there was more like me in your army. I would let them do what they want – and the potions do make them look like real soldiers. But I decided to ask you what you want."
f68664b1-d84e-4799-bfef-4a931131dd95: "The {g|Swordlords}Swordlords{/g} taught me to rely on myself and my skills – which were forged by sacrifice and struggle, not by drinking some potion. But you're not Aldori. You have every right to establish your own order. Must I bow to the officers' will, or will you trust me?" {n}Kassil peers at you, sweat running down his temple.{/n}
e4d2cbf3-a700-43f0-8e8a-29c6d0098da0: {n}Amiri looks at you ironically.{/n} "You southerners have strange ways, you know. I don't know whether you're their chief or their nanny, {name}. Are they adults with weapons and deadly skills, or naughty children you tell little rules. I still don't understand your ways here in the South, but I'll do what you told me to."
577ddd66-4e67-44af-9ea3-fb234c83462c: "That is right. Fighters must be responsible for themselves. Otherwise it's not a fighter, but just a bug wearing armor. If the potion is good for them, maybe it'll help them live. If not, then it's their own fault they died."
1a02408b-7ca8-4b74-9b2e-e635758bc461: {n}Regongar looks at you with respect.{/n} "Protecting your reputation, eh? Very wise. We don't want the neighbors spreading rumors that you're doping your fighters. I'll take care of everything myself. You'll have nothing to do with it. You are a deep thinker, {name}."
3b174c3c-d988-434a-b2b6-13d1a96466be: {n}Amiri frowns.{/n} "I'm not drinking this stuff. I decide for myself how I kill my enemies. But you're the chief. Your word is the law for the others."
9ec13be3-e59c-4650-ac2f-ba5722768dac: "Starting tomorrow, we'll have potion production in every camp. It'll turn your weaklings into real head hunters. Just point them at the battle and stay out of their way!"
14118d74-48a3-4d31-bd5d-87c11c3fa465: "The stuff makes your arms stronger and you vision clearer, but it clouds your mind. It befits a savage – a goblin or a bandit – but not a fighter who goes to battle with a cool head."
1926d8b5-662a-484f-958a-2593daafffb8: "It makes you mad. Makes you want to fight. And it makes you strong as a bear. And there's something else..." {n}Amiri frowns and waves her hand.{/n} "Oh, never mind about that."
659ba4a9-c6d5-45ef-9d66-c82d16ecf3e2: {n}Regongar's eyes grow dead. The half-orc looks away from you.{/n} "The quietest time is just before the thunderstorm... And then... drip, drop... plip, plop... And then it bursts! And flashes! Your soul groans, and whizzes, the wind howls, and the thunder strikes!" {n}Regongar licks his dry lips. He seems unaware of the electricity arcing between his fingers.{/n} "And you are the storm! No one can stop you. That's how it works. I tried it. I know what I'm talking about."
ff732643-b99b-4fd7-a499-1a4d5a6e04e0: {n}Amiri's gaze is incinerating.{/n} "I want to stay out of it. I'm their commander, not their nanny. Let them drink whatever they want to as long as they're ready to fight."
1edc2fd2-49f8-43a7-8682-2e9995408c60: {n}Regongar's mania suddenly fades. He speaks quietly.{/n} "I've been thinking... Let's make all our fighters take these potions. Then you'll have an army of real cutthroats. They won't care about death, pain, fear, or really have any feelings at all. They'll kill without hesitation. Burn villages to the ground without a second thought. What do you say?"
2202e113-0d1a-4cfd-a03b-3fa89a20ad61: "I appreciate your trust, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}." {n}Kassil pauses, and then continues in an earnest tone.{/n} "I am glad that you've taken my views to heart. The potions will be prohibited as of today. Any who produce them will be punished."
81ef2c2c-5797-4d13-be5a-c204f5a116fb: The familiar road rolled out before us as our hero{mf||ine} turned toward {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}. At {mf|his|her} back, the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g} had yet to reveal all their secrets to the daring adventurer who had decided {mf||s}he would be the one to conquer them...
c3c73a72-af94-40a0-a711-649d73da1837: But really, what would be the point of such a strange endeavor? Much easier to just return to the reliable shelter of {g|Restov}Restov{/g}'s walls, set up shop, maybe start a family, and live out the rest of your days like any other citizen — in peace, warmth, a bit of boredom, and the full confidence that tomorrow will be just as orderly and predictable as yesterday...
500fcc76-00ee-4176-a94a-f12088fd4ec4: Hey, did you really think I'd choose a hero{mf||ine} like that for my book?! Ridiculous! No, our daring leader, after indulging in a bit of nostalgia for that old {g|Restov}Restov{/g} flair, turned {mf|his|her} back on faraway {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g} and followed the call of destiny — to the unpredictable, wild, beautiful {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g}!
db753bcd-f294-44be-af53-29f169784bbb: "Do you know anything about the ancient dwarven fortress in these lands?"
6f41e41c-71cb-4602-a186-6424563b3a71: "You look a little unusual for a dwarf."
984b3bdb-4350-49d9-8617-a5fafe52ef0f: "Have you heard about the thefts plaguing in the city?"
62cabc44-fb30-4174-9a2d-5d9c7ac91848: "Tell me, do you have any books by Willas Gunderson?"
69d97b20-2c83-4902-b4dd-877b7feccc16: "Does the phrase 'fifth in ten' mean anything to you?"
372a7646-b865-449f-9deb-78432f5a7ca5: "From a practical standpoint, you're probably right..."
51c38640-b441-4386-8e1e-08ebc34adb7b: "Heh. Kinsman, whatever the explanation, a dwarf without a beard is a sad sight!"
8e27d8f6-5577-4df1-8724-45310caabdf3: {n}A young dwarf, red-haired, neat and surprisingly clean-shaven, stands leaning against a sledge-hammer. He's busy reading some book, but as you approach he looks up and bows slightly.{/n} "Greetings, Your Grace! I am Verdel, a blacksmith. What can I do to help you?"
3d1da6e2-935c-4c54-8118-9ca61bacf744: {n}As usual, Verdel is taking a break from his labors in the blacksmith shop, reading a book. When he notices you, he stops reading and bows.{/n}
8f3bf385-4426-4638-921e-1537a628a458: "Nothing at all, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}. Three dwarf clans used to live in these lands — the Woradash, the Langebukk and the Skjegge. My family is Skjegge. But we moved off to {g|Mivon}Mivon{/g} two hundred years ago, together with Aldori — fleeing from the Conqueror. Our grandfathers made a safe bet that the {g|Swordlords}Swordlords{/g} would need swords! Anyhow, neither me nor even my father have ever been to the old fortresses. I vaguely remember from grandfather's stories that the Langebukk stronghold was supposed to be somewhere nearby. But no, I'd have no idea where to look for it."
9015be15-7656-4d70-abbe-28aef1f9fb15: {n}Verdel sighs and runs his fingers through his hair.{/n} "You expect to see a beard, eh? No offense, but what's the point of a beard? Especially when you're a blacksmith and working with fire. You burn it once, dip it into lighting oil and catch a spark from the forge, and your beard is history! You're better off without one."
386246c0-080b-4635-b548-d8bd925a0918: "What is there to tell, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}? I'm a blacksmith. My father was a blacksmith. My grandfather was a blacksmith, and his grandfather too. Besides, every one of them were remarkably fertile, so I have plenty of cousins, second cousins, third cousins, and all of them are blacksmiths too. Pretty much all the weapons in {g|Mivon}Mivon{/g} were forged by someone from our family. That's why I moved away from the old home grounds. My skills are more useful here, that's for sure."
fc7e3e07-0904-4063-89b8-7c10d4120a05: {n}Verdel looks a little confused.{/n} "Well, different things... It's nice to take a rest with a good book. Just now it's 'Valour and Honor: Ten Adventures of the Splendid Willas Gunderson in {g|Absalom}Absalom{/g}'."
e4dd09e7-3bf4-41e0-b9c5-f5318651e0ab: {n}Verdel frowns.{/n} "Heard? Your Highness, I myself am the victim of those thieves! Stole my tools — right from under my very nose!"
76078478-ecd4-4da8-b0a9-f36a5f4ab826: "I was in the back yard, getting coal for the furnace, and I heard some noise inside. I ran in — and the thief jumped right into a magic portal and vanished! I didn't even get a good look."
fe4ece76-3b05-4049-a100-a78496157201: "It's like you're interrogating me! Uh, of course I do. Everyone says he's bad, but I like him. The guy writes with feeling... I mean, used to write."
23a0b485-690b-4867-a925-5c60c9485cc8: "Is this about Gunderson? He has a book titled 'Ten Adventures'. It's some of his best work!"
df585dd3-3eeb-4728-bf27-49e612002e96: "Well, for once in my life, I got approval from a kinsman!"
20c57b84-a361-4009-b6a0-aac7e85bad6d: "You don't say. Why, they might start taking us for elves!" {n}Verdel chuckles, but it's clear he has no intention of changing his opinion.{/n}
b3e4fdcd-7b95-4487-b0cb-93df6b3f9332: "Practicality is my middle name, right!" {n}Verdel nods, content.{/n}
ecdddc84-9624-44d2-9216-b900ac9c4727: "I concern myself tirelessly about our mission's success. I think three steps ahead, just so that our expedition can reach its goal. And what do I hear in return? Unprovoked insults!"

0f575913-1ba0-40b6-9d5a-f02dc9fb070c: "This fog... It enshrouds, entangles, suffocates... If only I could learn how it was created! But my powers wane. I have barely the strength to call out to you.
