Well, glory passes quickly. A few miserable decades later, and no one recognizes you on the street anymore. What a shame."
e345f61c-03e9-410a-8f5a-a1cfab881152: "Once, long ago, I could spot an enemy and pin him to the wall before he could even think of attacking. Some said I had eight eyes and looked all around at once. Though it seems I've outlived my nickname." {n}Anoriel stretches her arm forward. Her palm trembles noticeably.{/n} "I've been drinking so much lately, it's best I don't test my skills too often."
34d624a2-80a4-4644-bf53-2ea314e9afbb: "Uh, no, I've got enough things to do already. You'd better manage on your own."
9e9e33d1-92e5-4265-8e67-22b9e95621cf: "I sit here waiting for adventurers who are in need of help. We may be sitting here in a backwoods tavern, but in {g|Absalom}Absalom{/g} I have a lot of friends who are eager to make a few coins. They have brave hearts, but shallow pockets. A little gold would be a welcome change for them. I can send them a message, and they will come from Absalom through a portal. If you're interested, just give me a sign, and we'll arrange everything right away."
ecc951c0-4130-4a9c-a42c-5d7fd6e7cfa2: "I have friends like that. Just decide who exactly you need, and they will come on my signal. This will cost you {custom_companion_cost} gold pieces."
0ee0ff5f-a3bb-40a3-a5af-b1ff16b8a688: "It's a school of adventurers. We search for those who are eager to test their skills, and we educate them and give them ideas about where on {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g} they might seek their fortune. They look for forgotten knowledge, secrets, and lost artifacts. They are explorers and pathfinders. We're a sort of mutual assistance club for adventure lovers. We exchange experience, share knowledge, and keep careful records. — In case it proves useful to future expeditions. And also, we publish books for thrill seekers... and bored urban teenagers from wealthy families."
db7b708d-afea-488c-a8ac-ced1db511d85: "All sorts of adventurers. We have representatives from all races, religions and beliefs. The Grand Lodge is in {g|Absalom}Absalom{/g}, but there are many smaller lodges throughout {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g}, and the venture-captains direct Pathfinders to their goals from across all the corners of the world. There are many renowned heroes in the {g|Pathfinder Society}Society{/g}... And many scoundrels as well, whose service to the Society has brought them fame."
6900ec62-0590-46fd-bc16-6c6e016d30b7: "You mean, who does it serve? No one in particular. Pathfinders try not to get involved in the quarrels of others. They serve only the spirit of adventure. And, sometimes, they happen to save the world. However, that doesn't mean there are no black sheep among the Seekers..."
e59127cc-94ac-45a7-8410-4a5b81202d83: "The {g|Pathfinder Society}Society{/g} is an interesting community. There is much to tell about it."
b3a97915-5388-46b5-be82-13380aa20081: "You want to know how one could exchange the life of a Pathfinder for this sorry drunken rathole?" {n}The light in Anoriel's eyes goes out as if someone had blown out a candle.{/n} "You lose all your friends because of one scumbag, and then you'll understand. I was the only one to return from the final campaign of the Reckless Six... and whatever is left of me... can't be called a Seeker anymore."
8ac4a230-7790-4045-9f20-7160c3e9720f: "Voltar called to his god, and a ray of light shone forth, sending the vile creatures running. I almost believed for a moment that we had a chance..." {n}Anoriel catches her breath and starts to talk faster.{/n} "That part was the worst. It seemed like we could get out, if we could just make it a little farther... But then the zombies overwhelmed Voltar like a tidal wave. Ghotry lost her mind. She scrambled up a staircase, whispering the words of a children's song and screaming in terror. She jumped from the tower — to escape whatever ghost was tormenting her. The fall maimed her, but she survived. And after all this I... I was alone. The darkness closed in over me."
2224cc69-c46b-4bf2-826f-073105cbabc5: "We were attacked by the undead... Skeletons, zombies... but that wasn't the worst. What filled me with terror was the invisible dark entity crawling among the stones. This... thing... was driving us crazy — literally! Jaqueson rushed to a stone statue and beat it until he broke all his fingers. After that, there wasn't much use for his magic wand, though the poor fellow never gave up trying to help us. Berberton fell behind when we began our retreat. The last time I saw him he was squatting over a heap of carrion, gorging himself... and sobbing like a newborn all the while, I swear by {g|Pharasma}Pharasma{/g}!" {n}Tears glint in Anoriel's eyes.{/n}
71e7d047-d662-46c7-aa40-209dbb83259d: "When I came to my senses, we were all in cages. All of us except for Vermelt. He was free, unscathed — and extremely pleased with himself. And the undead were under his command." {n}Anoriel clenches her fists.{/n} "The bastard betrayed us. From the very beginning. He'd decided to keep those damned books for himself! Adrissant wasn't his friend, but his competitor. Vermelt staged his death and went to find books while we fought off the undead. He used us as fodder... and those who survived were to become sacrifices for his ritual! We were betrayed by the one we trusted most!"
8e521c3d-d79d-4f9e-9b9f-d147394a6f5a: "I was hunting. Got a little lost in the mist — which is the first time that's happened to me. I guess I should go easier on the drink. But don't you imagine I'd be scared of a good fight! If only I'd known I was missing all the action... But I see you've got everything under control."
94955458-8a25-4b0f-b8c0-576dbcd27a00: "We were to be sacrificed in Vermelt's ritual. The madman had decided to transform himself into a lich — and for this he required souls of the living. He'd prepared everything else in advance — after all, such a ritual demands extra precision, and his immortality was at stake. Vermelt probably thought he was ready for anything... except for Ghotry." {n}Anorel smiles sadly.{/n} "Brave Ghotry. She'd come to senses by then, though she'd suffered some terrible wounds. But she was determined that she wouldn't let Vermelt carry out his plan. She would not become a sacrifice on his altar. With her broken fingers, she managed to pick up a sharp stone and open her veins. In her final moment, she summoned the grace of {g|Pharasma}Pharasma{/g} for aid — and her prayer was so powerful that the goddess's messenger responded. The spirit entered her lifeless body and waited patiently, ready to strike."
8e944782-00dd-4297-a62a-3ee5a2ccee01: "The time of the ritual had come, and Ghotry was carried to the altar. At the very moment that the dagger was supposed to end her life, {g|Pharasma}Pharasma's{/g} messenger left her body and flew into a rage. It was... well, there are no words to describe its splendor!" {n}The elf stares at the floor.{/n} "But poor Ghotry. She was bolder and purer than any of us. Her sacrifice saved us. And she didn't even get a decent funeral... By some miracle, we managed to free ourselves and joined the battle. Vermelt's ritual was broken, and the mage transformed into a pathetic, undead shadow of himself. The only thing we could do was finish him off. Our friend. Our would-be executioner. The final feat of the Reckless Six. And then we ran."
69710c09-b4a4-4542-9f3b-b710b8927c87: "That very night, Berberton has finally lost his mind and killed Voltar. Jaqueson died of his wounds. I reached {g|Absalom}Absalom{/g} alone and handed over those damned books to the {g|Pathfinder Society}Society{/g}. I was promised the post of venture-captain, but I... couldn't accept it. I looked at my new comrades and saw future corpses. In the end, I decided to get away — as far as I could. And so I ended up here. A worthy place to bury yourself." {n}The elf sighs heavily, but then her face clears and she suddenly smiles.{/n} "But I look at you and I remember the old days. Not those terrible days in {g|Ustalav}Ustalav{/g}... but the better days, when we were all alive. And brave. Together. It's... a strange feeling, but a pleasant one, too."
b732d16e-b06e-440d-a234-4a715b7e8f00: "Do I really have the honor of speaking with {mf|His|Her} Highness {mf|him|her}self? My respects, {mf|King|Queen}!"
c3f833e0-bdcd-4b85-b5dd-05b4ef16fe6c: "Enough. I shouldn't have gotten into this. Who am I to stir up other's feelings with all my chatter? We'd better forget about it for now. Maybe I'll tell you more some other time. But not today."
bd32f106-7ad4-4e59-93f8-5416f6dd49d3: {n}The elf shakes her head.{/n} "I have no wish to fill your sleep with nightmares. When you prove that you can stand firm in battle, that you can achieve victory without losing yourself along the way... then I will tell you of the horrors that waited us in Renchurch."
5538f082-3718-4475-a896-a72fa46e24f0: {n}The elf utters a gloomy sigh.{/n} "You've dealt with the Stag Lord, so I'll tell you my story. I hope it will make you think twice about looking for any more trouble."
42c9a472-8dd8-45db-9be3-8106d36a1e9c: "How can I refuse {mf|the King|the Queen}? Very well…"
21ad1405-9589-46b5-99e3-58af6161ef4a: "It doesn't matter how. All that matters is that I put the Pathfinder's life behind me after that." {n}Anoriel gives you a piercing look.{/n} "You don't need to hear this, {mf|baron|baroness} — at least not yet."
bc920064-bc74-461a-adfc-72319e31e2fd: "You know... this is the first time I've told the whole story to someone, from beginning to end. I was afraid that it would hurt to speak of my lost comrades, but... it seems I feel better now. Amazing, right?" {n}Anoriel plunges her fingers into her bag.{/n} "I want to thank you. This once served me faithfully. I think it will be in the right hands if I give it to you!"
6948ea75-f15a-4294-8b9b-eaf36a7d8cd1: {n}Anoriel rubs her hands together.{/n} "Great, everything is wonderful! Just now I'm waiting for someone to take a new Society mission. You see, I got this map from the archives..."
540fa20f-c700-4cf2-a1df-9c9979e39484: {n}Anoriel gives you a false smile.{/n} "Oh, never mind that! I didn't like the idea much anyway…"
fa5b3c72-8ba9-490d-9552-47b112186745: "I'm the venture-captain of the local {g|Pathfinder Society}Pathfinder Society{/g} lodge, remember? Where else would I look for adventurers, if not in the tavern? By the way, if you happen to be in need of reliable assistance, I can help with that. I have plenty of friends in {g|Absalom}Absalom{/g}, eager to earn a few coins. They have brave hearts, but shallow pockets. A little gold would be a welcome change. I can send them a message, and they will come from Absalom through a portal. If you're interested — just give me a sign, we'll arrange everything."
c869ca8e-3bcb-4a1e-b94b-63bc49a2d3f3: "And now, thanks to you, I run the local lodge of the {g|Pathfinder Society}Pathfinder Society{/g}. Don't you remember? I'm the one who came to talk to you about establishing it."
e3f5c74a-6ee9-4c8d-851c-92c85f3cdfa0: "Some mess you got yourself into," {n}the elf says in place of a greeting.{/n} "How can I help you? Won't be easy to gather fighters in these circumstances, but I'll try. Just give the word!"
4bdeecea-1f07-435a-ac4d-7f97c587c0be: "Think as long as you like. I'm not going anywhere."
f18cf5e2-d703-4cac-8676-116dacd8b397: "Also, I can summon the tutors from the {g|Pathfinder Society}Pathfinder Society{/g}, who can retrain you and your companions. They're quite willing to do this for free, the first three times you request their services. After that, the price for retraining will gradually increase. Such is their way of doing business with all new clients."
36a80d89-a5af-4582-bedf-86dbb6730371: "Just Lander? No last name? No title?"
9742a2f4-9974-4c42-b1a8-95b7e0b2e25a: "Please, tell me again what you're doing here?"
bc1905ed-6052-4c1f-9fb4-dc7ca0db8838: "Tell me once more what you want from me."
a58de0a5-fa87-4e4d-96de-a7e423d64a71: {n}A handsome, well-dressed young man of about seventeen years old looks at you with a polite smile.{/n}
61786129-073a-4bfb-83a6-402033e45a90: "So, you're the famous slayer of the Stag Lord's gang, soon to be a baron{mf||ess}? Pleased to make your acquaintance. My name is... Lander."
b403fd52-6885-476f-88c1-61c5700a4cbc: "Well, let's just say I'm here... incognito. Under my circumstances, it's wise to keep one's lineage to oneself."
88cca767-120c-4c1b-8055-15094635a6fe: "Oh, no, I'm not from here. I'm just visiting, you could say. I wanted to see for myself the heroes who managed to conquer the frontier lands, and the Lord Mayor was kind enough to invite me to this wonderful party."
51d38587-a1a8-4849-8b6a-fd7a95999e3e: "Truth be told, that's precisely what I wanted to speak with you about. You see, I am an heir to one of {g|Brevoy}Brevoy's{/g} Noble Houses. I won't say which, but believe me, a newly appointed baron{mf||ess} with no connections would do well to have a friend like me."
450093bb-3dd6-43fe-bc21-3ecce428455a: "Wait, we've only just met! This is the whole point of parties such as this — making connections that could eventually grow into alliances!"
f19d4620-e0d9-4721-99a2-d1a7d8853e88: "Your Sarenrae is a real hypocrite! Forgive this one, punish that one... Calistria's teachings are simple and fair: you get offended – you get revenge! It's all honest, no tricks or pretense!"
54dab8f4-d721-42ae-917b-dfa546c37e91: "The debate between mercy and revenge has gone on for thousands of years. Do you really think you and I are going to settle it now? You and your goddess have chosen your path. I follow my goddess a different way."
84ab0bcc-2bfe-4858-8867-63e86daface4: "It's great that at least someone in this party besides me understands the power of words! Perhaps you will really amount to something in time, Linzi."
e9aa3498-d9c8-4b4a-9f1e-1fee05a2ac86: "You really think so? It's... That's very flattering. Thank you!"
ebdbe047-d2b4-46f2-a0c1-1b71fd08259a: "Looks like we missed our chance to find these strange cultists, discussing their goddess. Let's hope we don't regret it..."
efe9e1f4-2239-4919-833b-77f06d71fbd0: "Not all of us were born for adventure, Mim. You'd better go back home."
15df164e-1d57-46dc-b439-dbcc79ddda83: "Everyone makes mistakes. But some give up, while others stand up and go on! I'm going to climb this mountain, no matter what it takes. What about you?"
fb15b843-3528-49e3-8207-acd0722538eb: [Use magic] "I have just the spell for you..."
1dda15f0-e67c-4240-be4b-ecb5aac73397: [Try fixing the dislocated joint] "You didn't break your ankle, you twisted it. Hold on for a second, all right?"
b1d5a4e0-1468-4cdf-92ac-fb02662f5de6: "There's no fracture – it's just dislocated. But I'm not sure I can fix it myself..."
db881bf1-4cf7-4479-9fe6-c4006bb7173c: "I'm sorry, I was trying to set it back in its socket. But it seems too badly twisted."
8ccb7283-141b-4704-bbe5-4c5ee45c116f: "Watch your tongue if you want to keep it."
85f978a6-9df3-4ff7-999d-2fd28b5295d6: "You decided to go on, even after you saw giant spiders?"
0dd106e3-73ff-4ad3-9f41-e0aaf6482c3d: {n}{d|Mim}Mim's{/d} clothes are dirty, and her hair is matted.{/n} "Good gods! I feared I would... I would have to stay... here forever..." {n}Tears are running down her dirty cheeks, leaving light trails on her skin.{/n}
f320e983-97a6-43ee-9a36-724407fd7a17: "I... I wanted to climb {g|Talon Peak}Talon Peak{/g}. It was... a sudden decision. I just thought, why put it off? Why ask for someone else to help, like I always do? Why can't I just get my wish by myself? After all, I left father so I could achieve everything on my own. So, I decided to climb the mountain alone. Skies above, my pride nearly sent me to my grave!"
7d27a36b-9b7d-4da4-be37-6e65ede5e3ad: {n}A smile appears on Mim's pale face.{/n} "After all, what good would an ascent be if there weren't any obstacles along the way? I'm not giving up! Let's go! To the top! You're coming with me, right?"
21d7cce7-b0af-4a71-8149-8543992919b3: {n}Mim lowers her head and sighs heavily.{/n} "You're... you're right. I should know that my place is in the workshop with my tools. Just show me the way, and I'll be off."
932a0e63-0255-4440-a9f3-3365d011f937: "I think I broke my ankle... I was fighting some spiders, and stepped on a stone, and it slipped, and I tripped and fell, and hit my ankle... I managed to drive away the beasts, but it's still messed up. It hurts too much to walk on. I crawled for several hours, but I couldn't..."
d7c99a73-e9e6-46aa-b90c-095ed8102e6e: {n}Mim relaxes her shoulders in relief.{/n} "Whew... That's much better. Thank you so much!"
fb094ddd-5b22-4c57-be43-151c3636a097: {n}Mim's ankle is swollen and red. It looks more like a dislocation than a fracture. You palpate the area to find the bone intact.{/n}
2ae140f6-aa8a-4a67-a734-9bfcc86f07ce: {n}Mim's ankle looks swollen and red. You'll need help of an expert medic...{/n}
573f263e-9249-4e73-a410-fe7d83c18d18: "Wait, what... OUCH!" {n}The joint clicks back into place.{/n} "Oh... well... It feels better... Much better! Thank you very much! Here, I'll try to get up..."
c1bdaac1-a4b7-412a-9f16-7ac398535073: "Wait, what... OUCH! Devil's mercy, that hurts! What the hell do you think you're doing?"
b98a32f6-3ba8-439a-a68b-2b51405f2d37: {n}Mim looks away.{/n} "I see. Well, thanks for trying to help."
191a4fc6-5025-496f-be32-7837651ad75a: {n}Mim inhales, then breathes out slowly.{/n} "Just... don't. All right?"
fe9091d1-6133-4bd1-8ff2-c23c1ffdcab6: "So, the bones are intact... So that's good. I think."
1526769c-feae-47a4-923b-ffb2192ccbae: {n}Mim flinches and lowers her head.{/n} "I'm sorry, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. The pain is clouding my judgment."
5de8196e-63dc-4db4-b966-9f07a4300ef6: "Yes... I can walk now. But where should I go?"
70532c7c-e88d-4468-bab7-7848fff2b895: "Don't get me wrong, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. I... I suddenly realized what my third wish would be. What I need to do, to find my inspiration. I must climb {g|Talon Peak}Talon Peak{/g}! To see the world from that height, to rise above myself... that's what my soul has been craving! But I don't know if I can make it."
c791554d-d8be-4e63-98d4-1515d611602c: {n}Mim's face turns red.{/n} "I'm a mage! Before I tripped, I was handling them just fine! They were still afraid to attack, the spineless creeps..."
d83b11b5-3895-470f-922e-b9a15081e911: {g|Culture4_3}[Choice effects]{/g} "My soldiers risk their lives every day for these lands. Let them enjoy some well-deserved glory. Let's order the series of etchings from the artist."
d8a53926-24b5-412b-8d1f-65ba171794ff: {g|Culture4_1}[Choice effects]{/g} "Let our neighbors learn all about the talented people of our lands. We'll help the musician."
336d026d-ed8a-4fa5-8181-d785d56ea4cd: {g|Culture4_2}[Choice effects]{/g} "It is our duty to preserve the culture and traditions of the Stolen Lands. We'll support the provincial teacher."
70f843c8-738b-48e6-985b-617b7975bfb5: "{name}, our Treasurer informs me that we've managed to save up some money allocated for culture – a substantial amount, in fact! I talked to my friends in the artistic communities, and I've found three projects worthy of support!"
11ce1155-874f-49d5-bb26-15f3441f911e: "{mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, my calculations show that we haven't spent all the money we've allocated for cultural development. I have three projects on one of which we could spend the surplus."
82293338-a5ad-43fe-8e7e-c39ec1035816: "The Treasurer reports that we've allocated more money than we've actually spent on culture. A considerable sum of money remains. Money must be put to work, so I suggest you invest it in one of three projects."
295542c2-1ebc-4e3f-bd39-5fda51d97e7d: "It's an easy guess, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, that I suggest you pay attention to the folk wisdom collector. I myself am working on preserving tales from the ancient times. He's working hard on preserving modern-day tales for our descendants. The one can't do without the other, and both complement each other nicely!"
7ff7beef-dfb1-4c08-82a3-293b8a77855e: "At first I thought of a local violin player I know. He's always dreamed of traveling around the neighboring lands, playing his music. I also talked to a provincial teacher who is assembling a book of local legends and traditions. And finally, I kept receiving letters from an artist local to the capital – I have no idea why. When we met, she offered me a series of etchings depicting your 'brilliant officers' and the 'great feats' of your army."
56e37bc7-0710-4f66-8eff-4b44c39e7fe4: "The first is a famous local violin player, who wishes to tour our neighbors' lands. The second is a book of local legends and traditions assembled by a provincial teacher. But the most promising is a series of etchings depicting your military campaigns. This artist's love of her motherland... it's most impressive!"
723a442e-b34f-49cf-bb18-946d809bfe0a: "The violin player I told you about is an old friend. Even the most callous listener is touched by his music! Besides, he has plenty of friends in the {g|River Kingdoms}River Kingdoms{/g}. His concerts will be of the highest standards. They will attract crowds of fans, and every one of them will be grateful to you for giving them the gift of such lovely music."
70cd1dc1-28cb-47b5-b0ff-c3f2685a66c3: "The violin player's endeavor is commendable. Besides, when people hear his music and learn that you, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, are the one who made his concerts possible, then they will certainly grant you their favor and respect."
c94fb643-fe3f-46de-9bb1-b8aae9be76af: "A musician wishes to tour around the {g|River Kingdoms}River Kingdoms{/g}. It's not our best option, but it could enhance your image among our more sensitive citizens. The provincial teacher's proposal is the least promising. A book of peasants' superstitions and stories will lead nowhere of interest."
e7515794-40dc-4269-a649-b24a4535b739: "Excellent! Let me tell him! He'll be so happy!"
82e8b877-232e-4b25-be56-bea2038f5387: "I'll discuss with him the details of his tour, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}."
020a322a-03ed-4d30-beba-8117f7185c50: "Yes, well, that's a fine use of our money..."
c1e9fe07-ba56-4a6d-9128-8b2d79cf7791: "Hm... I'll hate to upset my friend... But I'm glad for the teacher!"
7bc64f35-492e-4768-99bf-58d34ca09fe1: "I'm sure we should support the musician. Your patronage of the arts will make you famous across the {g|River Kingdoms}River Kingdoms{/g}!"
508f00c6-b7a6-4360-966a-72fd67feedaf: "First of all, we can send forth our outstanding violin player who wishes to tour the {g|River Kingdoms}River Kingdoms{/g}. Second, there is the provincial teacher collecting the legends, beliefs and traditions of your subjects. As a third option, we can order a series of etchings depicting your army's feats and campaigns."
a181cc16-9ce0-4a2a-bd15-9360aa02f88f: "Considering our position, I believe that supporting the artist and her workshop would be most useful. You might print many copies of these etchings, and thus elevate the prestige of military service! Besides, she herself wishes to paint your 'glorious army' and 'remarkable warriors' as faithfully as possible. She said she would not fall victim to the provocations of whiners and cowards."
8837220f-2707-4ca3-8c96-80f31ca2e884: "As to the series of etchings... I may be blind, but even I can see this artist's true, self-serving motives. And I can't say I agree with her desire to glorify the army and the officers' life. Art must reflect life, not distort the truth."
5ec890e3-7bec-4708-ba20-379983d04bab: "The legend-gatherer's work seems the most useful, and not only for our descendants. Your subjects, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, will be proud for their culture. Thus they might dedicate more time and money to its development..."
1b6f4964-9dcb-4e9e-a354-9182142fb848: "The provincial teacher is very naive and sweet, but his innocence only deepens his vision. You should hear him speak of the folk culture of the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g}! Your subjects will be very proud of their origin and culture after they've read his book."
adc49019-7d2c-479a-bece-4c1a07468092: "The artist seemed an awful back-scratcher to me. I'm sure she only came up with the military theme to get herself a big order. I hate flatterers and apple-polishers. Especially when it comes to art!"
c8469c27-181b-4248-b1b1-2a50908fb377: "I'll tell the violin player that we'll help him! Oh, he'll be so happy!"
c1b09c45-f9a4-4ddc-b5fb-c1d694b5a3e9: "Then I'll inform the teacher he can count on our support."
eb8007e6-995a-4fbf-97ef-c2187a15014c: "I'll order the series of etchings... and see that it's done to our specifications."

39ab7ae3-4b8b-4478-b233-3a1a8a73d210: "Yes! Not to offend the other gods, but she's the most important of them all. All the other gods guard the world as it is. But only the {g|Shelyn}Eternal Rose{/g}, the goddess of beauty, calls us to the world as it should be!"
f8a9282b-6df9-4a3d-9ea6-aa6e5a8ec3c3: "Just a moment, I just got something..." {n}Linzi quickly scribbles something in her notebook, then raises her eyes and smiles at you.{/n} "Hi!"
902c4bca-5aec-4f5c-942b-ac7163109270: "Hmm... I haven't seen him since I ran away from home. I hope he's all right! I ask {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g} every day to grant him a long life – and new students!"
dbffc022-7d81-422a-b2b0-af644c5b7f60: "You're the ruler of {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g} now! I don't know what else I can tell you... But I will try!"
a876eb2a-bc8c-4678-bccc-962e6590b16f: "I wonder how {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g} will fare now, under your rule!"
9b8d58da-2138-4780-8fb2-ecea4cd932b6: "Many sighed in relief when Irovetti lost his throne. But maybe they shouldn't have – who knows what you have in store for them! Either way, the years of his rule will not be soon forgotten. It won't be called {g|Pitax}Pitax's{/g} golden age... But perhaps its 'gilded age' is closer to the mark...
4b35d18a-81aa-4f4d-a497-0e25872e149a: "At first Tessie tried in vain to get rid of me. But later, when I told her I was staying behind in {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g}, she even shed a tear. I wonder where she is now... I wish she would visit us, and see how beautifully you fixed things up here! We used to avoid the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g}, but now she could come and set up her stand, and the customers would come flooding through!"
c17b2c97-5296-41e0-9902-5719f3d34f59: "Of course it's a book about you, but it's my book! Understood?" {n}The small writer's eyes glow rebelliously.{/n}
96aa9ae5-4504-43b0-8631-50ffdd47a4b9: "I know!"{n} Linzi says defiantly.{/n} "Rulers oppress writers. Sometimes even torture them, with a bit of execution thrown in for good measure... And so they etch their own names in history – as disgraceful tyrants. All while immortalizing their victims as heroes!"
ee82b413-e21e-4544-9e00-be8d66cf8438: "And I would prefer to turn every army barracks into a library, and eat cream pudding for breakfast every day. But you can't always get what you want. That's true even for rulers!"
8ddc8bc7-564f-4374-91d8-b00bfb55df87: "Ha ha ha! No, I am not going to make up any fiction about you! And why would I? I wouldn't be able to invent half of the adventures you keep getting yourself into!"
5c3eb32e-e940-4dfa-a6fe-c1dca42e0ad6: "I think you underestimate the power of the written word! A quill may not be mightier than a sword, but one strike by even the sharpest sword is still just one strike. The written word may be read by thousands and thousands, for countless years to come!"
05179e6c-5c99-427a-9ac2-bca2d06c9119: "Ha ha ha! How wonderful! Seriously, do it! Ban my book from your lands! Can you imagine how much the sales would grow everywhere else? As {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g} is my witness, if there's a higher honor for a writer than to author a popular book – it's to author a forbidden book!"
a62a43cc-de4d-4f98-8377-af490a150ccd: "Thank you for your trust. I will not set out to please you, of course, but I still hope that you'll like my book as much as my other readers!"
5c8acfe9-139f-42dd-ab65-8303096f853e: "I swear." {n}Linzi puts her little hand over her heart.{/n} "Truth, only truth, and just a teensy bit of imaginative exaggeration!"
c7b81f4c-a815-4ed2-b494-40aa5f4f2675: "Well... Yes, I can admit that. Sometimes one has to bend a few details for the sake of dramatic effect. It's called poetic truth! I write about everything as if I saw it with my own eyes – even parts of the adventure that I wasn't around for. But I do always carefully question everyone who was with you at the time! Think of it as of a general picture. In the end, you're the hero{mf||ine} of this book, and I am just the storyteller."
378013f6-6a9f-42b4-8d27-72b963a4e3d4: "I wasn't even with you during your first feats! But who wants to read about how I roamed the swamps with that miserable Tartuccio, while you were defeating the Stag Lord? No one, of course! So I wrote about you. I'll sit down and write my own biography some other time. When I'm very old, ha ha ha!"
53d1ec2a-e1a4-4882-8c8c-340eca78abf3: "At first Tessie tried in vain to get rid of me. But later, when I told her I was staying in {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g}, she even shed a tear... I wonder where she is now!"
934d111a-006a-4ebd-9663-9cea9723ab04: "At first, she'd have been glad to be rid of me. But in the end, when I told her I was staying in {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g}, she even shed a tear... Oh, I'm so happy she's staying with us! But she's so restless. Once she gets tired of this place — she'll be gone!"
6a53c005-6940-49d7-a090-92f3ec702b07: "This is what the {g|Academy of Grand Arts}academy{/g} was like under Irovetti... Of course, everything's different now in {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g}. But neither students, nor teachers, nor citizens will ever forget what happened."
a7eb9928-eea1-48cd-8ddd-b4704b8d9428: "Yeah, right! A classroom feels too small for me now. Maybe I'll return — to give a lecture or two, ha ha!"
074f9acf-8f9d-4cfa-97b8-6593280ae022: {n}Linzi shakes her head slowly.{/n} "No. I don't want to go back. Not to the {g|Academy of Grand Arts}academy{/g}, or to {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g}. I don't want to ever see the place again. I just... don't want to."
326d3447-d356-4ba6-b0da-b3072e2e05de: "In full swing! The press is working day and night. Turns out there aren't just readers, but also writers in our lands — they keep bringing me new manuscripts! Some are even readable without crying!"
647e8500-b5ca-4de6-aee9-a25b0046864c: "We're writing constantly. You know, when I was studying, I of course suspected that it wasn't all fine and dandy at the {g|Academy of Grand Arts}academy{/g}, but I had no idea of the scale of the catastrophe. Professor Eobald told me things about Irovetti... Horrible. You'll read it when we finish it!"
84b1ff93-4f39-49e3-8e75-5ed9088bd3b0: "Yes. 'The quill is mightier than the sword' — unfortunately I only learned the truth of this saying after getting blood on my own hands. I'm scared of the power words can have over people. But I can't be a coward! Since I possess this power, I must use it to change the world for the better! You change the world with the power of weapons and royal decrees. And I... I'll see to it that your legacy is more than just another dusty chronicle for future generations!"
4e687268-1d39-49d6-b8ed-61f10ccd06e6: "Honestly, it wasn't easy to forgive Eobald for lying. But the more we work together, the more I understand why he hid the truth from me. What's really happening at the {g|Academy of Grand Arts}academy{/g}... If it comes out, the only thing left will be to burn it to the ground. And we hope that someday it might become what it must have been at the very beginning!"
ea0e600b-ef78-4a1c-9cd1-cef0f30afbf5: "I thought teacher used to tell me about scary things. Now that I know what he DIDN'T tell me, it makes my hair stand on end. I'm afraid our book will destroy the {g|Academy of Grand Arts}academy{/g}. But if that's the case... maybe it can't be saved!"
0b892aa6-713f-43c9-a4e7-e7db3fdd0e76: "What's there to say... The books woke my urge to travel, but it was only thanks to Tessie that I managed to really get out of my village."
d88756dd-d4b4-486e-818e-4084d6a88f58: "Yes. You know, before I used to think I was some kind of preacher of good and beauty. I thought the delicate intricacy of words could make the world better... But who am I to change other people? They're not chicks, and I'm not their mother hen, there to cuddle them with warm, comfy lies! I'm a bard. My job is to honestly tell the stories that must be told. Like yours. To preserve them, to save them from being lost to time. And people — they'll make their own conclusions. They're clever enough on their own."
16dd86f0-fb0a-494f-a6e9-8f9a9ceaae01: "So much for the calling... We're jesters. Our job is to entertain the audience! When a bard tries to act as a preacher or open people's eyes to truth, it ends in stupidity, or tragedy, or both!"
7e27ad53-e8ca-44c1-847e-c2226215bd8e: {n}Linzi lingers, then sighs dully.{/n} "I had a fight with her. A big one. Well... I wanted to talk to her about the best way to describe her hair color in the book. And she..."
c33d08e5-9ad5-41ba-b2a3-24e2167aebd3: {n}Linzi pouts.{/n} "She said my book is trash. And I'd be no better if I busied my time with... ugh, I won't even repeat it!"
37c77e78-a8ae-42d8-9cca-c995c4ca4f9c: "Yes! I mean wait..." {n}Linzi licks her lips.{/n} "I wasn't hurt... it's just... oh, it doesn't matter!"
ed84945f-ab11-475c-830a-65c1eadf31fb: {n}Linzi lowers her head sorrowfully.{/n} "You're probably right... But I'm doing it for her! You know?"
8ed19518-364b-474b-a5d6-6b472c865bb4: "That's how everyone is! While the author is working on the chronicle, everyone is happy to heap insults on them. But then, when your names are glorified through ages, who do you think you'll be thanking?!"
415bcd63-15f2-4e89-ae8d-357b8472e410: "To be honest, Valerie hasn't been herself lately. She's usually polite, though she can be cold at times – but now it's like she's changed! And it's all after, you know..." {n}Linzi gathers her strength.{/n} "After she got that scar."
27a43693-4e07-4103-957b-83ce4f815d77: "I talked to her before, and she wasn't very nice that time either... She's gotten so spiteful after she got hurt! Though she keeps saying she doesn't care."
81c835e3-03f6-4d3f-b27e-0c85b54f6ee8: "Oh! You haven't heard of them? How can you be a hero{mf||ine} without knowing one of the most epic stories in the history of stories? They... No, I won't spoil anything — you should just read about them yourself, every single chapter! Their adventures are what gave me the idea of going on a heroic quest and writing about it to begin with... And now, look at me, here I am! On a heroic quest!"
1079344d-aca3-44df-b74d-b65d191bd66c: "You worship her too, right? I'm so happy to hear that! For some reason, I think that a leader following her call has the chance to create something beautiful in their lands... Even with such lackluster material as the Stolen Lands!"
92a0f1f9-e581-4d17-af55-c8ea64e7d486: "Ah, this." {n}Linzi holds her arm for you to get a clear view of the ring.{/n} "It was a gift to me from my first teacher. It's magical — imbued by the powers of Shelyn, no less! When I get myself in trouble, it transports me to a safe spot."
a81dbb94-eeb5-4b2e-9d99-2cf6d86736ac: "Sooo... Please, don't be angry with me if I suddenly disappear from a fight. I'll wait for you here! Promise!"
adf21f24-0a42-4ec6-95a9-d5ca7b56e9bb: "Regongar, why do you get so tense when I come close? Are you afraid I'll bite you?"
f217685f-41b4-4245-b4db-253ce4bdb7b3: "I'm afraid you'll stick your nose in my business and try to teach me how to live. And I can't kill you yet... Even though sometimes I really, really want to!"
9d2dadb7-65b2-47d2-abb4-4769c552804b: "You know, I'm a {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}! It's not polite to kick me out when we're in my dominions!"
b5e6d1e0-550d-4358-bc73-46a06fd29efb: "Watch your tongue. I don't remember giving you permission to take that tone with me."
37a7b345-e392-438f-aa92-adbf7aac9c69: "That was a fine way to wake up – for both of us! Well, so long!"
11ea449e-529e-4f14-8d55-7fbd5e7a802e: "You almost fell on me? Hmm, now that's something I wouldn't mind…"
fa3dbcf7-b3d2-4dc0-ba03-79b933554981: {n}Still half-asleep, you slip on your gear and suddenly hear the angry snap of a tail against the bed post. Looking up, you lock eyes with Kalikke, glowering and embarrassed.{/n}
14830556-7a7d-4fa8-9fa7-1045ce931b0c: "{name}! You and Kanerah... I mean... we suddenly switched, and I... could you please get dressed faster?!"
4a537f74-0952-4a76-85f9-c87a57ea8579: {n}Kalikke turns pale, then nods.{/n} "As you wish. I'm sorry. And now let me freshen up and clean up the house…"
e4009aef-7a9a-4162-a552-1f33881d9957: "If I throw water on you, would it be considered high treason?" {n}Kalikke covers her mouth and bursts out laughing.{/n} "We accidentally switched in our sleep! I almost fell on top of you when I came out of the portal! We've never had such a silly switch before…"
e2bb6c9a-5d5e-4866-969f-1abd10ae27bd: "Yeah, right. So you and my sister... ah, doesn't matter! Goodbye!"
f366c9d6-a31b-4ddb-ae6a-e3cf664014bd: "You know what, Kanerah is enough for you! Of course, my sister usually shares everything with me... Oh, what am I saying! That's it, goodbye, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}!"
e3ead47f-24b2-4e80-a292-946a61841537: "Why are you so concerned about death? There are so many interesting things in life! I don't understand how one can die without trying Absalom's famous blueberry cakes!"
767dc5b2-fbf2-4816-a14a-f49eda8a23ce: "Blueberry cakes as the meaning of life? Hmm... There is something in this. I suppose even the end of times would be more fun with a blueberry cake in your hand."
82abf95e-ef80-40cf-9fe5-2a91159b1b4d: "I killed you. Why are you here again?"
191ab0b5-1c40-499f-b507-bf706bf5b4df: "I saw Linzi talking to Nyrissa here, in the yard. What was it? A vision or an illusion?"
7b92ee96-7bb8-4490-93e7-102b13bc0429: [Attack] "I think I've made it clear that I don't want to have anything to do with you!"
620922a1-8b8e-4d9f-8f44-51f0059e82da: "Once I visited Nyrissa's dominion — in a dream. As soon as I got here, a great radiance appeared..."
8d27f7b1-8926-4838-a070-047c2b5c45de: "Fine, I'll play along. How can you help me?"
1ccd0640-5394-4c50-b674-fcf4eeadc30f: "Evindra, a reflection in the mirror talked to me in the House. It's a human, a wizard, and he had the same lantern you gave me. Do you know anything about him?"
f5d778f0-4a00-43df-b050-3850f6029c19: "The Knurly Witch offered me a deal — her key to Nyrissa's Shrine in return for the Wriggling Man's life."
7952a424-956a-4f56-acc0-d306423823e3: "The Wriggling Man offered me his key from the Shrine in return for the Knurly Witch's life."
47aa1120-0476-4414-a912-270f83c5028d: "My head is spinning from all your fey dealings. Can you explain again what's going on and what it all means?"
4e1b0066-d887-467f-a1c6-d7cfcc566307: {n}The nereid seems to be paler than usual, but her blue eyes glow with resolution.{/n} "{d|c51 Evindra Capital}I{/d} was so afraid you might not get here, but you made it! Although getting here is just a small part of what must be done to survive and win..."
00f954b0-2365-453c-8d53-f4a5c932740e: {n}Evindra the nereid, who you killed at the {g|Whiterose Abbey}Whiterose Abbey{/g}, icily stares at you with her huge blue eyes.{/n} "So this is it. You are my {d|c51 Evindra Killed}murderer{/d} and my final chance as well. I suspected that you would get here sooner or later. It seems I have no other choice but to help you."
05815d60-09ff-4f00-9da4-c29a386e03d3: "You're back! Do you need a hint or any help?"
64eea8ed-4268-4036-a94a-a0b39d362263: "I see that you... have changed. It's strange, but I feel the ghost of something very familiar — of the former Nyrissa. Nymphs can bestow special powers on those who they care about, but Nyrissa seemed to have lost this ability together with the love that was torn from her heart. And yet... how did you do it? It's her gift, and it ties you to {g|First World}the First World{/g}. It's a thin thread, and a feeble one, but it must allow you to be reborn here, as we are."
0b441328-7e62-40cc-b17d-f5004395fb1f: "Before you continue, remember two things. First — the House is full of phantoms, living memories of what has happened. You can see them but you cannot change the past. Second — the House lives not only in multiple times, but in two... states. I call them 'reality' and 'irreality', although each is real in its way, dangerous in its way, and each has its own secrets. One is {g|First World}the First World{/g} as it is. The other — the world of Nyrissa's thoughts and dreams."
cfa544b0-510a-4884-ab72-ed9b71482377: "The sorcerous mist you see here exists in both reality and irreality. It was created by Nyrissa to guard her dominion from invasion. It will hurl you between reality and irreality, and all about, preventing you from reaching the heart of the House and other secret nooks. But I've brought something that will help you. Take this lantern. Light it and hold it high, and the mist will have no power over you. But if you need to step from reality to irreality or back, then hide the lantern and let the mist carry you."
d817a8ae-a9aa-4020-b04e-c02192ce5571: "You are holding Briar... it's an artifact of great power. Use it wisely!"
80855231-c087-49f5-8662-d523309d07ec: "And last piece of advice. An artifact of great power and sorrow, Briar, is hidden somewhere in the House. Find it, and use it wisely!"
1244ccca-18ba-4bb1-924c-b8ef3d302b60: "I knew we'd meet {d|c51 Evindra Exiled}again{/d}." {n}Evindra the nereid, who you last saw at the {g|Whiterose Abbey}Whiterose Abbey{/g}, is staring at you.{/n} "Nyrissa has become more and more restless and reckless lately. It was easy to guess that someone was interfering with her plans — and even easier guess who it might be. You are in grave danger, {mf|king|queen}."
4a3b298d-67c8-41ef-afb7-1d6b258b8336: "It is called the House at the Edge of Time. It's Nyrissa's place of power, her citadel in {g|First World}the First World{/g}. It is frozen in time... and scattered throughout time. There are rooms of eternal 'tomorrow' and rooms where something that happened long ago still lingers. If a random guest took a bite from an apple and left it here a thousand years ago — it would remain unaltered to this day. I know it's difficult to understand for a mortal. Even among us, the children of the First World, only {g|Shyka}Shyka{/g}, the {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g} of Time, can fully comprehend these mysteries."
f84949b4-2b20-4c74-9dd3-8dd035455659: "Everywhere and nowhere. This is her dominion. Here she may hide in any shadow — and turn any shadow into a weapon. Nyrissa does not prefer open confrontation... she will try to defeat you through her servants, and she won't appear until the end. I suppose, though, that there is one place that is especially important to her. It's a room in the heart of the House, on the second floor — the Shrine where her cup, the Apology, is kept. If you reach this place, Nyrissa will appear. She would have no choice."
ab92d19d-4d89-471c-a95c-e85395854611: "A memory. The house showed you what happened here in the recent past."
8b9c5e70-fda7-4af7-86a0-0594d0790f80: "There is a well here — magical, just like everything here. It will allow you to get inside the House. Get used to it — here in {g|First World}the First World{/g}, things can have very unexpected uses. Be careful! Nyrissa will know your every step inside, and she will do her best not to let you leave. You — your kingdom — is the last grain of dust for the Apology. There is no way back for her, or for you."
d729955d-066c-4837-a130-854c70b669d4:
"You are in {g|First World}the First World{/g}, and I am its child. Here in our homeland, we don't die forever, but return to life again. The {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g} have always been especially close to the First World, and since they were overwhelmed by the Bloom, the laws of life and death that govern the fey began to work there as well.
You can try to kill me if you wish. But far better that you listen. You require help, and I need someone who can stop Nyrissa."
fcbfc963-9a54-42a7-95a1-9b28cfe4cd1f: "You've been to {g|Whiterose Abbey}Whiterose Abbey{/g}. You've seen what Nyrissa did to me. I know what a monster she's turned into, and can't help wishing with all my heart that I could stop her. It might sound strange, but I'm ready to kill her. I love her too much to see her like this."
651c9788-318c-4122-a37e-09c90cb9866c: "I'll tell you everything that I know. You must have questions..."
cdf8b027-ea92-4d9f-aa35-3a3fc2ed96d3: {n}Evindra shakes her head sadly.{/n} "No. But this House has been the death of many upon many. As for the lantern... I took it once from the body of an unfortunate traveler, who accidentally stumbled into {g|First World}the First World{/g} and died here. But I know well who gives such gifts. It's the {g|LanternKing}Lantern King{/g} — one of the {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g}, the one whose lips once cursed Nyrissa. It's better if you never meet him."
75acf800-b4fe-4895-9f38-2e5a1bea4da3: "Do what you feel is right, but I would be three times as careful with either of those two. They are Nyrissa's most loyal servants, who she took to her bosom after she stopped trusting us, her friends and sisters. Their souls are full of evil, just like her soul is now."
5b6e1faa-1666-4255-9ea1-c48e8dd6ee1b:
"Of course. Ages ago, the {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g} named the {g|LanternKing}Lantern King{/g} cursed Nyrissa and her closest nymph friends. He stripped them of their immortality and turned their souls to evil. Only I managed to avoid the curse, against all odds.
Part of Nyrissa's soul, the part that was filled with her good and light, was taken out and turned into an artifact called Briar. The Eldest hid it in the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g}. Nyrissa's servants tried to find it, but to no avail — only the gnome Tartuccio managed to do it, but you must know more about that than I do."
ada05046-1f88-4085-91bb-e4e51067e759: "The curse required that Nyrissa destroy a thousand kingdoms. Each time a kingdom was ruined, a grain of dust fell into a magic cup called the Apology. Now there are nine hundred and ninety nine of them — The number of kingdoms fallen to ruin in the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g}. Your kingdom must be the thousandth. If it falls, Nyrissa will be able to go to the {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g} and ask for forgiveness for her transgression. Please do not let this happen. The Eldest are cruel gods in my world, and they must not triumph."
aa11cf68-b6df-46bc-bfc3-cf4d01f929b5: "You are so kind, so naive... But there are many evil people in the world. Will your goddess be able to protect you from them?"
1c967571-a036-4fdf-91d3-0f075f578ef5: "I pray for her to grant me patience, not protection. One day all this will end, and then you will be the one in need of protection."
4de424ad-0138-4f86-87f5-721df4ebcdd3: "Your tone gets on everyone's nerves. Isn't it difficult to keep your acid-tongued remarks to yourself?"
97084fa7-98e7-47b3-997b-53d84b45a444: "It's called honesty. When I don't like something, I'm not ashamed of saying it. It's much better than spreading fake smiles and pretending everything's fine, while secretly harboring nasty thoughts."
4f1316d8-450e-41b7-982e-b9642eb9d8bc: "You are just wasting paper. Who would believe a word from someone like you?"
052f9d29-7f4f-42ba-a5d1-e20a22b904b9: "Someone will! They'd probably put more faith in an army of immortal elven chroniclers, but I don't see any here. So I'll just have to suffer for all of them!"
5386637f-336d-4d18-826c-38940a49b78a: "By the way, Jubie, pray tell me..."
e5c511ce-6e19-4238-ab61-70393cd2cb63: "No, YOU tell me: who gave you the right to address me in such a disrespectful manner?! I certainly don't recall ever letting anyone call me that. So please, do refrain from such vulgar familiarity in the future."
956d62cd-999d-4411-bcf0-b5a46630f939: "You look unhappy today. You need to have some fun. You want me to read to you in bed, the way you like?"
a321012b-1627-41b1-aea6-28538f5bdd93: "OCTAVIA! Damn it, not with everyone around... Hmm, never mind. We'll talk about this later."
26a7242f-a830-498f-94a0-4520884c0770: "Deal. But break your promise and I'll make you regret it, even if I have to claw my way out of the Abyss to do so."
fe51d2c6-200d-46c1-a464-e99f73837f88: "Stop! Listen, we can make a deal. You've probably heard things about me, but I'm a reasonable man, not some insane murderer. If you let me go, I'll leave these lands. In exchange for my life, I'll point you toward a cache holding my share of the loot. Dovan of Nisroch always keeps his word!"

0d9d5cce-1591-4aa4-b8b7-991af68a885e: "However, your people won't get off so easily. {n}With a heave, you lean into the crowbar with all your might, and there is the scraping of stone as the lid shifts slightly and a waft of foul air emerges from within... corpse rot.
Taking a breath, you are about to continue forcing the lid off when suddenly the sarcophagus shifts from within — and a heartbeat later, a huge rotting hand curls around the edge of the lid and begins to force the sarcophagus open the rest of the way!{/n}
83a853b1-1345-4284-9cac-fd33b8059d82: {n}You have no idea where the sarcophagus came from, but you know enough about enchantments to know there must be an easy way to open it. Experimenting with the engravings in various combinations, you discover when you press your finger against the skull symbol with your hand on the lid, the cover slides aside easily. Your triumph is short-lived, however — as the lid slides open, there is the sound of something... something huge... stirring within the sarcophagus. You hear a rattling whistle like air pushed through a leaky bellows and scraps of flesh fly from the sarcophagus... whatever's inside is huge, angry, and far from dead.{/n}
bc97cd0c-1ddb-446f-9c4a-143cc37ce37e: {n}You struggle with the crowbar, but after several tries, it's useless — the lid doesn't budge.{/n}
33aa8312-09f4-42c5-9008-e6ed2d8479e5: {n}After many desperate tries, a broken hammer, and a sore back and shoulders, you manage to crack the lid of the sarcophagus... a horrid smell wafts forth — corpse rot. A heartbeat later, a huge rotting hand curls around the crack you've made, and locks around the edge... this is quickly followed by the scraping of stone as the hand begins to force the lid open the rest of the way!{/n}
a6703328-0962-4444-a4c4-72c168db558d: {n}There doesn't seem to be anything remarkable about the sarcophagus — nor does there seem to be an easy way to open it.{/n}
6f601b79-f41a-48fe-9260-ae28c7a49d1c: {n}Magic presence here is obvious. You can sense powerful necromancy energies, but can't figure out the specific spells in use here.{/n}

4cdda6b0-eeef-4942-acc2-b0e3e97b51e9: "I feel so dreary! I want to punch someone so hard!"

9a728458-8087-4b1f-b0cf-33501bde0a43: We hurried to explore the bookshelves.
4705f59b-e110-4c19-82c9-f4f0369b87cf: The dusty table by the far wall didn't escape our notice.
f1e00245-f7ae-423c-a7a6-5a43dd507a39: It was impossible to ignore the piles of papers, scrolls, and files on top of the bookcases.
ea662fba-a5d7-46bc-b388-9157be5b8473: Having decided not to bother the ghosts of the past any more, we left the ancient tomes alone and returned to the library.
554d1e57-d89f-447c-b327-28c23d13dc89: Behind the mysterious door (that opened with a loud and creepy groan) there was a dark room, far less spacious than the main hall. a520ada3-a620-4445-8028-c81853667fb7: Whoever was that ominous medusa who encountered us in the library, neither she nor any other ruin-dwellers ever had gotten to this corner. We got an opportunity to be the first people in many years to peruse these bookcases!
3d877343-e418-4145-a4fb-1af280e807fb: The silence within the secret room was thick, almost ominous — no, in fact it was really ominous! Now did our heroes dare to disturb the peace of this dusty archive?
8d8f387c-32b6-4eb9-a417-9adf8607bd48: Seems like the ancient dwellers of this fortress tried to get rid of book-moths using the same chemicals people use today for torturing — and as soon as the acrid dust touched the skin, it burnt like acid! 6f54ec06-3ef5-454d-a161-7de057abdc10: Ignoring the dust, we continued to explore the shelves. True heroes cannot be stopped by a little dirt and grime, or even residue five times older than us!
ea3d5864-ca5a-4b25-886f-1b650e1e3d08: The search ended with unexpected success — among the rotting books and old scrolls we found a heavy tome in good condition. 28de281e-66d0-4015-bafa-3ab98cbb3e3c: As soon as we reached for the book on the top shelf, the pile of papers, disturbed by awkward hand, started to shift, then slid, faster and faster! All we could do was try to avoid the paper avalanche from the heights of the bookcase!

01a0084c-847b-49bd-9430-224bf0b5ebc0: Even if there was something of value on the top shelf, it was not our destiny to discover it — after falling from their 'pedestal', the fragile tomes, scrolls, and notes had collapsed to dust.
cc9d5838-16ad-4970-8efe-ce7cb03e029b: Among the rotting books, we found several spell scrolls in good condition. I wonder: who could hide magic scrolls in this gloomy fortress? Alas, some mysteries defy being solved!
3aca88ec-7e1d-4ea9-bd25-926c74f335fa: After we were done with the makeshift 'storage', we went back to exploring the secret room.

bb390f5e-6732-48ec-ac87-bacecb73b293: "Oh-h-h! Your Highness! Happy, happy to see you! What brings you to your loyal city — to your loyal governor?"

582a9970-227e-4d23-81f1-24a6b560a8ef: "Moving along, Your Highness, moving along... Trade is thriving! The old families keep wriggling, though. Still trying to claw back pieces of their former wealth... But let them claw all they like. This city is ours now!"

ac2fc60f-3819-417b-b128-3c5085a87656: "Get out! We have nothing to discuss!"

f674c553-2933-4f22-99cb-ffea0af97d3c: "Not today!" {n}The gnome dives somewhere under your feet and vanishes.{/n}
f5d4f1fc-a5d4-48b3-8398-9e1a77944e1e: "So what? What do I care about these singers?"

0cb1e8af-4a31-448c-b3db-5964db103e13: "What? What are you saying? Ilora? How could she, how could she... Did he hire her cutthroats? Hers — and not mine? Why? Why, why, why..."
502d7808-3a94-40b0-829b-4e79e1a2fa70: "Ha ha — sounds like a fine idea! So what of it?"

f7e0a431-a046-4540-a426-b58b87b1e6a2: "We haven't and we shouldn't! I'm a plain honest trader! What do you want from me?"
4d6cd7a5-aee9-443e-a43c-e0dec571d4cc: {n}The gnome's dim, reddish eyes are anxiously scanning the faces of passers-by. Noticing you, he draws his dagger.{/n} "You?! I don't know you! Don't come any closer. I have no business with you! Get away or I'll cut you!"

173150cb-8a2d-4916-8338-a37c34dd4ffa: {n}The gnome's red eyes roll about wildly, and he anxiously cracks his fingers.{/n} "A deal, huh? Sounds like a good deal, yes, good deal! You have my support. Don't you betray me, though, you hear?!"

8e2dea3d-8d9b-4276-aaa2-b157956712ee: "I learned what happened to your child, Ekun, a shame. Now if you kept her locked in a cage-"
cdbd37a4-0d9d-4bc2-86d5-4e1a0be81964: "One more word and it'll be your last."

34711514-30f9-48dc-ad9a-9f774b7492a1: {n}Linzi's eyes glitter and her nostrils flare with rage, but for some reason she speaks in a whisper.{/n} "Such... such insolence! Such unforgettable, monstrous, unimaginable insolence!"

53a749b7-2605-4f79-a9b3-fc426835d028: "Betrayal! Blasphemy! All who remain loyal to the great Armag — to battle!"

a4c7e212-5968-4be6-a8a2-0111f78925f0: "One of our Sisters is slain, and the other is {d|c31 Good Sister}missing{/d} — probably never to be seen again. And the killer stands right before you!" {n}The women raise their hands in perfect unison and point their fingers at you.{/n}

0d0278a3-cde6-4b51-94d0-84ced46f0ed6: "It's about time. The barony's status didn't reflect our true power, and only restrained our growth. In so many regards we already surpass both the foolish Aldori and the spineless Surtova."

dff9157d-03ad-457c-a7a4-883e04375add: "A monarch's crown is a worthy reward for your feats. But remember: history speaks of many for whom the crown was simply too heavy!"

04782253-9bcc-4d78-9fb7-a914d67d14c7: {n}Regongar strikes Kalannah across the face.{/n} "Get out of my sight, you filth! Thank the gods that my friends are so soft!"

1b58cbcb-b72c-41a9-9b85-78fe1175bedd: "I repent! I swear, I repent! As soon as I get back to {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g}, I'll give a fat donation to every good deity's temple. {g|Sarenrae}Sarenrae{/g}, {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g}, {g|Iomedae}Iomedae{/g} — whatever you want, just let me go!"
1c7f5b4c-6c91-4643-9bc5-c7531b1cd722: "Hey! Amiri! Teach me how to slash like you do! Hero will find use for that!"
51a1bb37-8b86-494b-b722-90fe51572056: "Oh boy… You are bold like a Kellid but too weak to fight like us."

e92c7018-3a84-4288-b5d1-b48d09872bc8: "You're strange, Harrim. Dwarves are usually fun. They like the bottle, they like to play and shout. But you just mumble all the time."

c05399cd-387a-4990-94ff-26f27ca399cb: "Why do you still remain in this world?"
f72e77c0-ba13-48cf-9560-881d16815f74: [Attack] "You attacked me first — now you'll pay!"
961c0ab8-d3d9-4c2d-8d98-6ccb5c6b5f46: "You've suffered enough and paid the price for your mistakes. If before you can travel the River of Souls you need forgiveness — I forgive you. Go in peace."
f88147bd-0d63-48bb-8670-df71d37ce0a7: "I'm sorry. I'll make Vordakai regret what he did to you."
74c053ff-5e54-4177-9e3d-ff6daaf5f4dc: "You deserved your punishment. You caused the suffering of countless innocents — this is the price you must pay."
dd2c3520-af86-4c3f-9103-1b7f9991748f: "Have you seen Vordakai? Tell me about him."
9694eba3-9abf-4796-b8f9-c918a46df0dc: "Wait! Mercy!" {n}The ghost's voice is faint, as if speaking from far away.{/n}
38dbddda-7c12-458b-b7dc-fd56e25259ea: {n}The figure before you looks... vague, indistinct, as if it could dissipate into the air at any moment.{/n} "Ba... {mf|baron|baroness}? Is that you?"

eeb9b1ce-5fc5-4a73-b5a4-94f1d7fb1980: "It's not my fault! It was a mistake! A huge, foolish mistake!"
312fa8e8-3521-4cc7-82b8-2f42244bcaf3: "I was wandering through the mountains. Searching for something... something that would prove my worth, make others sit up and take notice, a little respect. 4c6eb309-efc8-471f-a479-1dc0944a756e: "Then something... happened. 46c1ad49-0361-4b48-8774-0c5d4160323f: "I... just wanted to take a look! So… I know it was foolish, but I saw this bracelet... entirely of jade! An entire fortune, worn on the wrist! 69338193-5137-4dc2-a3c6-20379637f2e1: "After he was finished with me, he slit my throat with his finger… but I didn't die, he released my soul through the wound so that I might forever be amongst those who died as a result of my weakness. "The souls of {g|First World}First World{/g} creatures don't follow the same laws set by the gods for other living beings. If we die, we lose a significant part of our power, but we are born again with all of our memories, looking just the same as before.
But this only works for deaths on our home plane. That is why my kin avoids traveling abroad — they fear the forever-death that awaits them in other worlds."
d2817df5-c9ae-4e84-961b-dd08a48b81c8: "The {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g} have always had a strong connection to the {g|First World}First World{/g}, though this is not the sole reason. Somewhere in these lands, the {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g} hid Briar as part of their curse." {n}Evindra closes her eyes and, in a singsong voice, recites,{/n} "Let your unrequited love guide you — as it guided you to your first kingdom, so it shall again."
6c63d69a-4101-400f-8221-63453231fc2a: "Nyrissa was deprived of the very part of her essence that led to her bold plan in the first place. They took it from her, and for ages she has been seeking what she lost. It must be excruciating — to feel the call of what was once an inseparable part of you, and to be unable to find it."
c917edb0-04a0-414a-b607-7a69388471e7: "Who can say? In my limited understanding, the {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g} are cold, distant, alien beings. Nyrissa will bring them her filled cup, and then... I can't even imagine. But I doubt it will end happily. What they did to her, the fate they brought upon a thousand kingdoms... it all seems unimaginably cruel. Whatever they have in mind must be yet crueler, I'm sure of it."
fdcfb866-0e6f-4ff3-9bd4-ff75e888f2f8: "Of course. It is hardly a topic one would want to discuss for long..."
7999c932-cc1f-4b46-a5a8-43c8765459cd: "There is one thing... Find Briar, the artifact created from the stolen part of Nyrissa's soul. I know not what power it holds, but I am sure — if anything can alter the sinister story we have all become characters in, it is Briar."
35248cb2-372a-4c52-80e1-b52f5a4e720e: {n}Evindra frowns.{/n} "I can only speculate, but... perhaps you should begin your search by contacting Irovetti. He's spent a long time searching for Briar, at Nyrissa's command. As to how you might obtain any information from him... well, that is another question entirely. I wish you luck!"
d3b948cc-c0b3-4ea7-82f6-669f86dc6498: "You found it, did you not? Briar... I can feel its power. Like hearing an echo of her laughter — so pure, so familiar... This cannot be anything but a piece of Nyrissa's soul. Good. Very good. Keep it close, and do not lose it. When the decisive moment comes, it will help you!"
cba89e17-3a35-4105-ab71-a87689b91094: "The same thing she wanted from the successful aspirants who came before you — willingly or unwillingly. For centuries, she has sought out strong, ambitious, promising people within the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g}, helped them grow and build their own kingdoms — and then pitted them against one another. This is what happened with Armag, the proud barbarian chieftain. This is what happened to Irovetti, the cunning schemer. And this will happen to you as well, eventually."
72f39558-455d-487f-a486-61a7f06cd389: "Within the city, Elina the innkeeper takes care of me. In return, I help her purify and enchant water for her drinks. It is so nice to have a friend again!"
02b00b61-206a-40e3-b534-e1d59c2cd61a: "But the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g} are sewn to the {g|First World}First World{/g} with the threads of the Bloom. It affects everything — even the life cycle. Those who die within the Bloom or in places like {g|Candlemere}Candlemere{/g}, where the First World and {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g} are close as twins in a mother's womb, will return to our homeland and be resurrected there. This is why you can find so many fey creatures in your kingdom — curiosity drives them here."
3ebc210a-2f74-4a39-baba-b96fd70c0c0c: "There is... one more reason I've spoken about immortality. My poor sisters — the nymphs — shared the burden of the curse with Nyrissa. The curse tore them from the eternal cycle of life of the {g|First World}First World{/g}. Now they can really die, even in the First World — just like you and everyone else around them. I suppose the curse didn't impact me as heavily. Perhaps because I tried to dissuade Nyrissa from her plan at the outset, or perhaps because I tried to fight the evil that plan bestowed upon us."
859d6009-9aa7-41fd-9760-412f5b75eaf4: "Drinking and fighting... Amiri, don't you understand how empty and ridiculous all this is?"
9f0d06ff-9cc2-4750-8bb1-2e505271a762: "Your head is empty! And your face is ridiculous. In fact, you are ridiculous all around. A good fight and some booze – what else do you need to be happy?"
236ad340-587a-45d0-9390-05417b962a11: "I'm glad of a chance to relax a little, but… shouldn't we be busy hiding our tents? Or are we just going to leave it to luck?"
05c03454-a24c-4a52-a740-146e27c635b0: "I wonder — what if someone happens to walk past us tonight? Won't it be easy to find our camp, since we didn't bother to hide it?"
74dab38e-c135-4b72-905d-ed1ba3612160: "I could explain how we might best conceal our camp, if such is your wish. I learned much while commanding a squad."
79d996c4-b188-43a9-9a7f-57b61f1d4c35: "I advised that we hide the camp. Monsters can be a problem, as are evil-minded people."
c1fd6887-02b7-46e3-bcb8-66dea8e2cbcf: "Why hide from monsters anyway? If you don't kill one tonight, you'll be fighting it tomorrow along with its friends."
87a1edfd-03ce-404c-b69c-16266956309e: "I agree. I've no concern for sleep, but I require silence and repose no less than the rest of you."
d8a1a8a7-e148-4ebd-af32-ff1cc552fd48: "Fruit? Tuskwater oysters might be better, if you know what I mean."
2f136851-f988-4a3e-a4ef-d53c66b1d9d1: {n}Meeting you at the capital gate, Tristian puts his hand on your shoulder.{/n} "Before you are abducted by your advisors..." {n}The deva smiles.{/n} "Let's hide from them. Your chambers. Wine. Perhaps fruit. You and I."
e4cf5705-49a6-483e-b47b-82520a11ee28: {n}Tristan's expression of sincere bafflement, well-known to you, appears on his face.{/n} "Oysters? Of course, if you like them..."
f3273242-53fc-4dda-be6e-9dd6d0ca196d: {n}Laughing, Tristian holds you.{/n} "Ha, then an abduction is imminent! And I will be the abductor!"
ecd86b43-a683-480f-9722-58e7f81ebc34: {n}Mixing with the crowd, you race towards the palace.{/n}
75fda2a6-faa4-4155-8c32-12d83196c845: "You're not human and you never will be! You're nothing more than a disgusting parody."
1434dc15-40f1-41f9-802e-e5d00e3c09a9: [Attack] "A monster is always a monster. I'll free my lands from your kind!"
8dcb5e1f-f96c-4232-99b4-0f5ef8270a28: {n}At the ruined gates of {g|Trobold}Trobold{/g}, you see Jazon walking alone. Seeing you, he waves his hand.{/n} "Hello, borba. Why you come here?"
3fb87acb-4192-4f35-b0ac-f50cb0b2902e: {n}Jazon shakes his head.{/n} "Borba killed trolls, but it wasn't borba who started war. Hargulka wanted war, got what he wanted. {g|Trobold}Trobold{/g} fell because of its king."
95362e87-cb90-40bf-88e9-7d6dc6be5641: "Jazon lives here. {g|Trobold}Trobold{/g} is no more, but stone walls still stand. Plenty of space, plenty of food in woods. Plenty of time to think."
f4bc6ed4-bdbe-43dd-b495-911440966be8: "No. Jazon does as he decided. No attacking people in villages. Eats only forest borba — deer, boar, but not people. Jazon wash his fur, brush his fangs. {g|Trobold}Trobold{/g} is no more, but Jazon is still Jazon."
005f2b3e-bdaf-461a-97ec-40ee9955a055: "Me Jazon. Had another name before. Like other trolls, went hunting, ate borba. Then Tartuk came, talked to trolls. Explained how humans live. Only Jazon left."
07548e0b-c7ca-4412-b787-7ee764fed21b: {n}Jazon bares his teeth and roars. For a moment, it seems like he's about to charge you, but he instead pounds the nearest rock with his fist, sending rock shards flying.{/n} "Don't say so, borba! Jazon give everything to be Jazon! Jazon won't go back!"
dfbbea4d-4155-469f-9d21-c8cbc741fdda: "It's difficult to live without faith. I couldn't do it."
38a2152a-c054-425a-862e-f6c6bccc68ca: "Forgive me if my words seem rude, but... You only need faith because you've survived what you have. You need faith like a lame man needs his crutches. And I need it like a healthy man does."
f97e5fbe-7cb9-4798-9499-bfa2175bc528: "Jubilost. We are allies, not enemies. Why are you unkind to those who shed their blood with you?"
1d84378b-a71c-4ff9-9ca5-c73bfeec0aab: "I'm unkind? Ekun, my dear friend, I'm incredibly kind, tolerant, and placid towards our entire troupe, even to those who may not deserve it! Besides, what you call 'unkindness' I call 'honesty'.
a49a1662-aad4-48a4-a0ed-2965fa3953a1: "Sometimes the carelessness of this party is cause for great concern. No one even tried to hide the camp!"
a196369f-9ecc-4c1d-80c3-8be486570c39: "I once served the Swordlords. I must admit, their people would never leave their camps out in the open like this!"
192fa03b-ce1a-4e05-835f-7eb651469022: "You're right, it is unwise. But perhaps this is the will of Sarenrae, and the light of our fire shall lead some poor soul to salvation..."
f1c760ff-eba1-4110-bebf-841669871e0f: "Screw it! I laugh in danger's face. Let 'em come — I'll knock their teeth in!"
a91756e3-a85f-440d-88ce-e8a440b32b69: "Alright, I'll play scribe. We'll lodge your formal complaint properly, and pass it on to the {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}'s chancery. We do have a chancery in the {mf|barony|barony|kingdom|kingdom}, don't we?"
45e4761d-5e1c-4c42-8d92-6daa26363b55: "Ha. Give those war dogs free rein, and they'll give us military order every waking moment. You'll have us doing drills on the training ground!"
c7f3b676-f72b-436d-ad9f-286d0a633384: "Bravery and carelessness are two sides of the same coin. Maybe our leader thinks we can handle whatever comes our way!"
1a672044-72be-4b21-a946-486412852ad3: "Bravery and carelessness are two sides of the same coin. Maybe our leader thinks we can handle whatever comes our way!"
41a1c299-98dc-4155-a375-18efc9ce766d: "Jubilost is a renowned scholar and author. Talk to him."
15208538-8da5-4f1b-8e85-9d3295dc20de: "Linzi loves stories. You can talk to her."
d542362d-6a16-4a18-8a12-f100144177c1: "I'm sorry, but I have to go!"
13fa07d4-0857-48bc-9057-b703ba33361c: {n}A young woman catches your eye. She looks like she has come from far away. She approaches with a dancing gait and addresses you, speaking in an unfamiliar drawl.{/n} "May the Perfect Human protect you! I am happy to meet you, o worthy one."
52c9a12f-8146-4975-9c16-343015770d74: {n}Shaynih'a notices you and smiles broadly.{/n} "Destiny has brought us together once more, o worthy one! This is no mere coincidence! The Perfect Human is telling us that our paths are deeply intertwined, like snakes coiling around each other in an act of love!"
1e30fc1b-54c7-4a4b-8584-16dd4e4c8348: "Perhaps I chose wrongly when I decided to become a muse. Until I can answer this question, I shall remain true to the calling I've always pursued — weaponsmithing. a84bf025-90da-4d2f-baa0-2a62b7ca4637: "Ah! Let us see, then, how learned this man truly is! I hope this esteemed opium inhaler will enthrall me with the depth of his knowledge and the richness of his verse!"
ea1b0d92-115e-41b6-87c5-f1601040c41d: "I am grateful, o worthy one! I shall relate to you the story of my ancestor Vu Balak. Let us see if she is nimble enough to write it all down without omitting any of the colorful details!"
68956574-cd36-4e3e-91cd-27f52384743a: "You, o worthy one, can help me find my calling. I am beset by doubt — what if, by choosing the path of a master smith, I am making a terrible mistake? After all, I, Shaynih'a the Tulip, have seen many wonders, the likes of which your humble realm has never heard of. And I wish to recount them. But alas, I cannot write in your language! For this reason I require a writer, and a worthy one!"
68f697d8-988a-4948-8fe7-24eee9394fe0: "I am a traveler from the Impossible Kingdoms of Vudra! I was led here by the will of the gods, by my love of amazing adventures, and by the promise of inescapable retribution uttered by my former husband, who has since become a revered sage and a dead man. I never doubted that my path would bring me to a most worthy ruler, one who would help me. — And now you stand before me!"
a65fe941-e7ca-498e-843e-9c2a720bcff5: "Go, o worthy one! Our paths shall cross again, for that is the will of the gods!"
a200e5d0-b2e7-41d9-811f-382faef369ea: "My name is Shaynih'a, but you may simply call me the Tulip, as all the best of my friends do! Ever since the sun rose today, I've had a feeling that I shall take part in a grand encounter — one that shall change our fates forever! And, lo, it is so. Praised be the Perfect Human for this gift he has bestowed upon these eyes that see the future!"
acea4fd2-6e0a-4f06-8fb0-791cb70c1302: "I have witnessed master Chokhek cover emptiness in tattoos, and a human grew out of them, for these patterns were so intricate and deep that the ink became more important than the flesh. Trust me, for I have woven the tale of these events myself! Perhaps I have been destined to become the muse of a great writer! If, o worthy one, you find a suitable scribe for me, I shall pay you back handsomely with my wisdom and advice!"
08d7d790-f76f-4315-bb13-19a3dfb42e9b: "At a feast, Mahka once swallowed a whole tiger and the beast's rage and hunger burned in his veins – until, consumed by it, he ate himself. For Purusav was a reincarnation of Mahka, bent on restoring the empire to its true glory. Eventually, Purusav was defeated in battle and his empire died with him, but it was Mahka Abihcara who spawned the terrible race of rakshasa – cunning beasts, half human and half animal. Trust me, for I have met these creatures many times!"
17e39f90-ced8-4876-ba71-e15973764b84: "Mahka always dreamed of leaving a mark on the world. And he did, but not in the way he expected. It was not on the battlefield that his name became immortalized, but in bed, surrounded by concubines. Each may be mistaken in choosing their own path, even the wisest of all! Perhaps I am destined to be your advisor, o most worthy one? Or your lover? Go now, for I need to be alone to think upon my words."
0e8735f8-427a-4061-a6df-7fa3b178ba54: "I greet you, o most worthy opiumist! I have heard much of your wisdom. Now, lend me your ears, and I shall tell you a story that…"
ca803c5d-b408-4a50-b1e9-0f5a2d637c28: "I greet you, young Linzi! They say that you are writing a book. b5aff198-f7c8-4996-9568-9a9b7e1f34ea: "Just a moment! Why on earth do you call me an opiumist?! Who came up with that?!"
10794a16-d333-4485-a666-92f84aa5f2fc: "Ermm, isn't every learned man supposed to be an opiumist? Back in Vudra, I met many noble and illustrious scholars. I have noticed how empty your eyes are, and..."
3fa3c363-2e02-4e50-a456-5b41c7f82929: "Never have I inhaled anything, nor do I intend to. And I find it highly unlikely that a whole caste of intellectuals would willingly expose themselves to such substances in order to lose their minds!"
d1be9325-ff0e-47c0-96c9-38b3bfab2967: "It is as true as the fact that the fastest black genies can outrun light beams, thus evading the touch of the sun, which is fatal to them. Trust me, for I have seen this with my own eyes!"
464c380c-3f78-4548-8e78-723c1eaa309e: "It seems to me that you are spinning these wild tales on the go. I very much doubt they have anything to do with your actual travels. I have no interest in such things." {n}Jubilost turns his back in anger.{/n}
a5ac9a02-ce1b-4458-b0f3-046ddc643240: "Hold on, four years? Are you sure that he ate absolutely nothing? Maybe it was, well, you know, some sort of moderate fasting? More like a diet? Like when you do eat, but only a little bit…"
6e4ab7e4-78e8-4a22-bffe-767db051c9db: "No no no, why would you think that? Breaking his askesis would have been a shameful weakness! He did not eat at all. I..."
2b91fd27-3702-47de-ae6b-270c38ca1bca: "Wait a moment. Four years?! That's impossible! If I skip breakfast and dinner, my stomach hurts so badly I can't even walk! It's really hard to believe that the monk could spend a whole four years like…"
2d2131b9-3210-47d1-8074-a56fa5f3715c: "Young Linzi, by paying attention to such unimportant details, you run the risk of missing the heart of the matter! a01b93d6-6a8c-4639-87e0-2eb6cce61350: "Mmm…He swallowed enough stones to fill his stomach? And lived? And never had to eat again? 3826ab80-a9d2-436a-b1de-c357da78f565: "I thank you, o worthy one! It is such a shame that your path is the path of a ruler, and not that of a wordsmith!"
e8b53a97-c929-427e-8ed1-2e0fd699eefc: "Hm… Perhaps I'm not as good at telling stories as I thought. After all, putting the events of the past into words is not quite the same thing as witnessing them!"
3ef4535c-ef45-4835-8df4-99a3a33d16e4: "This truthful story was divined for me by a woman who had eyes on the palms of her hands. c04286e7-e4b7-46bc-908b-84bea7d9f1d0: "Your 'dream'? You are talking about Nyrissa, right?"
5324c9da-bdc7-41ca-b9ab-5ab00c06706d: "Nyrissa manipulated you. Accept it and rest in peace, shadow."
422f1c55-095d-424d-8691-fc5aaf34646c: [Attack] "You are a stranger in this world. I've killed you before, I'll kill you now!"
1e063dc3-552b-4273-9353-895cf2134d30: "You do realize you've been dead for a long time?"

83b7caa8-d0eb-44e1-bc1b-5ea4f5d7ca1a: "She chose you, right? My dream..." {n}You hear dull melancholy in the shadow's voice.{/n}
c5cfe21a-f321-4e64-9ce4-a2d20fa924e9: "You spared her life, right? My dream... I doubt she even remembers me, but yet..."

b74fc71b-2e35-49fc-8cbe-3f79c598e6a2: "Dead? So what? I have my memories, I have my gang, I have two hands to draw a bow. Nothing is stopping me from conquering these lands, as I've done before."
