1cec7140-abbc-45af-9a48-c530dc99b079: {n}Kimo coughs in his fist, clearly embarrassed.{/n} "I almost forgot... Please, come and talk to me! I... I have to ask you something. Something personal."
9f30732f-6adf-401a-b551-bef7b471e573: {n}Red as a lobster, Kimo leaves the throne room.{/n}
d1df9ac3-a76c-40c1-81d1-9b772c0e3712: {n}His face drawn and haggard, {d|Kimo}Kimo{/d} bows to you.{/n}
f7278bdd-6749-48a6-9e19-73358c34c241: "Forgive me for not coming for so long. And please accept this humble gift – my final gift to you."
9dc8bef1-e7c1-4e58-a13d-aa8fbdc2c112: "She has rejected me. She will not listen to my pleas. My work has no sense anymore – just as my life. I shall bid you farewell and leave these lands forever."
da480211-ec7a-4ad5-b1c5-7699d5a000c7: "Farewell, {name}. You've helped me on this path – but you couldn't have known where it would lead me." {n}Kimo sighs deeply and leaves the throne room.{/n}
3d5fc9c4-ec80-413b-9b70-b4742afe477c: "I'm Kimo, Kimo Tavon! A carpenter, engraver and so on. I can make bows, and spears and staffs too… but my bows are the best! I have something special in mind – a bow that will shoot an arrow's deadly reflection with each shot. I will make it, I know it! If only my inspiration doesn't fail me."
ab0a630e-eb65-4226-985e-2cbd5144513a: "Do you know where stolen goods are sold?"
dfefd73b-2d42-4e43-81d8-db17287ea833: "What is the secret of your success, Hassuf?"
30542310-c3cb-4386-9ec1-4ea9e027f52c: "Why did you leave Absalom, the center of global trade, for some young barony in the Stolen Lands?"
79ea7c0e-d9fc-4180-be44-1149a6472a62: "Come, come. Tell me why you left Absalom. I insist."
8518de70-ea54-43a8-a82c-f10f38056a33: "Has trade recovered from all the hardships the town has endured?"
543045a9-7e1d-45eb-a848-8354e4aef3e0: "The guards were told that a half-elf named Sharel robbed you. Is this true?"
3b6b757e-fb17-4825-a4c4-64ce44de5032: "A Vudrani asked us to give you this letter. She claimed that your families know each other."
96d6c61d-804f-4abe-8448-3b4368ebf390: {n}The man bows to you, spreading his arms a little.{/n} "Hassuf from {g|Absalom}Absalom{/g} is happy to welcome you, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}! Come, take a look at the best wares we traveling merchants have to offer. Please, come, take a look."
5db4aef3-99b0-46ba-a901-9380a21b9c7a: {n}Hassuf squints cunningly.{/n} "How very polite — you do not ask me directly! But no, I am not involved in such shady dealings. Although the local traders sometimes claim otherwise..."
27c9564a-d5ca-42c3-afae-2ec7ab2af28d: "Some say that anything that's lying about will be stolen in this city — but then cannot be found for sale! You are not the first to ask after stolen goods: many hope to find on the black market what precious things were stolen from their homes. But alas! It would seem the thieves have their own ways of getting rid of the stolen goods."
0cea4718-7f85-4b78-aa5d-0304e094384b: "My pleasure, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}!" {n}The merchant smoothes his mustache and commences his story with an air of importance, speaking in a sonorous voice, gesturing widely.{/n} "Hassuf's family was not rich, and he, as many in {g|Absalom}Absalom{/g}, had to start from the very bottom. As a child, while his peers chased pigeons and stole apples at the market, he worked at a tannery... Oh, I can still smell this disgusting stench..." {n}The man pulls out a heavily perfumed handkerchief and waves it in the air.{/n}
2a44c375-0793-4d36-b148-be5f9676a588: "There is no secret! Perseverance, strength of character, attention to detail, the gift of persuasion, charm... all this among many other things are key to success in my profession. But if I did have a secret, who would I be to share it with anyone?" {n}The merchant laughs merrily, his hands rubbing his sides.{/n}
599bd561-ccdd-43e0-a79b-e03c0856227b: {n}You see a dark-skinned wiry man with a weather-beaten face and a happy smile on his face. He is dressed luxuriously, and his dark hair and neat mustache are exquisitely coiffured.{/n}
e1b55b58-eba9-42ff-9bea-49a268fee29b: "Ha ha ha, this is a long story... I don't think Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness} would be interested!"
1e979567-4536-4e9e-a28f-332b4cd6eea4: {n}The merchant groans theatrically.{/n} "Very well, as you wish, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}... It was about a woman. When I was still young, I fell in love with the daughter of a judge — an important person in {g|Absalom}Absalom{/g}. For many years I tried to win her heart, but she was cold as stone. I should have given up... but this is not in my character. In the end I did manage to win her love — but I was unready for it!"
a0dbb016-c0cc-4bfc-9a6e-fe5639a86b58: {n}Hassuf swallows and rubs the back of his head.{/n} "As {g|Abadar}Abadar{/g} is my witness, the flames of hell burn inside this woman... I could not live with her for even six months! Tenderness and passion one day — screaming and scandal the next. Sometimes she would break into my office during business meetings to make a jealous scene — and sometimes pulled me by my collar from the finest taverns in town! I couldn't sleep! I was nervous all the time — and it started to affect my business. I realized there was nothing else to do but run... Leaving her and remaining in the city would be impossible. Even in such a city as {g|Absalom}Absalom{/g}."
1135f740-9946-45f3-b745-8da617b3abde: "I decided never to return. And I still fear that wildcat of a woman will follow my trail!" {n}Hassuf stops talking and stares into space without blinking.{/n} "Although sometimes, after a couple of jars of wine, I still remember her... Perhaps it was I who unleashed this tornado in her? If somehow I'd behaved differently..."
2552e8ac-a4b3-408c-b8e3-87fda5feedee: "It's been a terrible tragedy. But we've stood our ground and overcome it. We now sell almost as many goods as we did before the catastrophe. And we're even lacking in timber, stone and construction tools — the prices are sky high!"
e0409347-c078-4f52-b113-308f2239e1bd: "Ahem. Well, the young apprentice worked hard, saved every coin, and soon managed to purchase that tannery from his former master. Then, as soon as he had enough money, he opened his own trading agency. After ten years, countless deals, and many tours in his caravan, Hassuf was one of the most successful merchants in {g|Absalom}Absalom{/g} — thus writing his name indelibly in the history of the great city!"
e9a1ab6e-8ce9-409d-b4d4-d0cb207b1214: {n}The merchant looks at you with pleasure.{/n} "Well, how was that? I'm looking for a writer so I can dictate my memoirs, ha ha. I think many would find it interesting — and useful — to learn more about me."
479d9f3f-e33d-4ee5-9a80-0499dcbe0e6f: {n}Hassuf shakes his head, surprised.{/n} "Sharel? Robbed? Can't be! He is a great young man, and a capable tailor! We agreed I will lend him money to start a shop, at a humble rate of interest. But he didn't steal a single coin from me! I can vouch for him — give me one moment!" {n}Hassuf pulls out a sheet of paper and scrawls out a short letter, adds his sprawling signature, then hands the letter to you.{/n}
9067c603-1566-4c97-8109-5de37772b9a7: {n}As soon as you finish speaking, Hassuf snatches the letter from your hands and immediately breaks the seal, quickly running his eyes along the lines. His face grows pale, and his hands clench. He takes his time ripping the letter into tiny pieces, enjoying the process.{/n} "Damn that disgusting wretch and that entire family! They decide to send me a letter, as though I don't know that only poison trickles from their mouths?!"
d952f148-c0e9-4a3d-898a-2f80cb385e7e: {n}After calming down a bit, Hassuf turns to you.{/n} "You probably did not know what was in the letter — all the better. You shouldn't burden yourself with a feud between families living on opposite sides of the world. You did your part, and I am grateful to you — at least for caring to deliver this letter to me, though it was written by traitors. Your intentions were pure, of that I am certain."
1390b18e-1dcb-41e6-8ab7-28df4acea560: "Your sword is so amazing. I could never have imagined someone wielding such a huge blade."
b97b65a9-f9de-448b-bf68-b947ca16c40a: "Right! I took it from a frost giant – as a trophy! I slaughtered so many of them giants with it! Now when they hear my name, they shit their pants!"
1cb2483c-ba4a-48fe-b650-33db99cfcd7b: "How did you come to be in these lands, Jhod?"
5aa5872a-7f40-4819-8e83-6f2682cc3a89: [Conditionally Release Jhod] "I hope you won't forget to reward your rescuer, old man!"
ded4dcd9-99ea-47f9-b872-a13b5d8e1b83: {n}You see a dark-haired man of about forty-five, though the wrinkles on his face make him look sixty at first sight. He's currently a prisoner, judging from his tied hands. He slouches a bit, squinting shortsightedly at the light as he moves his lips as though speaking to someone invisible. He jerks his head up as he notices you.{/n}
4e78b97c-617a-4e75-adfd-9f68b9e9d31a: "Praise {g|Erastil}Erastil{/g}, someone finally chased off those scoundrels! Thank you, stranger. My name is Jhod Kavken. I'm a priest of Erastil, from {g|Galt}Galt{/g}. Those bandits attacked me as I was crossing the river, said they wanted to take me to their leader, make me heal their wounds. Not a chance! The strength granted me by Erastil is meant to help honest people, not robbers!"
704d4d12-0c5f-4562-93b7-f498450d2122: "I was led here by visions, sent by the {g|Erastil}Elk God{/g}," {n}Jhod says with veneration.{/n} "Erastil showed me that somewhere in this wild land lies the Temple of the Elk — an ancient shrine, forlorn and desecrated. I saw the ruins of the temple, and the shadows of a predator lurking in sorcerous fog. I felt the echoes of the vicious rituals performed at the once blessed place. I have no doubt — Erastil revealed all this to me so I could stop the ungodly sorcery that's desecrating the temple!"
2237b569-0335-46f7-b46f-606d830be888: "That I don't know. Visions, even divine ones, are often vague and unreliable. I know only that the temple is somewhere near, in the {g|Narlmarches}Narlmarches{/g}. But I'm afraid I won't be able to find it myself, what with bandits lurking around every corner in this place..." {n}Jhod shakes his head sadly.{/n}
41f11c79-929a-4ac5-9706-cc4082ce5cd9: {n}Jhod mutters a bit, rubbing his hands.{/n} "Oh, these times — to be as surprised to meet an honest {mf||wo}man as to see a manticore at a vegetable stall! Thank you for your help. I've exhausted my supply of prayers, but I'll gladly repay you in the future, once I've restored my strength. Come to me if you ever need to be healed or blessed."
4e375028-32ef-4211-a4f2-28969afeacb1: {n}Jhod shakes his head in disapproval.{/n} "You think me some ingrate? I may have exhausted my supply of prayers, but I'll be ready to heal you or bless you once I've recovered my strength."
0072a5d7-bfb1-4cc3-b364-00d4bed1670f: "I'm afraid an old fool like me won't be able to handle the mission given me by {g|Erastil}Erastil{/g} on my own. How can I search for the temple when the bandits around here won't let me take a single step? I'll head to {g|Oleg's Trading Post}Oleg Leveton's Trading Post{/g} to rest and think on what to do next. Please, traveler, if you happen to discover the ruins of the Temple of the Elk, come inform old Jhod! My gratitude will know no bounds."
b7450f1d-cf29-4b60-a7fb-5b3895a4d2e0: "Jubilost? Are you alive? I saw Nyrissa trying to kill you."
847900ba-5bb0-476b-8302-94e9d887c932: "So you let yourself be tempted by Nyrissa..."
30de6f25-f042-4a2d-bf75-14867720d15f: [Attack] "I have little patience with Nyrissa's servants."
5c66ae1c-e8bb-4cfc-bf15-d6eed5aae985: {n}Jubilost is writing in his notebook, looking as focused as usual.{/n} "{name}! I didn't expect you to get here so soon. Just a moment, I'm almost finished!"
07b556b5-6063-4414-804f-80cfe6335298: "It's amazing that you managed to get here, {name}. I kept hoping that this wasn't going to happen, and bloodshed could be avoided."
17212514-7105-4a9f-b494-a132bda1db2a: "But not every death is final. I understood completely how the primal gnomes felt, when I returned to life here, in the House at the Edge of Time. The Host {d|Jubilost Immortal}didn't lie{/d} — I'm connected to {g|First World}the First World{/g}. And this connection is something more than just a chance to die a little less fully than the denizens of the {g|Material Plane}Material Plane{/g}. The First World is now... inside me. It's an eternal, seething, ever-changing. And it protects me from the {g|Bleaching}Bleaching{/g} better than any magic."
f0886b99-7033-4c94-91cb-cbbbc9ef3b2f: "But guess who helped me? Xae, our insane ghost friend from the dungeons under the {g|Candlemere}Candlemere{/g}! Though she's not a ghost {d|Jubilost Xae}any more{/d}, and significantly less insane, but who knows... According to her, she never died in a dungeon, but safely opened a portal to {g|First World}the First World{/g} and even regained her immortality."
d899e1ba-1041-4faa-9dee-2e54e59c8e33: "But guess who helped me? The unforgettable {d|Jubilost Nyrd}Nyrd Zottenropple{/d}! She seems to be settling into {g|First World}the First World{/g} quite well, and she hopped here like a grasshopper using her teleportation. She dragged my breathless body from under Nyrissa's nose, revived me, and brought back here with a heap of wishes, half-mad stories, and a request that I bring her something she calls books, but which I call kindling."
919c7dfc-1dec-4e7c-94aa-ecb7effdb3b5: "Far from trying! She did kill me! Not that I was unprepared for such an outcome, but it's still an unpleasant and rather painful business. I'm not sure yet if I'm even going to include it in my publications. A painful death is not the sort of experience you want to read about over and over on a rainy evening by the fire."
2f69ecd6-7c5c-497a-b115-7b1c55546cf6: "Of course. I just can't wait to pay a visit to Lady Nyrissa. I should like to help her become history — both literally and figuratively!"
3b463dfd-d29d-425d-a0e1-adf62a1ca5c7: "{g|Shyka}Shyka{/g}, the {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g} of Time, informed her that for this she has to thank a {mf|king|queen} from {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g} and some young — young, just think of it! — gnome named Jubilost. Shyka told Xae that she'd be able to save us in the House at the Edge of Time many thousands of years later. And she did! — She waited, she came, and she saved!"
37cac94e-0c35-455f-8b15-0af2011d4149: "Strictly speaking, it was threats and blackmail, not temptation. But yes, I gave in. Why not, in the end? If she helps me do what you couldn't — find a solution of gnomes' exodus from {g|First World}the First World{/g} — that would make up for everything else. I might not be comfortable with killing my former companions, but sometimes the ends justify the means!"
14bf747a-d1ca-4d42-9b84-f4645b7fedb6: "Jubilost, talk to me. What's the secret of the incredible success of your books?"
271799c7-c1a1-4f2a-9e48-55dfff5a70b5: "Ha! You wish to know about sleepless nights, failed experiments, and painstaking work? Well nothing is preventing you from buying 'The Secrets of Writing by Jubilost Narthropple'...."
b9feb881-30ce-4e23-8ef3-a5877c9a34bb: {g|Stability8_1}[Choice effects]{/g} [Pay 2 BP each week] "Sacrificing safety is folly. We'll pacify the people by lowering the taxes."
4e6a40e4-5734-4273-b8a6-5993f5b6c4d6: {g|Stability8_2}[Choice effects]{/g} "If such is the will of the people, then we must surrender some of our control. Certain security measures will simply have to be let go."
74e6d70a-1017-45e8-bff2-03944206f64b: {g|Stability8_3}[Choice effects]{/g} "We cannot allow ourselves dance to the commoners' tune. Scatter the rebels and outlaw such gatherings — for their own safety."
7fc3ec04-d1e3-4c93-a528-6b79e89df1d6: {g|Stability8_4}[Choice effects]{/g} "The guards of this kingdom have been through hell and back. They deserve a raise."
d8fa0c2e-b78a-4b0a-862f-1d649ab034cb: {g|Stability8_5}[Choice effects]{/g} "A tired warrior is no use anyway. Let our guardsmen enjoy the rest they so deserve."
602e1950-ab4c-452d-ae27-a5b359aea6cf: {g|Stability8_6}[Choice effects]{/g} "They've brought my wrath upon their heads. Every man and woman who shirks their duties will be shamefully discharged, and replaced with a mercenary."
9978c262-5073-49f9-a08a-4b0f8a8f0455: {n}Ekun's face is darker than a storm cloud.{/n} "Big trouble, {name}. People on the streets. They demand... 'a return to freedom'." {n}Shaking his head, Ekun continues.{/n} "They demand that we reduce the number of guards, the frequency of patrols, and ban personal searches..."
857fc8e0-c848-46bd-a1ac-e0f98c35cd30: {n}Kesten's voice is grim and harsh.{/n} "It's a revolt, Your Highness. The simple folk have flooded the streets. Pamphlets are scattered throughout the capital. The way they put it, we're 'holding the people captive in their own country'. Everything we've done to protect them is misinterpreted as measures to limit their freedoms."
f911216d-c3b9-4f59-a149-84e2ba98a9be: "The lousy peasants! Who do they think they are?! {name}, your subjects have taken to the streets, and dare to make demands! 'The guard watches our every step!' Just think of it — they want us to stop personal searches, lower the number of guards, decrease the patrols..."
acae4f28-a021-4556-8dc1-6e6f4c5249f2: "My advice: do not clench your fist even tighter. It is not right for everyone to suffer for the sins of the rash and the shortsighted. But I would not give in either." {n}Ekun wrinkles his forehead in concentration. After a while, he continues.{/n} "What can we sacrifice instead of sacrificing safety? I can think of one alternative: money."
111acccd-8773-4b81-bc02-b82d3d5da06d: {n}Kesten stands in silence, then continues.{/n} "I'm afraid we'll just have to give in. At least partially. It would certainly be cheaper than trying to placate the people by lowering their tithes. And it's safer and more just than using force to run them back to their homes."
bf04a919-c06a-4b76-97c8-cd9e8611f040: "I'll tell it like it is, {name} — if there's one thing they hate, it's that I've brought this place to order! See, they can't loiter for days on end anymore, idle away their day and then steal whatever they can get their dirty mitts on! My hounds are watching their every move. There can be no deals, no appeasing them. — Just give me the order, and my boys will have those dirty oafs back in their homes, hiding under their beds!"
6b44b96d-3bb7-4cd7-b4d4-9440f2df0fdc: {n}A deep furrow crosses Ekun's forehead.{/n} "The guards have revolted. They refuse to work. They say, we 'fill every gap and patch every hole' with them. This cannot go on."
4d107475-0a81-4449-892a-0b1c1eced1db: {n}Kesten's ever-grim visage is painted with concern.{/n} "Ill news, Your Highness. The guard refuses to go out on patrols. The officers have declared that their people will not take up weapons, until the conditions of their service are improved. Truth be told, it is rare for a kingdom to see their guard take part in so many battles, wars, raids and monster hunts..."
46ae5a72-47f7-4746-8ecf-f6191467a8af: {n}Regongar's voice booms across the throne room.{/n} "{name}, your good-for-nothing runts have gone on strike! Made demands! From me! When they were starting out, I was like their ma and pa! I taught them which end of a halberd to hold! How to shake down a vagabond! How to talk to the merchants, and make sure they pay on time for their safety! And this is how they repay me! — By refusing to go out on patrol?! By asking for a better quality of life?!"
ad6fc7fd-d07a-4146-b437-74372dcebd9e: "Mercenaries can never truly replace warriors who fight for their homeland. Firing some of the guard would mean leaving someone without a defender. I think instead we should raise their pay."
faa185a7-12f3-4d2a-88e8-50d36f694d08: "Your Highness may instead pay for the services of mercenaries. But I think that our boys deserve some time off. They risk their lives every day, and they need to spend more time with their families... while they still can."
af7e7171-b148-4954-8cc1-298c6f5c3de9: "I would kill the bastards if I could! There's so many damned people around — and not a single soul you can trust! I say we just cut the dead weight, fire the whiners and replace them with mercenaries."
ea296da0-5939-4d53-87d8-5a9452a6674b: {n}Ekun's shoulders relax in relief.{/n} "I'll talk to your advisors. We'll come up with something."
f7e53e47-fe99-43db-9ab0-639d4e7ebba3: {n}Ekun nods in contemplation.{/n} "It will be as you say. Perhaps it is for the best."
e9b6d4ea-f04c-4c0c-84ec-466b0edef26b: {n}Kesten's face softens considerably.{/n} "Your Highness only makes it even clearer to me that this was the only proper course."
0eaac491-704e-44f4-90ac-cdd28c9a80f9: "I'm glad of this. I will deliver the good news."
d7aff6d1-97d9-468e-9886-6fb424975063: {n}A slight smile crosses Kesten's lips.{/n} "Thank you, Your Highness! I'll go and tell your people the good news."
3e7cae23-35ef-4fe2-bfde-e4e789d5e4ce: "As you command, Your Highness! I shall pass along your orders!"
b38967e8-e614-4cf4-8e77-ac9a31917494: {n}Regongar snaps his fingers and grins.{/n} "Ha ha! That's just perfect for the lazy numbskulls! They'll come crawling back to papa, begging for us to take them back — and we'll give them nothing! The treacherous bastards!"
b6b3ed89-67a6-4467-bbb0-f4e90d562766: "Oh, I'll enjoy this, {name}! My boys'll clean up the streets in no time!"
0846976a-a62f-4950-b4a1-02287384f65e: "Let us raise a toast to those who fought bravely, and died a glorious death."
064a0afd-1ad6-44b1-be29-7ea1354a37fc: "We should honor the memory of those who are no longer with us. Let us raise our goblets."
a82abf83-6fe8-4b29-a607-892f80231fc8: "The dead don't care what toasts we make."
c1a16ced-a0e2-487f-878d-bbae3a0421e8: "I could tell you a few things about this peculiar ritual. But perhaps this time I'd better just join the toast."
610c824a-71f8-4f21-87f2-b5df0d4a3039: "That's right. Here's how we honor the fallen fighters. Not with whining. If I drop dead one day, drink in my honor 'til the mountains shake!"
49dcd222-4970-4d32-a736-7db09ecc7fcf: "Their feats will not be forgotten! I'll make sure of that!"
7995b75c-5631-42a0-bb94-73002bb67c49: "I heard you singing as we walked! So beautiful! Why don't you sing for us now?"
5cfdeeef-fdb0-4708-9d0c-23eca3884ee4: "My singing is not like yours, sweet Linzi. I sing for myself, as travelers sing in the desert, during a long journey on a camel's back, with my face covered by three layers of cloth, to hold back the sandy wind."
eac9b748-eeee-4264-b099-3d7f16c25417: "The wererat died from taking the potion."
6a466bb4-5028-4f1a-ab9f-03c84ce865eb: [Lie] "As soon as I fed your potion to the dog... spots appeared on it from head to tail! And then it had orange saliva dripping from its mouth!"
43811427-c3a5-4d15-b6f7-ed5b4dfa8631: "I need to buy something from you."
2ff531ba-3be1-4365-bcce-57f6a8f0b412: "I bet a gold piece that you're not even listening to what I say…"
28e4d317-8fa4-4707-825f-d98938e60f40: "Speak clearly, old man. What on earth are you blathering about?"
54366e64-4007-407f-ae86-e92f689ef3fe: "The potion clouded your mind. You attacked me."

dae2938a-797c-4423-ad9a-6e991ba27fee: "Our trade depends too much on the coins of others. Constant rate fluctuations make our money changers rich, at the expense of everyone else. Your country needs its own real currency!"
ddc03cf2-d14a-4be5-bf2d-03455c2130de: "I have a plan that will make coins decorated with your noble profile far more valuable than the gold they are made of. 2b0f9621-cef6-4df5-bdfe-2791c0c827c7: "Thank you for your trust.. I will give the order to begin minting coins, and prepare the announcement about new tax collection rules. You'll see – a coin with your profile will soon be worth three times its weight in gold!"
7c17236f-f102-4570-a262-723597f7bbc2: {n}Kanerah grows gloomy.{/n} "Well, what is best is often the enemy of what is good. a5316cb9-690c-4f2e-8efe-d982f97f2285: "Your books are known everywhere, read everywhere – even forbidden in some places... How did you achieve such recognition? Or is it a secret?"
0a42ea96-94d0-443a-bf06-ed73c6bfa827: "It's no secret, girl. First of all, it's a lot of hard work. Day and night, without closing your eyes, tireless. And second of all... I'm just talented."
f5e6368e-1310-4d7f-8459-dc0e487b9a2a: [Jokingly punch Amiri on the shoulder] "So, warrior, are you ready to beat the hell out of the Eldest and his minions?"
11c949dc-a9a9-4c43-8ab3-9bd41b204b23: "Do you want to tell me anything before we set off for battle?"
e9a328d8-a8e1-4dbb-be96-5bdfcbbfa85c: "All right, enough talk. I know you don't like it."
8416bb27-f336-4228-ae84-9ec54ec30501: {n}Amiri ruffles her dark hair with her hand.{/n} "Ha... We were just getting ready for our last great battle — and now we're doing it again! It's a good thing I decided to follow you back there at Aldori's. You definitely know how to have fun, chief!"
019e5540-8584-4962-b3a0-4984bba96589: "I do! You're a good chief, and our tribe is all right, and we've been through a lot of good fights! Don't think I'm sucking up or something... it's just that I live like I want now. And that makes me sing inside!"
80ed1440-9e6d-4f12-b467-e3d76311ed0d: {n}The barbarian grins, then returns the friendly jab.{/n} "Oh no, I'm not ready! Wait, I need to polish my sword — and tie some ribbons to my belt! Then I'll be ready for battle!" {n}Amiri laughs, pleased with her joke.{/n}
a7feb908-1b04-4259-9594-23afd7b49cf1: "Right! Go on, chief, give the order!"

691866ac-63f9-4d95-b125-6f23abef9db7: ...Nok-Nok decided to hide right in the cauldron set over an open fire!
5a255571-5bd0-44ee-b463-430718bc5f37: ...Nok-Nok climbed on the roof of the nearest hut.
bf44795e-5f3b-4b4b-92d2-ccb117c93841: ...take to his heels and run around the fire.

bbbaece6-428c-44f0-baa8-19e59af5c6d3: He offered his adversary a chance to lower his weapons and forge a friendship stronger than any feud!
6d62ef18-ffc9-4954-acee-398a6c9a3f31: He leapt out from behind the goblin king's back with a wild howl, trying to frighten him!
4ab5a0b8-e67c-473e-b918-d6949444117b: ...fall to his knees and beg for mercy.
a30d2886-2120-4340-b174-8f474b00215b: ...began to shower the king with insults.
c5c564e0-46c4-4773-8c31-14137fd9120e: And so it came to pass that we would bear witness to a true goblin duel! Renowned scholars would have paid a steep price to be in our place... and would have paid thrice more afterwards to be anywhere else than inside a camp teeming with goblins!
5064338d-01a4-415f-aa6b-5b661689c5c2: The news the king was going to fight the insolent intruder spread through the tribe like wildfire — the goblins gathering around the fire began to yell and shout so loud, it was as if they wanted {g|Lamashtu}Lamashtu{/g} herself to hear! f0aea54e-c8c3-4c12-aa7b-6ee83074dfbf:

"Nok-Nok gone!"
Who would have thought?! While the whole tribe was busy listening to the baron{mf||ess}, our "champion" had vanished! The startled king came to his senses and began to tear apart the area, shaking his blade and screaming curses!
cd2a7e92-2726-4833-81e2-91fdc867003e: The king wasn't the sort to tolerate sneaking right under his nose. Screaming in rage and raising his blade, he rushed at Nok-Nok!
0fdd9572-cffe-4071-894b-ecde3a10fde1: There was no time to think — Nok-Nok was standing right in front of an enraged, seasoned goblin warrior eager to skin him alive! Our fearless companion had nothing left to do but to…
b5d22b46-c1ad-4969-992b-d87b0b592d9e: Goblins are known for their ability to slip through the tiniest cracks and to fit into the smallest spaces. They are also notoriously voracious and bad at predicting the consequences of their actions. It shall remain unknown what was the downfall of our goblin friend — the haste or the desire to feast upon whatever was left in the cauldron, but it didn't affect the sad outcome.
6da9984d-2ee2-4ab8-b136-47a8b07720b9: Nok-Nok's undertaking ended in a yelp of pain and an overturned cauldron, whence tumbled out our scorched companion, his skin steaming and covered in the foul brew.
bcaaec3d-b56c-47b6-93cf-98d76021a145: Indeed, our nimble little friend had somehow climbed on the roof of the nearest hut and was now looking out from behind the edge — clearly, he was about to throw at his enemy the first thing that came into his hand!
552f6dd9-11a1-414f-a19b-e6f05dde5af9: Doing his best not to betray his anxiety, the unsuspecting king waddled straight into the trap! Nok-Nok sprang to his feet, took aim at his opponent, and with a victory cry, threw...

de14a5ea-9e46-469f-8575-de4dda3a996c: Such treatment infuriated Nok-Nok's opponent even more, and he spun around in rage trying to see what was the cause for all the merriment. Nok-Nok had no more time for joking around!

c580546d-7629-4cfe-80ae-62b9249c1c2c: Is dry grass indeed the most dangerous thing one can find on a roof?! Whatever the case, the straw caused no significant harm to the bewildered king — it just stuck in his already hideous crown.
fd07bc9a-ce5a-4858-9cb2-2cb68c020377: We reminded Nok-Nok that the ultimate victory still lay ahead. We had to face the true villain — the shaman, the one behind infecting untold numbers of people and spreading the horrific disease.

4155e872-43e1-4ae8-98e9-9cc5c7160d46: Nok-Nok decided not to test his fate and give up. Perhaps, this might have worked if he were battling someone else... but goblins are hardly known for their mercy and compassion!

fe1d9b91-528c-4db3-a5ba-adfc2b3fcfcf:
I can state with full confidence — none of the long-legged witnesses of this duel could have expected the deranged goblin to do what he did next. Or may it be that pulling off such insane stunts is the prose of life for his folk?
Without thinking twice, Nok-Nok...
7e1529b1-5e65-4da3-a674-a889e09ae9d8: To our amazement, Nok-Nok swayed on his feet, rolled his eyes, and collapsed into the dust as if poleaxed! Taken aback, the audience went completely still. Silence hung in the air.

14c2c191-b2ae-431a-bd84-f3be38c4df9e: So, how did this unusual and victorious adventure end? It ended with Nok-Nok's utter triumph, who not only humiliated the despicable goblin king, but was also rewarded with a well-deserved trophy — the crown that had previously adorned the chieftain's head!
2404a6ae-d819-4e65-b797-5e5a8c40c1de: What a ludicrous idea! How did it get into the head of a cunning and treacherous goblin? Obviously, it didn't have a good outcome...

0d225d70-574d-4bf5-a29f-e49bd83661ed: ...just to jump out of his skin the next moment and flee from a swarm of furious wasps, screaming wildly as he did so! Only a crown was left lying on the ground — it had tumbled off the head of the fleeing coward.

b26a74d7-c842-4ef6-aa1c-db2aa57c419f: Nok-Nok scolded the king roundly — he lambasted his dubious ancestry, the king's over-attention to cleanliness, manners, and even called him out for engaging in intentional bathing and washing. 4a843201-f496-4364-9470-b4a928fc4f9b:

0568e56f-502a-4261-b370-0e0615122d3d:

f706f42c-7751-4f5b-8015-c9a947cac7fa: "Amiri, I've been meaning to ask you for a while now. Do you do anything special to style your hair?"

0959a4b7-6351-4527-9aef-6ceefe71603b: "You'll have to turn down many similar offers. But eventually people will come to realize that the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g} have changed forever. Henceforth, everyone is equal before the law."

990f8e65-7520-4032-bb61-52d090dbe7e9: "I will be sure his colleagues are aware of how painful his death was. May they mind their own business in the future – and not forget what happens to those who fail to do so."

55d9be2a-1d24-4f85-8c71-6b609465c76b: "Surely, this fool is merely a symbol. He himself is not important. 18041486-8cf6-4b98-a53d-eb16beaf3eca: "Why so upset, my dear? I used my mastery of illusions to fool the slow-witted soul eater. It will get its victim — three of them in fact... and it will believe that it captured and killed Kanerah. And then it will leave, and your problem is solved."
2f88d614-9ca4-4528-9354-3602deb3e724: {n}Kalikke looks at you, eyes filled with despair.{/n} "Please, {name}, we have to save them! 32ef40ed-3cd7-41cf-8561-8997f4fc7776: "Follow your heart, of course. Isn't that the sort of trite wisdom you all love to repeat?"

3027ae2a-fb4a-4717-ae43-90e4acf1fe16: "No!" {n}Kalikke prepares to dart off, but only takes a single step.{/n}

b6bf38bb-d679-4015-9302-0c78635c922f: "When will I be allowed to get some sleep... What's going on here? Wait... what?!"
1e6feecb-ad1f-4b17-b382-396b812c21e5: "Never — I repeat — never again stand in my way, Tristian."
92eb55a0-3980-4a5b-a718-82f53f5847ab: "Will you come with me to the meeting?"
d03b3b8a-50e1-4245-876f-93141e87f36a: "Amalia looked at you very fondly, don't you think?"
af026041-d994-4014-96e8-a279657f5384: "Oh, stop. A little fun wouldn't be so bad, would it?"
ac31b621-59c5-408a-a822-88e164bfe124: "What do you think awaits us at the meeting?"
95199761-add5-4510-8dbd-698babf54f7b: {n}Tristian looks down at the leaflet he's still holding. His face is sad.{/n} "A meeting at the appointed place... there are even directions how to get there. It looks like it's time we visit this sacrament."

a2a1f63a-c1f1-47f1-9f36-654be52fdb19: {n}Tristian holds your stare.{/n} "I will pray to {g|Sarenrae}Sarenrae{/g} that I will never have to do it again."
8f90d714-51be-4a61-891c-10d757d26f53: {n}Tristian breathes out.{/n} "Just... just try not to let this happen again."
2f070dd7-ba88-40ca-8222-3f54fb4a0bc7: {n}Tristian smiles half-heartedly.{/n} "I'm not the one you should apologize to, {name}. Instead, apologize to the poor frightened girl. Anyway, nothing terrible happened, so let's get back to business."
0055f10e-21f7-44e4-bdd5-f20ce016f1d1: {n}Tristian shakes his head and turns grim.{/n} "You distract us from our goal."
0fa545f4-f0d8-43e1-9d40-fc2ebf6f6d5f: {n}Tristian cringes.{/n} "Please stop. Not only is she merely a child, but she's also under the influence of these insane preachings. I must help her, not take advantage of her gullibility."
f84fff3a-22ff-4b95-be05-2fc6f36ed124: {n}Tristian looks again at the leaflet he's holding.{/n}
02296c3e-4654-479e-804f-a8bf38b9e783: "I would insist on participating in this investigation. I cannot let you go alone, after I dragged you into this strange affair."
1d1e89ed-ce9c-426c-8e66-76ad1f9793bd: {n}Tristian looks pensively into the distance.{/n} "Whatever awaits, this mysterious First Faithful will be there. Judging by his title, he's the one who invented this insane Kingdom. I believe that talking to him will solve many of the riddles we face."
459881fc-2ba0-4456-8742-40019575ae95: {n}Tristian sighs heavily.{/n} "I worship {g|Sarenrae}Sarenrae{/g} myself. But my faith has little in common with the faith of these cultists. They fill the heads of innocent children with pernicious and dangerous ideas, which they cannot fully understand."
74f07934-3325-4284-bfa2-0c8def44aaad: {n}Tristian looks at you sideways, a shy smile creeping across his face.{/n} "Funny you should notice. An unusual observation. But please, let's return to the matter at hand."
74cae802-9cdb-4429-b312-a894783fbcbd: [Pay 100 gold] "Here is your money. Just take it back to where it belongs."
6ab79a6f-0bb5-41c0-940b-6c5d5039747b: "Are you crazy?! This is my royal throne! How can you demand gold for that which is rightfully mine?"
0fb58bdc-1db5-4aa5-a0bc-b5ce30c9a25f: "You will return my throne this instant before I hang you from the nearest tree!"
b8847ccf-f317-42e6-a26f-1e241274e4e0: "I can do without this junk. I have to go."
bac88d3e-d599-4691-b5be-f414da0dbed4: [Pay 200 gold] "Here's your money, you robber. Now return the throne to where it belongs!"
cdfd052f-d443-4cb9-9295-68bfe4290d2c: "Hey, Chwurk, we've met already! Remember me?"
21c2feb0-682c-44de-ad45-92bc2cbd419d: "How did you manage to get it in the first place?"
0ccc9da0-8c8c-49a3-9ab9-ae168a982c0f: "For this piece of junk? What should I do with it? Carry it on my back and entertain people? You keep it!"
03922652-b94e-43ca-bb99-5451e46dc29c: [Pay 50 gold] "Fine, you convinced me. But you have to put it back where you found it. Do you know the way?"
519a562f-e428-4350-b020-c5e609a4ee2c: "You think I'm an idiot?! I'll find another chair, newer and shinier! And you can keep dragging this thing around — you'll be the fool of goblins everywhere!"
6914bf5b-e157-4b4d-a282-07555df6ca50: "Fine, I'll help you out as a friend. Give me this throne."
487b9168-6d42-4d99-9df9-8f6fd82ad2bc: "It's your own fault! Come on, get lost!"
6efe8f44-0a77-46d0-bab8-1cb602fe724a: [Attack] "I'll take this throne if I have to gut you to get it!"
f2730f7d-76bc-4efd-872c-7bf8982a8a9e: {n}As you come closer. the goblin gives a wide grin and waves at you. A ramshackle cart beside him is sagging under the weight of the junk within. Amidst the trash, however, you notice the glinting of gold and what seems to be hints of fine cloth — seems like only the owner of the cart can sort through this mess.{/n}
5c854e31-b030-4d11-8f7e-4de61e14e29e: "Hail, travelers! Welcome to the Chwurk's cart-around shop! I be having all! Pokers, glinters, clothers — choose what you like if you have money!" {n}Chwurk appraises you with greedy eyes, as if sizing up how much coin you have on you.{/n}
38f86153-6683-4714-aaca-c72804df3b58: "You again? We trade! I be having all, just say yes!" {n}The goblin points at his cart, packed to the brim with a heap of trash and treasure.{/n}
175f17dd-582a-4e26-aca3-ced5e924befa: "Eh? Ah, this chairy! It be good chairy, sturdy! Ornamenties on sides, soft seat, fine back! I be giving it off for hundred money! You be not regretting it! Why you staring at me like that? Is that a deal stare?"
6a7f2a2b-84ce-4a38-bd0a-ec3d46c3bdca: "Hey, stop! Don't beat me no more! Take it, take it, big deal! I be no stealing no more, I promise!" {n}Chwurk leaps away from you and cowers behind the throne.{/n} "Me be taking it back where I took it, just don't hit me in the head no more!"
98ca1a28-54f3-445b-a5b7-87fd0d839d2e: {n}Chwurk is still, trying to wrap his head around what you've said.{/n} "That true?" {n}He scratches his ear.{/n} "Right! Me be asking too little! It be worth two hundred money!"
2aa94121-6b2f-442c-b766-3a219e46b3b3: "Hey, why you be like that? I die of hunger if I be giving my goods for free! You give me money!"
fbb6bee5-8bd8-4c0d-83f1-a6c6c8d8163b: {n}The goblin sorts the coins greedily.{/n} "Money! Trureal money! First time I be holding it!" {n}Chwurk hastily tucks the coins into one of the purses around his waist and starts to mount the throne on the cart. {/n} "I be getting this chairy back in a heartbeat! You watch me!"
2ab850eb-f1e1-42cc-83e8-20514eb77531: {n}Chwurk screeches and drops to his knees.{/n} "Have mercy, adventurer! I be mistaken, I be not doing it never again!" {n}Chwurk wrings his hands.{/n} "You want bribe? I be giving you bribe! Many valuables I be giving you! And take chairy back! Just don't hit me no more!"
26cc4fd7-0b29-4d8d-b43a-ad2d88dcafdd: "Look, what I have!" {n}The goblin digs a wand out of the depths of his cart.{/n} "It be doing WHOOSH and doors go open! I be entering, taking all good stuff and leaving!" {n}Chwurk hastily tucks the wand back.{/n} "I be having some other whoosh-thingies, but I no showing them to you, they are mine and not for sale!"
181e96ac-f370-45d8-9012-909e978795f0: "How so? What about deal? Just hundred money! Come on! It be a good chairy, you no find this nowhere else! What you say?!" {n}The goblin makes several steps towards you, obviously unwilling to let you go until you make a purchase.{/n}
7609d5b5-1c99-4507-87c3-69bbfc9f671b: "Stop! Stop!" {n}Desperation rings in Chwurk's voice.{/n} "Let it be fifty money! You take this!" {n}He turns towards the throne warily, as if expecting trouble from it.{/n}
16a6b509-a382-47ed-ba92-0fc648ab3450: {n}Grimace of offence appears on Chwurk's face.{/n} "Why me be having this chairy! You take it! No money! Just no leave it to me! It be scaring other customers from me! It be ruining my reputashun! Take it!"
9ed9cf87-33df-4258-8426-1b2eaf634651:
{n}Chwurk bursts into tears.{/n} "Nooooo! You have piiiity on meeee! Don't leave me be with this cursed chairyyyy! Take it! No, I be taking it wherever you say! Just don't leave it to me!"
{n}Chwurk dives into his cart, grabs a pile of trash and thrusts it into your hands.{/n} "You take these too! I be doing everything you want, just don't leave me with this chairyyyy! Shame, such shame, me be mocked to deeeeeath! Me not waaant! Me never take other's trash no mooooore! Neveeeeer!"
724c4004-5536-4c17-9272-5b3e161dbcb3: {n}Chwurk looks you up and down with indifferent expression.{/n} "You adventurers be all the same! Dirty, skinny, why I should be remembering your kind. But if you be buying stuff..." {n}Chwurk thinks for a moment, then shakes his head sadly, as if confirming his memory of you is lost.{/n}
2f182ab1-3834-4c96-85c8-b4d295718047: "Since goblinking be downed, it be too bad. Me be self-riding roads and wandering around villages. No one be giving money, all just come to watch and pointfinger…"
3ac83a90-c81b-4f7c-83bf-43c5640cca63: {n}Before you have time to do something, a magic wand appears in Cwurk's hands. He waves it — and the world around you flashes with blinding lights that dance before your eyes, making you sick. Through the noise of blood pumping in your ears, you hear the goblin giggling and the wheels of cart squeaking as it moves away from you.{/n}
3484dd75-2724-43cc-90aa-34fa9c1d73b9: {n}When your sight returns to normal, Chwurk and his cart are gone. You start to wonder if the strange goblin was just a hallucination.{/n}
6f1c8c42-a64e-4833-b7d1-bc1389b40899: {n}Chwurk takes a deep breath, obviously relieved.{/n} "That's right, you be taking it! I can even drag this chairy myself — not be a problem for me! Now, now..." {n}The trader hastily mounts the throne atop his cart, covers it with some rugs, then looks around cautiously.{/n} "Me never be taking no things without permission! No want get in trouble like that again!"
65bf3fa2-ac08-4f5c-a1b2-06df9b4d5b33: "Listen what I say. No bargain with him. Nok-Nok knows sure, Nok-Nok tried. No do it."
3e5259c9-8c1d-467d-a895-25b71b5c7b43: "I be going new dungeon, have new goods! I sell, you buy!"
fc35bbdb-110f-4891-b2f0-9841c09c5c26: "While I was still alive, I had so many wonderful feelings, but didn't have the strength to achieve my goals."
2daed942-02c1-4777-b4d9-449a804b6fef: "Now I have sufficient strength for anything, but my goals... there are problems with my goals."
c5eed1c1-a5dd-426a-9f60-5c3ca3381591: "I'd like to learn more about you."
da8e4e13-25e1-4abc-a28d-33bd1669af80: "I need to discuss politics and affairs of the {mf|barony|barony|kingdom|kingdom} with you."
2ac01861-40b0-4ac6-af4d-3e9dfd007144: "What's the situation between the Royal House Surtova and the Aldori Swordlords?"
51a95052-8cc2-44b3-b148-03125c58e802: "What can you tell me about the River Kingdoms?"
f17cfcba-db90-4026-a501-45a6aea9f6f0: "Indulge my curiosity — do you have family? Close relatives?"
b1d87e60-6d63-4218-be80-3039c3858f7c: "You must have seen a lot over your years of diplomatic service. Do you have any stories that stick out as particularly interesting?"
54300a3b-0f4f-4c4b-96c6-2effdcc8d976: "Thank you. Let's speak of less personal matters."
c583f9cf-52b2-40f1-a31e-62f2325da996: "How long will you be staying with us?"
65168e38-fd64-4379-8eca-b4899b60b58e: "I'm looking for new advisors to assist in governing the country. Would you consider taking a position?"
00e460f7-7bab-4626-bb0e-3c4c1fe17898: {n}Shandra Mervey, envoy from the Royal House of {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}, bows her head courteously.{/n} "{mf|Baron|Baroness|King|Queen}, it's good to see you!"
508d1efb-1161-457c-965b-e06258b920fd: "That is what I'm here for, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}."
6544dcab-4570-449f-ab32-dad795b87970: "Answering this question will involve delving a bit deeper into history. You're surely aware that the {g|House Surtova}Surtovas{/g} and the Aldori each ruled their own sovereign kingdoms in the past. When {g|Choral}Choral the Conqueror{/g} invaded our lands, his might was incontestable. The Surtovas recognized this and bowed to him, exchanging their crown for status as a noble house. They were able to not only retain the house's influence in the region, but also save the lives of their subjects."
ef4f89f7-4c89-4298-adcd-90f1b4d66d66: "In typical Aldori fashion, they chose to mount a reckless campaign against {g|Choral}Choral's{/g} forces without so much as scouting the size of his army. As a result, their own armies were decimated when they encountered his red dragons. But instead of taking a lesson from the tragedy, the {g|Swordlords}Swordlords{/g} chose to nurse their grievance over the past two hundred years — and now they may have finally found a way to strike back."
bc9994b9-dfe1-4866-8cdd-21ba998c43b7: "The Aldori aren't even a true noble house. They're a motley rabble of upstarts who take their name after they learn the secrets of the {g|Swordlords}Swordlords{/g}' dueling style — there's little actual noble blood spread among them. But they're impulsive and ambitious — they obsess over the past, rather than focusing on the current and future prosperity of {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}. They need to be controlled, and {g|House Surtova}House Surtova{/g} can see that clearly. That's the situation as I understand it, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}."
964236a1-df96-40fc-aba3-50a334d2bd0f: "You are well within your rights, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. What would you like to know?"
711e118c-ab64-43fd-aa30-dfaacad77e75: "An interesting story, you say? Well, I once had to spend a summer in Artume. This small kingdom in the {g|River Kingdoms}River Kingdoms{/g} suffered from frequent bandit raids, and one gang in particular, practically a small army, was especially troublesome. They had somehow managed to find an informant from within the court — this unfortunately gave them plenty of information to interfere with trade in the area, including trade with {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}."
38e7cb50-67b8-484a-8111-c17ffdec2fad: "I announced to the court that I was awaiting the arrival of a particularly valuable caravan, and Artume's rulers were to take measures to ensure its safety. A squad was sent to meet the caravan, but the bandit gang struck and swiftly slaughtered the soldiers, capturing the cargo. The bandit leader was triumphant, and three merry bards started spreading news of his victory far and wide."
e5a99238-8e75-43d0-8355-3958c2dd0e7c: "The next day, a different gang attacked the first, hoping to seize the treasure from them. A week later, two more gangs entered the fray, and then more and more... Eventually, all the Brevic guards had to do was recover the stolen goods from a field of corpses. So, for the cost of three bards' time, we were able to protect our merchants and expose the bandits' informant from the court. I hope this simple tale can provide some insight to you, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}."
4928c280-01aa-4fca-806e-46166b78811c: "Of course. A daughter and two grandsons. The boys are a bit spoiled, but they show promising talent — I hope they'll go far." {n}Shandra shakes her head, a faint smile on her face.{/n}
1765512c-5bca-4ad6-afb6-a011127a8797: "Now, if you were to ask me where they live, I would have to promptly redirect the conversation. The first thing any good diplomat learns is to hide their weak spots. In all of {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}, only Lady Natala and {g|King Noleski Surtova}King Noleski{/g} know where my family lives."
60e2cede-8d68-4c75-bc74-868c4258ec31: "{g|River Kingdoms}The River Kingdoms{/g} are useful to {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g} — we sell the majority of our exports there. I personally spent a great deal of time there representing the interests of {g|House Surtova}House Surtova{/g}. My job was to help the River Kingdoms prosper, while at the same time helping them grow fat bellies rather than steel muscles, if you take my meaning. These lands can certainly be appealing, in their own way, but if I was asked to describe them in one word, it would have to be 'chaos'."
6d2626a4-d343-4599-a7f3-e94aa0a0bd80: "From a political standpoint, only {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g} and its ruler, King Irovetti, have any real power worth watching — both as an ally and as a potential enemy."
8ec7d158-e4f5-49d3-995c-58c719d34584: "Ask, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. I'm happy to help."
6ca421e3-d5e2-42cb-a3c8-de89be0c1041: "I'll remain for as long as Lady {g|House Surtova}Surtova{/g} deems it useful. You need the advice of an experienced advisor, so I'll provide you with information to the best of my ability until my lady calls for my return."
1688bed3-f944-486c-9fe2-d86dfcbf9c35: "{mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, my whole life I've been a councilor, and I don't see myself in any other role. I am well familiar with all the mechanisms that help to ensuring the loyalty of the citizenry — or at least a part of it. If you assign me to this position, I'll direct all my knowledge and experience to your benefit."
fc9fb9fa-815a-4c65-b218-df3b25798369: "Whether I enjoy a thing is not a point for discussion. By my estimation, your polite words are a way to express concern over my ability to fulfill my obligations. I assure you, I haven't encountered any situation I was not equal to. I shall seek audience with you only in cases where I believe the problem demands the ruler's personal decision."
a0bb8189-d3bf-42df-bae4-213d69c72ae3: {n}Shandra takes a barely noticeable breath before speaking.{/n} "As prior experience has shown, we have unresolvable differences in our opinions regarding the country's governance. Perhaps I should step back and give someone else a chance to be your advisor."
8bc7e964-0940-45d4-9252-3dcda19d8485: "You came HERE to hide from the violence?"
77ef908c-2462-4bf6-be3e-a83c1492500c: "I don't care what you were doing here. Get back to the capital — they need your help."
9c001a3e-2d69-44cf-be0a-a84a3b14e9da: {n}Bartholomew squeamishly brushes himself off, then performs a hasty bow.{/n} "Your Highness! Right on time, as always. Thank you for once again coming to my rescue!"
39fc1fb1-f906-4f53-a13b-3a65b024f90b: "Your Highness, as your loyal subject, I took every possible measure to protect your kingdom's most valuable asset — myself! My knowledge is far too important to just let it vanish upon my death. So I made the executive decision to leave the walls of the capital and come here to hide from all the violence in the city!"
cd911b5f-3765-495a-b523-ebb57cfac936: {n}Bartholomew swallows a few times, then sighs.{/n} "Forgive me, Your Highness. I lied. When all... this... started, I took it for a chance to gain new materials for my research. Taking advantage of the confusion, I returned to where I captured my first troll..."
58625700-0116-47ac-b029-bb4500ea56ac: "...and was captured by these beasts as a result! They seriously thought about cutting my face off to examine my head from the inside! Can you imagine? Cruel, brainless savages!"
bd448a6f-3e96-4000-9e64-3799e10a0238: "Well, thank you again for your timely appearance and saving my life! I'll return to the capital immediately — even a city swarming with monsters must be safer than THESE dungeons."
d2409692-7bf8-4330-9065-7c2489ca4572: "Oh... Oh! So that's how it is, now, Your Highness? After all my loyal service? Well, then, as you wish — I'll go. Farewell!"
6bdb486f-5fa4-4df1-bb1f-6939b02f3b02: "I respect useful books, but who needs shallow stories? Fables about a knight who slew a dragon won't help you, if you meet a dragon in real life."
f03fd080-a958-4456-a2ec-02be6f1bd517: "Then they'll write books about me! 'Linzi the Dragon Slayer'! Or no, more like, 'Linzi, Who Was Not Afraid To Challenge a Dragon, And Got Heroically Eaten In Her Prime!' Sounds good, huh?"
61aa2571-c0f9-4977-a980-7f982ec24887: "Octavia, why do you always primp your hair, huh? Why the hell you need to? Who are you going to charm here? Trolls or something?"
72add38f-336b-43ea-a83b-ac42a5685252: "Everyone has their little weaknesses. I like to look pretty. I didn't get a chance to do it much in the slave camp."
d4de0bbc-065d-40f6-9143-9de9e8f88881: "Sometimes I ask myself, why does Groetus give me healing spells. What's the point of healing those who are meant to die?"
597d065b-1a14-4df2-ab71-9cf3cfd8edb1: "Why does he give any powers to his followers, if he's entirely impartial to them, as you say? Perhaps this world is important in some ways, even for Groetus?"
d3fa2de0-5e07-4e4c-8378-389494599866: "I like your stories – and it doesn't matter how much truth there is in them. They bring peace and give us hope – something so many of us lack."
f71c1bd5-8b37-4138-a5fd-c261e8e1dc2c: "There! At least someone understands the true benefit of storytelling! Everyone keeps saying it's 'genre work' or 'escapist'… Thank you, your words are like an elixir to my soul!"
767748bf-1bf0-437b-8797-0d177db14e06: {n}The stonework here has crumbled, leaving a huge boulder to block your way. Fortunately, there's a large girder sticking out of the nearby debris. It may help in removing the obstacle.{/n}
19969b7d-7ed9-4459-bac7-579cffe513dd: {n}Pushing all your weight and effort against your makeshift lever, you manage to shift the boulder. It falls into the chasm, rumbling loudly.{/n}
a39d5a45-db0a-467e-b444-ccef36cded5e: {n}Pushing all your weight and effort against your makeshift lever, you misjudge your own strength, and the girder snaps in two. It's unlikely you'll be able to move the boulder now.{/n}
78669126-c4f6-4b25-a2a6-ee290b9d9f19: [Search the belongings for information or valuables]
6dda8ae7-ba13-4609-9f44-9ed3f2730da0: [Break the jars and spill the wine]
55985113-e2ca-444a-b467-cec523dd5323: {n}The bandits' belongings are piled together in a messy heap.{/n}
d47d221c-3432-4965-b05f-eabc2f2af94d: {n}You find a cache under all the clothes and blankets. Opening the lid of a small hollow, you find a box full of bottles. An inscription on the side reads:{/n} "Wine for the Stag Lord. Don't you dare steal it, fools! I'll make sure you rot!"
bb487527-282e-4c10-aac1-4ceac1f6ceb6: "Stealing? How could you even think that! I was just looking for the toilet."
e85881e9-9f77-40f6-9319-0053331329c8: [Attack] "You should have pretended not to notice me."
9b43afc3-0558-4a43-b15b-6385b19e5a10: "Pretend you didn't notice me, and you might survive to see tomorrow..."
68aa0175-881f-4b04-8a03-d9f0b3709980: [Bribe the barbarian with 100 coins] "This is just a misunderstanding. Surely we can settle this matter peacefully."
7683edb6-9814-45da-a723-ad8ed04ce7f6: "Hey! What're you doing? You trying to steal from us?"
ea45cc54-9f71-412a-8341-f115fc412e72: "Ha ha ha! You townsfolk are hilarious! {mf|He|She} wants a toilet! Just go outside and use the bushes!"
a06e00fb-63a5-4ab9-b405-25c1a8e4639f: "You take me for an idiot? Bad call!"
aa152421-7050-4daa-879f-603f4396199d: {n}The barbarian stares into your eyes coldly, then looks aside, steps back, and disappears.{/n}
3d29848c-49ea-4130-a1dd-665079b85f9e: {n}With a grunt of contempt, the barbarian quickly stows the coins.{/n} "You city folk are all just thieves, just wanting to snatch and flee. Fine, then, get lost before I give you what you deserve."
44ef4cb1-4d68-406f-9bfb-7325970ab71a: {n}Regongar draws his blade, which crackles with tiny sparks of lightning.{/n} "Shut up, turn around, and walk away. Forget you ever saw us. 9f2887e7-f058-4599-ad25-bfac9c6e1172: {g|Population9_1}[Choice effects]{/g} "My kingdom is in need of a noble class. Appoint those who possess enough power and influence to rule over their lands."
ec9a2343-42df-4b25-9890-d4ebd2e4234e: {g|Population9_2}[Choice effects]{/g} "The Stolen Lands managed without aristocrats before, they can live without them now and in the future. Let the people decide who they want as governors."
0b240766-ce44-4951-8a4a-9efd5c73b3d5: "{name}, your kingdom is growing, and its problems grow along with it. They must all be addressed, and this leaves no time for the trivial things. {mf|Barons|Baronesses|Kings|Queens} normally appoint others to deal with the little things. Sometimes it's the mayors and the local leaders. That's how an aristocracy is formed... a circle of power holders... But no matter what you call it, we can't do without such a group of trustees."
e8a7ffbc-e5a3-4db8-93ca-7dab689e9be4: "{name}, your kingdom is growing bigger. No matter how many advisors you hire, your officers can't address every problem and issue. A monarch should have vassals: knights, mayors, guild leaders, local chiefs and elders. It is they that form the natural aristocracy, the high society of any kingdom."
02761c63-ed47-4c3d-9824-c7f2c7631c13: "I will personally select those whose ambition equals their talent. They will be powerful enough not only to give people orders, but to protect them. c7132fc5-84f7-4e20-9684-7c30b9afddfb: "Perfect. I will announce to people that there will be no strange 'barons'. From now on, they are a self-governing the kingdom. This will make them so happy!"
1b98ba89-a909-4566-9b4d-96e8dafc5a4d: "Many knights and adventurers seek to become your vassals, and fill the vacancy left by the local bandits you've exterminated. But what if they want more than you're willing to give? This will only puff them up. They might even start bossing people around and hurting them."
885722db-f9a5-4cf8-b4e3-73a2d5f75b45: "There was a time when bandit chiefs were the aristocracy of the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g}, but we put an end to that. Many knights of honor now look to serve you, to become your faithful vassals and enforce the laws of your lands."
dfa1cdeb-c1cd-4dd1-9e2d-3fa247f9a238: "The bandit chieftains hold the greatest power in your lands. They already imagine themselves as the barons of your kingdom. Take it from me, giving them even more power would be... Just plain dangerous."
b038e604-9b51-4b0b-934f-a576b0a4c506: "Who lives in the villages and towns? The people! Regular citizens! Let them govern their own lives! Our cities and towns have elected their mayors. The villages have chosen their chiefs. They are the pillars we rely on, not a bunch of self-absorbed sloths!"
ff67b17c-bbe4-47a0-93a0-88ce1fba9f69: "Unfortunately, the only people powerful enough to be granted titles are the local bandit chiefs. I'm afraid this situation is all too typical for the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g}. Law and virtue is overtaken by brute force and deception. One might expect them to behave with dignity and respect if they become true vassals of the {mf|King|Queen}."
a213a1cb-2841-418d-b080-499972e6e7c3: "It's only natural that the law now rests on the shoulders of your royal vassals, not 'representatives of the people'. 395b93d2-41e0-4500-bfca-6140d4820c3f: "Look around. What if someone is following us."
f433f0e2-c432-48a3-a837-c01437aeb874: "You're always on the lookout for an attack! But just think about it: who in their right mind would follow a party including the invincible Ekun and a few of his insane friends?"
5f8324bb-84c6-41e6-bad4-a9f0091e1a7a: "All I do is look around. Everything is so different here, so unlike my homeland. Even the sky seems different!"
e6afaca7-ae0a-4d41-8eb3-ce7ef3c75014: "Admirers, I suspect. They're hard to lose, even in this backwater!"
a3662a38-3db4-4421-92cb-d64803085829: "Who might you recommend I meet here?"
2213b659-7805-472c-a039-b038f78cdc25: [Attack] "You look like a spy to me. Prepare to die!"
e827c8a8-0364-420c-bb08-ee88b7ccf868: "I've heard King Irovetti can be too persistent in his flirtations."
a97c7e3d-1325-49c3-b737-82a382c37623: "I believe Linzi had a question for you..."
fff8397b-f6b4-49d4-86da-b6706bbc7b5d: "If Irovetti didn't banish Eobald, then why did he send those cutthroats after him?"
9a1c5f7f-7299-4a43-b91f-bc787aa29507: "Why would Atalia hide the circumstances around Eobald's dismissal?"
8aead85c-2e8f-4ddf-b2d5-c47f687e3f77: "Thank you for telling us the truth."
17873b5e-0aa3-4098-9437-27ea620d4e9e: "Tell me, are the songs you compose for Irovetti as bold as the ones you sang at my capital?"
86883ab5-4ab3-48cd-b567-7ce15930e98d: "Oh, {name}, the famed baron{mf||ess} — no, excuse {d|Annamede}me{/d}, the {mf|King|Queen} of {kingdomname} now — has come to visit us! It is such a delight to see you here!"
0f59eb43-c145-4310-9c9e-dec8a2275eb1: "Our visit with you was quite a celebration — though it did end on a sad note. I hope there won't be any unpleasant surprises this time."
4b0e1b41-e60c-4629-8eb4-fd63f5862d41: "I've heard tales of your feats. It's a pleasure to finally meet you!"
020121b9-9eda-40e2-8671-252580f5f167: "Your hospitality was a bit lacking during our last encounter... but no hard feelings. Welcome!"
ff4f1517-065c-449f-b9e2-4f3264b58de1: "You could have easily asked any of my admirers who Annamede Belavarah is. That'd be about three quarters of {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g} — and the rest are all my haters, ha ha! You don't get to be the best among a city of poets and musicians without gathering a few enemies along the way. But why should I concern myself with hacks and soreheads?"
ed188fce-38ca-43ab-a5ef-553d8bde3a47: "Our beloved king has run this tournament once in several years since he took the throne. Guests from all over the {g|River Kingdoms}River Kingdoms{/g} come for it, from Daggermark to {g|Mivon}Mivon{/g}! It's a pity {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g} didn't honor us with any representatives this year — I guess the Aldori aren't in a very festive mood right now... On the bright side, we get to host you for the first time! And {g|Calistria}Calistria{/g} willing, it won't be the last!"
38b1ffab-a856-4404-bcd1-af7c9301aa7e: "That depends on what you're looking for. If you're in the mood for pleasant company, well, you've already met me! And if you're in the mood for some schadenfreude, you could listen to the whining of {d|Liacenza}Gasperre Liacenza{/d} — his family lost the {g|Pitax}Pitaxian{/g} crown in a card game. Or maybe Atalia Gitaren, the Headmaster of the {g|Academy of Grand Arts}Academy{/g}, who seems to think her skill at bureaucracy makes her a good bard... f1ef77b3-ee40-42a7-88df-a5be3bff6dba: {n}Annamede's face darkens for a moment, but she quickly regains her sweet smile.{/n} "Love him or hate him, you can't deny he's a great man! {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g} was a boring place before him — only pirates, fences, and other scum did any business in the area. I just pray that {g|Calistria}Calistria{/g} breathes the same love of the arts into the withered hearts of some of the other rulers in the region, who'd prefer to squander their resources on saber rattling!"
71e7e79b-8e9a-46d2-b480-ff0156d7acb3: "Some may say that King Irovetti doesn't have a taste for arts. Any successful person gets haters spreading dirty rumors about them. You should hear the things they say about me, ha ha! Pay it no mind. Our king is a man of exquisite taste, with appreciation for all kinds of art!"
e62b3d45-c7a5-438e-af04-e05d527f01a7: "Of course he has enemies. Lots of them — just like anyone who's actually accomplished anything in life! Take some of the old trade houses, for example — Liacenza and some others, whom he stripped of their power. They'd love to see him at the bottom of the river, but even now, in their mutual sorry states, they can't manage to work together! There's also Irsei Caelysse, Captain of the Guard — he was just seething with indignation when the king brought new rules to the city. But who wants to listen to the whining of failures like them? Irovetti brought a golden age on {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g}!"
c8606595-82bb-4d13-a806-1fcb7aadf315: {n}Annamede purses her lips for a moment, then replies slowly, choosing her words carefully.{/n} "I'd prefer not to discuss the private life of His Highness with strangers, much less my own. a3c6b2e3-f1e3-4488-97b0-8b079ff6fd4a: "Maestro Belavarah! I... well... do you remember me?" {n}Linzi blurts out, turning bright red.{/n}
aee1b10e-3b99-491b-9fea-f0663aad78f1: "Ah, Linzi! Of course I remember you. You and your nonsense at the poetics exam..."
64afe484-7185-4ef0-910d-7f8ff4957e45: "I hear you have your own publishing house now! I didn't take you for the entrepreneurial sort, but I'm happy you've finally found your calling!"
a9eaf679-83aa-485e-a15a-ea138e698f55: "I see you've found a comfortable position in {mf|His|Her} Highness's court. Congratulations!"
504b8e34-de7c-4d57-ae19-0d508938d908: "Oh, yes, he did move to your kingdom, didn't he? I'm curious how he portrayed his dismissal. 901cd00e-5d1a-4160-984f-7d6df75dfa26: "Wait! I'm sorry, but... I really need to know the truth. Why did Irovetti kick Professor Eobald out of the {g|Academy of Grand Arts}Academy{/g}?"
5a638855-be96-4c0d-ba60-da3aab2c54b0: "He'd planned to return the old man to {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g} and make Atalia reinstate him into the {g|Academy of Grand Arts}Academy{/g}. e1473bbe-db48-48cf-9740-a1ee8def635d: "Well... Eobald is a very fine teacher, of course, but he pays too much attention to how his favorite students perform in class, and not enough to their... extracurricular activities. Why worry if they steal a trinket here or there, or maybe rough someone up on occasion, so long as their poetry and music are exemplary? ada4b5db-fcc7-450f-905e-e777fc84de06: "She doesn't like to discuss the {g|Academy of Grand Arts}Academy's{/g} internal affairs. Behind that neat facade, there are too many events she's looked the other way on over the years — all in good faith, of course."
bb16f4c1-b605-43b6-8f80-65f18a72af31: "Atalia expelled the lot of them. And as always, Eobald went to stand up for them... but this time, he discovered that her patience was not boundless. 23ec2c0f-f257-4596-ab6a-3afb99040c23: {n}Pale, Linzi looks at Annamede with huge eyes, unable to utter a word.{/n}
da43862b-b18e-4d07-ad6e-32dcfb19e518: "I can't believe it... Teacher lied to me all this time? I'm going to learn the truth as soon as we get back to the capital!"
f891912b-6786-44a8-bb87-85d21a7e093a: "I'm not sure you should be thanking me — I see poor Linzi's not too happy with this truth... Hey, come on, girl — cheer up! ffe0163f-fdfd-4a6e-a995-79f08e0162ba: "Oh? I just hope it isn't about any of the lectures I used to give you at the {g|Academy of Grand Arts}Academy{/g}. Go ahead, ask away!" {n}Annamede smiles encouragingly at Linzi.{/n}
6b31eaca-ecd1-493f-b93f-409d439b3eb3: {n}Linzi turns bright red, takes a deep breath, and blurts out,{/n} "Sorry, but... I really need to know the truth! Why did Irovetti kick Professor Eobald out of the {g|Academy of Grand Arts}Academy{/g}?"
5d3765d3-093f-497f-865b-5aaf034c0573: "...He is also an unsurpassed singer, a skilled hunter, an excellent horseman, and able to bake fancy breads while juggling daggers! If you begin on the path of singing the praises of your superiors, dear, at least use your imagination."
68bec47c-6e93-4782-a164-aa59da7ac75a: "What am I hearing! A respected scholar, an author of so many books, articles, and memorandums... lied? Unbelievable!"
388c672e-42d2-47a6-8bda-a3abe031015c: "Just as behind any nice facade. That's what they're built for, after all."
58a76809-8ac9-4e3f-8f8e-2a7c1162549b: "In the hands of a ruler, even death is political currency... Though none wish to recall that, sooner or later, fate will use it to pay them as well!"
58fa11f4-d2d3-4b9c-afda-0b180509a6c8: "Have my humble verses so offended you that you still recall their sting? Please, Your Highness! 7b92952c-e336-4636-b2b6-cde0e8579c1a: "What do you mean, you were "not raised in a cage"?"
2238a0c8-9013-4e45-851f-efc5b160a548: "I'd like to know more about you."

203cf5cf-c48e-46a5-85a7-e878375fffa6: "I thought I told you to leave."
df517fda-9755-4df8-ba51-791f364df7f3: "If goblins don't write, how do you remember anything?"
d1f49477-5071-4a26-afb5-ed63c6b16ae2: "I'd like to ask you about goblins."
6c477b17-5710-4936-b366-dabca42145e7: "Right. You don't like Linzi. Enough about her."
dd050c80-0e84-4547-afaa-8ab8cfbf40d1: "But... that was a rhyme. And a song."
ba5b474c-46a4-4471-86d8-85c1cbdbcce2: "You... just did it again. On purpose?"
0925d0cd-6a41-4952-b33d-77c821e5a337: "If you are making light of me, I promise you'll be wearing the next hangman's noose."

37a2a5f4-405a-4356-ad43-4ef69b9a0a2f: "I still say you all mangle your speech. You're worse than most of your kin."
8933630d-fb82-4439-b255-e45130c1946c: "I heard your tribe is building shrines to Lamashtu near the capital."

7a49b836-ad30-46fa-ae2b-c16f13e9bfda: "I guess, I have no choice but to visit those shrines..."
939f35f4-372e-413d-acb2-2df1cf28b669: "I haven't heard much about goblins since the Trading Post. Where're they?"

98f7c5b4-d764-4593-8cc5-ccd94b383dda: "You've been more than a Hero and you've proved it. You dealt with the, uh, Mighty Munguk, saved your tribe, erected great temples of Lamashtu, and survived a goblin king – twice. And won."

deb8d699-44ea-4ae1-86a5-c158ca31c998: "Get some sleep, have some food – there'll be dangers ahead to take your mind off things."

b855589e-70ec-42ab-901a-c00e1574b41c: "Why not embrace it? If you can disarm problems with a trick and have them laughing along with you, then you're more king than most."

3d06c6fa-fdaa-4a0f-8d9e-3bc3240b8d9e: "Look, take it or leave it. You want to be a hero or not?"
abdd0b6c-8181-41c5-9cbf-68a1e30eb5c3: "Uh, to be clear, this isn't a paid position. And no murdering and stealing, either."
868f028f-8f3b-4e80-9feb-ba4995977406: "Nok-Nok, I pronounce you Hero of the kingdom {kingdomname}, Hero of the Stolen Lands, and grant you a title that can never be taken from you: that of fellow Hero to {name}. Rise."

834b957a-ba14-4d54-b361-5f9236c998b6: "I'll let you sort that one out in your own."
f80325a1-49cc-47dc-8bd8-65431545f646: "Do what you need to do – I have other matters to attend to."

f79d8ba6-144d-4034-99be-accea5a76257: "The only open question is — what role will you play in our confrontation. I suppose all I can do about that is to wait and see. Until then — farewell."
466a7230-6b5f-495d-a813-af6467a17816: "Excellent! In that case I'll establish my capital immediately. It will be a thriving trading hub, and its king will count himself in your debt. You won't be disappointed, you have my word on that. And I always keep my promises."

96c8e176-84d0-4abf-9c2e-a9c3b0602ce0: "Such a beautiful story! And the name! It reminds me of my favorite pirate books! Oh, so many stories are swarming in my head..."
80d6e16b-9b96-47c0-a8c7-add05fd2e80b: "Considering the questionable motives of honorable Darven, here, I would typically advise you to decline. e94ff1a9-4b1c-4f30-ac11-c88e5cf0a76c: {n}Octavia laughs musically.{/n} "How romantic! I would be curious to see Brineheart, if you're ever lucky enough to turn it from dream into reality..."
fc207042-23e9-4c05-ad89-a3e614b02c56: "Give them to me. Nok-Nok knows what do with them. No tell you — don't ask."

2a8e4524-66b4-4763-823c-e98e430007c6: "I used entrails for a stew. You ate with others. So don't beg."
fd34afc5-34ad-41cf-8988-a3a4f7240746: "What do you think of your stay ashore?"
f41a2f88-be92-47ab-a659-a185492d934c: "You talk about Blakemoor with such confidence – do you know him well?"
b5aa3e9f-c6d3-4cee-bb10-6943b4169ef8: "Because I will help you set sail again."
b7897405-8873-46cc-9508-cb26d95b641c: "Because otherwise I'll turn you in to Wellar."
afffbcb0-cb93-44fd-9880-31d0943c21ce: "Because my gold is looking for a new owner. Ten thousand coins."
61d825f5-a1bf-4a93-b4ad-8a29dd2d7a24: "Because you don't want to die of old age in this tavern."
5399d60c-48bd-482a-8af3-539b3d66be7a: "Because the crew is drunk and they won't notice if I break your neck."
9abe966d-b1af-4194-9417-e754087e121a: [Attack] "You're insolent. And you'll pay for that."
bd51b4bc-4b35-4bb2-88d5-d046575b1631: {n}A grim man with long brown hair and an unpleasant face is drinking in the corner, alone. He doesn't seem to be pleased with your attention.{/n} "What do you want, {mf|mister|missy}?"

01922f57-9dc3-4b1b-ad16-3a6b58603bb6: "Because I don't need company. That's a hint, in case you didn't notice." {n}The sailor sighs heavily.{/n} "Why is it, that when a person drinks alone, everyone wants to join him? Over there, there's a whole crew of sailors, eager to share their tales..."
030a905f-13c8-4b9c-80fd-dbaad8d7b1c7: "Ha ha! We should never have relied on Blakemoor's punctuality. He's a special person, that one. But never expect him to know what time it is. As for me, I don't care so long as there's enough beer."
4bc91873-193a-4ad7-94c1-bbdd9ffb7949: {n}Blutmond winces, realizing that he's said more than he intended.{/n} "By the kraken! Okay, just stop yelling ... please lower your voice, {mf|mister|missy}. 5d505b1c-7361-4b06-8066-598df9475077: {n}Blutmond takes the gold with a lazy gesture.{/n}
2092e3d1-a701-47c2-94b5-2f6cafa332bb: "That's quite an offer! You rarely meet a stranger who cares so much about your own concerns." {n}In the blink of an eye the sailor pulls out a map and pokes it with his finger{/n} "It's here."

bd0b0d33-20e6-4d9d-b6ab-e1c6f2ff2620: "And why should I tell you? Like I just said – Blakemoor doesn't like guests."

f6977018-39a2-4d52-b1ef-7b7d5a015abb: "Oh, you're a clever one. Now can I drink my beer in peace?"
9f93b039-bc32-4ec3-83e6-ab5ffe7208f6: {n}In a single movement, Blutmond manages to take your money and leave the key in its place, though a second ago his hands were quite empty.{/n}
1c165c78-1ee4-4344-86c1-6df96131b6bb: "That's an interesting argument. It's true, I'd prefer to die at sea." {n}Blutmond gives you the key.{/n}
783dc0f4-0e3e-46c9-a751-7217df180a16: "I was told by circus fortune-teller that I would die at sea, during a storm. It's calm today. So I'll live for now."
26dc34e3-8789-42d0-99e2-637e136df1d4: "And I'll tell the captain that you're looking for Blakemoor so you can take that crappy folio for yourself. I'm sure he'll be delighted."
fe9f7d47-b698-4e72-b992-792b2200170a: {n}Blutmond pulls out a map again, and insistently points at it with an unclean fingernail.{/n} "I already showed you, it's here. You want me to draw an X? Or a skull and cross-bones?"
9edd264b-91ab-4583-9927-a1c490855620: "Hey! Guys! We're under attack! Stand your ground!"
34e9e792-34d2-498a-a4cd-58cef6b91a44: "Whatever you say. We aren't going anywhere soon."
86ba0e3c-5081-4f67-826c-866964451883: "Don't, Tristian! As you said, evil can tempt anyone! You're stronger than it — fight it!"
f95b6cdf-6bae-4788-a502-1bf8adc87f04: "Tristian! I don't believe you're doing this willingly! Stop it — for me!"
4a6abebd-e85a-42e6-82d2-b195999935ed: {n}Tristian's silhouette, holding the Oculus of {g|Abaddon}Abaddon{/g}, is a stunning contrast — a terrible darkness against the shining portal. 806c255e-634a-4edd-912a-f3458959b957: [Pull away] "I'm sorry, but I wouldn't want to ruin our friendship with unwanted... entanglements."
950f55a5-cfff-45ef-ba50-805819487ef1: "I want more with you than just a bed."
240fd78c-9fea-4c38-992f-94b1813b4caf: "I would never do anything to hurt you."
d078f7cf-64a0-485b-9d0b-8de8f7098071: "Can I count on a few hot nights too?"
4a9cda99-fe54-4771-8ca2-9fd54ca5523d: "Is this... some kind of test? If so, believe me, it's not fair — you are very hard to resist!"
b70081b8-9032-47f1-b5e1-9537087a03df: {n}As soon as you return to the city, Valerie invites you to the tavern — to drink wine and discuss the latest events. After a few hours, the conversation has drifted, and you begin to recount stories from your past lives.{/n}
cf8207c1-457a-41eb-8801-607efb785da2: "Just imagine: the poor archer, cursing like a sailor, is trying to tear his quiver out of the kobold's mouth, while the kobold keeps chewing on it! 6ad5ea08-70d1-4e9a-b9c9-e49a3c0f2c22: {n}Valerie thinks for a few moments, then takes another sip of wine.{/n} "His name was Toma. We met when we were clearing the poachers out of the Gronzi Forest. 29274b50-ee17-40c9-a331-db8d61719143: {n}Valerie sizes you up.{/n} "Of whom? Of a person in my distant past?"
94132348-e399-4655-aa7a-b6ed5152564d: {n}Valerie maintains a long silence. The air around her grows cold. You finish your drinks in awkward silence.{/n}
bd518819-7a48-4644-9c53-d89f4501a212: "Lovers... that's an interesting word. It implies a certain kind of special relationship. If you mean love — no, there was only affection and trust between us. bc5617e8-95d4-4b6d-ae8c-739ed9022090: "Why? Because everywhere I go, cheesy romantics and high-flown conversations follow me... Ha, though they don't any more — thanks to Fredero's scar!" {n}Valerie grins mischievously.{/n}
28f4ca63-d4db-44ac-827a-97e5a3032cda: {n}The girl tilts her head and looks at you sideways.{/n} "Sometimes I think... about how much you are like Toma. Not in appearance, not at all. I mean that being with you feels so easy. And I trust you so much."
9090f0e9-0bf5-4112-b8d5-97dfab3a6b91: "Really? What I offer isn't enough for you? You want it all, and now?" {n}The girl sadly shakes her head, then pulls away and drinks some wine.{/n} "All right, just forget it."
26836449-6d2d-4a8a-8a8b-9ee93f95d40f: {n}Valerie lingers, processing your answer.{/n} "Fair enough. Truly, we shouldn't." {n}She laughs awkwardly and looks away.{/n} "All right, I'll tell you another story then. Have you ever been to the Lake of Mists and Veils? Well..."
299692db-f5c4-4385-ab62-0f4278ed4794: {n}Valerie finishes her wine resolutely, as if gathering her strength, and climbs to her feet.{/n} "The entire palace is at our disposal. I expect we can find suitable accommodations."
789e5de8-9278-4a58-aa24-23ce7983ef2e: "With Toma there were no professions of love or promises that neither of us would keep — just affection and trust." {n}Valerie blushes.{/n} "… and some pleasure."
a49ce2a2-daec-4a3b-ad5c-d5585b01b4f3: {n}Valerie looks at you for a few seconds. You sense curiosity in the depths of her eyes, and... Fear? Insecurity? Desire?{/n}
54996671-afbe-4e80-a979-9b3b42f0bdca: {n}Keeping her eyes fixed on yours, Valerie rises and leans forward, towards your face.{/n}
1eedaa0f-a91b-4b7d-9763-93f17d9eb9d6: {n}The girl casts an apprehensive, almost resentful look at you.{/n} "You know, when I want to kiss someone, I am fully aware of my actions. You said you liked me... and I like you. Why complicate things?"
e12065c2-aec3-4996-a8fa-c54d3a34191f: {n}Valerie shuffles away from you, and apparently sobers up. The familiar mask of polite detachment appears on her face.{/n} "I'm sorry. I was inappropriate with my commander." {n}Valerie finishes her wine in a single gulp and gets up.{/n} "My apologies."
ac37cd6c-79a6-4df9-83f2-4b2c1126082e: {n}Valerie's grazes your lips with her own, then kisses you again — impatient, almost greedy. Pulling away, she runs her finger across your cheek.{/n} "So... do you want to get out of here?"
c331d6b2-4812-4b5d-a65b-916a98694df5: {n}Valerie chuckles and draws closer.{/n} "Relax, {name}. I wouldn't confuse you... not like that!"
f00bd158-e564-4c97-a7d5-587674650eb1: "I'm looking for someone. Can you help me?"
ef304203-141b-493a-8aa7-adbc5383dbaa: "Do you let everyone into your house?"

4cc5a672-dcd3-4590-ac1c-a3197515a6cd: "Poor choice of words. Forget what I said."

f2997929-1941-4938-9ee9-6aaf17925465: {n}The woman looks at you with caution, throwing quick glances towards your companions.{/n} "Your Grace..."{n} She chooses the words carefully.{/n} "What an unexpected visit. I am the hostess of this place, my name is Dumra. How can I help you at this hour?"
