cfbc0c86-f3ed-48de-9913-788b2131143d: "Oh... They'll be beyond hope. Their lives will be ruined... I feel sorry for them, you know. They had everything one could hope for. Status, wealth, fancy houses. Why did they have to go and ruin themselves with Razmir's poison?"
92f3ca9d-a870-4e2b-ba58-3576b5c2f4c6: "I don't like the severity of the punishment, but the fact that both of us regard them as criminals, not victims, is satisfying. Justice may be cruel, but it's better than chaos and lawlessness."

ff585ef8-2c14-4796-a934-ba117f272234: {n}Nyrissa stops, and with her last word, incredible, ice-cold silence fall upon the ravaged throne room. b8918a13-b25b-437d-b922-8c74a1a6c2c8: {n}The echo rolls farther and farther from you, like a wave, catching up the fragments of the cursed cup, sweeping away the shadows of the dead kingdoms. 0c708855-62a7-4a4e-b1b8-70c2b895d047: "Did I tell you I don't like dying? Well, I don't. Perhaps we should stop this pointless exercise and speak seriously?"

edb7ac4e-c96a-462d-a2a7-26c5d7e407b6: {n}After you speak, silence falls, deep as a chasm. Light pours from the eyes of the {g|LanternKing}Lantern King's{/g} mask — still the mask of paternal care, though you do not mistake this for what lies hidden behind it.{/n}

bde82e34-904e-4a4a-b981-0bcef3ac0aa7: {n}This is all the {g|LanternKing}Lantern King{/g} is able to say. You feel a heavy burden, invisible and ominous, lift from your shoulders and dash towards your enemy. An enemy who is now, after Nyrissa's words, mortal and vulnerable.{/n}

a9e02847-e29b-4acd-b3ab-9b87e22bfc45: {n}And with this final sound, the ground around you begins to tremble. Nyrissa rushes towards you and clenches your hand. 6527f37e-d56e-4bc4-8627-6f3087b5c556: "That is easy." {n}The voice of the {g|LanternKing}Lantern King{/g} sounds careless and relaxed, but you cannot say if he is truly calm.{/n} "I will return your kingdom to {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g}, and strengthen its connection to the {g|First World}First World{/g}. cec42e8e-b7b5-4173-9540-f4d5d5ccf109: "Tristian, my sister's skylark, betrayed you. He used you to infiltrate Vordakai's lair and bestowed my sister's curse upon him. 4eae6d01-609d-4519-982f-812273994074: We are not like you, heartless fey. As Nethys is my witness, Tristian is not my friend and never will be. But leaving him in your hands is inhuman."

b3e24e68-0ff2-4aff-8901-12c59a7985cc: "To hell with the idiots who managed to get captured by goblins. I want to crush their insolent chief who dares build a fort in my lands."
c89b04c2-9212-4982-8d2d-d66d1e5bac66: "The prisoners mentioned a shaman. The leader?"
beeb2c9c-0f6b-4261-b793-d74b3b2e2c79: "Can this goblin camp have something to do with the seeds?"
31c4ca5d-3c3e-479e-9791-b0f7ed116b0c: [Attack the prisoners] "I cannot risk other's lives — either my soldier or my people — by having you run free."
40482f8a-f9c0-4e8e-9b9f-2759a05fac10: "We discovered the magic seeds are transported by water. If the shaman is infecting prisoners on purpose, then anyone who has consumed the water can give birth to a monster. There's no time — I have to kill them all."
66516560-19b7-49cb-a691-92a85d864aa4: {n}Kesten nods. His armor is covered with cuts and scratches, there is blood on his gloves, but he himself is uninjured.{/n} "You are right on time, {mf|baron|baroness}. We were losing hope — no longer, now that you are here."
611a8c4a-14cb-4342-a41b-a715298e4e30:

{n}Kesten regains his composure.{/n} "Whatever the cause, the surrounding area is thick with goblins — only one of the scouts we sent made it back. 7bf4713e-7d78-4e44-b8e2-14071844a60e: "I wish you good fortune, Your Grace. Send the ones you rescue our way — we'll protect them."
6ab45b7d-1602-49b7-81d3-973d2c9631ca: "You won't be able to pass the camp without a fight in any case. Save the people while searching for the chief! They are your subjects, after all!"
7674b185-777b-40fc-98ea-1bfe7c452475: "The scout mentioned seeing a large white beast at the hilltop — he thought it might be a wolf. If true, the goblin king must be somewhere in the camp."
71837c06-cedd-4082-8e41-0c3f72e1f77e: "The only way to find out is to get inside. You'll have to get past the gates and see what's going on in there."
605056a1-5198-4bcc-9cac-a9b3ec0928e5: "Some are injured, many are exhausted, and every one of them is terrified after what they've been through. e7ae3ad8-e6c6-4d99-a929-9fa5ddb93902: {n}Kesten turns pale.{/n} "How... How dare you say that?! We know how to save them! I refuse!"

6cb428b2-130d-4ec4-b2cf-0d3104d7bc1d: [Lock the cage securely to prevent the owlbear from escaping]
f819618f-f2db-420b-9cef-a1fb89df865e: [Try to quietly kill the caged owlbear]
d6d7ef53-881c-4208-8cf5-7588d43efb2b: [Step away from the cage] "This owlbear will help us fight the Stag Lord."
c210aa32-0df5-4eb8-858f-f1b619ff2de5: {n}The caged owlbear seems to be worried. He growls softly as you approach. It looks strong enough to break the cage's door.{/n}

a22f33d4-e78f-4918-910d-952444e75a1e: {n}The owlbear is angry — that's about all you can understand.{/n}
0a38b8f3-d0e1-4098-86b0-e7783e708de1: {n}Your efforts don't seem to have accomplished anything — the cage door still looks like it would be easy to open.{/n}
9481bf56-67b0-465e-ac0f-ef67664b9421: {n}You wait until the owlbear looks away, then kill it with one quick blow.{/n}
c55ce94e-7916-469e-a0bf-58e8a21ace2c: {n}You accomplish your goal, but the owlbear gives a long, roaring scream before it dies.{/n}
436b90a1-2dcd-4e5f-b5ae-a65835b3866b: {n}The cage is locked securely. The owlbear looks at you sadly from the corner of the cage.{/n}
9c4c535b-0ba1-414e-a1b1-afd9677315f8: "Why are you watching me stitch? Do you think such a pastime unbecoming for a warrior?"
b6d58368-c21b-4652-9c4b-c45c85d28421: "You stitch like you fight. A steady hand. A neat seam. It's good to watch."
3aad87d6-7109-46f2-ad4a-10c9b646ecb2: "Ekun, have you heard about silent hermits? They take a vow of silence and just sit there without moving for days. And at night they quietly gobble up the gifts that the pilgrims bring them."
fbea9456-5a98-4caa-9ed9-df2d229b67ce: "What does this have to do with me? I don't sit still. And I talk – to those I have words for."
fd7b72c3-a382-460c-880d-617a570dacff: "Nobody believe Nok-Nok will become Hero. Even Nok-Nok doesn't sometimes. But every day, remind self to try, and keep at it!"
9a6d1773-ed31-4ae9-9a30-7dbedc55c387: "Hold on to your values. When the whole world laughs at you, only the strength of your beliefs will let you reach your goal."
adfb09f8-8174-4df0-9504-49ffac905692: "You need to have a hero's heart to be a hero. But it's not important what others call you. Just believe in yourself!"
ed2c9e0f-9e5c-41b2-bf27-61cf6c8f52d7: "I'd like to know more about you, Eldest."
cb17adae-80a1-41e0-8d52-68d0e2139601: "You were silent when we asked if the Eldest would help us..."
91b59a39-59b5-4701-9515-cc4d22e36d77: "And what will happen if the curse remains with the one who created it?"
546d1e83-0d30-461e-9cac-cc7e4181b73a: "So your advice is to reject the curse? How will that help us?"
9796b4b5-204b-4c44-ab5c-2b9ff8087ab2: {n}The last of the three {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g} remaining in the meadow barely notices you, yet you don't feel arrogance or hostility in his silent indifference.{/n}
b6216e86-04f7-4841-8ffa-bf671e6b39e3: "The lost prince is the {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g} of forgotten things, sadness and solitude. c1462e22-6af7-492f-b45a-57ed27efce2f: "I'm known as the Lost Prince. The Lost Prince, a lost {mf|king|queen} — we have something in common, don't we? a74d5ed7-bc43-45a8-bce9-7277850cfedd: {n}The Prince shrugs slightly.{/n} "A serious conversation abhors crowds. I'm going to help you."
71d9381d-e536-4db4-b269-a457b575a826: {n}The Prince lifts his eyes from the ground and looks at you, then at Nyrissa and back.{/n} "You must know much about curses, or you wouldn't be standing before me now. 3a7d8baa-c1a9-41a4-a50f-11628c94b779:
"I have no answer to this question, though I've seen it happen more than once. Many things can influence the outcome. Will, faith, and the powers of the curser and the cursed, are all laid onto a non-existing scale, and one of them tips the balance.

68ea4361-cced-401d-97ad-df128d481921: "He will be cursed." {n}The prince says this with the same sad indifference, and yet the words sound frightening, and poignant.{/n} "That is the order of things: the more involved you are in anything, be it a feud, a friendship or even the relationship between a master and a servant, the more unexpectedly this bond can bind you. 0b322ca2-70a4-447f-97d5-1b63237c9f79: "Not only to reject it. To return it to the one who cursed you. Tell him directly that he has no power over you, and let him choke on his own poison."
b7f41118-0049-4f03-9c2e-3fd9a6f7ffec: {n}Nyrissa bows gracefully.{/n} "Thank you, {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g}. We will heed your advice."
75697094-0af1-432e-a616-575c920fa77e: {n}The prince nods pensively and lowers his head to the ground once more.{/n}
864440dd-c784-4d65-a35e-acab3a0eb10a: "I'm dying to know how I come out in your book..."
3a31409e-48ed-43c7-ae8c-b54b03ee1935: "You know... You're so mysterious! And controversial! It's almost like I'm writing two different characters, not one."
75842ef7-2ead-405d-8ac8-9e624ac316f7: "What will you do when we win?"
21977be6-4f15-41c4-92ba-69189ab3d58e: "Will you help me in the battle with the Lantern King?"
2ca2c55a-2fea-482a-bc3e-8444c94ee9f0: "I see you've made peace with Evindra..."
cf0b7429-115b-4b8a-8311-44d579ce6598: "Did you figure out what we learned from the Eldest?"
a36096d7-3453-4b7d-844c-762e88f0dd38: "So strange. We've been through more than many have in ages, but we've barely ever... talked." {n}Nyrissa's soft smile lights up her face like the springtime sun.{/n}
21f4ea41-1632-4168-9879-ca4ebb02ee4d: "It pains me to see the wound that the curse has left on your soul. Oh, how I wish it were my burden alone..."
d9853f1c-e30c-475e-8985-152e5b56d2a4: "And my poor {d|c41 Good Sister}sister{/d}..." {n}Nyrissa stops for a while. cd744aac-694e-4106-b535-aa15315a3fa3: "My grumpy cousin..." {n}Nyrissa says with both bitterness and tenderness in her voice.{/n} "She'd never leave me in trouble. She would run to my rescue, scolding me the whole time!"

486b472b-9909-4693-812a-553f73e435c3:

d04c21c5-e3ae-48d1-a8ad-fc95ef3eabdf: "Take care. And come back to me..."
aa478cbe-f568-406b-9b5a-508002953f13: "I hope so, and I'm preparing for the final battle and what will follow. The {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g} put weapons in our hands. Now we just have to use them."

4f1de235-16d5-49d0-9d99-ec2b4c1737ef: {n}The petals of this huge flower are glowing with a soft light, and its scent carries a hint of spice which you find strangely relaxing. Despite this, however, you can't help but notice the sprouts and spikes of the plant look… fanged, almost predatory.{/n}
9c249993-3f4e-4103-95fb-764332a82d95: {n}Whatever enchantment the flower possesses, you are still able to hack it down easily, and the glow fades.{/n}
bc13565d-936b-485e-8389-6eef598945e5: {n} As soon as the poison falls on the petals, the petals blaze with a bright crimson light. The air around the flower trembles — either in heat or supernatural wrath.{/n}
92d96cb2-8d3c-441d-be42-bc3da292921e: {n}A shining magical aura surrounds the Everblooming Flower. It seems so familiar — exactly like the magic emanating from the bodies of the Bloom victims, but stronger — much stronger. There's no doubt: you've found the source of the disaster.{/n}

4c0a140f-8a26-45fd-b0c9-d8d9cdeaee48: "I want you to leave Valerie alone. She serves me and owes no debt to Shelyn!"
2098a229-7a25-4c0a-9e42-10bc1fda16d2: "I only came to escort Valerie. You can deal with each other without me."
90c8c7e4-ccbe-477a-ab1d-daee1921bfd0: "Maybe this trial will bring you peace?"
ff0a67bc-976b-478a-855f-821d4c515069: "If I were you, I'd tell these smug prudes to go to hell."
fc931d25-2030-4ec9-bdc5-6676cd4215ae: "Suppose we agree. What trial are you talking about?"
c10e4743-10ff-43aa-8490-28e2ec11fb4a: "I'm not interested in playing your little games. Valerie and I are leaving."
77417d06-b195-4806-ab31-badb32122add: "I see there's a whole company here..."
05e9f5d9-732a-436c-8a4b-7b28769c76a7: {n}A white-haired priest looks at you over his glasses.{/n} "Look who's here! {mf|Baron|Baroness|King|Queen} {name}! My respects. And I see you have brought company..."
51902624-1954-436a-9a0e-e10c5a50ec1a: {n}The paladin wearing armor strikes his open palm with his fist.{/n} "Finally! For a woman balancing on the edge of excommunication, you are sluggish, Valerie!"
2607703c-3037-434f-961b-2f9a0ac72949: {n}Valerie slowly turns her head toward the paladin and gives him an icy look.{/n} "I'm never in a hurry to meet those who would seek petty revenge upon the innocent for another's alleged transgressions."
ce93a358-422d-4bfc-a0af-81320dfbd32d: "Please, everyone be calm. Let's not hurry in with accusations and hasty decisions. In the end, we're in a sacred place. Arguments under this vaulting are unacceptable."
e1ff6035-bf46-4b1c-bf64-31a631a8d52b: "My name is Laryen. I'm a priest of {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g}, and leader of the local congregation. 18571705-7371-43ba-b13f-2daf840ef797: "We say the truth, and you call it 'dirty rumor'. We're the protectors of {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g}, and all who call her patron. a4d9e58b-3889-4ee0-a665-224fbc9e754d: "I will pass unremarked the vaguely veiled insults. 867f736b-3095-408c-ab00-e5c2e135fec4: "Please calm down. Although I do not approve of... the methods of respected Hegend, I will not tolerate jokes at the expense of a paladin of {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g} in her very temple."
7a69fcbd-aae9-478e-958e-b1a86c8e6545: "The temple of the Lenses is a new abbey for one of the orders of {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g}." {n}The priest looks up at the vaulting in admiration.{/n} "A beautiful architectural masterpiece, isn't it? ad820f84-9d46-4dba-a430-c41df6fb6dba: "We shall carry out all the necessary procedures. Valerie will answer for her transgressions against {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g}!"
e30832ea-fc89-474e-8516-1e5d18f0c545: "I? For my transgressions? {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g} has to answer to me! – For ruining my life for so long!"
b42846d9-c8ce-42b6-a015-278ae68ac2cd: "I tried to forget everything they stuck into my head in the Order, but I remember one thing for certain: {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g} is not revengeful or stern. I don't believe your words, paladin!"
486bd1b3-8f6c-4d5c-b71c-e20204e6a124: "As long as Valerie is in your lands, no creator who crosses into your borders can feel safe! 498fb5cb-624a-40a2-8917-ab69a6aca48c: "Divine responsibilities surpass all worldly vows and commitments. Valerie was promised to {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g} – and rejected that honor! Now Valerie returns to her Order – and insults Shelyn again! It's time to repent and answer for your transgressions!"
107b77d4-19ab-4793-b54c-f40a8e6e7c57: "You're right, Valerie: our goddess is not stern with those who misstep – which is why you need not fear the divine trial. Its name is just an old tradition."
28f5183e-9d47-4ecd-92eb-243e44dedf80: "Heretic! It seems there is no other hope for this soul, so deeply blackened by pride, than the divine trial. {g|Shelyn}Shelyn's{/g} judgment shall cleanse you of at least part of this abomination!"
8afe0793-6eab-4b5d-b479-ddae97e5b4f9: {n}The paladin puts his hand on his weapon.{/n} "Forgive me, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, but if you leave, this will mean only one thing – an insult to {g|Shelyn}Shelyn{/g} and disregard of her will. b42c6af9-966b-4edf-a120-4b959cbff944: "My respected companion is right. As Valerie has arrived at the Temple of Prisms, the divine trial must commence. Besides, would you come all this way if you didn't want to settle the matter?"
105afb65-f6a9-442e-b8f2-e2bc16d8378f: {n}Valerie clenches her fists in silence. It seems the scar on her face darkens and deepens.{/n}
2cfde41b-dbd5-4e2b-9e3d-72d26e7ca467: {n}Valerie looks down, and an expression that could be taken for abashment freezes on her face.{/n}
c8b0fde2-7263-42d9-9ff9-3171ceb3c73f: {n}Hegend grabs his weapon.{/n} "This is the last straw. You will wash away this insult with blood!"
d52f5a3b-a903-4e51-8be8-476598c1981a: "Thank you for agreeing, Valerie. Let's begin."
36c94682-a668-4731-bab9-ab61a7e99760: {n}Laryen folds his hands.{/n} "A divine trial is a special ritual carried out by followers of a god for someone who has lapsed in their faith. b0a7f898-2365-4c11-882b-35b688533f65: "Making peace indeed! Valerie, who rejected my lady, should not count on being coddled."
5cd00f78-96db-46f2-8923-bb257f04934e: "Of persistent disrespect and insolence towards {g|Shelyn}Shelyn's{/g} order, and the goddess herself. 1e913656-514c-4d18-9db9-08dae482b22a: "If {g|Shelyn}Shelyn's{/g} newest order appears each time another one stops persecuting me, my disrespect for your goddess will only grow. You are creating the very thing that you so diligently fight – but are incapable of understanding this."
2e5ece22-ae0b-497c-8f71-1b9ef25a67e9: {n}Eveld bows in a refined manner.{/n} "My respects, {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}! I came at the special invitation of Sir Hegend. How could I refuse a paladin of my beloved patron?"

12f79c68-82c1-4e16-8793-ae83e863fda1: {n}The wrinkle on Valerie's forehead softens.{/n} "We settled our argument in battle, Fredero. As for the scar, I've been wearing my wounds for a long time."
9be0e876-7000-441c-b6c4-1ee3db0c4bd7: "Ha! That's the spirit! If the conversation keeps up like this, a fight'll be on!"
76b5fcde-026e-4079-9898-c7d2a69cd0f8: "And you enjoy mocking Valerie and the {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}? Why are there so many hypocrites among followers of supposedly kind gods?!"
5b91792d-fdb9-474f-81f2-f2d7d233ad88: {n}Harrim looks up and around. The dwarf mindlessly thrusts his hand into his beard and tugs at it, mumbling something fiercely.{/n}
48ec01bc-dc6c-4082-99d4-44fb91f732c9: {n}The paladin notices Nok-Nok and chokes with fury.{/n} "And this... How dare you drag this abomination into the temple of the goddess?!"
d87552f5-373a-462e-81fa-86d91d38eb0b: {n}Nok-Nok grimaces and sticks his tongue out.{/n} "Yes! Stink is awful! What are those, flowers? Eeeew!"
2d519ee7-1369-4b6a-bc45-73dd9ada19db: "Who are you? Or what are you?"
b5e357d9-830e-4cea-90ac-79180ceb9b30: "I'm not inclined to trust strange voices in my head. Show yourself."
5e983eaf-fcba-496a-b4c4-6ef96105a2ee: "Where is this stone you spoke of?"
e0dd1b82-9942-4dbf-92c5-c4a99729c34f: "I'll... see what I can do. I'll go there now and take care of the 'predators'."
0c29e434-770d-468e-8e5a-3b31c9466e4a: "Reward? You will reward me if I help you?"
10cb8651-1804-4c65-bba3-df66c54389f5: {n}You hear a strange, faint humming noise, like a swarm of locusts in the distance — then suddenly, the noise rises to a painful shrieking in your ears!{/n}
edec4f00-5f07-4415-b4f3-15f0dbb5ed4a: {n}Suddenly, you find you can make out words in the din — the words are disjointed and hard to make out, but someone is clearly trying to speak to you.{/n} "Help, yes?"
cd8eeb23-0146-4211-8ebe-f6377f53b2f6: "Traveler. Way home. Friend. Jester. Jest. Escape. Trap. Pain. Wound. Blood. Powerlessness. Blood. Cold. Heat. Darkness. Darkness. Darkness. Light. Predators. Attack. Run. Loss."
f9d09267-9573-4907-92cf-41ae4f526d89: "Help. Help. Help. Help. Help..." {n}The creature keeps repeating the word over and over again, until it is swallowed by the painful background hum.{/n}
c549c81c-7454-4b4b-886b-7f8cfb954034: "Stone. Predators. Multitude. Powerlessness. Help. Defense. Cleanup. Path. Home."
b1feb337-36ba-40d6-a28a-3e74b2e107e5: {n}Drawing upon your arcane knowledge, you discern that the strange being, whatever it may be, has stumbled into a trap which turned out to be a portal, and was injured. You are not sure what the predators are it mentioned, but they must have attacked the creature while it was on this side of the portal.{/n}
96217ce9-23ab-4952-b816-864230576cad: {n}You are able to piece the jumbled words together with some difficultly — near as you can tell, the stranger is asking you to get rid of the mysterious "predators" that drove it away from the stone.{/n}
98ca8ee7-eccc-4e9a-b2ce-360ac045934f: {n}Rustling and whistling is all you hear in response.{/n}
b660d90a-1cdd-45dd-82be-118e8df3775c: "Who are you talking to? Me?" {n}Octavia looks around with a raised eyebrow.{/n} "There's no one here. Are you seeing things?"
fe7a2275-5d1c-4171-980c-40bb60a32179: {n}Ekun freezes and watches you closely. He remains silent, but you notice he is reaching for his weapon.{/n}
ddc60611-bb99-4421-9817-8862577aaa35: "Easy there! If you've decided to act the fool and start talking to yourself, at least stop shouting!"
460b4cfe-a1b9-46ea-80a6-9ccb4f3147b4: "What, is this a jest? I must say, you've picked a poor time to show off your... Sense of humor. Drop this ridiculous charade at once."
177930a7-836a-42f0-984b-84d516b7df95: "Help! Help! Hill! Top! Predators! Home! Home!" {n}The humming in your head fades, then vanishes entirely.{/n}
bf0fcc1d-acd5-4735-933e-bde5f557f6c9: "No idea who you were talking to just now, but seems we're in for another adventure!"
23bd9c9f-933e-4b0a-865d-2bc3779a366c: "Wonderful. Our fearless {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}, who, mind you, has not at all taken leave of any of {mf|his|her} senses, except for the 'common' one, has struck a deal with {mf|his|her} imaginary friends. My heart may rest easy! Surely, these 'predators' are nothing more but an unruly mob of meadow bunnies."
b890dabc-fa1c-423c-b425-f6f25d78b6f3: "Don't take this the wrong way, but... have you lost your mind? You were talking to yourself! Are you sure that we should do whatever it is you were talking about with your... errm-m-m... invisible interlocutor?"
122ba075-9180-4694-85b8-7c065d6a06db: "Presents. Bag. Items. Multitude. Hill. Predators. Banishment."
ecb2f74d-b676-45ad-a81b-298a25408a2b: "So why is everyone staring at me like that, hunh?"
c1b848fe-bf49-4745-84f5-fbca62ec4813: "Did I forget to wash my face after I ripped out that creep's throat?"
504acba7-9ff9-466b-9df0-13ca9c271cfc: "How did this sword end up in Amiri's hands?"
64a30ce9-f94f-475d-8d67-74b99ab6ea6d: "Why did you haunt the Six Bears tribe?"
eade030c-854a-44e9-8bfc-3be3ac3a33c3: "What will you do now that you have the sword back?"
64c15e34-e345-4a56-ba26-ab9e8376d2c2: "Sacrifice Akaia. Let him die with honor."
0f893a68-21fd-44fa-9405-623cb73dce4c: "I am also a chieftain. You called me your chief. Sacrifice me!"
a30b144f-8623-4b8a-94ca-90414150601f: "The ghost said he lost his immortality. Let's just destroy him once and for all! And when his brother appears — we'll deal with him too!"
bfe5a69f-7e4a-4ae4-8b49-3c18fb639092: "What happens if you don't seal the sword?"
3bc58cc1-b7e9-4623-9ca7-cd6d926077f8: "Amiri, you little thief! Mortal fool, interfering in the affairs of eternal beings. It is time to return what was stolen."
7b41affc-4b6f-4072-b563-c65fa668b0f0: "Shove it!" {n}Amiri throws the sword at the ghostly giant, who catches it and gazes upon it, twirling it in his huge palms.{/n}
3493561f-09f3-4a97-8f20-1e256e064560: "Fine work... You surprise me, mortals. Your life is but a breath in the wind, a snowflake in a hurricane. But nevertheless you can at times create something that will last through the ages. This sword is even finer than the one that was stolen."
8e00e13e-45ee-4127-9ce2-7067a862ea9d: "My name is Fionn. Once my brother Kean and I were powerful rulers of the {g|First World}First World{/g}. Together we were nearly equal to the {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g}... But not quite. "
48ba4a6d-765f-42ea-8a6e-4f25b4045e7d: "Eternal, serene life in our land was not enough for Kean. He wanted more. He wanted to become equal to the {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g}, and conquer new lands. First, he began to devour our subjects, drawing on their strength — and then he tried to do the same with me. As punishment, I banished his soul into the sword, which later fell into the hands of Amiri."
aa25421f-184f-42c9-ac82-3f774b68dadf: "It is the prison of my beloved, hated brother Kean. The murderer of family and friends. A ruler who dreamed of greater power, but who instead destroyed the people he ruled!"
83946898-b1d0-4cf9-9c55-0ddeec39148f: "You nearly released Kean by breaking the sword. And he may yet free himself, if the sword is not sealed! But do not be afraid, mortals. We have here everything for the ritual — the ritual that will seal my brother in the sword forever."
4c7909e3-122b-4878-9124-27595ff065c5: "My brother was very powerful. When I imprisoned him in this sword for his crimes, I created a very dangerous artifact. With sweet lies, the sword persuaded my servant to plunge it into my body. It drained much of my energy, turning me into this pitiful creature you see before you — a ghost, a shadow of my former greatness. My brother, in turn, used this power to escape into your world — but in this he outwitted even himself."
d7add669-e766-4a33-a92b-a298658dcf7f: "Our strength is linked to the magic of the {g|First World}First World{/g}. We are far less powerful here than we are on our home plane. Once here, the sword lost its strength, even its ability to speak. It did not bring happiness to the giant who found it. It did not bring happiness to Amiri, who looted the giant's corpse. Having broken the sword, you nearly freed my brother — but now we shall seal it forever. "
458aeb66-48e6-4432-907c-f861fed2ce5e: "After I was struck down, a treacherous spirit fled with the sword into your world. Powerless, a shadow of myself, I followed it — for I could not allow its prisoner to free himself. I found the body of a giant who once possessed the sword. I found the bodies of barbarians killed by Amiri. I walked invisibly among the tribes, listening to their speech and tracing their thoughts, until I learned the sword's fate."
ef7f1b54-8695-40db-a076-9b2a9c1138a4: "I demanded that the Six Bears tribe find the thief. This was only fair, for the sword was stolen by one of their own, and I would have it returned. If only Amiri listened to me at our first meeting, much trouble could have been avoided. But even immortals cannot rule fate. Everything happened as it happened, and now the sword is in my hands."
92c5e07e-dfdb-4652-b3dc-78af375bc653: "I will not avenge your theft. I never desired revenge. I only wanted to ensure my brother, imprisoned in this blade, would never break free. I once thought returning him to the {g|First World}First World{/g} would be sufficient, but now I realize this would not be enough. There is only one way to be sure."
13d2df5e-6082-4d99-ae7f-9c62a1c51cbd: "I will cast the spell of imprisonment once again, this time — on myself. I will place into the sword all my strength, which my poor brother so craved — and thus I shall share eternity with him. This sword will become our common tomb. After that, Amiri, you may keep the sword for yourself. But not before the ritual is over."
5c3bc9bc-9e1e-4a34-b51c-206048fb90c9: {n}The giant brings the sword to his lips, whispering a spell. A stream of light flows from him into the blade. Already transparent, the ghost becomes barely visible. {/n} "The end is near. There is almost nothing left of me. I am the shadow of a shadow. I am dust and ash. My power, my immortality — I give everything to imprison my brother forever. There is only one thing left..."
972234cf-378a-4cfe-b7fb-b45dee05dc9f: {n}Amiri whispers through pale lips:{/n} "Forgive me, sis..."
08ef32f2-3b8e-46aa-af6c-2b8d585c9726: {n}The giant hands the sword to Amiri.{/n} "To finish the ritual, the sword must be plunged into the heart of a chieftain. I would give my own heart, but I no longer possess a living body... However... There is another chieftain here. Do this, Amiri, and let eternity come to an end."
06175768-1341-47f9-96cc-59fb311e986a: {n}Amiri falls back, turning pale.{/n} "No! No, no... I won't do it!" {n} She turns to you. {/n} "What is this!? What should I do now?"
ccce5de4-4387-49b2-8da7-c353d992560d: {n}{d|Nilak}Nilak{/d} comes forward.{/n} "Fionn spoke truly of the threat of his brother's release. I must protect my tribe. Do it, Amiri. I am ready."
e6ffd308-2209-4c1b-a525-8460c642cae4: {n}{d|ChiefAkaia}Akaia{/d} pushes her away.{/n} "Step aside, girl. This tribe needs you. Hey, you, evil spirit! A former chieftain is good enough, right? "{n}The ghost nods, and Akaia thrusts himself forward. {/n}"Come, girl, strike! At least I'm still good for something."
71a83966-4d15-4c57-812a-ed46da2fb241: {n}Akaia steps towards Amiri, his back straight and chin held high, looking hard into her eyes.{/n} "Do it!"
ba3be468-9bdb-49c8-b0b2-9458747476ad: "I was once called..." {n}Amiri says thoughtfully, then turns to her fellow tribesmen.{/n} "Hey, men! Before my exile, when I kicked your butts — you gave me a nickname. Remember? Come on, say it out loud! I won't beat you for it this time!"
e914c534-f254-4d4a-8eb6-4444c92e78b8: {n}Amiri's face brightens.{/n} "Really, what's wrong with me! Hey, ghostly! You're finished!"
99711a60-7d42-441e-b9d8-275e5a466a2b: {n}The men glance at each other, one of them hesitantly says: {/n} "The Soft Chieftain?"
22eb19ce-d27e-45ae-9ec8-c10abaa497d5: "No! You're mad! What are you doing? He will return! You will not stop him!"
56b2bb73-08b3-46dc-964b-2cc4a38c5115: "My brother will free himself. He is as an endless storm — greedy, cruel, unpredictable. He will do great evil, and he will start with Amiri and her tribe. He remembers you well, but I cannot see his mind — perhaps he will seek revenge. Perhaps you will become his plaything... Either way, you will not survive."
85a4132a-2fb5-4c77-8332-7eee0b87adf2: "True... You can't throw a rock without hitting a chieftain here. I'm also a chieftain — remember, how you presented me to the {g|Tiger Lords}Tiger Lords{/g}?"
832904fa-3b5a-4daa-bd43-9a327425eaca: "Hey you, ghost-face! You got your chief!" {n}With these words Amiri places the hilt of the sword on the ground before her, and throws herself onto the blade.{/n}
55118d40-c127-400f-9b19-b1d74f74c8ec: "Oh, no! If I must spill the blood of my kin today, it will not be hers! Start praying, old man!"
5bc62914-1d2f-491c-ad18-99b23386ce1a: "Relatives... It's the same story everywhere, whether in the world of mortals or of demigods. Relatives are the first to become mortal enemies."
d2681df9-99bb-434a-83ab-d5d4ef547a67: "Fair? They didn't even know what they suffered for. You punished innocents. Don't call this justice."
d50c58c8-f83a-4853-a993-84f2405709d2: "A criminal's tribe always answers for him. So it has always been and shall always be. There is no justice more ancient than this."
239849d3-3a7f-40df-845a-bddf17d31bc0: "Wait... So all these troubles could have been avoided if we'd simply talked when we first met? That is to say, if someone hadn't started swinging their sword around without even a chat? Well done, Amiri! Well done, indeed!"
807eb1a8-0048-43b2-9ac8-2897330c7add: "It's mortal pride. We leave this world, and so leave behind what we created. That's {g|Torag}Torag{/g}'s teaching."
7e7adebb-a273-4d9e-908b-df249b1c04e8: "And what point is there in that? This sword may exist a thousand years, or ten thousand, or even a million... But even then, it will not survive the End Times."
a672d275-889f-4e9c-bb01-5bbff1264392: "Don't laugh, gnome. In the hands of fate, we are all but toys — both mortals and gods alike. One word said today can create or destroy a kingdom over the course of a century. It has happened before. It will again."
14a3bea9-fda7-4f90-9faa-ae1bbf84f8bb: {n}Valerie lowers her head.{/n} "He may not have been a good person — but in the end, when it mattered most, he acted as a worthy ruler."
5b6dec8a-a44f-4d82-95bb-3045b2cf88cd: "What took you so long? You want a sacrifice, porker? Suck it!"
010abf42-fb40-42c4-a0ea-ceacf96ddc40: {n}With a dead-pan face, Amiri swings her sword.{/n} "That's it."
ac722019-0930-4fc6-b940-75fb085b5d11: "Hey! HEY! Don't even think it! I still need you around to become Hero!"
0f745e22-dc73-40f3-9553-6e91d941d423: "No. No! Never! You hear me? Nilak will survive! She has to!"
f7da5e15-f0d1-4c10-a0d8-ef4c25f61436: "If it wasn't for you, I wouldn't have survived there. I'd have died under the lash, or jumped on a guard's spear."
f482fbb2-1b94-42f2-81b1-a6951c859aa9: "I wouldn't have survived without you either. Your rage gave me hope, even on the edge of despair."
b52e442b-9fd3-42b3-b529-f51067c89781: "I need to think of a title for myself. Nok-Nok Allterrifying. Or Nok-Nok Allconquering."
fddcad3a-68bd-4698-9cb8-0f6a622dd600: "You did your duty by warning me, and I'm grateful. I'll set off to find them immediately."
8ba25aca-ea4e-4758-922e-ed08fd3412ba: "Where do you think they may have gone?"
3216542c-7b59-40a8-af40-1ed43edf64b2: "Hmm... what if they got into a battle without me. Can't let them have all the fun — let's go find them."
0ba99b7e-02b8-4112-bf6e-1d5609dca427: "They can fall into Rovagug's jaws for all I care. Get out of here!"
1a2e4fbf-cb78-4cad-9598-e2ab55ea126b: "They will have to deal with it themselves, I can't leave my responsibilities here to chase Ekun."
5ba44c15-25f9-4787-94ff-6feef41f4715: {n}Elina's face is pale, and her red hair is a mess.{/n} "It's awful, Your Grace! Ekun is missing, and {d|Ntavi}Ntavi{/d} too!"
2de78c92-20be-4b3c-8bc1-05b55bf2ca75: "He was happy for a while after our fest. Things were going well... but then he started feeling down — restless. His thoughts may have turned to his family again. And then this... {d|Ntavi}Ntavi{/d} kept turning up."
ac64952e-682d-48fd-8473-9900e9ea6846: {n}Elina looks surprised.{/n} "A-As Your Grace wishes... thank you!"
71fc8c02-03bd-4523-82c2-337a47e88c33: "If only we knew for sure, Your Grace! There is one spot though — a bridge over the {g|Gudrin River}Gudrin River{/g}... travelers have gone missing there, they say it might be the work of giants. Ntavi was close when some woodcutter told me about it. And I'm thinking, maybe this woman dragged Ekun there?"
f8c0380c-c50d-4a79-9333-0c5e1c343ceb: "And the more he talked to Ntavi, the worse he got. She was whispering something in his ear, and he kept ordering more and more wine... then last night they left the inn, armed to the teeth! I tried to stop them, but I couldn't... they haven't been back since!"
ba563ecb-021a-49c6-be72-2b73275c4de0: "In {g|Erastil}Erastil{/g}'s name, Your Grace, please find Ekun! My heart says this won't end well."
a22c77f7-69a8-4439-90aa-ac4711c0a404: {n}Elina looks at you, terrified.{/n} "F-Forgive me, Your Grace... I'm leaving..."
0287ca0d-8908-4f04-8e59-c0b00aecfac7: "I... I see, Your Grace. Oh, I hope nothing bad happened to them..."
92e74f3d-9f47-4000-8194-fe65884620e6: "Lightning is good, of course... But still, all this magic is just fooling around. What matters in battle is a sword!"
e1890bbd-4671-461c-aacc-20207037f5dd: "Ha ha, you're just jealous that I can do it and you can't!"
f35bbd9f-e6e1-4bea-922d-25410362d9bd: "I'm glad we'll be together for our final battle."
3a9266b8-d9e2-4c89-a666-aebace19cbb0: "I nearly lost my crown – and my life – but still you stayed with me until the end, Kanerah. Why? I'm not much of a patron nowadays..."
db9d3421-da3a-4d4f-b6a1-fd686147518b: "You look so preoccupied, Kalikke. What's on your mind?"
5b1f3ec5-b0f2-4f4c-94f3-5701553505ae: "It's time for us to visit the Lantern King."
c2ad0e75-e95f-4a6c-8e2d-dd439a0dcec0: {n}Kalikke seems deep in thoughts, but gives you a warm and sad smile.{/n}
815691f2-22e2-4145-aa29-665a71f738b4: {n}Kanerah seems to be calculating something in her head, but chuckles when she notices you.{/n} "I'm ready for battle!"
2ba77044-2914-47ad-90b9-be2f86cd2d70: {n}The sisters stand quietly side by side, focused and resolute.{/n}
2ba9e035-26e5-423a-942f-bc2caa96a3fd: "Don't take me for one of those fidgety creatures who change sides at the first sign of danger. That's no way to achieve success in life. And as for you..." {n}Kanerah winks.{/n} "Let's say in your case I'm drawn by affection."
9a5b4d81-c8c2-4387-857e-b4cbb5ebea9f: "Of course you're glad! What would you do without me!" {n}Kanerah laughs, letting you know she's joking, then stretches and turns a bit more serious.{/n} "I can't tell what is to come, and this makes me uneasy. But my gut is telling me we can handle it!"
e1d74160-1cb3-499c-94f4-c2739946842e: "This land can only have one ruler!" {n}Kanerah smiles a predatory smile.{/n}
5ee54baf-4ebc-4839-b619-bdd42d702267: "We'll do whatever it takes, to recover what's been taken from us and save this miserable land."
6d006bac-9568-4ba2-bdf8-5d99f5c92966: {n}Kalikke sighs and blushes a little.{/n} "Just – terribly silly things. I've never done anything like that before!"
7ac87dfa-863c-4b8f-b3f2-522449f125ff: "It turns out that it's not so easy to be the heroes of song and legend... but we can do it. I know it. I believe it."
7724fcba-1f14-46ed-a070-aaf33bdea03c: "Hey! Careful with the spells! Keep your acid away from my writings!"
a7002234-0d1d-4d51-8ce8-8ac7f1be7321: "Who cares about any of your piles besides you? Go ahead, waste your paper. – Maybe it'll keep you quiet for a while!"
75efd9c5-0b7a-409d-9530-cd33392fabf0: "What are you jotting down in your notebook all the time?"
a83fa869-143c-44cc-a998-b6481d2e4c24: "Tell me something about the history of the gnome race."
33210c13-e5ce-424c-aa4d-813a74cd5fce: "You must know a lot about the First World."
4580b7a6-4472-421a-8ffe-0ae0ac1ef95e: "Tell me, why have you studied the First World so thoroughly?"
1bc10b99-b190-4b42-9430-34408747e71d: "Thank you for the conversation. I have to go now."
05c6742d-e0e7-484b-b90a-f7565cc2263b: "You've traveled so much! Tell me of your travels abroad!"
810082f5-9b77-4fdf-a3a9-6a407bce5d2e: "So you write books and magazine articles?"
b3fe02c2-1eb5-4b88-a6f6-5513326430c6: "You wear glasses. Why won't you ask some cleric to heal your eyesight?"
08b30732-ee8c-4963-be5a-9ba452176777: "Thanks for telling me about yourself. Let me ask you about something else."
0f5618de-7763-42b4-8dc2-a79ed288c0c7: "So you travel so much as a way to fend off the Bleaching?"
ba204652-39e0-4a71-9f67-e9393f62e2b9: "Let's change the subject. I'd like to learn more about the First World."
5cc8764e-d9e6-470b-a087-31dbfee7bd92: "Thank you for your story. I'd like to ask you about something else."
a675d4dc-50c8-4488-8493-a2c7d5438487: "Are there any sentient beings in the First World?"
cc57f3d6-38c7-45a7-9bc3-379928c10dc2: "You know a lot about the First World. Have you ever been there?"
63d31642-9afe-48cc-8740-6b94dd5af0e1: "I'd like to talk about something else."
da95a726-b393-4ff7-86b2-130c4c5a7142: "What are you hinting at? I'm only fulfilling my duty!"
19c6e614-11ba-43f0-99ae-05f7b78cd483: "I do what I have the right to do!"
53c17e0d-d5aa-4dd0-8fb0-0f8698f29341: "Even the most useful advice is better received if it's offered the right way. Your advice sounds like your only aim is to please your own ego."
a7284045-67e2-4c1b-8860-cfc4ca50aefe: "I will be honest with you too, then – you've become rather too fat lately. So accept this friendly help – tonight you go to sleep without dinner."
99374c1d-a036-4f24-96bb-18b9c878674d: "Very well, you can behave as you like."
f712146a-887a-4f5c-aa7a-4e8c14b0a598: "I've read your article about the barony. Should I be flattered?"
d29d2749-3d90-4963-a71c-97c278d4c11c: "I have received the journal with your article. I thought it would be worse."
adba61ee-b806-49bd-97f8-bb25e566a590: "I have read your article about the barony! How dare you publish such trash?!"
0839f4cb-0db8-4d2d-9d1b-67ea15432df2: "I'm fed up with you. You need to go."
e4034b93-fdd3-41ce-952a-bab772548b7f: "I certainly have. Now leave my lands at once."
5e0aebd9-3540-41b0-abdb-8a380e200b5c: "I wanted to talk to you about the Inconsequent Debates..."
edc28d6b-b82f-403f-b640-919bf777e82a: "Have you figured out anything about that riddle? – The Host's 'answer' to your question about the gnomes?"
29189a78-f4fd-490a-97c9-aa191e35ee19: "Remind me how that riddle went again."
dfbd9c1a-5b6d-4071-bc90-91dd8dce4407: "I was surprised that you didn't want to be freed of the Zottenropples' spell. Why did you willingly suffer it?"
ebb66bba-b20f-4a72-9474-b150c49d03db: "So you let them continue their prank to help them? That's a worthy act."
c03f2f59-18df-461f-bbc2-614f476c4c6f: "You shouldn't have played along. Each of us chooses how to face our troubles – with dignity, or by humiliating ourselves and others."
0b161e57-28a8-4796-9928-455e34765b94: "It's stupid to help useless weaklings, especially those who are trying to harm you."
962dcd21-0f94-4e52-8460-e5a8f7391823: "I found Gunderson's book – the one we were looking for!"
459803f0-f33e-40dd-988c-fa1c08b0dbb4: "I found Gunderson's book, and more than that – I solved the riddle! On the twenty fourth of the month, I found someone named Luna in the corner of a tavern."
f8618571-9992-48a1-8336-26727e95bdd5: "What are you going to do now?"
3ac2bccd-fa13-4417-8f9a-abbd6cc9f2ab: "What do you think about everything that has happened?"
bc78f8d1-08cc-45ba-9527-3b287f5b3972: "One thing they say about us gnomes is that few of us live long lives..."
25fafd23-edd8-47ba-819f-f113487444fa: "Of course. I've heard about it but never witnessed it myself. What does it look like?"
810bba41-4dc4-43bf-b5d0-7feff7e51f09: "You don't have to tell me. I've seen myself how the Bleaching develops."
e1e8958b-b77b-42af-b688-968e3aeaa628: "Ha! I became a baron{mf||ess} for entertainment! I think with all the commotion, I'm safe from the Bleaching."
ad579044-4ed3-4bed-8305-bab3dce07ec6: "You worship Desna, don't you? So do I."
5a5f581c-c4e0-4170-a0cf-2e49a0c350c7: {n}Jubilost raises his head and closes his notebook.{/n} "Ah, it's you. How can I help you?"
0ff9e8db-e3c8-4535-9e3a-f088eaa5001b: "Come back when you run out of clever ideas again."
e4c1cd5d-846f-416f-b1ba-33dd5442b24e: "Notes on our adventures. Good ideas that come to mind. I don't know how it is with you, but in my case, my mind is constantly producing thoughts and ideas worthy of writing down."
1188bd93-0aff-4fb4-a032-6dcefe898ecf: "Some I use in my articles and books. Others I will share with the audience next time I speak at Forae Logos in {g|Absalom}Absalom{/g}. Some other thoughts should be kept out of the public view for a while. Our world isn't yet ready for certain revelations."
2832449e-f522-42ea-b149-d321fd55ddec: "I've heard this request so many times… Well, as we're traveling together, I suppose I can give you an interview – free of charge, of course."
4862cfb2-426a-42cd-89af-1d0963064a3e: "All of {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g} is my home. I am a citizen of the world. Some might say my home is {g|Absalom}Absalom{/g}, that great old patchwork city. It's there that my books and magazine articles are published, and there I am held in particularly high esteem, owing to my vast knowledge. – In fact, once I was invited to the College of Mysteries itself! But I prefer to think of Absalom not as home but headquarters, where I go to plan my next adventure."
e79024df-4fdc-469a-bc9e-d8710d5505ba: "I've visited every country worth mentioning in {g|Avistan}Avistan{/g} and {g|Garund}Garund{/g}. I've even trodden the exotic lands of Tian Xia. I've seen miracles you couldn't even imagine. And in every place I've been, there was a home that would have gladly received a renowned explorer such as myself."
04e6ec4b-10cc-444f-a563-e4018b69bd26: "The famous name of Jubilost Narthropple is known even in the most remote corners of the world!"
36276562-991d-4140-9d4f-1d6737708853: "You know, the line between persistence and importunity is very thin. And you risk crossing that line." {n}Jubilost sighs.{/n} "Do you think I haven't mentioned my birthplace because of my forgetfulness?"
cc2c36a2-619e-4f1f-9ff6-976797187dcd: "I was born in {g|Taldor}Taldor{/g}, if you must know. The empire is in decline nowadays, but still cherishes the illusion of its past glory. It's a country torn by prejudice. In Taldor, my mind was trapped in a cage of restrictions – birthright, poverty, and their "beggars-be-damned" attitude. I left the country as soon as I understood it."
f2c2a014-7732-44ec-adc3-d607fe291af5: "So if you ever try to rekindle any patriotic feelings in me, you'll be disappointed. My first article in The Independence was about {g|Taldor}Taldor{/g}. The magazine was almost closed as a result of the scandal that followed – and it would have closed, were it not for crowds of my supporters, marching in protest under the windows of the publishing house, making its editors change their minds."
30d2f8d2-d833-4fa9-bb70-fd26f6c4aeef: {n}Jubilost tilts his head, peering at you.{/n} "I've written a fair number of articles and essays on my journeys. And if you'll excuse me, I haven't the slightest desire to retell them all to you right now. If you wish to learn about foreign lands, pick up any issue of The Independence and read all you like. I'm sure you can find my magazines even in this hole of a place."
ad1b0988-1891-468b-8f89-afcb6879d521: "I certainly do. I'm too generous not to share my thoughts and journeys with other minds who search for knowledge. Judging from your face, you don't belong in that category." {n}Jubilost sighs.{/n}
06b4941c-bf9e-4ac4-9dad-c12f48c4c5ce: "Among my scientific works, I'd recommend the range of articles published in National Alchemy. If you prefer lighter reading, you might like Traveler's Essays or the scandalous The Independence. If pictures capture your attention better than words, page through the Illustrated Atlas of {g|Avistan}Avistan{/g}. And you should give your cook a volume or two of my Culinary Almanacs. Trust me, it might help."
50c0e0cd-8e94-4bcc-9aa1-8347572d04e4: {n}Jubilost throws a speculative glance at you.{/n} "Some have tried to blame me for a sleazy romance novel called The Five Sins of {g|Sarenrae}Sarenrae{/g}. I have no idea on who spread these crazy rumors. But if you like such frivolity, I've been informed that the novel's sequel, The Sixth Sin, was recently published."
f891cb19-be99-4655-86ba-3878871e0685: {n}Jubilost throws a cutting glance at you.{/n} "I'm sure you could have figured out the answer to that question on your own, if you bothered to use a logical approach. At least I sincerely hope so. I prefer to think of you as of lazy person, not a stupid one." {n}Jubilost tightens his lips.{/n} "Well then, I suppose it's my fate to enlighten you. All right, there's no time like the present!"
1a02b5bd-6054-44f7-827b-e1a62e82bf6f: "Let's build up to a logical conclusion together. So, starting with the obvious... A cleric's services cost several hundred gold coins. Spectacles cost a dozen gold coins. So maybe I just couldn't afford to pay the cleric? Incorrect conclusion. I earn enough, besides, some clerics would surely help me free of charge, because they're fans of my incomparable talent."
42aa1b97-675c-464e-ada3-47e2dd16e4c1: "The answer can't be the money, then. So what is it? Let's explore further. Surely you've noticed that I'm a rather famous person? Just to be clear which circles I'm famous in: my scientific articles are well-known among the students and teachers of various institutions of higher education. My articles that satirize the rich and powerful are extremely popular among the minor nobility, traders, and workers – that is, among anyone who doesn't have any power for themselves. – The kind of people who don't usually have enough money to afford an expensive cleric."
ccb990d4-08d1-47e5-b47e-02b380341097: "Well? Can you add it all up and find the right answer yet?"
28de28c5-cd90-407e-9a4b-1005148176e0: {n}Jubilost doesn't let you get a single word in edgewise. Apparently, he's uninterested in your reaction, and is just enjoying listening to his own voice.{/n} "My spectacles are something that unites me with my readers. People are more open to those who share their social status. Many of my readers can't afford to heal their eyesight at the temple. So when I, too, refuse such healing, I become closer to the people. My spectacles are part of my image."
025ab867-5cfd-48f7-a15d-53d060b7422c: {n}Jubilost exhales at last.{/n} "I believe I've managed to explain the basics of logical thinking. No need to thank me."
9fe91d2c-f86d-4a74-8a54-460fc4da3f49: "What have I come to? Jubilost Narthropple, famous explorer, writer and scientist, is reduced to giving simple lessons in history. Very well, ask away. What questions do you have?"
29877328-59c0-4c7a-bd26-fd2405797c04: "What has the world come to? To see a gnome ask another gnome about the history of the gnome race. The gaps in your education are so huge, I doubt that even I would be able to fill them."
24ff2cbb-876e-49f0-8db8-45534da4f3c2: "They came here in ancient times from {g|First World}the First World{/g}. You do know what the First World is, right? If you don't, ask me about it some other time. I used to lecture on it at a couple of institutes."
594ba745-ec00-493b-903c-98dabf9f8af4: "Certainly. Long and happily ever after." {n}Jubilost shakes his head in remorse.{/n} "We'd live as long as elves, were it not for the {g|Bleaching}Bleaching{/g}."
63945e9c-98dc-4a20-967c-27048f4faa30: {n}Jublilost stares at you, then nods slowly.{/n} "You see, I enjoy being alive. I like to eat pancakes in the morning, I like to write articles for magazines. I like it when I leave the publishing house in {g|Absalom}Absalom{/g} and a crowd of fans immediately mobs me. So I don't intend to die at the peak of my life because of some stupid, ancient curse."
ffe5e214-5271-4c8c-a303-5317f1bdbb0a: "According to the understanding I've accumulated, the gnomes were an immortal race until some of our especially insightful ancestors came up with a brilliant idea. They decided it would be fun to learn how it feels to be mortal. I would like very much to meet those gnomes. I wouldn't even kick them, I'd just look in their eyes without a single word. Too bad they're all long dead by now."
35d83f70-f979-4db9-a6da-4b1b8a82eac5: "As everyone knows, a stupid enough idea can be extremely contagious. So the gnomes caught this infection – all of them, without a hope for cure. So they found a way to {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g}, and decided to settle here. And – you'll never believe it – they got just what they wanted. They severed their link with {g|First World}the First World{/g}. They gained mortality, the {g|Bleaching}Bleaching{/g}, and a heap of local diseases that have been keeping our race on the verge of extinction ever since."
b4d45585-4536-4d87-abb8-e4431527c479: "That's the curse of our race, which only struck after the gnomes left {g|First World}the First World{/g}. To put it simply, gnomes must constantly have new experiences. If a gnome gets into a rut, so to speak, he Bleaches."
78afbd1b-9edb-4847-8651-dae3d52416de: "We start to lose color – literally. Our skin and hair become pale, and the worst thing is that our soul loses color, too. If the process continues unchecked, the gnome dies. History recalls only a few cases where gnomes actually died of old age. Most of them perish either because of the {g|Bleaching}Bleaching{/g}, or in the middle of some crazy adventure they've joined, just to stave it off."
497cb666-6b65-48bb-8690-8dad8457153c: "But don't you dare imagine that everything I do is just for fear of the {g|Bleaching}Bleaching{/g}! I tell people the truth about the world that surrounds them! My theoretical research aids the development of different branches of science in various institutes! Yes, sooner or later I'll Bleach and die, like any other gnome. But the name of the famous Jubilost Narthropple will live throughout the ages!"
db999dc1-7069-40ad-bbda-c4a775e7f6f9: "Well you've asked the right person. I am an expert in studying {g|First World}the First World{/g}. Give me your questions."
5f1a6f0b-8a61-4436-ad2c-0fdc2dd0ba22: "It's huge, wild and extremely unfriendly to the unprepared traveler. Nothing remains constant there. Matter changes before your eyes: what was a mountain yesterday becomes a river today – and that river flows upwards. The trees touch the sky. The heat of the desert can melt metal. And hurricane winds can tear a person apart."
1a63a8a1-e50f-4519-b17e-6598dce336e6: "But it would be wrong to think of {g|First World}the First World{/g} as the plane of total destruction. Creation is just as important there. The deserts spring alive into forests, and when the hurricane subsides, animals emerge from hiding – huge, wild, as untamed as the world itself. The First World epitomizes life in its original chaotic meaning."
ecabace8-d6e5-4f94-8765-925bade71d71: "There's a theory that gods used {g|First World}the First World{/g} as a training ground, to practice their ability to create matter. They then abandoned the First World to its own fate, and wandered off to create {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g}. Some say that the inhabitants of the First World still hold a grudge against the gods for this."
d2c9f0fa-d889-435d-a479-aad9f5b65de5: "Mainly through magic portals, created by skilled magicians. But the price of such a portal is usually in excess of several thousand gold coins. There is another way, of course. There are documented cases where spontaneous portals to the First World have opened in remote places on {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g}, where, as mages say, the boundaries between the two worlds has grown thin."
6688b965-30f8-4c6c-9b73-6dc290b49e21: "But spontaneous portals are rather dangerous. – You never know what's lurking on the other side. Only desperate adventurers and madmen use them – and of course romantic suicidal idiots who think that good common sense is too boring."
7ff32997-86de-4050-9877-b39861fbf0e5: "Of course. The fey. And all their relatives, and all their relatives' relatives. And then some more fey besides. Sometimes one meets leprechauns or satyrs there – which are actually another type of fey, just called by another name. And all of them are immortal, by the way – at least within in their own home world."
2f352822-6f6f-457a-86e2-8773c79cbfb5: "The souls of the creatures of {g|First World}the First World{/g} have no connection with the realm of mortals. When a creature of the First World dies, its soul just materializes in another body, similar to its old one. It's not a pleasant experience, and the resurrected creature loses almost all of the powers and abilities it developed over its life, but keeps all its memories and personality. It's still much better than a mortal death, I would say. Sometimes the process doesn't even take long – a killer might meet his victim again the following week."
838a717b-d712-4111-a822-8f927d0b6823: "Naturally, this immortality has influenced the way First World inhabitants think. For instance, fey enjoy mischief and tricks that can easily end in someone's death. The fey think it's just funny, and anyone from another world, who falls victim to such tricks, doesn't end up having much to say at all."
c437d297-788a-4610-8df1-246f848e0a92: "Once, the gnomes were immortal relatives of the fey." {n}Jubilost sighs.{/n}
0552891e-aa77-43a4-ac35-bbc53f7c3305: "It's commonly assumed that the Eldest rule it. They are overseers, but more just a glorified version of fey lords. Power attracts pompous blockheads in every world."
3ea214dc-ad55-4d44-b66e-7d060f32963a: {n}Jubilost stares at you with interest.{/n} "Yes, yes, duty. Protecting your subjects and restoring order. Objectives so noble I could weep. Unfortunately, noble objectives can coexist perfectly happily with pompous blockheads. Are you quite sure you're not one of those?"
852d131c-88d2-4489-ba77-8f41bff5a989: {n}Jubilost stares at you with interest.{/n} "Yes, I've met plenty of pompous blockheads who believed they had the right to do whatever hideous thing came to mind. So if you decide to join their ranks, know that you're not the first to walk that path."
1f17e841-808e-4074-9b28-3a720bf5fafb: {n}Jubilost gives you a critical stare.{/n} "It's fortunate, then, that this problem doesn't trouble your lands at all."
87951332-4fff-4c8f-b895-1f042a5ce796: "But let's get back to {g|First World}the First World{/g}. The {g|Eldest}Eldest{/g} possess the power to keep matter in the First World in a more or less constant state. That's why the fey treat them as demigods, and offer them prayers, just as we offer prayers to {g|Desna}Desna{/g}, {g|Erastil}Erastil{/g} or even {g|Lamashtu}Lamashtu{/g}."
ada3491c-fdbd-4cf8-81f1-74c97651a3f5: {n}Jubilost wrinkles his lips.{/n} "I haven't the opportunity yet. Unfortunately. My studies of the First World are limited to the confused statements of witnesses or scribbles in their diaries. Also I've studied the remains of some unfortunates who periodically fall out of spontaneous portals."
c3131d95-3e71-4df5-b522-6328e809a01b: "I keep to the hope that sooner or later I'll manage to visit that wonderful place. And certainly the notes I'd write on the place would be far more extensive and informative than all the ramblings on the subject I've had to wade through."
e90a2f32-f0c1-45c5-83ea-5acdcd1558bb: "Naturally, the main concern of my expedition would be the safety of its leader, namely me. It would be extremely foolish to go that far and see that much, only to lose the chance to tell anyone about it."
d3b2c09f-c69a-49ce-bf52-1e271e4a7a0e: {n}Jubilost looks at you for several moments, his eyes narrow.{/n} "I told you already, I like to be alive. I assure you, other gnomes share the same attitude. Between the {g|Bleaching}Bleaching{/g}, disease, and old age, we have a lot to yearn for."
c9003e08-ff29-42b4-b665-033652166cc3: "But the ancient gnomes for some reason decided that mortality, the {g|Bleaching}Bleaching{/g}, and all the diseases of {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g} are preferable to the immortality of {g|First World}the First World{/g}. I can't do anything to change that. But I can do something with my own life. I want to find a way back to the First World for all the gnomes of Golarion."
b794515c-b0b6-4019-882e-32dcd2719d88: "Unfortunately, to do this I can't just gather up all the gnomes and send them marching through the nearest portal. We're too attached to {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g} now. We've lost out connection with the chaos of {g|First World}the First World{/g}. We've become too mortal, if you see what I mean. When a gnome dies in the First World, he dies forever, like any visitor. But there must be something that can be done to solve this problem – and I intend to find out what it is!"
9598b0e9-719b-4c7d-ab34-22eca6ef38f7: "Jubilost Narthropple, the hero who returned the gnomes home. It has a nice ring to it, wouldn't you say?"
71f426bb-daf3-440a-9e5d-c3b740717b2f: "Do you think so?" {n}Jubilost looks at you above his glasses.{/n} "Why ever not, if I may ask? Perhaps you confuse superficially friendly words with genuinely friendly intentions? Believe it or not, I wish you only well. As a proof of that I can point to the fact that I travel with you, and that I'm talking with you right here and now."
d8a461b8-631a-468a-9f54-c3bae3b9b166: "Tell me, which do you value more. – An artificial smile? Or an honest attitude, bolstered by friendly advice and assistance?"
9ebde818-e295-4640-9c7e-30f1af3f82a7: "Here's another piece of advice, then: you should learn to see the essence rather than being distracted by colorful wrappings. Otherwise you risk swallowing something you shouldn't, because it was wrapped in golden foil." {n}Jubilost adjusts his glasses.{/n} "If you cannot separate the sense of my words from the way they sound, that's not my problem."
c237274e-66c2-4090-bab4-c902017c1e21: "That was a joke, right?" {n}Insult, doubt and resentment chase each other over Jubilost's face. {/n}"Well, I admit, I may overreact sometimes. Perhaps my manner of speaking may seem offensive to some. But I'm usually right, when you get down to it. And the truth, no matter how unpleasant, is always better than lying to someone's face! We shouldn't let such minor things as my manner of speaking or tonight's dinner harm our friendship."
544f2cc9-2f8e-44a4-b992-862c9732915e: "I thank you for this permission. Can I have it in writing – in case you forget someday?"
c82ba3bb-db5a-4f9e-9f92-e079bb324dca: "Trash?!" {n}Jubilost is so offended, he nearly drops his glasses.{/n} "Let it be known that this article is one of my finest works! Striking, precise – and exceedingly to the point! You should be proud that your barony inspired such a masterpiece!"
0245fe8a-3ff7-4671-a110-46dda9cbaa9f: "Are you proud that I haven't found anything in your {mf|barony|barony|kingdom|kingdom} worth my attention? Hmm. Well at least that means that there's nothing truly disastrous in your lands. So yes, perhaps you may be proud of that."
8a372814-9574-40e1-ae1d-952c48055198: "Flattery is entirely foreign to my works. Everything that I write is the absolute truth, and never intended to satisfy egos." {n}Jubilost looks at you over his glasses.{/n} "But in case you were wondering – yes, I'm impressed with what you've done."
29430f85-8e5d-41ee-9895-dd9385f19b82: {n}The gnome raises an eyebrow.{/n} "Oh? Have you thought this idea through?"
a04ec2c7-5920-4377-a80a-a966a7543ba7: {n}Jubilost chuckles.{/n} "Next time you should pay more attention to your ramblings. I've gotten quite used to them already, but the others might be puzzled."
b5127722-5870-4d8b-97c4-997915826ba0: "Well well. It's not the first time I've been asked to leave a state, so I shouldn't be surprised. But now I feel that straying so far from civilization was a mistake. There's nothing here worth my time or talent. Good luck with your little plot of dirt."
60190069-4815-4e1c-96b9-f6a53f2f4842: "{Name}! I never properly thanked you for your help at the Inconsequent Debates. I'm happy to do so now. I hope you don't think me entirely ungrateful."
427dc0b6-0e34-4810-9f0a-3e12464ff632: "If you want to apologize for destroying my chance at solving the greatest mystery of our era – then don't bother. And if you think you were right about everything – well then I'm even less inclined to talk about it."
94da5871-bcbb-4a67-aa15-766cf72ac0e4: "Not quite, but I'm working on it. I'll certainly inform you of my findings. I must admit, such an answer is quite in the spirit of the fey. It must lead somewhere, and I will find the trail!"
4c81d8b0-3dcd-4e50-b718-d83e4f82c98b: "Hmm..." {n}Jubilost locks his hands behind his back.{/n} "Well you see... I understand well what the {g|Bleaching}Bleaching{/g} is, what a fatal effect it has on gnomes. Those poor fellows were acting like that for no darker motive than desperation. Their foolish jokes allow them to live just a little bit longer. Do you see? I don't mind becoming the joke myself – for a while, of course, and not if my life was being threatened. It let someone live a couple days longer."
d3ac1628-e2d0-49bc-badb-56f51118701c: "As you wish. I'll continue to work on the riddle."
