1c3eb396-1889-40e6-ab6d-5476d3327a05: "Why should I want to remain? To quarrel with the likes of you? I've no interest in this. — Honest people are welcome in many places. Hey, Starlings! We're leaving!"
bf0003b0-2d62-49f8-96d7-49207f6550bd: "I have... we have a little brother. His name is Lorre. A halfling. He came to us six months ago. He's a smart fellow, but willful. He's good with his hands, and thinks fast. But he decided to put his talents to ill use. We caught him stealing back in {g|Galt}Galt{/g} — and almost lost our heads because of the little rat!"
49513074-68bf-4f28-ba24-d485c82c1e61: {n}Zandu examines you with his eyes.{/n} "So, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. We're nomads, so it's all right to blame all the evil in your lands on us?"
b090771f-2297-46b2-a4cb-ff300472eb15: {n}The man's glance becomes heavy.{/n} "Let the test begin then, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. Perhaps this time {g|Desna}Desna{/g} will smile upon someone other than you."
1269f302-221a-42d7-a8a8-4c4d1a4979d9: {n}Zandu gives you a long look and then sighs sadly.{/n} "Fine."
5f458409-48be-4f5e-80c2-d38e167d6594: {n}Zandu starts whistling carelessly, looking at the cards in his hands.{/n}
69af8982-2a55-45cb-ae0a-bad7f3f5df9a: {n}Zandu casts a glance at the other members of the caravan.{/n} "So be it, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, you win. Just don't harm the others, they have nothing to do with it."
36c82945-3065-4090-a865-d844d4c1b4c9: {n}Zandu turns away, but you notice a smug smile on his face.{/n}
d95c33b9-463f-4fd7-9083-d164794599e0: "I told him last time: we Starlings don't do such things. We may not much respect the law, but we live by our consciences. Lorre just nodded, like he was agreeing. But your presence here means he's up to his old tricks. That must be why I haven't seen him around lately! I'm sorry I didn't tell you right away — I was hoping I was wrong to suspect him. But truth be told, none of ours would do these things. And I'm not his mother to cover for him his whole life!"
dbfffbba-ab96-4fb7-a660-8548ab76738d: {n}Zandu stands up straight.{/n} "Listen, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. I know where he might have a hiding place. — He hinted at such a place but I pretended I didn't understand. But it's... our business. Family business. Don't send your soldiers after Lorre. The Starlings will deal with him, and we'll return what he stole. I give you my word — there won't be any more thefts here. The Starlings will track down rotten rascal ourselves!"
ed2ce62f-5b78-4b3f-bd19-0e3c72a53f3c: "Thank you, {mf|Baron|Baroness|King|Queen} {name}. I still hope Lorre can be reformed. He is a good lad. He just got some bad ideas about easy money when he was a kid."
da370ea4-c064-4d3e-84ba-e52a8e0f02cb: {n}Zandu frowns.{/n} "You don't trust me? Or the Starlings? Or anyone who's not to your liking? Too bad you tar everyone with the same brush, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}... Lorre might have made a mistake, but it seems you're treating others just as poorly."
7cc3b50a-eb90-4187-abad-4596d987acbf: "One's family is not just the ones you share blood with. Yes, I have sisters and brothers, but Starling recruits are not kin by parentage, but by spirit and conscience. Every one of our caravan is as good as family. And if someone has pointy ears or hairy feet — why should I care?"
d9a62613-58e2-432e-a2be-14f20c51e0c1: {n}The man runs his finger along the lines on his neck.{/n} "Yes... In case you don't know, it's a hereditary trait. Some {g|Varisia}Varisians{/g} have tattoos even in birth. No one knows why. My mother told me that I was born with only small streaks on my skin. And now look – I am covered in wisdom that no one has yet been able to decipher."
414f1014-9b71-4b97-8067-cb4d702af1de: "And you, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness} – you really are just like the people say. You're not torturing people for no good reason, and leave them free to live by their wits. Who would ever guess I'd say this, but I like this {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}!"
2158af8a-cc8b-44e8-a79b-dd15fc567376: {n}Zandu lets out a brief laugh.{/n} "It's easier to say where we haven't been. From {g|Cheliax}Cheliax{/g} to {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g}, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. We've walked all of {g|Avistan}Avistan{/g}."
a47d0b36-4044-4d59-9a20-054ccb5ccb2b: "As you say." {n}Zandu throws his cards skillfully into the air and catches them with one smooth movement.{/n}
6f546e46-f07f-45de-a5c7-72a92bb2a041: {n}Zandu wrinkles his nose.{/n} "Truth be told, it was not what, but whom. You see, the Starlings stand for freedom. So sometimes we visit the lands where this freedom is being trampled. We pick up fugitive slaves, and when we can, we get down to business and free someone."
0e7e0596-cdbf-48ef-b683-12df55ce72de: "We walked all the roads there many times, and eventually became bored. And so we decided to look farther afield, to see what's going on out in the world... and we got carried away."
9321240e-80ce-4805-94f6-34202bcfe3c3: "You are right about that." {n}The man scratches the back of his head.{/n} "I've been to many places, seen many things... but I saw such things in {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g} as cannot be believed. The Starlings have no business there."
94daa644-2d98-4b9b-8dc4-5dc82c08f9b2: "Are you talking about my family?" {n}Zandu nods at the others.{/n} "We are the Starlings, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. We are from {g|Varisia}Varisia{/g}. We live on the road, traveling the world. We heard that life here is easy, so we decided to come see."
160bcf14-ca94-4f67-b8f9-323a42af6d96: "Lorre spoke of a ravine where the river is shallow. Send your dogs there. Meanwhile I will prepare to leave – before you begin to hunt any of my other people."
976c5420-7cc0-4519-9aa8-0d4585014a31: {n}Zandu salutes you jauntily.{/n} "May {g|Desna}Desna{/g} keep you safe, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}! And thank you for not keeping your distance! With such a {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen} I could even start to believe in law and order! And don't worry about scoundrels like Lorre: we road people keep a watchful eye on our brothers!"
4260709c-949d-4e6d-bbd7-ae9b42c056a5: {n}Zandu nods, pleased.{/n} "That's right! The poor thing had it tough on the run – with shackles on her feet! But we nursed her back to health. And so she turned to {g|Desna}Desna{/g}. — She believes it was the goddess who sent us to her!"
292ff6a8-ed5c-4d57-8e97-e21d2f769417: "Pondering how to make the most perfect dive to the rocks below, are you?"
56b439e3-fb3e-455f-bb39-5e9f6554fe80: "Care to tell me who you are?"
c9b90f24-ca00-43f0-bf64-77099d25b463: "Is it your house south of here?"
545d2b15-3756-4aaf-9c73-5b3aaa6c34ba: "Tell me, was it you who gave the villagers Silver Dragon's scales?"
0ab8c604-2946-4370-a086-dc9fa6e427e1: [Attack] "Dragon's Voice or not, this place can only have one ruler, and that's me!"
3a5c60b0-615d-4c45-8f11-8dd943ff011b: "We have no need to fight each other. I won't harm either you or the village."
8729e33f-baf6-4e95-b61b-0dfac629798a: "I am the sole ruler of these lands. Never forget it."
3106612b-1bcc-4946-b8a2-f86208cfef97: "May I have an audience with this 'Lord Dragon' of yours?"
67c992a3-36d0-45f9-a313-a6c88ef9d7da: "I'm not hiding my identity — in fact, I've nothing to hide at all."
9dbc06ed-9a92-419c-aea2-f740a4278b68: "I know about your family. I'm… sorry for your loss."
4ab87e4a-d447-41fb-ac4f-1fd7a67a8bb3: "I found your oh-so-inspiring letter to your poor, dead wife."
88a5d526-9c44-4fc6-8aee-f5aaa67ef4d9: "There were some papers around the house..."
4799406e-e8d4-44f8-9aa8-df5f7b781771: "The tales you tell! These scales belong to a wyvern."
f8612a3a-bbd7-4668-82e9-6c6ce9c1ccab: "I don't know why you keep lying to the villagers, but your lies won't work with me. I know about the wyvern."
a14715e9-9e90-4d01-a7e1-96d01da8a665: "Lies, even seemingly-harmless ones, never end well."
af8dc57e-ad0b-4293-962a-23dbcac44563: "People are gullible. Using that weaknesses to your own benefit? I respect that."
8faf63c4-5f44-4cde-9174-06a8f1eb6770: "Are you trying to tell me, that even after you've lost your family, you still don't realize what damage lies can do?"
bde46540-37b3-41a2-aa37-5773f18ac1d8: "In any case, not every made-up story is a bad thing."
2fa3725f-df3b-48ec-911a-63fdbf6a81bb: "All right then, let me ask you few more questions."
45956d4a-01d6-4d13-9848-5fdcf69e1e1b: {n}A tall, red-headed man dressed in hunter's clothes is balancing at the brink of this cliff — one wrong move and he'll fall into the chasm.{/n}
b4c9bc2b-8236-4521-a93e-401a90cd22e3: "Oh no, not at all. Many would like to silence the Dragon's Voice. I won't give them the pleasure." {n}The redhead turns around and nods.{/n} "...Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}."
75e14f40-7308-4633-b921-1db68b2ddfac: "Well, it would be rude not to introduce myself. My name is Ivar." {n}The red-headed man watches you closely, but makes no move to run or draw his weapons.{/n} "If you passed through the village, you must have heard rumors about me. Once, I used to be a simple hunter, but now I keep the peace in this region by the order of their lord, the Silver Dragon."
7e431b28-14a4-443d-b31d-4063b601fa41: "That's what people call me." {n}The red-headed man smiles slightly.{/n} "These lands are under protection of the Silver Dragon. And I'm his most trusted servant."
bd0b1e72-92b0-4da1-99c9-84c372030c9a: "That's exactly what every new self-proclaimed {mf|king|queen} usually says."
262c5397-61a9-4d1b-9f97-88d7ece4843b: {n}The red-headed man gives a crooked smile as if you've confirmed his opinion, then he shrugs.{/n} "I didn't want to offend you. But I know your kind. You always want something for yourself — power, money, fame... all I want is peace for these people. You and I, we're on different paths."
201f457f-3880-4c2e-92ba-dcea88c794fa: {n}The red-headed man bows his head.{/n} "Well, forgive me for being so harsh. I just wanted you to remember — these lands don't need new rulers. A protector is enough."
86ecea8c-e351-4c61-be77-d115cdcb4641: "Don't be so eager to put a crown on your head! Remember, {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}, this village is under my protection."
e1a80232-0e25-4760-858e-5c929c0c1c3b: {n}He smiles slightly.{/n} "You waste your time — I cannot be bought, with gold, a maiden's kiss, or magic. Even if you were to try — and you're welcome to — the Dragon won't speak to anyone but me."
c0064669-a97e-4d4a-a707-db5fbc08a6f9: "I know everything that happens in the village and for leagues around. Of course I was aware of your arrival — such a prestigious guest, striding into our lands."
8d08952d-9745-4b47-a5c4-2e25916dc1c8: {n}The red-headed man raises an eyebrow.{/n} "That so? Well. Honesty is a virtue, and one that's hard to find these days. Especially if we're talking about kings, queens, and any who seeks to rule others. What do you want to ask me about, {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}?"
f277f621-1406-42c4-aa38-bce74a8dcbd4: "I don't waste my breath on threats."{n}The redheaded man is gazing at you coldly.{/n} "My way is a simple one — those who come in peace are welcome. Those who threaten the village don't live long enough to regret it."
d1faeba8-c680-47cd-8355-26d50d975d77: "Just don't take it as flattery." {n}He scoffs, but there is no malice in it.{/n} "Boot-licking the highborn? Never one of my habits."
6c98a839-04ff-4bf5-8754-046dbdbb4c8c: "I don't look for sympathy. And don't expect it." {n}Ivar falls silent for a moment and looks away.{/n} "Besides… I don't deserve it."
2c50b7bd-4537-42a9-939c-152e5dd2a212: {n}Ivar frowns, and his fists clench… but he regains control almost immediately.{/n} "I should have watched over my papers more carefully... Though... what difference does it make? What would it change?" {n}He shakes his head bitterly.{/n}
0a64452f-3b46-4aa9-b91a-f56246f347be: {n}He tenses.{/n} "It was me, yes. Who else except for the Dragon's Voice would do that?"
d610ff2c-2690-49ef-8a0f-b768647294eb: {n}Ivar's face darkens.{/n} "Storyteller, you say? If you only knew, what price I had to pay for my stories... Yes! I lied to the villagers, but the people needed something to believe in. If they need a fairy-tale dragon — I give them a fairy-tale dragon."
de32d55a-7701-4d28-b1ff-f42d962bd823: {n}Ivar stiffens.{/n} "Nothing gets by you, I see. Hnh. Yes! I feed wild wyvern from time to time and bring her scales to the village. People need to believe in something. So let them believe they live under protection of the Dragon."
a163c285-666b-413d-b99c-50923ba561b0: "Don't be so quick to judge, {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}. You may think you know a lot, but every wise man knows there's always more to learn."
c361367a-2b02-44ce-ac5e-51eafedd557d: {n}Ivar laughs, relaxing slightly.{/n} "Luckily, people don't talk about those kind of dragons yet."
3a1894e9-b859-4eb8-9fae-c2d5c5d3fd20: "I wonder how would you deal with it, if, according to the legend, the dragon was, let's say, a bright pink with sunflower spots!"
f95808c4-71dc-4563-8e55-0f55b4cbf115: "You want to know if I regret about telling lies to the villagers? Yes, I do, but I can't find another way. So, enough about that!"
0cb130be-cfe7-4796-b51b-688f81c1e122: "Why are you so sure that this "another time" will happen? I won't stay here long. There's an old saying — sluggish wolf soon starves."
4aee9935-9a28-41af-96a6-85e6cc164625: "You were less polite the last time we spoke."
79c53d60-5704-497c-96ab-785222349be9: "So we meet again, and not on the battlefield... Assuming this tournament isn't a trap, of course."
b9886621-bad3-44a2-aed7-3c21ede3b678: "So Irovetti considers me a rival? I didn't think I'd given him any cause for a feud."
cb168257-b115-42a6-9932-226e58652856: "This isn't the first year the tournament's been held — why was I just invited this year?"
a0e42da9-a941-44ab-bae3-89124deb10f4: "At least you're honest with me. I appreciate the warning."
bf15634e-1b62-4f63-bb6a-9998e529b0dc: {n}The man standing before you seems to spend a great deal of time perfecting his appearance. His cheeks and forehead are generously powdered, his hair is slicked back, and his carefully waxed mustache curls up rakishly.{/n} "Why, if it isn't {mf|King|Queen} {Name}! We meet at last. I paid a visit to your kingdom while it was still a barony, but alas, I had no chance to meet you. I'm Stefano Moskoni, confidant to King Irovetti."
866d2ff4-b941-4ca9-93c9-a1db824e4b80: {n}Since your last encounter, {d|Stefano}Stefano Moskoni{/d} has put on a little weight, and his appearance has become even more festive. As you approach, a polite smile blooms on his face.{/n} "Why, if it isn't {mf|King|Queen} {Name}! Please, allow me to congratulate you on your success!"
a658fffc-e150-47cb-bbf4-d231577a83c8: "How do you like our little celebration?"
6932b9b4-3ccf-4bc1-af2d-6f99a7fab81a: "I concede my mistake — I supposed I'd met a king for a day, whose state would last a few months at best. I'd never imagined you would match my king in dignity, let alone that your country would become a worthy rival for {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g}."
9d3f2036-60ef-4ca6-8ee3-17cf88444e63: "Of course it's not. It may be hard to believe, but King Irovetti's intentions are quite honest this time. Trust me, he'll make a move sooner or later, but for now, he's invited you for the chance to see a new rival with his own eyes. I'll let you in on a little secret — he actually thinks very highly of you."
516b6801-fd88-4157-99d5-2970306f30f0: "I mean no offense when I say this, but both you and your state were, frankly, inconsequential, not significant enough for our attention. But your victory at {g|Brevoy}Brevoy's{/g} border and your subsequent coronation changed all that. In truth, King Irovetti only invites those he's identified as worthy rivals to the tournament."
c829249f-d097-43f9-9b0e-e9a26a3aea0f: "The unfortunate reality is that your very existence, along with the strength your kingdom has acquired, is cause enough. What would happen were you to join with {g|Mivon}Mivon{/g} against {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g}? Or perhaps you might seek to extend your lands west and not stop at the border. What if merchants from {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g} began traveling through your lands, bypassing Pitax entirely? And of course, the most important question..." {n}Moskoni's grin turns predatory.{/n} "Do you sit securely on your throne, or does Pitax stand a chance of expanding east?"
4daa13a6-53b2-4971-970c-0e96f7090a1c: "Think nothing of it. I have great interest in seeing how events will unfold."
046e0606-4e76-418a-baa3-a29ba84f580d: "Until we meet again — and I'm sure we will."
de3e3d5e-9fc7-4d9d-8ae6-4d5c6ac18128: "Now that's real talk we have here! Come on, honorable Stefano – sing us another of your sweet political songs."
97d05f4f-b547-48df-9bca-a5b42ed2df09: "What are you doing with these fey?"
fbf3c6dc-0747-4221-ab1b-80915f2ef731: [Attack] "You shouldn't have looked for me unless you were looking for death."
166fe178-805d-4820-a86a-45fc0944b4eb: "I don't have time for your nonsense. Farewell."
f01706d9-00fd-467a-b3d6-7bd6ac4b76b8: "I worship Shelyn. Your words ring familiar and true to me."
02739f1d-1346-49ac-9256-651adf739b48: "I worship Sarenrae. Your words ring familiar and true to me."
889f0383-5a96-4b23-a321-a121095d3d22: "I worship Irori. Your words ring familiar and true to me."
61e93059-f990-494c-a70e-5a1b901c109b: "I worship Iomedae. Your words ring familiar and true to me."
95c9f6f1-f464-4f98-a04a-769188a7f4ea: "I worship Erastil. Your words ring familiar and true to me."
0c46b7c9-812d-4d8b-a10f-5fce62e643bf: "I worship Abadar. Your words ring familiar and true to me."
ae097949-8406-41dc-b215-ccfb7af1c8b4: "I worship Asmodeus. You think your philosophy would be of interest to me?"
d3dbb28d-ca9c-4648-a726-ab67659af90e: "I worship Zon-Kuthon. You think your philosophy would be of interest to me?"
04dee326-4210-411a-bb60-b3659bb3528b: "I worship Urgathoa. You think your philosophy would be of interest to me?"
6a7ac305-b167-4c0f-bea4-722160686558: "I'm an atheist. I've no interest in religious orders."
a4d93d37-2bee-432f-b2ba-6cdb568f2859: "I worship Gorum! Do you really intend to preach pacifism to me?"
15025ee3-4bfa-4a23-8d60-4f19ad2aac68: {n}A satyr and a nymph are watching a dark-skinned elf whose arms are dancing, gracefully making magical gestures in a sort of ritual. Noticing you, she stops her ceremonial dance and greets you with a light bow – respectful and dignified.{/n}
80514544-b512-4b68-bf14-faefd2b1c259: "You are {Name}, warrior-{mf|king|queen}, the first to bring peace to the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g}. I sought a meeting with you, and fate has allowed our paths to cross. My name is Kamala."
1345225d-8928-45dc-9d27-30d64931be96: "Kamala the Phoenix from the Suramgamin Order, humble follower of the Wise Way of teacher Avalo."
9d4a916f-7782-4b71-9138-36b34bd86e1d: "Mysterious and sinister events are happening in your lands. The border between worlds grows thin – and someone's hand reaches through it, plotting the deaths of you and your subjects. My brothers and sisters from the Suramgamin Order have come to help you stand firm against this unknown enemy – if you desire our help... And if you pass our trials and prove you are worthy of it."
5ae9aba3-50c2-4ad5-9ccb-122582276644: "They were brought into this world unwillingly, and their mischievous temper could mean a lot of trouble for the local people. The border between worlds here is thin and feeble, like the worn-out cloth of a monk's frock. I have charmed them to sit still for a bit, while I prepare to send them home."
5b542785-11f8-4a20-b6ed-894f0b04dd71: {n}The Suramgamin Order is relatively unknown, but you've heard stories. They are followers of good and order, whose teacher Avalo, a native of {g|Jalmeray}Jalmeray{/g}, preaches complete non-violence.{/n}
9f4251ed-a54d-417a-afe1-2097afc11bc0: {n}You've never heard of this order, or a teacher of wisdom known by this name.{/n}
891edb92-764d-41c9-bfdd-cf4706d99a46: "This is unfortunate. Very well, Your Highness, we will trouble you no more."
efe17e45-8656-428b-b217-d8df308f1d29: "Teacher Avalo founded our order to help people who walk the path of good remain steadfast, and to give those who've lost their way a place to come back to. The backbone of our philosophy is non-violence. This doesn't mean we are helpless, but we believe there is a future when no one in our world will wish to take up weapons against their neighbor."
67a3fa78-d639-4d0b-bd97-6b4254229dc6: "The heart of the way is practice. The ability to subdue anger, negotiate without threat, to quell a conflict before a spark becomes a fire – I imagine the {mf|king|queen} must be familiar with such things? With your permission, I would like to test you – here and now."
97876fc8-9230-4ff2-93dc-ed1a1132c41b: "Look at these fey. I charmed them so they wouldn't interfere while I open a portal into their native world. I will release them now. To pass the trial, you must convince the fey to remain still, while I prepare to send them home. Try to do this without threatening them... And don't let them charm you!"
0796a6ff-c645-45c2-b191-917c6d0b3dfc: "What? A whole world without fights? Then what would we do? Just lie around and get fat? I'd like to see you try teaching beasts and monsters to be peaceful — and how the peace lovers who follow you would handle them!"
e047d561-3c05-4e29-bbda-9e231dbe82f5: "I am not familiar with these teachings, but they sound very similar to {g|Sarenrae}Sarenrae{/g}'s faith. It is amazing, but I think this is someone who surpasses us in peacefulness."
88ba911f-5c10-4d24-b246-2481b3a7cc7c: "I hear peace and wisdom in these words. Like the sound of the sea within a shell. If there ever comes a day when the fire of anger fades from the world, I would like to see its dawn."
e18ae1e8-1517-40d9-bc42-35a2e1065ec9: "Heat cannot be separated from fire, as anger cannot be separated from a living soul. Teaching peace for all is a lie, a dream, or just folly."
784a3aa5-408b-4a6c-ba82-d64590f425f5: "No wonder! That's one of the deities Master Avalo studied to glean some of the grains of truth he used to build his philosophy!"
30012338-4421-4d23-ba16-184861781e17: "We know you pray to an evil deity. Still, we wanted to take a look at you and see for ourselves — are you really so evil? Could there yet be seeds of goodness sleeping deep in your soul?"
ec9069df-f8b5-4203-8823-298fd7f03486: "It doesn't matter. There are atheists among us, too. We don't blindly follow deities — we simply use their lessons to help us become better people."

a143c0ab-abe6-42fe-b14b-d4a05a78139d: {n}Shaynih'a smiles joyfully.{/n} "I knew that wise Hassuf would be most pleased to receive news from home. All of this reminds me of a wonderful story, one that took place a long, long time ago…"
0993d357-ebec-4039-93f8-ac2d56bfbc97: "There once lived a mighty warrior by the name of Khorkhor. His mother was a white shark, and his father the most lustful – and most inventive – of all mortals. 41460195-6607-41f8-a038-330275eea0b7: "This story teaches us that however long and difficult the most worthy path may be, happiness, honor and triumph always lie at the end of it. 0ef4b53f-943e-4c3c-a63f-8fc3a634db61: "As you can see, both honor and disgrace may live in the same body, even though it may belong to a person of worth. 5003cf22-2f79-4a1e-b057-1bd461076cc0: {n}Shaynih'a hands you a heavily worn piece of metal.{/n} "I have heard, o worthy one, that there lives a Storyteller in your realm, whose eyes can see into the memories of things. 6848ffbd-3267-4547-87ff-d500bcdf5d06: "Maharajah Khiben-Sald etched his glorious name in history when he conquered the kingdoms of the genies. 9a7a72b4-1cee-477a-9df2-ad2683fa491c: "As you can see, even a mortal can accomplish such great deeds that their memory shall live on longer than the palaces built by the magical genie. For it is still forbidden to utter the name of Khiben-Sald among the genie, so much is it hated! Let others think of you as a villain or lunatic – all that truly matters is that enlightenment and devotion to your own goals blooms in your heart! It is decided. I shall continue my work on my path to mastery, and will create a masterpiece which will immortalize my name. May it serve you well, whether I be praised for it by your friends or cursed for it by your enemies!"
13140131-e61d-4207-9b20-7e23d08aba34: "I am flattered. Where should I begin?"
5d7f2112-076a-4cdc-af73-2b009de265ce: "Until we meet again, o worthy one! It shall happen sooner than you think – the Perfect Human has told me!"
e7464017-7b6b-41e0-bfc2-3cd7bd6b9bb7: "Oh, they often say this about the Vudrani! Know then that the gods have given me such lessons in humbleness, that it is quite against my nature to lie and spread falsehood! Have you ever been to Niswan? It is the capital of the Island of {g|Jalmeray}Jalmeray{/g}, the city of a thousand rooftops, above which flutters a thousand silk banners. Not water, but the finest wines flow from their magnificent jade fountains! There isn't a city more beautiful in this world! But Niswan's greatest jewel is its Houses of Perfection, monasteries wherein the world's finest warriors train."
34e05a25-a989-40f7-ab9d-f54f3b74ea94: {n}Shaynih'a's eyes glisten, and her movements become so smooth it's as if she's beginning to dance. It takes her a moment to stop herself.{/n} "Vudra is a land of wonders never seen in your realm. As witnessed by the ten thousands lines of Mizravrtta Brahmodya, as recorded by the wise Balazastrin from the words of the goddess Likha. Vudra is fifty thousand years old. That means that it is far older than the rest of the world, which grew up around Vudra to become its outer mantle, like shells and weeds grow upon the bottom of a ship."
0765b6c4-8760-46b5-9198-553156d0862d: "Yes, I am of the rajah caste, although I have lost all my lands." {n} Shaynih'a speaks in a sing-song manner, as if she were reading a ballad or verse.{/n} "I once disturbed an ancient city of the dead, one that lay hidden, deep in the jungle..."
b8b4ceaa-3aa0-49c1-873f-5055db509444: "Have you heard of Rudrakavala? High in the Vudrani mountains lies the Adhaarm monastery. Its monks are pious and devout, their duty is to feed a dead man whose green-skinned body floats over a black metal altar as he meditates. Back when Rudrakavala was alive, he was the vilest of the rakshasa. However, one day he stepped upon a river bank and became a seeker of truth. And thus he stood for a thousand years, unmoved..."
c59332ac-b97f-4fe8-9b1c-057494f0d16b: "This is a wondrous land! You have such strange cuisine! And kobolds? Incredible creatures, we do not have them in Vudra. And those insolent creatures... Squirrels! I have never seen such fierce creatures!"
8e7d0782-ca2d-41e6-896a-88129e23b2a5: {n}The Vudrani stares at you in surprise.{/n} "Insolent? I am a rajah, same as you. We are equals by caste. True, I hold no power, but what does that change? The sage Ulvantha told me a story. Once, he was a groom to the moon herself, but he angered her with his rapturous nature, and was expelled from the plane of Nirvana..."
e2ab7ee7-144b-48ed-81f8-b44f78779270: {n}A sly smile crosses the Vudrani's face.{/n} "Greed is a dangerous thing. Have you ever heard of the Consortium of Aspis, o worthy one? It is the union of the greediest merchants of all Cheliax. The head of the Consortium in Vudra learned of an abandoned palace of the princess Chhaya, rumored to be filled with fabulous riches. He hired guides and porters and set out for the palace, and the treasures they found there exceeded their wildest expectations – but their robbery had not gone unnoticed. They had awakened an evil spirit that sped towards them, taking the form of a white cobra..."
34d2748d-0302-436a-8cb0-f931c5ae8c87: "O most worthy one! It pains me to ask of you yet another favor, yet {d|Shainiha}I{/d} desperately require your aid! I fear yet again that I may have made the wrong choice when I set myself upon the path of master smith! A rumor has come to my ears and has upset my heart, making me doubt myself! The Perfect Human has sent me a sign — a sign that shows I was fated for a great undertaking! I beseech you, help me!"
0044d77b-207b-4f93-a031-8ee29809b64e: "But this land lacks order. The gods granted Vudra castes. You have none here, and that is why there is no order. For when you meet a member of the lowest caste, you know that they only barely deserved to be born human. In their previous lives, they were animals, or maybe even a vile things like kobolds, who are lower than even the lowliest beggars. Trust me, for I have more than once faced their wicked nature! Whereas when you encounter a member of a higher caste, be he a padaprajna warrior or a rajah as you and I, that signifies that in our past lives we were pious and noble, that our words were strong and true. It is that understanding that these lands lack."
75c5cb54-78bb-41e0-b502-bf26c3dc8d82: "Of the Kingdoms of a Thousand Wonders? Where should I begin…"
176af80e-06b7-441e-ac10-9ffcc91ae6cf: "As you wish, so shall it be. I have many interesting stories for you."
6965803d-e1b8-461e-88fa-1cd37ff36ee8: "...The Aspis realized that they would pay dearly for their greed, and ran as fast as they could. The foolish Vudrani who had helped them ran as well. They built ships and fled their homes. Many turned to piracy, and you can find them still in the Protectorate of the Black Marquis, now known as the Mandagara League. Woe is the fate of thieves and outcasts! Others settled in Kaer Maga in {g|Varisia}Varisia{/g}. It was they who took the pyramid-box from the palace and hid it from the Consortium. This box is covered in the finest oil, and carried by dead men, and inside the box lives the Child Goddess."
68a2b90c-b419-4f1a-ad3a-d854d9953c4f: "Trust me, for the Child Goddess spoke to me once, and foretold that you and I were destined to meet! The Vudrani hope that the deity's protection will save them, but it is this box that the evil spirit seeks. It has since transformed into a demonic ship, and it comes into ports by night. Sailors who look like crocodiles search the towns, and the ship is gone by dawn. There will come a day when the ship finds Kaer Maga's port, and the Vudrani will pay dearly for their greed. Vudra knows how to protect its treasures, and it is best not to seek them, o worthy one."
aa56d9c6-ae9a-4119-8e4f-3660f2ea7595: "... To ensure that he never again falls victim of his ill nature, he carries with him the skull of his mortal enemy, and consults it on all occasions. Trust me, for I myself have heard the words of the skull's wisdom! Once, this wise man Ulvantha was heading north. However, his path was blocked by the local rajah's army, who was waging war against his neighbor. The soldiers were ordered not to let anyone pass. This infuriated Ulvantha."
a49c2909-e7e0-453b-8425-81b8aaf1d9e3: "But, following the skull's advice, he did not kill them on the spot – after all, the soldiers acted honorably, neither buckling to his wrath nor flinching in their duty. Instead, the wise man took some rice from his bag and boiled it, making an army of rice soldiers. The rice soldiers then tore the rajah's men apart, while Ulvantha visited the rajah's capital. He then overthrew the rajah and placed a dead whore on the throne, as a reminder that power is as fleeting as life. So do not hurry to think that your position of power might give you a strength that I do not posses. Only noble behavior and enlightenment truly matter."
979c5285-fa09-420c-a42e-04e72e377cbd: "Once the Monastery of the Unblinking Flame became jealous that the Monastery of the Unfolding Wind was known as the house of the greatest masters. Many turned down the invitations of the Unblinking Flame in order to join their white-robed rivals. The Monastery of the Unblinking Flame swore to make them pay for the insult. In the streets, the markets, and the palaces, the red-clad monks would insult the white ones, provoking them to bloody duels."
40cfda39-dc2c-4332-9282-95e6d2fbfa2b: "Niswan shook as if from an earthquake. Trust me, for I witnessed it myself. In that life I was an arrogant master of the Unblinking Flame and my pride demanded war. I knew that my days were numbered, and desired nothing but to see the Unblinking Flame triumph. In my arrogance, I could not see how much suffering I brought to the people. Those who were struck by a monk's fist fell and did not rise again, and those who were touched by a priest's finger were permanently crippled in body and mind. We fought with honor, seeking to demonstrate our mastery, not murder our enemy – while the townsfolk died by the thousands. And we did not care."
b407ec11-0ac6-4f52-9606-40d58e0c5291: "Our students, however, secretly arranged the Tournament of Unseen Mercy, which took place on a bridge over an abyss. They fought, and it was agreed that the losers would be shown no mercy, and their bodies would be thrown down, into the abyss. By dawn the bridge was completely empty. It was then that we, the masters, saw how arrogance had weakened our Houses and deprived us of our future. The ambitions of the past were all that remained. It was a bitter lesson, and it was then that I swore in all of my incarnations to be always humble and straightforward. I have since kept my promise, no matter how strongly I may wish to embellish my story!"
893e4cb7-74a8-46f5-b462-f310a0524094: "As I have recently discovered, one of them lives nearby. The noble Hassuf trades in your capital. I confess, I am too nervous to meet him. I fear that my anxiety will cause me to behave inappropriately, and I may disgrace myself for it. Would you assist me in fulfilling my duty and deliver him this letter? I do not believe that my heart can be at peace until this letter is delivered! One cannot be a master when beset by such distraction."
59396011-126c-4178-919a-cb6daf90b6e7: "It is the land of genie, monks, wondrous beasts – and gods, of course. Vudra is home to thousands of gods, while in other lands they worship mere dozens! The Perfect Human is the head of the pantheon. He is called Irori, the Master of Masters. Among the gods he is as a maharajah, ruling Vudra and all of its Mahajanapadas, or kingdoms as you call them. Each kingdom has its own rajah. The wealth and glory of even the feeblest among them is such that would make even the wealthiest of your rulers rage in envy. Trust me, for I was once a rani myself."
c6c20307-a9d1-47f0-b728-bd21129b45a6: "Of course, we would need many a week to discuss all of her wonders!"
2444efa6-c4b3-48d0-8fb6-6bf26fdc34e3: "The walls of my palace steadily absorbed their attack, but in the end they turned to dust. I was preparing to die, but the red wind suddenly fled in terror, banished by a strange traveler. He was a vanara, half-man and half-monkey, and he wore the orange robe of a priest. I wished to thank him but he had little interest in my treasures. He offered me to play the wise-men's game of BARME, and if he won then I would have to give him my throne."
b0aa617a-1bb9-48f4-acc2-4411d05c02ff: "I agreed, for how could I say 'no' to my savior? He easily outwitted me, hiding four pieces up his sleeve, while I only managed to brush one off the table and stash another one in my pocket. I ordered my guards to seize the vanara and put him in chains, as I had no wish to give up my throne. But by dawn the monk had fled his prison. — He'd used his tongue to lick a hole in his manacles. I knew then that the monk was Ragdya, the monkey god, a sage, a petty thief, and the lover of a hundred brides. Trust me, for I have met many gods, and know of what I speak. I gave Ragdya my throne along with my apologies, and set out to wander."
d6b81b2c-5ffc-486b-abb8-502dfc6630ec: "A massive ant hive grew around him, but this did not concern Rudrakavala. A thousand years passed, and Diomazul, the god of war, came to visit him and offered Rudrakavala any reward, for he'd shown great merit. The rakshasa demanded all eight of the god's swords. Upon receiving them, he chased Diomazul into a dungeon and, content with himself, sat down to rest. Soon the other gods realized that war has left them, for it was much more difficult to resolve conflict and maintain order. And so they began to seek the missing god. To be precise, they found a young hero and tasked him with finding and rescuing Diomazul."
d7795916-e38f-4988-84fe-e357c1262236: "But he was terrified by the sight of the mighty three-headed rakshasa. While one head was reading Mizravrit Brahmodiya, the second was puffing on a hookah while the third was sipping wine. The hero didn't stand a chance in battle. But the rakshasa's bride fell in love with the hero. It is she that stands before you today. I put Rudrakavala to sleep with fragrant incense, while my prince took one of his swords and severed all three of the rakshasa's heads. I hid the heads in secret places were my groom could not find them."
13c671c6-15be-4209-8359-6f54309ecdc5: The memory of my treachery remains in one of his heads. I hope that it will never find its way back to his shoulders. But I'd best stay as far away as possible, in case that ever happens. So I prayed to the gods, and trusting in them, I jumped over the ocean landing in Varisia. From there my feet carried me here."
526f4505-4d3c-46c0-aab1-ca7e394c1a9b: "But they did not know that the wise man had taught his servants his techniques. While he slept, his servants captured the assassins. The pasha of the shaitans, also known as the earth genies, sent his finest warrior, Turmir, the destroyer of palaces. By his command, Khiben-Sald's palace fell and turned to rubble. The cunning wizard foresaw this, however, and fled to the island of Jalmeray."
8fc030aa-3f6a-4147-a03a-b6ed6bc9d1b8: "One of the royal marids, the genies of water, came to free his brethren from captivity. Of all the genies, he was the wisest. For three days, Khiben-Sald competed with the genie in the art of poetry. At the end of the third night, Khiben-Sald was so exhausted that he was about to take a ceremonial dagger to open his own veins... The genie, however, was first to admit defeat, and entered a copper vessel which the wizard then sealed. It was thus that history came to know the maharajah as the great conqueror of the genies."
775ce288-94b8-4cf5-b6b4-49cb0462f0db: "Kothogaz walked across the ocean, and the water reached only up to his waist. He was covered by a mighty shell like a beetle, and the slime from his body covered the waters like fat, calming the waves around him, and his many mouths dripped with spittle. Kothogaz cried out, and the putridity of its breath made creatures faint, bleeding from their eyes, their nose and their ears – while the monster's saliva burned through everything it touched. Trust me, for I have seen stones that were touched by this poison. Vu Balak, however, called forth the priests and they cast their magic. The ocean boiled and Kothogaz began to boil in it. The whales came surfacing all around him as he screamed, and his chitin hardened, becoming more and more fragile – until finally it cracked and crumbled."
afc7ee71-ed24-43a1-adc6-d98eab704550: "Finally, Vu Balak saw the heart of the Dance of Disharmony. He jumped so high that his mighty body blocked the sun, and the stars shone in the day. He then threw his spear and shattered Kothgaz's heart into a hundred and one pieces. We have managed to gather some of the pieces, but not all. Perhaps if the Storyteller were to read the spear's memories, he would be able to tell were the other pieces went. Then I might collect them to honor my mighty ancestor. That would be a truly heroic deed. Perhaps the path of a hero is what fate truly has in store for me."
4e1f7513-4757-48e4-bca3-1bf35b8c0b01: "One day, Khorkhor defeated the poisonous dragon Sruvara, who turned rice fields into nauseating marshes. But Khorkhor did not notice that Sruvara had scraped his white skin with its talon. Infection entered the hero's body, and he grew weak. He lied down to rest and remained there for a thousand years. Nothing could awaken him, even all the strife brought on by the fight with Kothogaz, the Dance of Disharmony. Once he finally awoke from his slumber, Khorkhor discovered that his homeland had been ravaged by this terrible attack, and he'd slept through the battle! Disgraced, he moaned and set off for a faraway gorge, where he would deliver his body to the scorpions, that they might eat his flesh and hide him from his shame."
83ddf2df-6824-43a3-8594-ce073c0999aa: "For three months, the scorpions ate his white skin and ruby flesh, but still the warrior endured. Even when he was eaten, Khorkhor did not die, for he was truly great. It was then that Bundha the Singing Butcher came to him. The immortal rakshasa told him that great was Khorkhor's shame, but more shameful still would be to run from it like a coward, rather than atone for it. Khorkhor's spirits were rekindled. He arose and, through sheer force of will, forged himself a new body out of iron. He accomplished many great deeds thereafter, and in the end he regained his position of honor and nobility."
02b7dba6-79b4-4b43-9c79-927d482cfd82: {n}Surprised, the Vudrani falls silent, shrugs and gives you a slightly displeased look.{/n} "Impatience is the mother of all sins, o worthy one. Be careful on this path. Return when you have the time to listen. Until then, I shall wait for you."
e9c26603-2b27-489e-879f-5a27ffd70c39: {n}The Vudrani purses her lips in disappointment and mumbles something under her breath, but soon she is smiling at you again.{/n} "I shall await your return."
2f329bf0-d69e-4055-9a46-326cdc292a9f: {n}The Vudrani freezes with her mouth open. Obviously, she was just getting to the best part. She snorts disapprovingly.{/n}
e545e607-065c-4b35-b146-96ace15cbc17: "Turmir chased after him, forgetting that the waters of the ocean could not hold his heavy flesh. As he began to drown, Khiben-Sald sent ships to save him, but only after Turmir swore to serve him. As compensation for the palace he destroyed, the genie was commanded to build the Pure Temple of the Maharajah, which was a hundred times more beautiful than the one he destroyed. Trust me – for I have seen this temple with my very eyes!"
86f28e3b-583b-4033-9045-1a558942414c: "You are wise, o most worthy one. But not patient."
69612f38-dcf0-4af5-9e26-1d0c07da2fbf: "A great evil returned with me to my kingdom. The macaques of Sikari, diseased and rabid, swarmed the land. They rolled like an enormous wave, engulfing and destroying everything in their path. They called this horror 'the crimson wind'. My warriors went forth boldly, but were overrun."
612ad92a-120b-470c-92e6-cbfbd9b38fb1: "Do you really like it when everyone looks at you like you're a venomous viper? Stay away, or it'll bite! How could you prefer that?"
b7da342b-b2e4-4fe1-84ea-9d611b4da747: "You see, my status allows me not to think whether others like me. On the contrary – it's they who must try to be liked by me."
9c209a3c-ddf8-43ef-a8f3-24e6f6d93e54: "The virtues of a noble chevalier are entirely foreign to Sir Lebeda. He kept inviting me on a date so persistently — and behaved as though he was deaf to my objections!"
65bd256f-f597-4b54-a0a2-9856d1a9b69f: "Just say that you will meet him in some quiet place... and I'll show up instead of you. I will give him more than he ever bargained for!"
86b6b274-07ac-4a18-ad71-5043a1c91bb9: "I should talk to him. About the void, and the ashes and the end of all that exists. About the pointlessness of life. And he will see that spoiling the lives of others is doubly pointless."
868b7ae6-2c0b-4c2b-8ea6-43bef2add74d: "Ha, ha. Some find it difficult to own defeat and stand back... Even when everyone around can see it's a lost cause."
6a347a96-ea90-4a53-a725-bfb9a69aaab6: "What the devil are you doing, relaxing here? Get back to your post, immediately!"
a7ddfe70-b834-40d2-b56b-1c4fafe7b548: "It's still strange to see you here, with wine in your hand."
545066c4-2b9b-4411-a061-630a40d09d08: "I don't like sitting in silence. Tell me, how have you been?"
2af92de8-43b1-4f99-8e01-16a81b6abd63: "Do you regret what happened by the trading post?"
30bc3119-dfd0-459e-a281-170dfb3d1497: "I just want to be sure I can still count on you."
c01cc09b-1691-4896-b43f-1f715b8ae135: "Don't speak to me in that tone."
eaabc841-f702-4ef4-978f-32f1c1453ccb: "You're behaving differently than I'm used to."
4b328f21-01a8-4c90-9d79-0238d6d7762b: "For me, you're always beautiful. Nothing could ever change that."
2c68d6c6-2d47-4c83-809b-a18af1f932db: "I don't value you for your beauty."
2187113a-51a3-4db1-b0cf-6088576c3db1: "I like you as a friend and as a companion."
e5f83a72-4b74-4231-8f70-18142ed27ecc: "One might drink herself into a grave like that..."
3b7865ad-ca32-49a7-bb0b-f287a391b8fa: {n}Soon after returning to the city, you realize Valerie is not at her usual post. Asking a series of servants and guards, you find your way to the city tavern, where you find the girl with a glass of wine.{/n}
d844ff1a-10d6-4bd8-a4f0-b7100ca5d93e: "{name}?" {n}Valerie looks up at you, surprised, and seems to blush a little.{/n} "Do you need something?"
cbea4bd1-f827-494a-bede-f1c5be175420: {n}A smile touches Valerie's lips.{/n} "Truth be told, that was the plan. Sometimes I need... to be alone." {n}Valerie pauses, then continues.{/n} "But I don't mind drinking with you. Since you found me."
b3814de2-16b1-4942-b2a4-e070639105d7: {n}Valerie's eyes turn into slits, and she reluctantly puts away her glass.{/n} "As you wish, Your Grace."
fdc32364-f73d-46e2-8a8f-fe115e6d34de: {n}Valerie scoots over, giving you some space. You take an empty stool and order a drink. For a few minutes there's a tense silence between you. The girl slowly sips her drink.{/n}
9c811e42-075c-45d1-a26e-14cfe320f109: "Like a mere mortal — is that what you mean?" {n}Valerie scoffs and sips from the glass.{/n} "Few would imagine it, but I have rough days too. Days when I prefer to hide from prying looks and just be alone."
111a4e38-27de-44c2-83fc-c8a56fb9fd66: {n}You slowly drink shoulder to shoulder with Valerie. At last she sighs and starts talking.{/n} "Since you and I met Fredero, I've started coming here more often. I don't care but..." {n}Valerie stops but then sighs and continues.{/n} "I don't care, but I'm getting tired of all the extra attention that's being so generously shoveled at me."
80127027-b2fb-4350-b33d-71bfd03cb8ee: {n}Valerie gives you a thin smile, running her finger along the rim of the glass.{/n} "Unusual. But I'll get used to it."
54fb371f-3b78-498e-8cf3-a540217fb3e0: {n}The awkward half-smile on Valerie's face turns into an angry sneer.{/n} "So? Does it change anything? Did my sword arm fall off? Or all my fencing knowledge, did it fell out of my head?"
d1378b69-0f58-4e61-b048-9e251a3f879b: {n}Valerie scoffs, studying the contents of her glass.{/n} "Fredero got what he wanted — a duel. And then he left us alone. — Isn't that what we wanted?"
ce3f8dc7-cfe7-4a22-8f88-0bb039c83374: "Oh no, our beautiful Valerie has stopped being such a beauty! Her wonderful face is ruined. It must mean there's something wrong with her!" {n}Valerie slams her hand on the table fiercely.{/n} "I have to say, I want to scream at everyone who keeps looking at me with terror and regret: where has your adoration and veneration gone? Vanished with one swing of a sword?"
5aa43521-b313-462b-8610-e7be77312fc8: {n}Valerie turns around and looks right at you.{/n} "And what is that supposed to mean, {name}?"
7225f15a-4865-44f6-9f2b-077239733d5f: {n}Valerie scoffs.{/n} "Just like everybody else, you're used to seeing what I prefer to show to the world. Anyway, I think I know exactly what you mean. The most obvious thing."
c8c47d7d-8107-43e2-9257-791b732d2028: {n}Valerie finishes her glass in one gulp and slams it on the counter.{/n} "My apologies, Your Grace. I was out of line." {n}The girl stands up and walks out of the tavern.{/n}
9577ade5-d6ce-4ab5-82c1-938a0e73a7c2: {n}Flushing red, Valerie turns to you and with an almost daring sneer.{/n} "It would be strange to expect anything else from you. — You, just like the rest of my admirers, now consider me... how should I put it... damaged goods! Well, where are your compliments now? Do you like this Valerie?"
7abe21c4-a674-4210-a516-967a1a3abdec: "What?" {n}Valerie stops. Blinking a few times, she stares in your face, as if trying to find signs of deceit.{/n} "But..."
338d0191-a881-4943-b962-c1913ec1d447: {n}Valerie winces for a moment, and then laughs, relieved.{/n} "Your honesty is like a breath of fresh air, {name}. Another woman would slap you, but I thank you for your honesty."
d84b864e-0752-4fbb-a3a8-67dd934c7d23: {n}Valerie pauses, and then stands up.{/n} "I think I've had enough for today — both wine and honesty. Please, don't worry about my ability to serve you. I vowed to fight shoulder to shoulder with you, and I'll not break it."
8a5fbe84-9686-40c5-aaf4-5ad342936c78: {n}Valerie bites her lip and looks down. It's the first time you've see her respond like this to a compliment. At last she looks away and answers softly.{/n} "Empty flattery, no doubt. But thank you anyway."
d69f6e92-78d0-4732-b8b5-3af559e010e2: {n}Valerie looks away with a sad smile.{/n} "Really? Well, thank you for your words."
0b89abb7-6cd9-4049-94ed-65454f50f9e8: {n}Valerie freezes — then sighs in relief and laughs.{/n} "Of course! Forgive my hot temper — I don't know why I got so wound up. I value our friendship as well!"
217dd8e8-3da8-4c12-b561-1a91da7742d8: "Of course! As if these... these fools pay attention to anything else!"
37a47d0e-22af-49bd-b3c9-37ba7fc0bebb: "One just might, and maybe it's for the better! No one's going to notice anyway — because of this!" {n}Valerie points at the scar on her face.{/n}

b4a26680-ef25-4c5f-a115-19f5bcc2ddc0: "Why did you invite this Gunderson to Varnhold anyway? Do we really need even more foolish treasure hunters in this backwater?"

5fa06f91-0765-456f-936f-a0fcb25cce62: "I agree. Perhaps we shall find a cyclops treasure around the corner. 902f6183-3bd1-4d1c-b78f-d532c8f24e0c: "What a story. We've hardly solved our problems with the centaurs, and we've already got a whole new riddle – and a personal chronicler along with it! 6ead4f49-4ee2-41e6-ab56-57080f784e21: {n}The joyful mood drops from Gunderson's face. He looks at you askance, and fiddles with his bracelet hesitantly.{/n}
cca44439-14e3-43b4-9bd1-c283cfb7c7e6: {n}Willas frowns.{/n} "It's only jewelry. What's the problem? Did I break a rule or rob someone?"
995d2fd6-8522-4f8c-9596-5dbe168c0ba3: "You won't find a better specialist in ancient treasures on either side of the Tors of Levenies!" {n}Willas shows you the bracelet readily.{/n}
97dc97b1-1763-4730-a1b8-c0e48e7af36f: "This knickknack? I don't think it's of any interest to you."
8616c604-0a17-4a29-b988-3b688b05ea1f: {n}Maegar arches his eyebrow, surprised, and looks at you with slight disapproval.{/n}
232564ff-bdce-4982-b70b-cdc0c5c44122: {n}For once, Cephal expresses solidarity with his commander.{/n} "{name}, you should learn to be more subtle. As for you, Sir Gunderson, you'd better stop playing games and speak plainly."
f984e850-be49-40f8-a4d7-e8a2a4218462: "Someone is conducting a bit of theatre..."{n} Cephal mumbles, drawing a sneer from Maegar.{/n}
4fae1c96-9e3d-4e5d-9cb3-2464593da097: {n}Maegar frowns at you, as if you were ruining his game. Then he turns serious and looks at the traveler.{/n} "Sir Willas. What is that bracelet you're wearing?"
058b079e-471b-4bed-a564-fd09d237b640: {n}Gunderson grows skittish under the Baron's heavy gaze.{/n} "I'm... em..."

e074ac55-162e-4cd1-8c10-bfb81fab6063: "Forgive my lack of tact. What were we talking about?"
254799ca-dedb-4856-81ce-d59f1c925f3a: "The people are complaining. They wish to see their ruler looking after their safety, rather than merely enjoying the comforts of rule."
5dde8d54-b73a-414f-af33-5dce81c966b2: "They shall have to steel themselves with patience. We shall protect the {mf|barony|barony|kingdom|kingdom}, but wars are not won overnight."
7d5c558d-0832-4d92-a56e-05e99da133c7: "Funny peoples. A chieftain sets an example, but if a tribe can't stand up for itself, what good is it?"
c6c33127-0b3c-403c-91cd-7b38caba6235: "In other words, they desire to see that {mf|he|she} is ruling to their pleasure, not {mf|his|her} own."
ed74652e-e039-459d-8c56-9fa6b6da4c90: "Regongar and you are like two boots that make a pair. Only both are left boots, ha!"
e9d3bfa3-efd9-462e-b12e-3826453f6b9a: "Yeah, that's right! Who else would need us, if we didn't need each other?"
4a01f671-41cd-4b83-be3a-e8d0c7f5213d: "By the way, someone promised to smother me with kisses... I'm still waiting!"
f6eb1b11-6105-4f42-83f1-7be4978aeaa6: "Regongar, what do you think you're doing?!"
89133801-1162-45f0-9414-9ed100cc4345: [Pull away] "Regongar, stop. Let's not ruin our friendship."
1204b3e9-5191-404b-9fcd-c8b0487b5f13: "Regongar, what are you... There are people here!"
95693b87-d252-46ad-8100-a7879f91b763: [Put your arm around Regongar in return]
ae8b5a99-847e-4f6c-a929-f33f42b4c50f: "I'd like to spend the night alone with Regongar."
b89dfbb1-e458-4680-a53d-6928523f35e4: {n}Returning to the capital, you, Octavia and Regongar go to the tavern to rest. After a couple of mugs, Regongar pulls out a deck of cards.{/n} "Want to play?"
60bf93fb-113d-4094-81e2-bb1c90c3b245: "A promise is a promise!" {n}The half-orc kisses you on the lips.{/n}
cc4a0b65-a0a2-4059-854d-471ec4b82bf2: {n}Regongar quickly pulls away his hand and scoots away from you.{/n} "It's just a bit of fun. Ha ha!"
89646cee-d507-474e-9c29-9edf8ec729bf: "All right, all right, as you wish! Friends it is then!"
3d606038-1b17-4fb3-aee3-8cbb9b887107: "So what? Are we doing something they don't like, hmm?" {n}The half-orc's hand is stroking your thigh.{/n}
b91d4ab7-f172-41b0-8b2a-2d840416b80b: {n}The half-orc clings to you, as his fingers stroke your thigh.{/n}
ab0329a8-01c0-4ede-b2a5-48d91d4cdd29: "Hey, mistress! Another round of drinks, we are dying of thirst here!
aa5840d6-dc42-4775-a003-c0b2bc7b991c: "The beer here is good, but there's too many people. Maybe it's time we go somewhere quieter?"
418f7173-daef-4977-a65d-e5b632327738: "I think it's high time... Octavia, are you coming?"
7c2c1fa1-35f2-42ae-88cf-b349f25ca94d: "The three of us?" {n}The half-elf laughs as she sizes up you and Regongar.{/n} "I'm liking this evening more and more... {Name}, what about you?"
8073f83f-ac93-4a64-8c61-cdddff36a136: "I don't think so." {n}The half-elf winks at you provocatively.{/n} "Have fun!"
4798e212-9d8c-441f-a07a-336413da83b3: {n}Octavia winks at you.{/n} "All right. Have fun!"
f525e157-b82b-47fd-ae88-1b41c2c15bf4: {n}Regongar reluctantly takes his hands off of you and scoots over.{/n} "Ah, that's a shame, then... All right — friends it is then!"
ce695d60-3a0e-40bc-8251-db9e43bae247: "Exactly... All right, boys, let's go — I can't wait!"
5fa93b84-84a9-4a29-a551-4b28d8001b8b: "Why not? What are we playing for?"
1ead9605-1e76-4046-8a3b-843d77ca6721: {n}Giggling, Octavia playfully slaps Regongar upside the head. In return the half-orc bares his fangs in a broad grin and starts dealing cards.{/n}
5cfee0fd-b468-48a6-8ac6-636d662adf73: "Reg, that's the sixth game in a row you've lost! Do you even know how to play at all?"
231016c9-1f5f-4ee9-844b-8c7919075c14: "Not at all!" {n}The half-orc scoots closer to you and, as if by accident, puts his hand on your thigh.{/n} "But I'm a spectacular undresser…"
619e217d-ef33-4ec2-b1b3-a6012f776bcb: "You know what I like about you? You're almost the only one here who's not trying to tell me that I live the wrong way!"
1f4d95a1-f04c-425c-b250-e3c46681073c: "Oh, live however you like, what do I care? Each of us writes their own story."
13248911-f25c-43ac-a07b-1240e69e2372: "And you know why? I don't see any point in wasting my time on an arrogant bully who never listens to anyone anyway."
9149e21c-aad4-4b30-95f9-b327f1fbb0ba: "And you know why? I don't see any point in wasting my time on an arrogant bully who never listens to anyone anyway."
609af043-c9ae-4187-850d-6913c1d7087e: "Nok-Nok, this isn't the King. This is something that looks like him."
39fd6774-5942-4fa2-8c73-a25077c69481: "That would be THIS goblin here. He got your message."
9bea4bca-0e52-4c77-88b6-38c9bd209b96: "It's definitely a barghest – demon, looks like a goblin – you know, like this one."
f9bf686c-a2a7-4596-95c7-1e973b6b810d: [Attack] "I've heard enough. I'll deal with you myself."
503bb5d0-a61c-416d-a0d6-a80553ab5fdf: "You've been tricked, this is a fight you can't win."
3219fa37-28ff-449b-b7d8-092f3bdefddc: "Then you'll return from whence you came, because we're not letting you kill anyone."
aea38ba0-f198-438d-8edd-7680a7590a17: "You do know you are threatening a high priest and Hero of Lamashtu, don't you? I didn't think barghests would dare kill any favored by the Great Mother."
3c9f35b5-8a2d-45b9-a832-ff004e169d01: "What terms did you agreed to? — Maybe you can turn this against her, get your revenge."
48625e18-7b1b-47ef-85ea-c19a9f2448ef: "But... you told her you'd kill Nok-Nok. If you don't, you'll anger her. If you do, then Lamashtu will get upset. My bet? I'd choose a fey's anger over the Mother of Beasts – but you made the pact, you lie in it."
26b0df48-7c45-4b08-bb7b-5f750e9b85c4: "One of my allies? Why not me?"
f153fe7d-3e99-4b99-a279-debd72341eff: "So you chose Nok-Nok. Very brave. Fighting me would have been more fun. And fair."
2a4eb794-ea16-49af-84a2-66a4154e44d8: "Well, then, Nok-Nok, you are no longer my ally. And worse, you are not a Hero, never were – I... I... I've always hated you, you... halfhead doorstop."
e69d14aa-a9b4-409f-82dc-c8356a95c64a: "Nok-Nok, listen to me. Cut yourself now, let a drop of blood hit the ground – then fight him only long enough to have him pin you with his foot, kick you, anything – do that, and he vanishes."
b32da097-b2e3-43bb-a075-8671550d198e: [Let Nok-Nok fight his own battle] "You'll have to fight him, Nok-Nok, you have no other choice."
2b12585e-8cae-4935-a2d6-b15d727b0124: "Hold on – maybe it'll drive them all away."
27723dae-aae8-48e3-9908-6fcc55204a92: "Now go out there and let him kick the hells out of you like a true goblin hero."
7500e20a-e92b-40e5-b359-163ddf53bdaf: "It's our best bet to end this without more bloodshed. Well, you might get hurt, but... forget it, go."
9145eab6-566e-4927-b5b1-b7d1fcaa4c10: "Stop questioning me and do as I command. Go."
7df912ec-f301-45ab-9581-e297ff35e1b5: "Well, at least I'll have one less goblin to worry about this when this is over."
553c2a91-ec03-49d5-b079-c3573adcb348: {n}Nok-Nok looks around, uncertain – you don't see anyone, and no goblin shapes about – and no sign of a goblin camp, either. Something feels wrong – there's a strange feel in the air, and that hint of sulfur, like you smelled on Nok-Nok's cap in the throne room.{/n}
35c16ce5-0381-480d-9213-21fe593ed6e6: {n}Nok-Nok speaks.{/n} "This the place. But… {d|GoblinKing}King{/d} not here yet?" {n}Nok-Nok sounds slightly relieved – but he still looks ready to bolt.{/n}
4bae0e8f-e1e9-48d2-be2f-af405f4e3d76: {n}Nok-Nok nods... and as he does, you suddenly notice the surroundings melt away into trails of acrid smoke... revealing a number of goblins, weapons at the ready.{/n}
5d5b21d5-7a40-4d0d-8cc5-d9e7fca8721f: {n}Still, while their weapons are drawn, they do not attack – they have a curious light in their eyes you haven't seen before – and it takes you a second to realize its determination. They don't look scared at all, merely stand at the ready, as if awaiting the command to attack.{/n}
af7ab28d-58a1-4609-993b-e27752d25eb5:
{n}As you take in your new opponents, a familiar figure emerges from the tree line – but walking strangely, as if fighting the urge to hunch down on all fours, almost feral.
The figure... looks... to be the Goblin King you recall, but something is wrong about him – it's like someone tried to cram a larger creature inside his skin. Tufts of fur, like that of a wolf, peak from his rags, and his eyes, rather than dull and soft, seem to hold cold fire in them.{/n}
d4aac425-0928-433b-8425-b64265e6ede4: {n}The king approaches, then stops, his face peeling back into an almost-demonic smile. This is not the king, but some creature wearing his shape.{/n}
803efed4-2d4e-47dd-b2f4-bee375daed3b:
{n}When you think it can't get any worse, there is a strangely familiar thundering noise, and into the clearing lumbers none other than the hill giant Munguk... and from the smell of it, he's definitely been drinking.
He stands behind the feral goblin king, his huge club of at the ready and gives a low rumble, then snarls, pounding his chest.{/n}
c2604a9f-784f-448a-82d6-7597f66c01d7: "Munguk say he not like us play trick on him, keep him waiting," {n}Nok-Nok whispers to you.{/n} "He say hard to wait forever for promised love, it worse than getting stabbed with lance." {n}Nok-Nok pauses.{/n} "Lance not kill him, though, I guess."
53c1d9eb-a3e9-42be-8b37-21586381b202: "Munguk say he not like us play trick on him, keep him waiting," {n}Nok-Nok whispers to you.{/n} "He say hard to wait forever for promised drinks, it worse than getting stabbed with lance." {n}Nok-Nok pauses.{/n} "Lance not kill him, though, I guess."
53d4fa3b-9e4a-4f3c-ab2c-82e7aae6ad39:
{n}The king gazes at you, and you feel your scalp rise – as he speaks, his voice is a rasp, like knives being dragged across metal plate.{/n}
"Which of you was once ruled by this ragged shape I wear? The sooner your blood coats the ground, the sooner my debt here is done – all you cattle smell alike to me whether you walk or roast on a skewer."
df4ca5f4-d34a-4bdf-8a37-4ab8ec794607: {n}The 'king' snarls.{/n} "I'm a barghest. I was summoned at the behest of a fey, to defeat an ally of one who claims this land… weakening this false {mf|king|queen} when the time of reckoning draws near."
c173ff04-ac30-4711-9d96-898a08dc83c7: {n}He nods at Nok-Nok and gives a barking laugh.{/n} "She said it could be any I chose, so I chose the weakest one at your court, if only to fulfill my debt all the quicker and leave this wretched place. The price was that I had to take the shape of this..." {n}He glances down at his body.{/n} "...humiliation."
b9921a62-ae37-4880-bca0-213fc450fd61: {n}The barghest growls... low in its throat, as if suspicious, then suddenly stops, sniffing the air. It advances slowly, and Nok-Nok looks about to withdraw, but you clamp him in place, forcing him to remain still.{/n}
82da2d53-1423-49c5-9d94-37c31911455a: {n}The barghest gives another sniff, then backs away, snarling.{/n} "It is no matter, I'll kill another."
87b94820-a4eb-43b3-97d9-9ad53017f4e1: "Spout you lies elsewhere, false {mf|king|queen}. I have no need for them."
dac7b34e-a243-428d-89ba-c6b30d308a7d: {n}The barghest growls, slowly and suspiciously, then to your surprise, answers in clear, precise speech.{/n} "When one of the allies of the Pretender to the Throne of the Stolen Lands lies beneath my feet, and their blood feeds the ground, I am freed – instantly, to return home and leave this vile plane behind me."
06fde29c-9503-4588-a59e-aa9800d9b943: "The wording?" {n}The beast glares at you.{/n} "Do you take me for a fool?"
80ff32d9-5647-4905-94cd-8390c9a0f554: {n}The barghest falls silent... and his eyes narrow suspiciously. Its skin twitches, and its lips peel back to reveal its fangs... it looks furious – but does not move to attack. In fact, it doesn't seem like it can... despite the blood-thirsty look in its eyes.{/n}
22bc02f2-6edd-4c64-bcb2-d8c5282d72ae: {n}The creature snarls.{/n} "I was told you are to be left for her. I care not why – but should you cross me, I've been given leave to slay you as well. It seems... she wishes you to suffer longer than this one..." {n}It grins wolfishly.{/n} "For the fey and those of my kind... that will prove a much longer time than your flesh can withstand."
6a14eca4-ee72-4d41-9ed5-19f3301d17be: {n}The 'King' turns to Nok-Nok.{/n} "Come, goblin... the sooner I make a sport of you, the sooner I will allow you to die... perhaps with your limbs intact."
971c4176-b33e-43b9-b8c5-6d13702666bf: "This we will find out soon enough, false {mf|king|queen}."
a5d9273f-bfcc-41fb-8934-f68a432dd350: {n}Nok-Nok turns to you, surprised, his eyes wide – he looks genuinely hurt at your words.{/n} "Not a hero? Never was?" {n}He pauses.{/n} "Also... doorstop?"
6da955f7-4be8-4e50-b65f-4ae2120c7e79: {n}Nok-Nok turns to you, perplexed... you realize he either doesn't believe you or doesn't understand what you're doing.{/n}
3aca32bd-c862-4563-b43e-98e09d554057:
{n}The creature seeing Nok-Nok's lack of comprehension, laughs.{/n}
"His split from you must be genuine, not some false oath or parlor trick. As long as he remains your ally, then I am bound as well."
58d5bf36-675c-40c5-bd18-47fe4c41ad76:
{n}The expression on the King's face is much different – it is surprise, but there is fear woven in as well.
Whatever you said, it worked... and you think it's placed the 'King' in a bad position. You try to ignore Nok-Nok's broken gaze as you face the barghest.{/n}
07ab0fbc-4c76-42c6-a3e0-d25c2775a906: {n}The creature gives a snarl, then takes a step back, then another... as if uncertain.{/n} "It is no matter, I'll kill another of your allies."
ec8915a6-2fe4-41c6-a3da-c68ace915d4a: {n}Instead, the barghest gives a blood-curdling howl, ichor spitting from its maw. It claws at the ground, ripping up great chunks of earth, then, swipes at you in a frenzied launch — and backs away, as if seeking to reach you, but unable to do so past some unseen force. Nok-Nok, behind an invisible wall formed by the shrieking beast, shrinks in terror.{/n}
e6b70f06-fcd9-4338-81ae-5ce817fcfb5c: {n}The other goblins in the circle seem to withdraw as well, terrified – whatever was keeping them at attention is broken, and you see fear coming in their eyes.{/n}
ec6e2cdf-5159-4357-8366-ebd587ef2d73: {n}The other goblins in the circle seem to withdraw as well, terrified – even Munguk seems surprised by the infernal fit – the hill giant backs away, as if from a rabid dog.{/n}
50cc4491-9753-439f-a9eb-09aa72409bf4: {n}Taking advantage of the creature's mad rage, you leap to attack — the creatures in the clearing falter, seeming hesitant to charge you and Nok-Nok, or get anywhere close to the tricked beast... you take advantage of the chaos and use their fear against them!{/n}
a61858e1-93fc-49b4-b99c-c3b1d2f8338f: {n}As you leap to attack, the barghest gives a howl, and the surrounding creatures charge you and Nok-Nok, echoing the barghest's howl.{/n}
8d4a5c61-66af-4555-9159-502d542dead9: {n}Nok-Nok looks at you blankly.{/n} "Let him kick me? Not sure like this plan..."
0ac9851d-2548-4762-a243-317c2272280e: {n}Wasting no time, you grab his hand, and keeping it from view of the barghest, slice it enough to let blood fall on the ground. Nok-Nok stares at his bleeding palm, until you forcibly curl his fingers back into his palm.{/n}
0251d98b-e0a8-4e5e-bb10-9891358d1b3d: {n}Nok-Nok advances slowly, and the barghest watches coldly, squatting slightly. Nok-Nok makes a strange sound in his chest, you realize he's speaking as if trying to soothe a guard dog, but no words are coming out...{/n}
1c7537d6-1267-4ce9-bdf2-06f6faea5e0a: {n}As he is about to reach the eager barghest, Nok-Nok stumbles, then falls face first... into the fire. Screaming, he howls and begins to jump in place, waving his hands in pain.{/n}
7bacbaaf-a966-4447-99d7-17b43fbec600: {n}Rather than attacking, the assembled creatures watch in surprise – and then, strangely begin to howl with laughter... infuriating the barghest.{/n}
de257b1e-af71-4c27-b123-a2f854263c01: {n}Snarling, the "king" leaps forward and hoists Nok-Nok into the air, then extends a claw – if you don't act, Nok-Nok will be gutted. Nok-Nok chokes and struggles in the creature's grip, helplessly...{/n}
5f349440-9e7d-4178-99d4-edbdd63b0b8b: {n}Snarling, the "king" leaps forward and knocks Nok-Nok to the ground, then begins to kick him a few times – you wince as you see one of Nok-Nok's teeth fly free from a kick, arcing through the air. Nok-Nok manages another scream, cut off as the barghest grinds its foot into his face, extinguishing the flames and his screams.{/n}
964d2067-362d-470b-9f1a-4b350bf36f04:
{n}When the unfortunate goblin is put out, the barghest glares at the surrounding creatures, and gives a snarl. Their laughter falls silent...
...all except one, a new voice, a little shaky, but one you recognize.{/n}
872bc101-b41a-4bcb-912a-8ab198c8466a: {n}Nok-Nok, bleeding from his split lip and kicks to the face, however, gives weak laugh.{/n} "Me beneath foot, blood..." {n}While blood already lies on the ground, Nok-Nok spits for good measure – adding more red to the ground.{/n} "...on dirt. Promise to mean flower lady done?"
21ae65f4-de3d-4eff-8535-50f66b437273: {n}The barghest's hand lashes through the air and impales itself in Nok-Nok's neck... the tiny goblin wriggles for a moment... then you watch him fall still. The barghest grins, then turns to you.{/n} "Creature died quicker than I'd like... but I'll take my time with you. I'll tell she who commands me there simply was no other choice."
ade610b5-fcbd-4c5a-8183-d55bc6a2c51f: {n}The barghest freezes in shock, then suddenly vanishes, leaving Nok-Nok alone on the ground. The surrounding goblins blink, as if a spell is removed... even Munguk looks confused by what has happened. Their shock won't last long.{/n}
75fdb549-5126-419b-bb32-c5ea47e106f4: {n}The barghest freezes in shock, then suddenly vanishes, leaving Nok-Nok alone on the ground. The surrounding goblins blink, as if a spell is removed... their shock won't last long.{/n}

5e662660-295d-4693-9c24-14e2e5752926: "It wasn't the most pleasant sight – those heads you'd sliced off. Of course, I can't judge you harshly for your decision, but still... cd8c24ec-f081-44c9-9734-198e7ca38553: "I could just assume you'd jump out of the ambush and capture the witch before she had a chance to kill me. 40865207-c260-415e-886f-9f49022ac7e2: "Gunderson himself doesn't bother me. It can't hurt to have him in the barony. 81b3369d-9643-4449-be73-51de5dc3aff0: "It's too bad the settlers decided to leave our lands. Well, at least that troublemaker won't be starting any more riots!"
a20089ae-d862-4d4d-9a4a-2d729795d2c4: "So the troublemaker walks free, and people who suffered her tricks have left Varnhold, so they won't be warning their fellows. This is bad! It means another riot. It's just a matter of time."
362feea8-f504-4f6e-af67-b64631c05c80: "So our people died at the hands of our soldiers, and the troublemaker who led them to their deaths walks free? What's to stop her from leading another lot of gullible settlers to the slaughter? I never expected such a failure from you!"
bd766bae-8b70-4d04-8a2a-8af4a1d1690b: "But yes, it was an insane plan. ffe74765-6b30-4037-abfd-3bdae75e09f8: "Of course, we won't go so far as to execute her. But keeping her in prison doesn't make any sense either. Let's take her to the border and give her the boot. 87008c10-7a7a-4c40-959c-35d9c9f9e7e5: "Well, we all make mistakes. The next time she shows up, try not to let her escape!"
d7ddf8b6-5b02-4ee8-8187-6fd8c5615e53: "I'll tell you all about it, but first pick your people. Three of our most reliable. There's a difficult task ahead of us."
fae5fce2-d786-47e3-a88b-2c97cd9abd45: {n}Maegar looks up at you and stares for a long time, as if he's thinking about asking you something else. But in the end he just nods.{/n} "I... thank you. You have no idea how glad I am to hear this."
9b5fb484-e3ce-460a-8ac3-55c4886687e3: {n}Maegar gazes at you, as if trying to read something in your eyes, and then sighs and nods.{/n} "I will consider that a 'no, commander, I'm not so tired of you that I quit and disappear right here.' That's something at least!"
a8769947-929d-45b8-b0f5-4a0c28aee5fb: "I received a letter with some threats. You do know how letters with threats make me laugh. Ha. Ha. 58bdd0d1-5755-4f7f-bddd-92404366410e: "One day I will certainly become a decent baron. I'll sit on the throne, sip wine and grow fat. e9316838-4793-4c23-a03c-41854f55ed81: "Remember that adventure in the three valleys, on the border between Rostland and Issia? 6fbc1603-54d0-473d-9ee1-0766bcff0d3a: {n}Maegar looks at you searchingly.{/n} "I'm probably not in a position to be jealous. But I'd still like to understand your priorities. 2ad6e27e-bdef-4b9f-8d02-997685813013: {n}Maegar casts an attentive look at you.{/n} "This barony is our common burden, {name}. I hope we have the same understanding of the great responsibility we bear."

7d12d318-5a83-4845-a51d-9523c868bd89: "Pff! Not a big deal! Find yourself a bear, tear a piece of his fur out, and slap it on your head! Done!"

85b3ef1e-97cb-459c-832a-65cadf1fccde: "Yeah, it's great! But it's inborn – you either have it or you don't. To learn magic you'd have to read books like Octavia!"

f8073316-a684-4495-a1eb-1d03967b162d: "Then I will order training camps built. Don't worry, I'll make sure the new recruits learn everything as swiftly as possible."

2052c88e-b3b6-4dc0-9cf1-27aa59ff13ab: "The Healing Light burns in the hearts of thousands upon thousands of believers. In trying to insult my goddess, you're only displaying your own ignorance."

fc9056c7-4525-4b48-9aec-d85d4be1a418: {n}As Regongar clenches his fists, Octavia places a hand on his shoulder.{/n} "Easy, now... Let him finish."

ae5a6b59-e911-4b48-a397-82905110ef8e: "Agdan thought a while on what to do, then wisely decided that a tribe doesn't need two chieftains — sold the weaker one to someone from the city to get back some of the gold he spent. e4e78f5c-dee1-4f6e-815b-abf89f1fea11: "Field rations sap all my inspiration. You want real poetry? Then give me real food!"
b03ff298-da97-482d-9559-012acb6d78f7: "Oh, now, now — don't worry, Nok-Nok. I can't steal something you don't have."
d947a1da-9f47-4d2a-b287-4c228445a963: "I am loyal to my subjects, not to a group of crazy fanatics!"
aa3f18f5-3708-47fe-8df1-83c51118b930: "Stop! You don't know what you're doing!"

4575bfda-6475-4e2b-b502-c997d56965e8: "It's too late to offer peace and friendship, isn't it?"

ae3c00de-2f84-465d-977a-d2401afe61d5: {n}Yelling and swinging their weapons, the crowd attacks!{/n}

6ddc3158-5e13-414a-a59d-a0f772a6d526: "Let me think. Hmmm. No. You stink."

7c805a34-6751-4094-8a86-8d179bee5afa: "{name}, it's time we discuss one of the gravest problems of the {g|River Kingdoms}River Kingdoms{/g}: piracy and all the crimes which accompany it. 48a0090b-6bf7-468c-883d-4a96c1b5da92: "{mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, I'd ask you to address an important issue. 69983992-6618-467d-9d00-960c88cb7854: "Once we expel those traffickers, our domain will no longer be seen as a safe haven for pirates. Were I ruler, I should do the same."
268f7ed5-c62f-4afa-8397-265961ef2921: "So, we shall put an end to the illegal trade of stolen goods in these lands. What music to my ears! 5c95c64a-70eb-43c8-af6c-3141804477e9: "A fine solution. Of course, we shan't tarnish our reputation. The sale of stolen and smuggled goods is far beneath us. 29f6d0ee-2b7b-40c7-84ff-698d94399198: "One might call it a boon – lawless captains bringing their fortunes here. But it's worth remembering that their money is covered in blood. ee9789a1-185a-4432-9e9f-545a6ba9d82a: "Someone else might suggest you take advantage of the situation: simply collect your fees and don't ask too many questions about the blood these goods are soaked in. I warn against tolerating things as they now stand. Establish proper customs in your harbor, and hunt down these lawless captains."
1b8d00bd-c49d-4b76-bd2a-754c2c65c6bb: "The merchants fear that you might yet put an end to their shady dealings, that the customs authorities and guards might grow increasingly stricter and less forgiving. c0aa8fb1-fb86-4954-89b6-6b0e4664affc: "I've put off this conversation for a long time, but I can't do it any more. 2c122a69-0f95-4916-96e6-a632aa6b2f45: "Since I took the position of Treasurer, I've dedicated myself to strengthening the legitimacy of your power. 0f530901-8b11-423e-b729-738bd5a8f206: "Yes, clandestine trade does bring a lot of gold into the treasury. However, your good name is easily sold – but impossible to buy back! 5961914b-a995-4aac-b620-7456dfe8a837: "I will go immediately to organize customs. That's the decision of a true sovereign, whose country will stand not for days and weeks, but for years and ages! b1f83b3f-ddc9-45a4-8959-7d4db6cc858b: "Why did you need the First Crown?"
290cede8-21db-4d02-90cc-4ae1d8ddd2fd: "Why are you enemies with the Knurly Witch?"
e22719dd-6897-4686-9276-5755705ac62b: "I have no more questions about this."
e59018eb-3608-4d00-b8cd-40f3d5e0c79d: "What if I give you the Crown?"
0e9846a4-06a7-4347-b734-62c81be23387: "Where can I find the Knurly Witch?"

db47ea7a-6b5d-4237-b68c-f81daa4f4874: {n}The Wriggling Man seems to barely notice you. The worms are wriggling, busy in their communion.{/n}
129d73f9-16f6-4a70-9cd9-7ed24f8da2d9: {n}The worms on the creature's face lazily ball up and untwine again.{/n} "Ask if you wish. But don't expect us to spend much time on you and your curiosity."

fdeb60a3-b4fd-4022-8cf4-1358efc9e9d9: "What are you hoping to do in the Shrine, foolish creature? Never mind, it matters not. Nyrissa will reduce you to dust the instant you set foot through the door. Should we waste our time talking to a dead {mf|man|woman}?"

6cae521c-02b2-42ba-8210-16c9c79f8dc2: {n}The Wriggling man replies with a hundred-voice sigh, full of unconcealed irritation.{/n} "Do we really have to spend time on this? Well, some new worm food won't hurt..."
9b5cbf29-8a47-4683-9614-f79e7d92b3d4: "Be careful on the roads of {g|First World}the First World{/g}, guest. You never know where they might take you."
83f4cd2d-554f-45d5-bde1-dd8dc59729e8: "What an incredible pleasure it is to hear this. You deserve our respect, guest. For this we shall give you a quick and painless death. Nyrissa shall know that I am her most worthy servant and protector!"
ab6afd26-92fa-4dea-9549-2ec3eb9c4dbe: "You are trying our patience. We hope at least you're not doing so out of idleness."
a0366d84-0546-4d42-be23-7383c6ca15c4: {n}A wave passes through the creature's body. The worms arch and twist. 575d99d0-5fae-45de-a63d-f1dbe783b7d0: "Time flies quickly, guest. Think while you can. Act when you're ready."
3605eb4e-8de5-46e4-9225-285a2e71b074: "It means nothing by itself. We would like to take it from the corpse of the disgusting witch, or receive it from the gracious hands of Lady Nyrissa."
f0caefda-8c2c-42c7-9a6f-dde98ce89614: "This feud is older than you can imagine. The Knurly Witch has always feared that we would take Lady Nyrissa's affection away from her. cf28bf08-fbe8-46f6-838e-fdda8dbaf993: "It's a gift with which Lady Nyrissa marked the Knurly Witch as one of her most worthy servants. This was before our arrival at the House at the Edge of Time. The witch has had her day. We want her death, and we want recognition!"
c80e8cac-e421-4efe-b1fe-d505e15a14f1: "It's good that you know when to stop. So many don't..."
6ce5d8d1-e8af-4839-8f4f-648fdb8d8d78: "What? What do you {d|c61 Mirrors}mean{/d}?" {n}You feel a strange tension in the Wriggling Man's thousand-voice question. e0ef0842-eefc-4a90-a944-8d80010f9a16: {n}Finally the mirror stops showing pictures from the past, and all that remains is a regular reflection of the Wriggling Man's cruel face — a ball of twitching worms under the shadow of a black hood.
