It will let the others of my family know that you are a friend." {n}She gives you a shallow bow and then departs for the docks.{/n}
3c2d8794-6675-4a88-86bb-9589c46da853: {n}As Eimar and Talwyn depart, Renshala approaches you.{/n} "I would be overjoyed if not the deaths of my people. However, thanks to you, justice was served. This makes us even." {n}She gives you a shallow bow and then departs for the docks.{/n}
a46cb6c7-7979-488c-89a3-549d1dc6a66d: "You are beautiful, Valerie, especially for a human. This is not meant as a compliment, merely a statement of fact. It would be a pity if this beauty leaves the world."
2a1c0b3d-ea51-4695-a770-0b8f613f90a0: "Do you suggest I follow Urgathoa's path and get myself stuck between life and death? I don't think I'd like it."
09a4f3a2-54a4-4a56-8ca4-d574766044fa: "How can you be happy, and make plans for your future? Every moment you laugh or peacefully enjoy your life, someone somewhere else is breathing their final breath."
1480f700-e064-41a0-8fc8-9f3010dfdae1: "Every time you open your mouth, my hope for a relaxing evening fades. Please don't get all wound up."
c6703c71-22b2-490d-aaf5-9bc063504056: "It appears that we've hopelessly lost the opportunity to hunt down the half-blood. My agents discovered the dead body of a priestess of {g|Urgathoa}Urgathoa{/g}, who he'd been chasing. As for Enneo himself, he's disappeared without a trace, just like last time."
36e5a832-81f2-40b4-975f-7d48ea517014: "Someday I'll write a play about our adventures... And you'll have one of the main parts!"
6b1b73de-c180-4627-92ad-09968cbdd305: "Then we'll see if there's at least one actress brave enough to go on stage and impersonate me... Knowing that I'll be sitting in the front row!"
981ce0cc-0d1d-4084-a276-e7c4b9e7c3dc: "You know, Tristian, we have much more in common than you think. You say everyone deserves a chance to atone. But isn't life after death such a chance?"
f224ec81-99c9-41bb-913d-ba99f28b5005: "Perhaps. If so, I pray that you do use this chance to atone at last."
8b48534c-35d1-49d3-b027-c2848dd3f9f7: "Tristian, tell me! Is everyone so boring in Kelesh? Or were you banished from there for your boring sermons?"
e8268bfc-6209-42fe-863d-afcb9f770ae5: "I went on this journey of my own free will, with Sarenrae's blessing... Why are you giggling? Did I say something funny?"
885363da-eb2c-4181-b00b-5d7645e4d58d: "It isn't my fault — I was attacked!"
5f23f727-cce1-4219-a04b-0083ba7e0d80: "You don't tell me what to do! I'll fight whoever I want!"
fbe2dd56-cad9-4afc-96f4-4bc0cdc75793: "This is a misunderstanding. There was no fight — I'm sure we can sort everything out here and now."
fb122fae-3ef4-40a0-975f-4fc2fea1288b: {n}A crowd gathers, attracted by the noise and screams. All the guests brought bodyguards, and you soon find yourself surrounded by a small army — not even counting Irovetti's guard. It isn't long before the king of {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g} himself shows up.{/n}
414b4788-fb93-4ea1-8616-13e1ddfa13b3: "What is this? A fight? At my tournament? Unheard of! Scandalous! A slap in the face — not just to me, but to each of my deeply respected guests! For shame! Disgraceful!"
9ebeccce-0d62-48bc-a251-822c6255e3cc: "A lie! Lying to my face! I already know what happened here — you drew your weapon first, broke my seal! Trampled on the spirit of peace and friendship that has always reigned at my tournaments! Stomped on my trust!"
e72e4f7c-fc02-4dc9-9892-63df7ce22666: {n}Irovetti ostentatiously covers his face with his hand.{/n} "Unheard of. Monstrous! I cannot condone this."
a6226005-ff3a-4381-803a-4282a5b55e05: {n}He sighs bitterly before loudly announcing,{/n} "It breaks my heart, but I must take all possible measures to protect my precious guests. Alas, today's celebration was attended by a crowned barbarian — a monster, incapable of peacefully participating in high society. It is with a heavy heart that I must announce that the tournament is canceled. With this monster present, I simply cannot guarantee this celebration won't turn into a bloodbath!"
87b9d03d-e59b-418f-bbb6-a51b55cc4e19: {n}The crowd mutters with disappointment as Irovetti nods you toward the exit.{/n} "Leave. Just leave. We won't stoop to your level by tainting this feast day with further violence. But know this — you are welcome here no longer!"
75a7f736-4205-4607-a6cd-c1d2a2e7dcac: "No fight, you say? But then why is the seal on your sheath broken? The very seal that has long symbolized the spirit of peace and friendship that reigns over my tournaments! You broke it with your own hand, and along with it, the feeble flower of our trust!"
b22a7ee5-d4e8-4eec-8092-6ddbfe6cbb46: "Do you hear that, lords and ladies? Do you hear, my respected guests? You can put a crown on an owlbear, but it will still reveal itself the moment it opens its beak. And the people of {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g} found {mf|him|her}, this bloodthirsty beast, worthy of a royal title?"
384bdc18-a384-4e58-81df-e5e6ca30b8ec: "What is this? Thievery? Infiltration? Espionage, here, right in my personal camp? Or an assassination attempt?! Unheard of! Scandalous! A slap in the face — not just to me, but to each of my deeply respected guests! For shame! Disgraceful!"
755c76c3-9acb-4b1d-b5ff-964d9ffa2a4b: "I cannot believe that you, whom I trusted from the bottom of my heart, would betray my trust so! Using the revelry and peace of our friendship to prepare a deadly trap for your host! Tell me — what did you have in store? A dagger? A garrote? Bomb? Poison, perhaps? No, no, don't say a thing — I don't want to know!"
20b6cdae-6ba9-472b-b14e-b0cb104b13ad: "Listen here, you crowned boar! You should be thankful {Name} even showed up at your stinking tournament!" {n}Regongar spits at Irovetti's feet.{/n} "Sure, we'll go. The food is shit, and the entertainment's only good for someone who got dropped on their head as a child. But we'll be back, you hear me? And when we are, we'll be sure to cut some royal bacon off you!"
f8083f96-67a5-4ce6-ac0d-778bdb3a0bec: "Oh, yes... I see you've found companions worthy of you!"
dd3471fc-0899-4f01-b27d-4b5a01d55936: "Do many people in Restov venerate Erastil?"
774c1231-1562-4a98-ad4f-1c9289740fd9: "I worship Erastil as well. Please, may I receive your blessing?"
612a8b17-4009-4d3a-9761-8fcb78cd8a16: "Bringing law into the Stolen Lands is a difficult endeavour. I would be grateful for any help you could spare!"
b3634c65-628b-456c-9192-7e40303d8c89: "You're dressed surprisingly simply for such a festive occasion."
39b9560e-99d2-4d39-8c31-6dde13857a4c: "It was an honor to meet you. Goodbye."
6dc5a240-06a9-4de2-a023-621d49bbe42e: "The gods are monsters, priest. Fretful monsters that don't deserve to be worshipped."
78c6571e-2023-4f6e-9941-eed4d17225e0: "I saw how you fought beside Jamandi that night... Your god granted you impressive power!"
c44ba120-f1ce-4ba1-acca-0bfe935bd7c2: {n}A handsome man with a weather-beaten face grasps your hand tightly in his rough, calloused palms. Unlike the rest of the guests in their festive clothes, he wears a simple robe — the only luxury you see on him is a holy symbol of {g|Erastil}Erastil{/g} made of solid gold. The other guests look at him with respect, some bordering on awe.{/n}
f3dfe60e-4cd8-4861-8862-9f43e7b94357: "Congratulations on your victory," {n}he says in a deep voice.{/n} "Allow me to introduce myself. I am Ezvanki Keeg, High Priest of {g|Erastil}Erastil{/g} in {g|Restov}Restov{/g}."
37240614-d138-4163-bed7-833ec782a70d: "They revere many gods in {g|Restov}Restov{/g}. They pray to {g|Abadar}Abadar{/g}, patron of cities, and {g|Pharasma}Pharasma{/g}, gatherer of souls... There are also some more rare cults. But there's no denying that the {g|Erastil}Stag God{/g} has the largest congregation here. And no wonder — people here have lived off farming and hunting for centuries."
e557eb56-3841-4e1d-9110-660443ce112c: "It's a pleasure to know the baron{mf||ess} is not only brave, but also pious. Let {g|Erastil}Erastil{/g} keep you in his grace!"
a273c9ac-d359-48e8-85a4-362fa530f7b3: "This is a truly noble undertaking. I believe our community will be able to provide you with reasonable assistance. We will help you construct a shrine in your capital, free of charge."
d0668909-9502-4a61-8733-b9d5f831ea50: "Our most pious aspirations are often hindered. But is it not the case that overcoming such obstacles allows us to become closer to our god? I give you my blessing, and I believe you will be able to overcome these hardships and achieve your goals!"
79aecf36-2e8d-4ff3-bc29-0a724093630a: {n}The corners of the priest's mouth turn up in a faint smile.{/n} "The nobles dress in silks and satins to stand out from the poor. A priest wears a simple robe to stand out from the nobles."
8238c46f-834a-4842-8c31-a4c3de8d2c99: "The higher powers have favored you so far. May they stay with you in the future!"
d806ecda-89c0-4e1f-b53b-aadeba678e6a: "Do you really believe that? Well, it saddens me to hear you think so."
d54bd5ca-30d4-473d-9012-f300160157a1: "Yes, I used to serve {g|Erastil}Erastil{/g} on the battlefield, but those days are long past. Now I call on his power to heal those who've fallen from a roof more often than anyone wounded by a sword! Of course, someone has to roam the forests and slay monsters, but I'm more useful to my congregation here, attending to more mundane affairs, like hospitals, shelters, and charity fairs."
82dfa3a9-57c3-4784-9913-6c8b5d94560d: "Why did you want that flower so bad?"
81d4309f-3ba2-4d59-ab91-2025b7fb6573: "I see. No need to tell me anything, then."
47fc43ed-528f-4312-884c-0569c0b381c6: "Are you going to tell me or what?''
1a52366c-74b6-4baf-bab4-eb0dfa8c2f2d: "What did you want to ask me?"
acc61fdd-20eb-4134-8a9a-b64af80cb80c: "You seem to put a lot of trust in this hunter's opinion."
7c2c51d7-767d-4ac5-a2fb-89370f055333: "Take a look – is this necklace any good?"
463c76d3-fa3e-4d56-ac68-1d8106cc083c: "Tell me what went wrong between you two. You had a fight?"
e166589f-b825-4795-aa52-42115feab34a: "What do you mean, she 'hid in her tree'?''
7cd0a71f-ce23-4908-8cde-4d1c0f70fc0e: "Show me on the map where to find her."
e58972ad-305f-4d2b-98a1-1386b8ae1914: "I see. Well, I have no wish to interfere in your affairs."
009d85f8-b152-4510-8645-ed9b3686bf15: "I've had a chat with your dryad."
2191321e-b238-478d-9284-96bdd9423aa9: "Go to her. She's waiting for you."
1fa5d884-5f32-4e7c-949f-07158fca9663: "It didn't work out... I'm sorry, Kimo."
2d71b61a-c3a9-414c-ad31-4bec583f6cca: {n}Kimo closes his eyes in reverie.{/n} "Kyonin. The land of the elves. The land of springs and forests. That is where I learned my craft..."
7207626e-da9d-4916-aeb5-8eb2c11c2642: "You would love it there. Everybody does."
144e1494-c0af-4a9f-9b62-6032091ee0e2: "Nobody made me leave!" {n}Kimo gives you an embarrassed look.{/n} "I just woke up one day, looked out the window… and the road called. And I went!"
d3a0640d-4f6c-436a-b23f-e61821048f96: "Oh! I don't want to tell! But since you asked me, it would have been awkward if I refused."
682aa980-d0bf-4164-9bfa-c85e95295bba: "But you must have been there already. And if not, then you should! You won't regret it."
7ef5d980-edb3-433d-8ad0-8ff351925d3b: "Well… fine then." {n}The elf sounds somewhat disappointed.{/n}
9db539cf-64c2-453e-91ae-ec01c5891327: {n}The elf awkwardly picks at the ground with the toe-cap of his boot.{/n}
d2aabbc8-def5-4fd4-a9c0-fb46ae3e06ea: "Alright, alright…" {n}The elf takes a deep breath.{/n}
4f65185d-0a16-4cfa-924d-d6e4082f638d: "I… I am in love. With a lady in the forest."
9faa36d2-5401-4dd6-b4d9-a6f6e75f2378: "That flower was for her. I cannot tell you who she is. But she had hidden herself from me, and that is what darkens my days."
4168301a-17f1-41bb-9815-efeac8986b40: "Thank you! If only I could be happy as well…"
f6fb390a-d1d6-4ebc-91b0-b32c13ec8a01: {n}{d|Kimo}Kimo{/d} gives you a dreary nod.{/n} "Good day…"
40bb15d9-40ee-48df-8cb5-bcf94647c1a1: {n}Kimo looks at you with regret.{/n} "Forgive me, friend! I did not wish to disappoint you…"
b6f2a1d0-725f-404c-8952-3367c3b1be5c: "You won't believe this! It's about her!"
a486ea7a-1d90-430b-ad4d-05070f80b4dd: "She finally agreed to go on a date with me! I need to get ready!"
9856b0d1-9835-44fb-be5d-7db52eadac73: "A hunter I know said that you only need one thing to woo a lady: a gift. Maybe... maybe an emerald necklace would do! But I wouldn't even know where to start looking for such a thing! Please, help me. I will repay you, I promise."
ed090a64-64c5-4d5e-afc3-ddda4d441f52: "Well… I don't really know… But surely, something that can't be found in every shop or roadside tavern."
9e2b63a6-cfad-40c5-b8e8-6469237473ae: "He talks a lot, and the other villagers listen to him." {n}Kimo bends over and whispers in a conspiratorial tone.{/n} "To be completely honest, I sometimes think that he's… you know… a bit slow." {n}The elf gives you a meaningful glance, his eyebrows raised high.{/n} "But he has a lot of experience. He knows a lot of things that I have no idea about!"
1556d929-e086-4044-a875-f6a391b4f392: "I knew it!" {n}Kimo is as happy as a cat that's found a pot of cream.{/n} "You are always so kind! And I will help you in return – you'll see!"
532cdc7a-0ff7-4e73-8b85-54db1a1c00fd: {n}Kimo is scratching his head helplessly.{/n} "Of course, {name}. As you wish! Thanks for hearing me out…"
7c1e1cf3-b622-42f8-8bea-09eb84f2dd38: "Oh, thank you so much! That's very noble of you – after all, you're so busy all the time…" {n}Kimo's face radiates wholehearted gratitude.{/n} "Take as much time as you need."
422ffede-61e2-43a1-8baf-49d6e89ed5d0: "I'll come up with something so… so special…" {n}Kimo's gaze wanders far away.{/n}
5a6303be-6c03-493b-9be9-3a2fb5d4f46e: {n}A happy, dreamy smile blooms on the elf's face. The next moment, however, his eyes widen, and huge beads of sweat cover his forehead.{/n}
2c03a34e-7252-47e8-930a-26f37e09cd51: "Then… then I should go." {n}Kimo gulps and gives you a weary sideways look.{/n} "Thanks, {name}. You've done me a great service. I already know how I shall repay you – I'll make you a bow. The best bow in the world! But now I must go." {n}Kimo exhales decisively and slowly walks away.{/n}
9012d229-8bd5-47fb-a04d-869a74160b67: "I don't know… Everything went so well after our first date. We spent every day together. We talked, we gathered flowers, we watched the clouds pass by… And then, one evening, she said 'goodbye' – and hid herself inside her tree. She hasn't shown her face or said a word to me ever since. No matter how many times I've asked..."
fdbeb0c2-e743-49fb-8380-2e8e979ea507: {n}Kimo heaves another heavy sigh.{/n} "She's a dryad… Her body and spirit are tied to an oak. She takes care of it and protects it. I met her when I was in the forest, trying to find my way to this settlement."
08f59c5a-1c7e-459e-a285-67301548e193: "But you can't help… Her heart knows no mercy. You cannot change her wooden mind…"
06e2d4c9-0d2f-483b-a391-1c4cc50aeb0f: "And?" {n}The elf's fingers are twisting into a knot.{/n}
1006d6ef-def6-41b5-8bb2-338d53f03c77: "I knew this would happen. Thank you for at least trying… It's time for me to go. Far, far away from here."
55a9a94a-1384-4163-af18-72cd34164760: "Most nobles are noble only in words. But you have a noble heart."
99776385-c28a-4587-9663-817a9b5ee8c2: "Thank you. Truth be told, the false nobleness you mean was precisely what I ran away from. To someplace where people are tested by their deeds, not by their words."
762876cd-5fe2-4795-8f00-81c01516cc38: "Poor Willas Gunderson! If only he knew where his thirst for adventure would lead him..."
691edb79-ea8b-44b5-b945-4c46f9322af0: "The thirst for adventure is not inherently dangerous. But together with dilettantism and a rare lack of ingenuity..."
4ddcda0c-4a79-4f6a-bc31-1dd315b035ff: "I often ponder this at night. How can you avoid trouble, if you don't know what it might be?"
e06b705b-1bca-4be7-a832-fd4643f92612: "If it wasn't him, it would have been someone else. And if not — then Vordakai's role would have been served by plague, or war, or simple famine."
b350982c-53b4-4dd9-a6c1-41b7259f362f: "Fearsomeful! Don't want to be like that, ever. Better stay dead for good. Even better stay alive for good!"
b211d5e1-8a17-49b6-b4b4-3b28ecd692de: "I saw what a terrible blow you suffered in that fight. Are you sure you're all right?"
1aa511fa-0da6-414d-9066-91a413eba412: "It's not often that one gets to see a walking corpse so close... And one that's barely standing, at that. You should heal yourself, or whatever you call it."
77fb23f1-409c-4258-82a3-50d95751960a: "I'm sorry, Jaethal. You were... gravely wounded today. Several times. They knocked the living daylights out of you! Ah, ha, ha, ha, ha!"
2700040f-38f7-42ef-809c-9c7e9ec60bf5: "I'm sorry, but your wounds... They still haven't healed. It's a horrible sight, but I can't look away."
e07b8c28-3064-48fc-9196-0f04db7ff8e5: "I wait when you become deadmeat. Dead deadmeat. Soon."
cb73e90b-62e2-48e6-b21e-5aaea97bb954: "Assuming I oppose Irovetti, will the old families support me?"
bf9daae5-fdc4-46d3-b693-318cfbca7ff6: "What I'm going to tell you will persuade the other trade houses to join the rebellion."
f0d5ca20-5036-41fa-86d4-58c7395e3b21: [Attack] "Pitax will be mine. I will cut down all of its elite... Starting with you!"
53e945ce-a645-42e0-9255-2decd8480362: "I have to go. Keep your eyes open."
c43fb781-588f-45fa-a589-b3fbd2d5260b: "And I suppose CASTRUCCIO Irovetti's least favorite joke is the one about his name?"
2bb58bae-44e9-40e7-b1cb-a505ab6a3ee2: "If that's the kind of comedy they teach at the Academy of Grand Arts, then I'm not surprised Linzi has no desire to return there..."
e2ac052b-e56e-466a-acf8-5fb2fb6649a4: "Regongar, we're having a serious discussion. Can you tone down the buffoonery?"
d825986b-661b-492a-b484-5b687f3fc2a7: "There you are, Your Highness. Irovetti is expecting you to bend the knee. But I suspect you have other plans..."
13cc3474-c9ed-4f68-8f1a-d78cc61752b5: "I am the head of the Liacenza family and the Iron Fox Trade House. We ruled {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g} not long ago, before that scoundrel Irovetti seized the crown — and most of our property. Now the old families hold but a sliver of their former influence. But we still live on... Quietly hoping for revenge..."
0bcf7911-4512-4f94-8ca3-9d845dfb1646: "You can count on help from the Liacenza family. But regarding the other trade houses... I've tried to unite them many times, but the stubborn fools would sooner die alone than triumph united. I have no idea what might bring them into line."
61f5a21f-3ecb-44de-a6a0-e7cd3920b3fb: "Of course this is sickening, but I don't think any of the old families would be sufficiently outraged by this to oppose Irovetti openly."
6315cc5b-2416-4940-a702-cc26a8430576: "I'm afraid this is nothing shocking. Every family has had business partners of that sort."
27c653a6-835a-4374-93c0-bb48f3cf0c28: "If you can find some dirt that will convince the other families to unite, then victory is in our pocket!"
e8697eda-76d5-4342-b7fa-7e32ae60b866: "By the gods... This is unheard of! I will immediately dispatch my people to the Abbey and the other families. If this is true... then Irovetti will face blood vengeance from all the families!"
575c818e-c9b3-46c4-89ae-84fcfeefb2ab: "Interesting! So he didn't create the {g|Academy of Grand Arts}Academy{/g} for his love of the arts, ha ha... But what does this have to do with the trade houses?"
6efab205-df02-46f4-bd0f-ed9efd15a2d2: "The forces of all the old families are at your side. We are ready to march on your command!"
f2b3d11f-42d4-442b-86a0-21db7b0fa6f8: {n}Gasperre greets you with a polite bow.{/n} "Your Highness. My family is deeply in your debt, as is all of {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g}."
7e53c225-7427-42fe-8a10-6004566d56a5: "Hello, Your Highness." {n}Gasperre's voice is polite, but a little cold.{/n}
b19775ca-c51d-49cd-bc9d-b009f410712e: "It's quiet in the city — if such a word could ever be used to describe {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g}. The old families have retrieved their property – with little trouble. The guild is quiet, and there are fewer drugs on the streets. It's almost like the good old times, before Irovetti!"
fbd3f09e-9f71-4ee4-b5cc-79ebabf47b5c: "Well... things are worse than they were under Irovetti... The thieves' guild is running wild – with your permission, no doubt. They take what they want and murder any who object, or oust them from the city. The streets are drowning in bloodbrush extract, which is now sold on every corner. It wasn't like this under the old families — we knew where to draw the line!"
4ad50fef-b238-40b3-8ad9-e12eef375438: "Not so well. There's fighting in the back streets, docks, and alleys – quiet, but ferocious. Assets change hands every day. The old families, the thieves' guild, new adventurers — everyone wants a piece."
50a85b11-0257-4dee-b4bb-a81261e4a798: "Horrible. I'll be honest with you, Your Highness. The first kings were no fools. — They created the city guard for a reason. Today, all that they tried to avoid is now happening in the city: everyone is fighting everyone else. The old families, the thieves' guild, and a whole crowd of new adventurers — all killing each other in the middle of the street. Not a night passes without a fire. You've made a tremendous mistake, Your Highness, and I'm not sure it can ever be fixed."
ceb173f6-073b-4875-acbc-92070160af69: "Must be hard doing business in a place called 'Pay-Tax,' ha ha!"
2133672a-097e-4ea8-86a2-dd2e6b34c984: {n}Gasperre chuckles.{/n} "Don't think you're the first to come up with that pun! I've even heard it's one of Irovetti's favorites!"
fa8a2b74-aa52-4f73-b8d2-650822520f52: "Ha ha ha! It's a gold mine of jokes!"
f83aebb5-96cc-492f-baef-8cf3694f83c5: "Heh heh! Once we've taken care of Irovetti, maybe I'll go there to give lectures. With a special course on gallows humor!"
c5661d87-6235-4171-80ae-9c55d8323adf: {n}Realizing you're not paying attention to his joke, Regongar starts to examine the street around him with a long face.{/n}
efa23ed6-3dda-4a3f-af8f-64b621e66f55: "Fine, fine... I'll be quiet. It was just a joke..."
e2748e72-9a6c-4917-a166-3d90b43b5c84: "I'm afraid for you, Harrim. This whisper... I fear it might do terrible harm to your mind."
e0139485-b440-44b2-b65c-606c1c4b798d: "Tristian, Tristian... I understand when others talk to me about insanity, but you are a priest – anointed to mysteries of your deity! Would you reject the revelations of Sarenrae, if they would cost you your mind?"
ab045919-5cbb-445d-85be-185a01033e06: {n}As you pick up the purse, a jubilant scream comes from the bushes, and someone or something starts yanking on the rope — so hard you almost stumble.{/n}
a15ea176-23c1-4c7a-aeba-24861a08f395: {n}Rather than fight it, you let go off the purse. It flies into the bushes with a KRAK, followed by a howling scream. A group of goblins emerge, snarling and shaking their fists.{/n}
eb07556f-ec5f-4e2d-9bf9-08e38a80d459: {n}Before you can react, you're pulled to the bushes still holding the purse. There, waiting for you, is a snare, surrounded by a band of goblins, screaming triumphantly. They snatch up their weapons and leap to attack!{/n}
ce0e861f-827f-4671-a4fa-134d80c791ea: {n}Whoever is holding the rope, he's strong — keeping a grip on the purse, you try to keep your footing, but you're being dragged into the bushes!{/n}
4697c7b9-5510-4b72-bb9d-04924e12cf77: {n}A large coin purse lies in the middle of the road. The purse is tied to a rope, awkwardly covered with dust as if to mask its presence — the rope winds its way to a cluster of dense bushes nearby.{/n}
aed82855-85fd-4368-901a-2a71f25f9359: {n}You pull the rope and there is a shout. A moment later, a band of goblins leaps out from the bushes, screaming and shouting.{/n}
064ac6c4-edca-40df-8fcf-14afe4c0fc4a: {n}The underground lake looks like a silver mirror. The reflections on its surface are so clear that you can make out every wrinkle in your clothes and the individual strands of your hair. What you can't make out, though, is anything that may be hidden beneath the water.{/n}
e329a1b1-356a-4f0e-a7b7-9bad2a479afd: {n}You dive deeper and deeper, pushing yourself until you feel the bottom of the lake beneath your hands, and something more — something metallic. A dagger lies beside the body of a young blond man. The weapon is in perfect condition, despite its submersion. It may be a trick of the mind, but as you leave, the dead man's body shifts, and it seems almost like a nodded farewell, like the man wishes you luck and hopes to be avenged.{/n}
8c785121-4574-4be7-ad37-17a79dd7e642: {n}You lack the strength to dive deeper. If this lake hides further secrets, they're doomed to remain undiscovered.{/n}
8b741bb4-89a9-4674-92f2-fadd53e8f063: {n}You dive into the lake. You once more notice the silvery quality of the water, as though it's been imbued with light, or perhaps radiates it. But the things hidden by the placid shimmering are horrible. Below your feet, at the bottom of the lake, float at least two dozen corpses. The dead seem to stare at you — some with the empty sockets of hollow skulls, and others with nightmarish dead eyes. One body floats past you, and you feel a small metal object fall into your hand. It looks like a signet ring.{/n}
1427045d-06e4-4e57-ab2a-fc508b565605: {n}One of the dead bodies wears a purple belt. Another is clad in a black vest with bright green embroidery... You easily recognize the insignias of the four Trade Houses. There are dead bodies here from all the great families that once ruled Pitax.{/n}
6b3a6b05-39fb-41d2-ac2b-733d6b543a92: {n}You lack the knowledge necessary to learn much about the dead bodies from just the visible details. You can only assume they were once {g|Pitax}Pitaxian{/g} nobles.{/n}
21fed278-1ea9-4e82-80f8-a67b3a531b2e: {n}You dive underwater, back among the corpses floating forlornly in the depths.{/n}
bed8e15c-e48d-49a4-9967-af98478c1c72: {n}Harrim clasps his hands over his belt and looks around serenely.{/n} "Such a lovely place... Once, the pointless vanity of life seethed here, but now there is only desolation and calm. Am I the only one who feels it? The beauty of desolation and cold imminence..."
c7a12da3-64eb-442b-a715-8871ebd8d289: "I sense Desna's mark upon you, stranger. Does the goddess teach her followers to attack the unarmed and threaten passers-by?"
f57d5efb-ba95-412e-8c1f-97986c6b475a: "How about we tame this insolent fellow's tongue?"
583e4544-c37c-4940-a696-71b97ffa850a: "You worship Desna, stranger, and Desna is a good goddess. Do not discredit her with unworthy actions."
795081f9-6f17-4f6a-ba03-b6499e5d75b7: [Look closer at the symbols that the centaurs are wearing]
87c3f376-f8c2-441b-a818-08f4fb7af88d: "Be easy, brave protector of the Nomen tribe. I know that you share no bonds of friendship with the 'two-legged', but we are not Taldans. We are not the invaders, who you once fought and killed."
feeac1ae-baba-4410-a550-5e2e65497089: "Maegar, we simply can't agree to that."
333f3dfe-af9b-4da4-9783-0064f1ee78da: "I don't want bloodshed. We must come to an agreement."
57ce6b6d-d4bb-4a7a-a414-d103680e1fe7: "By any measure, we are newcomers to this land. If we want to remain here, we'll have to respect the wishes and customs of those who've lived here long before us."
f0237706-a2a6-40c3-98bd-2cbf6be553f9: "Pff, so a tale about ancient evil is going to make us abandon this land, that we worked so hard to win?"
d596ea5a-7d36-4468-a276-3013ca21914b: {n}This once-quiet glade in the heart of the planes of Dunsward now resembles a low rocky shore, braced for the crash of a menacing wave. A team of centaurs tower above a handful of people, scraping the ground and rising to their hind legs from time to time. They seem nearly ready to trample their frightened prey into the mud.{/n}
88a56b49-f179-4e0f-9168-3992a8f9c3da: {n}Noticing your party, a woman in simple peasant clothes breaks away from the group and throws herself at Maegar's feet.{/n} "Your Grace, Baron Varn! Our prayers have been answered! We are the villagers of Old Stump. We wanted to build a farm in these lands, but we barely started digging the cellar when these monsters appeared!"
73e64daa-ac94-48c4-8348-e67248bed48d: {n}A muscular centaur with black hide and dark hair leans forward, thrusting out his chest and nearly trampling the woman.{/n} "Howl louder. The more of your kin you call forth, the fewer we'll have to root out from their holes!"
5f945579-6bcf-4cb4-b632-f716aaa3e4dd: {n}Maegar raises his hand in a powerful gesture, drawing everyone's attention.{/n} "What is it you want from these people?"
045efbc2-22c1-4cf1-bcf8-257cc4ac3bf5: "What do we want, two-legged? You ask this, after everything your kin have done?! You come to this land uninvited, dig up the ancient graves, and attack us, the guardians of the land. What do we want? We want to clean the world of the dirt you spread."
04bdc126-67d8-468a-b3c6-26c5fe31189d: {n}By the signs and patterns on their weapons and clothes, you recognize them as belonging to the Nomen tribe – a warlike clan of centaurs that long ago settled in these lands. In ages past, the tribe fought back {g|Taldor}the Taldans{/g} who tried to settle the region – and were almost completely wiped out. The Nomen haven't shown themselves for a long time, but they hardly hold any warm feelings towards you.{/n}
af3267c6-1a52-423c-811e-2c538c63ea88: {n}You manage to spot some symbols and patterns on the centaurs' weapons and clothing, but do not recall anything useful about them. You only vaguely remember that centaurs used to live in this region, long, long ago.{/n}
a9e4dd12-4e44-4bc6-be63-1e1c8442b737: {n}All the centaurs have pendants or signs depicting the moon – the symbol of Desna in her aspect known as Mother Moon.{/n}
d303ac56-dcf0-4871-8082-57294d3ff5c6: {n}You see a few symbols of obviously religious origin, but cannot determine which of the many religions of Golarion they belong to.{/n}
b7ed0fac-789a-498b-a9d4-9c6cf1f844a2: {n}Maegar nods in approval.{/n} "That's right. We walk under the same moon, stranger."
8b3073d3-1f25-4f20-9040-5e46f6ab823b: "I support the General's suggestion. A baron who allows insults and attacks cannot be baron for long."
98e99da7-2bd6-4ac9-a58c-cd0607751573: "Ah, and more the pity we are not Taldans. At least they knew how a ruler should behave on territory he plans to continue calling his own."
579035aa-e1b5-41c6-8faf-5d8bbb1f86f4: "I've always thought it a good sign when hostile parties begin with conversation, rather than an arrow in the face. If you will spend your time insulting us, stranger, then you will surely spend a moment more to explain, in detail, what my race – and my subjects – might have done to offend you."
af7b5232-0a25-4ab0-808e-9688d493ad16: {n}The centaur grins.{/n} "You have an easy tongue, two-legged one. You seek to make us drop our guard."
592d4f97-52d7-48d3-8ad7-a22fa3842488: "What have we here? A two-legged with reason and dignity? Not like these others. They are deaf to our warnings." {n}The centaur nods at the settlers.{/n}
192a8c4c-61ff-4172-b4a2-198c86e81491: "Fine, I will tell you. I will use the words of the ancient songs, and of Aecora Silverfire, who sees far further than any of your sages and rulers. We are the guardians of this land, and it is imbued with evil." {n}The centaur speaks in a measured melodic voice, carefully reciting a sacred teaching.{/n} "Evil sleeps here, under each burial mound, under each obelisk with one-eyed skulls. And you, two-legged, dig this ground like moles, stealing secret treasures from the ancient graves, and tempting their dread magic. You will ruin all. The one who sleeps must continue his slumber. The caged one must remain behind bolt and bar."
8f3d057c-50d1-4235-9505-bca4eddd0fc7: "You have been warned. I would sooner believe a liar and a thief than a grave robber like you. Now fight for your lives or run!"
e186022c-6523-4e96-b1af-ae18c0839efa: "Do you understand, two-legged one? I'm giving you a chance to take this rabble and leave. Go away from the City of Hollow Eyes, away from the burial mounds, away from the obelisks and the other cyclops ruins. If you turn away from the past, the Nomen tribe will leave you in peace."
f16897b3-b5ff-4fea-8c6b-96613c69d3bf: "Quiet, you two! I want to hear what they have to say."
84f59d34-79a4-45a7-bd86-f621e5e9c142: "Well that's just wonderful. By a rough estimate, he just demanded that we relinquish two thirds of the barony. – Including the most fertile fields and mines. Only the barren rocks in the mountains are free from cyclops ruins."
8744b34d-f8f7-4dd0-afbf-8fe175e57db3: {n}Maegar nods.{/n} "Listen, stranger. We cannot simply leave this land. But if your tribe will stop threatening the settlers, I will forbid them from entering the cyclops tombs. My soldiers will patrol the area and punish any trespassers. I would also like to meet the chiefs of your tribe. We should learn to live side by side. I would also like to learn more about the 'evil' that sleeps here."
2a027ef9-4b3a-46f9-8dc7-9cd72be16444: "The Nomen tribe is led by warrior priestess Aecora Silverfire."{n} The centaur speaks boldly, then frowns.{/n} "I do not believe a word you say, human. But I will give you a chance. If the two-legged keep their noses out of the tombs, then we will let them remain. Let them plant their orchards and build their homes. But if a single one breaks our agreement, there will be trouble. You have been warned. Hunters! Follow me!"
7945f4b1-0d73-47dd-aca9-fd629ad452ee: {n}Maegar tries to interfere but doesn't get a chance. The centaur's face darkens, and his eyes light up in anger.{/n} "A tale? I knew I should never have tried talking to you as equals. Hunters, to arms!"
7ef7146e-291a-40d7-a3fa-ec14d8e7e008: "Quiet, Cephal, and you, {name}. I think we can – and must – try to come to some kind of agreement. But of course, without uprooting two thirds of our villagers, and leading them into the mountains where they'll eat moss and stone. Let us talk, stranger. I'm sure we can find agreeable terms."
0ce52ccc-7f90-41b4-8af3-5fcabb7cb6c6: {n}The centaur shakes his head.{/n} "Mother Moon is my witness. I wish to avoid bloodshed. But what we guard is more important than any of our lives, two-legged!"
03e84185-96b8-47c2-a786-6d2d098013dc: {n}The moment the centaurs have left, Cephal sheds his nonchalant mask and turns angrily to Maegar.{/n} "What were you thinking?! These creatures are unpredictable savages, and from what we hear, fanatics as well. As soon as a trade caravan unknowingly stops at a wind-worn cyclops stele, or children run inside a tomb when playing hide-and-seek, they will return, and bring carnage with them. My friend, you can only make deals with equals, with those who think as you do. But not with half-humans, who attack villagers because of their primeval fables."
ba0c1660-d94e-40f3-b9fe-d14335d7cd2b: {n}Maegar looks down quietly at the dead centaur bodies.{/n} "This could have been avoided. I hope all their kin aren't such hotheads. I wouldn't want to begin my rule by slaughtering a whole centaur tribe." {n}He's growing more gloomy every moment.{/n}
28805ca2-7923-48eb-8566-f648498affd0: "And how would you like your rule to begin? With a village slaughtered by centaurs? Like it or not, but we cannot tolerate fanatics like them near our villages. If you are incapable of seeing the great cost they would bring the barony, then think of the safety of your people. Would you want children testing their bravery in a cyclops' tomb to fall victims to these four-legged savages."
f0dfa220-ad66-4501-b154-9f88ff8cd3b7: "Your Grace... about the tombs... Our younglings did go there! To that huge stone vault sticking out of the ground, to the south!"
57523102-df63-4e23-b7b7-39fcbad071ad: {n}Maegar curses.{/n} "When? I've half a mind to tell you about watching your children, but the truth is I was once young and stupid myself, and slipped my caretakers more than once. General! Regent! Let us go to that 'huge stone vault' and save the young fools. Drag them home by their ears if needs must."
f717c700-a01f-48b0-8a15-53f487ec09c4: {n}Maegar turns pale.{/n} "When?! Damn it, I only just promised the centaurs that none of us would set foot in the tombs. If they spot those fools poking around, there will be trouble. General! Regent! Let us go to that 'huge stone vault'!"
95697fa6-999a-4227-af53-da5df39ff2ce: "And you would prefer to slaughter them all and be done with it? Until we discover their motives and learn their location and numbers, wouldn't you think it wiser to proceed with caution? This doesn't sound like you, old friend. You would execute a small patrol on a whim, to watch all of Varnhold burn tomorrow? No, we must learn what we can of their motives, and determine the need for an armistice. But do not imagine me blind to menace these centaurs pose to our villages. I will take any steps necessary to protect them. But that does not include slaughtering an entire patrol, or ultimately a whole tribe, simply because centaurs lack all skill at diplomacy."
7f2f8d47-34b1-4092-8d8f-b99ef44b64ba: "Hey, has anyone tried to get Harrim dead drunk? Is he still so boring when he's loaded?"
261bcf79-bf34-41c1-93f1-855ae7417ef8: "Oh, Amiri, Amiri... There were times when I was never sober. This was long ago, before I came to Groetus... And I do not wish to return to those dark days."
8eb6bc30-9478-439e-be33-703c121bd79c: Did they look around, before rushing into the unknown?
8892e928-7f3e-4c6b-8dbb-323e419c7eb2: Or did they bravely step into the mysterious darkness?
38a28be2-0ef2-4e08-8fbb-f3c71dc06cc3: A long journey through the caves stretching around {g|Lake Silverstep}Silverstep Lake{/g} brought our brave heroes to another large, narrow crack in the wall. This time, however, the crack looked different from the previous ones.
b5c14348-6418-4bbb-a517-8e35aeb75f4b: We started to realize that we were nearing something mysterious and magical — more and more strange vegetation appeared on the cave walls and floor. Mold and lichen gave way to huge flowers, enormous mushrooms, and even some bushes brimming with berries, big and bountiful!
69c0380a-1105-44d3-8810-aa633eab5606: The crack itself was as odd as its surroundings. Within, it seemed pure darkness, thick and deep, was roiling beyond the crack — but what space lay beyond, none of us could guess. We all noticed a draft from the crack that seemed to rise and fall, like breathing, stirring the dust motes within the musty cave.
5ad5c8dc-ba63-470f-ab81-18fee5d40e0f: One needn't be a druid to understand the plants under our feet were unusual, to say the very least. They were too big and too tall, and the huge flowers had unnatural shades that made the eyes hurt to look at them. Perhaps it was the soil they grew in that caused them to grow in such a way — but who could tell for certain?
702a48a7-3e39-44cb-820f-f94ffeb45c8f: The plants blanketed not just the floor, but the walls, too — here and there in the darkness we could see gleaming islands of luminescent lichen. If that wasn't intriguing enough, stalks grew from the lichen, and on the ends hung big multi-faceted fruits!
432a1b5f-36fa-4f22-8f00-d5a709ee8127: Maybe the seeds of these strange plants had found their way here, blown by the wind from the narrow fissure? After all, it was strong enough to stir the motes of the cave, even part a hair or two on our fellows' heads. As if on cue, we caught a faint smell of pollen from the other side of the crack — perhaps beyond was the source of the strange garden?
40e2cae1-8991-4d8b-bdf4-d5283ca7e7b8: Readying ourselves, we decided to act — the first of us started to squeeze through the crack, cursing and grunting, your humble servant following right behind — the {mf|baron's|baroness'} chronicler can't allow a tiniest detail to escape her attention, so I had to be as close to the front as possible!
f14a8fe4-0fb5-4e2b-afcd-f678f248a12a: This time our path to adventure proved little to our liking! The crack in the rock was narrow even for me, and led us further and further, curving and twisting, until I'd quite lost my bearings. The wind from the other side became stronger and blew into our faces, bringing new smells — fresh grass, fragrant buds, sweet blossoms...
5a279d17-d7b4-47f1-ad35-7738f47480d0: ...then suddenly the ground gave way — the path had become a sinkhole! Blood rushed up to my head, my stomach sank to my feet, and I had the most peculiar dizzying sensation — my body was pulled in two directions at once, as if divided across some strange wall that separated "here" from "there"... until I was truly "there" and no longer "here".
51565376-e2b9-4c46-ae8b-883009d8f70c: I had no time to be afraid — my fall was quick and my landing was soft... we fell right into a cushion of thick, high grass! Pulling myself... er, herself... together, your humble servant immediately started to look around, asking what happened? Where had she been whisked off to with the brave {mf|baron|baroness}?!
9c0982a7-0679-48aa-a94b-2c4b00851845: I confess — even for me, it was hard to choose the right words to describe what lay before our eyes...
20478f6f-d92f-431d-99e9-3d079ab7cc48: So, what did our heroes do?
a80a109a-f014-440a-b723-6a303ec559ce: "This a crazy road allll way to end, even crazier than how we meet... Now someone try steal OUR city? Nok-Nok say — we go steal it back!"
8a8dfff3-da21-4bd0-a261-a314c1e20761: "It what heroes do. Walk together. Steal together. Stab together."
7a8c7700-8dd4-49a8-ace8-efa1443dbbba: "You show more than how be hero — how be more true self. You teach Nok-Nok how to jester. Use head, but not as club — use to trick enemy. Turn laughter back to stab people."
a4b9698a-c2f1-4a83-bb21-541a53072b87: "And you show me hero path, from goblin king, to great confronting of Munguk, to finding tribe again, and... uh, king-not-king again — hero path keep going. So do we."
cd757121-343a-4cb0-883d-95abc81b0acd: "Pffft — Nok-Nok not let you go alone. Besides... be fun. Nok-Nok never stole a city back before."
062b4150-7492-4166-b184-8d98aee2718a: "This a crazy road allll way to end, even crazier than how we meet... Now someone try steal city of Nok-Nok, King of Jesters? Nok-Nok say — we go jester thief to death!"
3d9c0626-4e02-48c9-87ff-f9bcb6b43e59: "Pffft — Nok-Nok not let you go alone. Besides... be fun. Nok-Nok never stole a city back before. Be tale of Jester greater than any Hero!"
1912b563-ec3a-4acd-8c06-a36b56feb6c6: "Nok-Nok never had to be hero — you showed Nok-Nok only had to be Nok-Nok. Jester. Not someone else."
de66da21-2adf-438f-b5ba-82a2578a3224: "All way from goblin king, to great confronting of Munguk, to finding tribe again, and... uh, king-not-king again — all led to being Jester. But need city back first, or Jester have no place to jester."
aa489aff-36db-4ee9-917c-1163e2413e56: "Listen, dead one, keep away from me. I don't meddle in your business, so don't try getting too close."
e04cc765-2f8f-4b38-ae51-a27d65a5e4cf: "We'll see what you say when life is draining from you, drop by drop. At that moment it becomes an easy choice: become undead, or become worm food."
8ee30c83-4f27-4c15-8d18-a52153d42d7a: "So, you deliberately sent the elves to their deaths? They weren't undead. What grudge did you hold with them?"
597d9d1b-39f7-487c-85ab-f8bbe102829b: "That's all well and good. But why do you come here now?"
23d97915-5e22-4928-b1f9-784575cf54f0: [Attack] "I've heard enough, and now it's your turn to feel the blade!"
8df3744c-b690-4801-8fbd-6300692b6012: [Side with Enneo] "It was a mistake for me to ally with an undead murderer. I now know that Jaethal will never stop, and I must support you, Enneo."
4e46c02b-f060-4cd6-b14c-c50d477c0622: [Side with Jaethal] "Jaethal has served me well. I cannot allow you to kill her."
e297c1bd-2bfa-4660-bd11-faf0ae3718e2: [Side with Jaethal] "I care nothing for such nonsense as the blood of the innocent. But I can control Jaethal, and that's more than I can say for you. Which is unfortunate for you."
852ca089-07b2-434c-b8ac-3e1d417ed67b: [Side with Enneo] "Allegiance with an undead follower of a dangerous cult — this is harmful to my reputation. That's my only reason for supporting you, Enneo."
30d5905f-63ca-4c22-a260-fb99cb5f392d: [Side with Jaethal] "You are a dangerous fanatic! Innocent people have died because of you. More blood may be spilled unless you are stopped."
50bc21aa-2e63-48fe-96e6-512261de6ccc: "Did you track down Jaethal right after her expulsion from Kyonin?"
f837688b-2a6f-441a-98fa-baf2a53c151c: {n}The false merchant {d|Enneo}Enneo{/d} walks towards you with an easy gait. His calm friendliness has disappeared, like a mask fallen from his face. His clothes are decorated with the easily-distinguishable symbol of {g|Pharasma}Pharasma{/g}.{/n} "I hope you've settled all your affairs with the poor old exile? It was an interesting show to watch."
7dce8056-7ad6-4d4f-a69e-c56b3b9dbaaf: "I don't have much to add, beyond what I'm sure you already know. I'm the inquisitor of {g|Pharasma}Pharasma{/g}, and for almost forty years I've hunted the undead and cultists of {g|Urgathoa}Urgathoa{/g}, for the glory of the Lady of Graves. I destroyed Taneka's coven. I tracked Jaethal into the wasteland and killed her — only to find that her hideous deity returned her to 'life'. To put an end to that, I made use of a company of naive young elves from a camp near the {g|Thorn River}Thorn River{/g}."
26283b83-2a01-436e-8be9-eb39211f8064: {n}The undead priestess tightens like a predator preparing to strike.{/n} "You... so many years later, and you come to me again. Why are you here? Why stand once more between me and immortality?"
66f0e40c-cfa9-4d45-b44f-049b82d84725: "What a stunning frankness." {n}Jaethal smiles lightly, almost affectionately.{/n} "Did you imagine, half-blood, that those youngsters could handle me and the {mf|baron|baroness|king|queen}?

232c2b4c-0f1f-4b65-a36f-f928ae0e168f: "Oh, what a naive fool I was! I had no idea that {g|Torag}Torag{/g} – that uncompromising, conceited god, glamorized by all dwarves – was capable of betrayal! 49271d03-9d06-40cc-a0f8-25e8df7f4bb2: "Torag is the god of craftsmanship. So every follower, especially the clerics, must smith their own suit of armor. The day when this work is finished is like the second birthday for a dwarf. He's newly born in the eyes of {g|Torag}Torag{/g}."
8bd14c00-a5d2-43aa-879b-8a84aec394bd: {n}Harrim sighs heavily and falls silent for a time.{/n} "My second birthday never came. I couldn't make armor. Not even a sword, not even a simple nail. 74c0e728-8e90-4345-8a64-e75aecfe6c59: "I was trying to drown my sorrows in drink, but even the owner of the cheapest pub on the road would laugh at me while he put those mugs in front of me. I couldn't take it any longer. I wanted everything to end."

00547ae7-82b8-461e-be64-afa83d27704d: "And that was the moment when the whisper from my god became more clear. It was like he was calling me. At last my sufferings had come to an end! It was a miracle, {name}! And I had paid full price for it with my torments."
6300f9fe-9a56-4ee0-ba53-5c723a69a6e5: "I couldn't control myself. I walked out of the tavern and straight into the nearest forest. And there I found the ruined temple of {g|Aroden}Aroden{/g}, the lost god. Several figures clad in robes were holding a silent service there, a service to a god I knew nothing of. None minded when I stood beside them. For the first time in my life I felt myself at home."
e3112290-d0b2-4311-97ec-e476ea1ea58f: "My new brothers told me that they were clerics of {g|Groetus}Groetus{/g}, the god of end times. They were traveling around Golarion, spreading the teachings of Groetus, despite all the persecution, contempt, and misjudgment they received from others. I gladly shared this burden with them. For now I knew whose voice had whispered to me through all those years."
ce98ec97-777a-4364-91a9-9ba907dcfd74: "You're a fool if you think so! An ignorant fool! Have you ever met a dwarf who can't handle a smith's hammer? Even our children craft knives! No, no, no, {g|Torag}Torag{/g} is the cause of my sufferings! The betrayer god deliberately cursed me – just to make a laughingstock of me!" {n}Harrim raises his hand and shakes his fist at someone above.{/n}
bfce25cd-2473-40ec-a6b0-b837be14d0e7: "But I won't let myself to get angry at you, {name}. You're an ignorant and blind soul, and my aim is to guide you through this dying world that marches towards its end. I will open your eyes or die trying. {g|Groetus}Groetus{/g} will be pleased by either outcome."
14a3fa59-9994-4fc2-bb2a-81f0356d4220: "The dwarven kingdom, yes. Well, it's to the south from here. It's survived many trials, and there will be more yet to come." {n}Harrim strokes his beard, contemplating.{/n}
bdd2991e-2737-4855-b4c8-b93ab14f2230: "Oh, no. Eons ago, all dwarves lived deep beneath the surface. And they did rather well, judging by the historic records. They built fortresses befitting noble dwarves. But our restless god, {g|Torag}Torag{/g}, sent us a prophecy – {g|The Quest for Sky}the Quest For the Sky{/g}. He ordered all the dwarves to abandon their fortresses and press upwards, to show their beards to the Sun, as they say."
ea8dac97-6be6-46ff-ab37-3d569782dcb6: "Oh, they are the peaks of creation! – Glorious cities, built by the ancient dwarves who'd finally reached the surface after many hardships, performing the final labor in their {g|The Quest for Sky}Quest For the Sky{/g} on the surface of {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g}." {n}Harrim's eyes glitter with admiration.{/n} "They are steadfast, tall, magnificent... they are beautiful!"
62fed95c-a484-4f07-bdbc-77346ebb1d22: "What else would you like me to tell you, {name}?"
38500f52-faa6-4e6e-99b9-7c7582982ed4: "There is no unity among the dwarves, {name}. The Five Kings rule over our people. They sit on the thrones of the five greatest cities, and with every passing day it grows harder for them to come to any agreement. The only thing uniting {g|Five Kings Mountains}the Five Kings Mountains{/g} is the {g|Sky Citadels}Sky Citadel{/g} of {g|Highhelm}Highhelm{/g}, the great dwarven fortress at the Mountains' heart."
9ddf62c2-511c-4d9d-9092-a7f9c98bb122: "This journey was long and bloody. Many dwarves perished on the way. Others turned back, keeping to their ancient strongholds – eventually to turn into evil duergar... gray dwarves. But those who survived reached the surface and founded {g|Sky Citadels}the Sky Citadels{/g} – the most glorious cities in dwarven history."
720340d8-0d31-46f5-afc6-19d80078830b: "The Ten Citadels were built by dwarves, but we've managed to keep only a few. The citadels crumbled, and the orcs, sworn enemies of our people, trampled their blessed streets and ruined the gorgeous palaces of the ancient kings." {n}Harrim's eyes grow misty with tears.{/n} "These were heavy losses, and a disgrace to our people, {name}."
ed943d0b-5c1e-42e3-b210-f27989e23b0c: "{g|Highhelm}Highhelm{/g} is the jewel of {g|Sky Citadels}the Citadels{/g} that remain. It is located in the heart of the mountains, and the heart of every dwarf. Yes, yes, my heart too."
8ec3d2fd-e8b7-4575-b2c8-2650e59cdf89: "There is a dwarven saying that, if an enemy reaches {g|Highhelm}Highhelm{/g}, every dwarf from all the corners of the world will come to defend it." {n}Harrim casts a sad glance at you.{/n} "I'd be there too. But not to help the Citadel's defenders. I'd be there to witness the fall of our people with my own eyes, and mourn it. I would fall upon the cold stone and raise my final prayer to {g|Groetus}Groetus{/g}."
d3819539-bc36-43ff-95a8-bf6fd1dcff6b: "{g|Groetus}Groetus{/g} is the end of all that exists." {n}Harrim smiles. He's obviously been waiting for this question.{/n} "Look around, {name}. What do you see? Look again and realize that everything will be destroyed. Our clothing and our armor will turn to dust. The walls of the palaces will crumble into ruins. The trees will fall. And you and I will die much sooner than that!"
c5ec65d8-c2f7-45af-81c1-9e33164a869e: "Of course she is stronger. For now!" {n}Harrim nods with dignity, stroking his beard.{/n} "{g|Groetus}Groetus{/g} is weaker than {g|Pharasma}Pharasma{/g} – and many other gods. I would be a fool if I tried to claim otherwise. If Groetus were stronger, the end times would already have come, wouldn't they?"
5d96759c-f0dc-4ed2-8ab0-06a7e00919ff: {n}Harrim shakes his head in resignation.{/n} "{g|Groetus}Groetus{/g} doesn't speak to his clerics. Actually, Groetus doesn't need any clerics." {n}The dwarf raises his sad eyes to you.{/n} "He only allows his whispers to be heard, and only by those who are dying to hear them."
9a294d25-e100-400c-90ac-b8623b2fbab5: "Then let me ask you, what do you think about {g|Groetus}Groetus{/g}?"
0073004c-b71e-4e84-8f63-57deee168c6f: "But the powers of other gods fade away. They dissolve slowly, a grain in a century. {g|Groetus}Groetus{/g} collects those grains and waits. He doesn't need to hurry. He knows that his time shall come."
91fe7a19-a204-457e-8abb-84f4492a6cab: "His words are unclear, but they call to you. His voice comes with the soft rustle of fallen leaves, with the woeful wailing wind at the mountain pass, with the roar of the raging blizzard... and it calls you to strike out on the road. Onwards, always onwards, over the pass, over the bridge and further along. Up ahead, where the edge of a grey robe flashed, and a candle sputtered for the last time before dying... Onwards, always onwards, until your feet can no longer carry you..." {n}Harrim falls silent, submerged in his own thoughts.{/n}
e4e7e534-21f2-4029-a60d-57e11e782a2c: "What else would you like me to tell you, {name}?"
248b4d7e-2e7f-4a4a-bf87-25fcd13f1924: {n}A broad smile spreads across Harrim's face.{/n} "I'm glad you think like that. We'll bring this truth to the whole world, and tell everyone that the end is inevitable!"
a90d9c18-d03c-47cc-b162-fc3c56878efa: {n}Harrim nods in contentment.{/n} "I'll be glad to talk with you about {g|Groetus}Groetus{/g} any time, {name}. After all, that's why I travel in your company."
822b22ac-ea96-4d3f-96df-2744f308ef37: {n}Harrim sighs.{/n} "Your denial means nothing, {name}. The end will come either way. But there is still time to talk further about it. After all, that's why I travel in your company."
730ea6dd-88f1-46da-a4b8-87376ea98b49: {n}Harrim lowers his head.{/n} "Such is your wish then, {name}?"
6bc2a57a-01a3-43a9-acfe-a775be8843f5: "Well then... everything comes to an end. So does our friendship. We shall meet the same fate, but now we follow different paths. Farewell."
d56bbf68-914d-4408-9007-b99a5cfec95c: "Then why do you disturb me with these obscure hints? Let's bury this conversation in oblivion and change the topic."
3a7b4f04-7051-4ccf-ba2c-6a1fce837c36: {n}Harrim looks down and strokes his beard a few times before answering.{/n} "I'm not sure, {Name}. This will likely bring nothing but pain. I suspect I will regret going to the ruins... But nevertheless I ask – please take me there."
0abf3861-cfcb-4bfc-b117-a4fb23ff1291: "I can't stop thinking about it either. Maybe it was a sign from above... But if so, what does it mean? Has {g|Torag}Torag{/g} admitted defeat and turned his back on the fortress? Did {g|Groetus}Groetus{/g} extend his hand to take what's his before its time?"
aeee3fa7-ccfb-4eef-8c2f-c7bcc0874008: "I keep straining to hear the answer... But to no avail. But I'm sure that it happened for a reason. Some day I will understand what happened and why. Some day..."
eed111c4-39e9-42b5-ae4b-124b3bf16778: {n}Harrim fiddles with his beard pensively.{/n} "Well... It's not as if I'm holding a grudge against the whole dwarven race. In {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}, the {g|River Kingdoms}River Kingdoms{/g}, in the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g} – I'm always rather happy to see one of us. Exiles like me, or those who left their homeland voluntarily in search of a better life – or even those who were born here and have never seen the mountains... I hold nothing against them."
b872024e-d5ae-4bad-86da-40dd95e9fe84: "But the Skjegge... You see, {Name}, they aren't just dwarves – they are envoys from my homeland and Torag himself. Like everyone who exiled me, who humiliated me, everyone I left behind – all of them have come back to torture me. They carry the spirit of {g|Five Kings Mountains}the Five Kings Mountains{/g} with them. A spirit that is more nauseating to me than the stench of a corpse."
239e8d90-c5ab-43bc-90a1-1396f12ccf23: "Don't. I would enjoy seeing those smug Skjegge led by {g|Torag}Torag's{/g} servant dig themselves a grave with their own hands and lie in it. It's probably petty of me... What's the difference who dies earlier or later, if the same end awaits us all? But please allow me this small pleasure."
0ddd2423-6065-43a8-9a0a-c0287c5c9e65: "I've never heard of any such thing… But you saw with your own eyes what happened. The paladin's words had the ring of truth – but what could this mean for me?"
14906dae-8201-4823-a76f-3adf02f98774: "Who gave me this gift – {g|Torag}Torag{/g} or {g|Groetus}Groetus{/g}? And for what purpose? What should I do with it? Questions keep rushing into my mind, countless... Everything is so confusing... So strange and inconceivable..." {n}Harrim's speech turns into barely understandable mumbling.{/n}
bc48c5a1-871f-42ae-b207-2f853bf2dedd: "Being right didn't require any wisdom or knowledge or even experience. Do you think it brings me joy to be right about this?"
e83e19cc-0a39-41d8-a24d-f7f4fd10150d: {n}Harrim strokes his beard pensively and makes a crooked smile.{/n} "But why should I lie either to you or to myself? Of course it brings me joy. But it's a bitter joy. The greedy and arrogant will continue to seek glory and wealth, but find only death and suffering. That's the sad comedy of our life, {Name}. We may laugh or cry at it, but no one walks from the stage without merciful {g|Groetus}Groetus{/g} drawing the curtain."
17fbad33-9f61-4f61-bb6c-e69a0d123cd5: "Have I made peace? Made peace..." {n}Harrim says this word slowly, as if trying to taste it.{/n} "There was war in my heart, and now it is serene – that is true. But can I call it peace? I think not. More like neutrality. I no longer torment myself thinking about them and {g|Torag}Torag{/g}, although the wounds they left continue to ache. But now it simply doesn't matter."
37db389b-249e-4946-b2a0-3426e2601927: "I used to think {g|Torag}Torag's{/g} followers were shallow, that they couldn't even imagine there was anything in the world besides their beloved god and their home mountain. Now I know that I used to be just as shallow. Torag, {g|Groetus}Groetus{/g}... Beginning of time, end of time... All these are only parts of a larger picture – a picture so vast that just thinking about it makes my head spin. But for a moment I saw it, {Name}. What can ridiculous resentments mean after that?"
cc89d364-29c4-4036-9e27-16140521e73e: "Oh no. Don't imagine you can use me as a siege weapon. That was a special case... Divine intervention! The Revelation of {g|Groetus}Groetus{/g} – not just his usual whisper, but a proper crackling rumble! That day..." {n}An insane light flares up in Harrim's eyes, and his voice turns into coarse whisper.{/n} "Do you think I destroyed only a dwarven citadel that day? No, {Name}, oh no! That day a wall collapsed inside my soul, inside my mind... A wall of ignorance which had kept me from understanding... from true knowledge..."
65b4cd94-9730-439d-a502-46c7d93b395d: "Oh, {Name}, if only I could share with you the truths that are opened to me! The truths that keep opening to me!" {n}Harrim clenches his beard, almost pulling a piece from it.{/n} "The truth about where time flows... The amazing forms that emptiness takes... The deafening song of silence that hides beyond {g|Groetus}Groetus'{/g} whisper... Now I know, now I know..." {n}Harrim looks through you with unseeing eyes, whispering something indistinct.{/n}
164474d3-e8d4-4d49-9f09-416cb365da0c: "Repent? You think I have to ask his forgiveness? The god who cast me out, who condemned me to a life of endless suffering? I would never return to him, even if he came asking for MY forgiveness!"
4e56e481-30aa-4f7e-82e6-581b13aed9e0: "No, no! You cannot live without faith. Everyone needs a guiding force, a higher power to turn to in dire moments. I am sure your atheism is just a phase of your spiritual search. Sooner or later, you will find your faith as well!"
a7e31dff-8e1a-4fa9-a2ca-732cc6963b00: "I helped you save your kingdom — will you help me protect mine?"
4dcc350f-fa0f-4f71-b33b-da22b8680856: "Get out of my way, and don't meddle."
8be8d755-bebf-48ea-aaba-89e0a01457b7: "Did the other trolls scare you? What happened?"
b3de35e2-3dd0-4652-a1f6-5ca0e0b51855: "Don't you come close to my capital!"
2617ffdd-4d77-4e37-bd26-93310dbf5851: {n}The old troll is seated on cold tiles. When he sees you, he stands and roars with joy.{/n} "Hmm, {race}! You alive!"
4a31bf30-6e7a-42a3-a670-096854ff5fa5: {n}Hargulka shifts from one huge foot to the other for a while before finally spreading his huge hands helplessly.{/n} "Hargulka not know, {name}. Trolls lived in peace, no touch borba... now this. As if forest grew inside dungeons. Strange forest... not like ours. Then dead Tartuk and his trolls appeared."
b25ebcff-d79d-4d41-afb4-e6eecd9734e9: {n}Hargulka growls in a low, dull tone.{/n} "Branded trolls. There been none since Tartuk died. These ones strange — no smell, no shadows. Alive, but not really. Tartuk is not real, but real angry. Started hissing about {g|Trobold}Trobold{/g}, treason, borb- you." {n}The old troll lowers his head.{/n} "Hargulka deceived Tartuk. Said must think and decide. Hargulka waited. Not want to fight all Tartuk's trolls. But not betray you, no!"
66ace80c-2e3c-473c-a9b5-766d0c6bf9c4: "Many ran away. Others hid. Rest fought Tartuk's trolls. Some stayed alive and ran, and some got eaten. A few agreed with Tartuk, went back to like before." {n}Hargulka lets out a rumble of disapproval.{/n}
de837ac0-7de3-4fce-8e46-290cf45a4814: {n}Hargulka's roar shakes the dungeon walls.{/n} "Hargulka promised help! Strong word! Hargulka will gather his trolls, go to your city. You protected {g|Trobold}Trobold{/g} — we will protect your kingdom!"
31d28d80-d00b-4bad-ac28-fa5d6a055ee5: {n}Hargulka lingers.{/n} "Leave...? Hargulka want to help... gather an army... go to city and fight your enemies..."
aae3c774-906c-42d4-96e4-750827a54441: {n}Hargulka looks at you, clearly confused and... maybe hurt?{/n} "Hargulka was not lying when he promised friendship. If kingdom does not need trolls, then trolls will save trolls. Farewell, {name}."
75e61cee-3fd5-4713-9545-5a95b4bef0ea: {n}Hargulka stands up and straightens his shoulders with a crunching sound.{/n} "We will crush your enemies! Hargulka gave his word! Strong word!"
8579fd02-344a-48dd-8c27-f74d3784e7b1: [Attack] "No one dares to trespass inside my head. Die, monster!"
a196696e-13cb-43f5-9bd3-aab8980a5892: "Why must I be the one who does it?"
f35ce2fa-4651-46e4-808b-61f560b02f6b: "Very well. I shall mete your vengeance upon the Stag Lord."
3a96e1cb-0323-46f3-8664-f5a5e8d7d819: "Can't you kill the Stag Lord yourself?"
576f0943-1999-41fa-a1a1-6eefd991136e: "So it was you who sent me those nightmares?"
44436ea8-97a5-4c16-87ee-6d3a03d5f3b9: "I've killed you already. How did you survive?"
34c3a0a9-8a9b-481d-a37e-62bb8f7cd4d3: "I refuse to help you on principle. You shouldn't have messed with my head!"
739cad07-c2d8-4229-b593-a86252434534: [Attack] "You dare to threaten me? You're no better than the Stag Lord and his bandits. I'll teach you a lesson!"
5f6dad8a-73d9-418b-ac78-2fe4c89cd833: [Attack] "Killing you may be pointless, but I'll do it again anyway just for fun!"
c783d662-4bbb-440f-818a-b239642429c2: "Isn't it beautiful that Urgathoa gifted you with undeath so you could see your death avenged?"
29e7c74b-94b1-47c3-8327-b17c0c358179: "Revenge is a holy pursuit. Calistria would be pleased if I avenged you."
969b8769-c771-47d7-ac89-f070f32195d9: "Becoming undead — such a horrible fate! Pharasma would want me to help you find peace."
d26f6e86-0048-4f97-b724-138ad9f9d516: "Becoming undead — such a horrible fate! Sarenrae would want me to help you find peace."
2adb6b4f-77ce-4309-a3b7-cf75c1bc3e7a: {n}The corpse's face is bloated from being so long in the water. The stench from its toothless mouth is so foul that your eyes begin to water. The hand, clenching a sinister-looking spear, is covered with scabs.{/n}
8efb770a-a637-4a7f-991e-1c8073057529: {n}Suddenly you feel faint — as if a cold, wet hand is placed heavy on top of your head. Wet hair sticks to skin, and trickles of icy-cold water run down your face and shirt. A hoarse whisper rises inside your head:{/n} "There you are..."
ffc1f08b-e9ba-458e-a587-667caa59f1f1: {n}The bloated face of the drowned man yawns open at you. You feel once more faint, and the invisible wet hand falls upon your brow again.{/n} "Greetings, {name}..."
921e7be4-1f84-4a05-9704-4f0d23b28739: "Davik Nettle..." {n}A storm of bright images flashes before your eyes. A long time ago, this person, then a living man, came here from Brevoy, constructed a rope bridge, built a house, and lived in it, collecting payment from those who crossed the river.{/n}
4c70c1c8-330d-4da8-8bd4-d1f1ce5279b5: {n}You see a vision of a man wearing an antlered helm. You hear a muffled groan, and the helm drops to the ground with a loud thud. Your hands are covered with hot blood... too much blood.{/n} "Death... to the Stag Lord."
079347ed-07db-47b9-b84b-c7cee079cc01: {n}You see a vision of a lovely spring day. Sunbeams shine warm against your cheeks. Three men approach the house by the bridge, one of them wearing an antlered helm.{n}"The Stag Lord"...{/n} Angry faces, a quarrel, the glint of an unsheathed sword... Suddenly the Stag Lord's greedy eyes are twisted by surprise. The master of the house has unleashed his hounds!{/n}
97a4592e-2b85-4601-a086-08cfea27dd08: {n}A burning smell stirs you awake to the sound of loud barking. Flames are crawling up the walls. The sound of breaking glass, the bitter cold night air... you are outside... Outside the house, and something is wrong. An arrow strikes deep in your shoulder. You hear the guffaw of ten throats. You run, already in the middle of the bridge. The man in the antlered helm cuts one of the ropes. An ear-splitting scream fills the air.{/n}
d763a3c9-a45c-4e35-99d6-b435c70b5283: {n}You feel invisible fingers, cold as stone, draw aside a wet strand of hair from your forehead.{/n}
e813316b-13ea-4437-af7a-d688a0110d66: {n}You are taken in a whirlwind of visions and images, and you see... yourself! You lie with your eyes closed, thrashing in your sleep... finally you scream and wake, drenched in cold sweat.{/n}
42a167ea-ca5b-47b3-9f0c-4b2e75e39560: {n}The drowned man, who'd been sitting motionless, nods his head.{/n} "Come later... take the spear..."
dc66bdcd-6f94-4345-bb0f-4ccbc32d85d5: {n}You see the Stag Lord and his cutthroats trying to build a new bridge here... Then running madly away from the rotting monster. The Stag Lord has avoided this place ever since.{/n}
7534fd8c-501c-4253-900e-76e3f4465a62: {n}The drowned man grins at you with blue lips.{/n}
496580f3-fc70-4743-b21c-d83d9dd92065: {n}Gurgling, deep-chested laughter pierces your skull, clouding your vision and flooding your ears. All else becomes muffled, as if you are trapped underwater. You shake your head to cast off the apparition.{/n}
3530a638-3234-4b08-8a6d-e86a41e4ec61: "I sense evil... But not evil committed by this poor soul, no. He arose on account of some evil done to him."
fc01cdf2-0a09-4d8a-ae8e-1f48b7468c76: "Why not? Isn't this the very mission that brought us here in the first place?"
85bfbf2a-6f97-45d1-a40c-5ebc7769338c: "Don't you hate it when someone asks you to do something you were going to do anyway? It makes me want to do nothing, just to spite them!"
b01e6db2-be8d-443e-bf20-b0e430e6520c: "Well, at least we won't be doing it for free."
d8eaa400-2ce9-4849-96aa-52e7074133c8: "I would help him even if he wasn't going to pay. He has such a hard life... Well, a hard undeath. That must be even harder!"
7617c7f7-b0f7-4cc9-9330-85f0a0ed4d07: "You're always helping scum like this for free. As if our own lives are easy!"
3c56863d-024f-4921-a932-13e78364577a: "Right, no more chatting with corpses! Let's hang him out to dry so he'll stay out of your head!"
44e150ea-cadd-4cd1-ac77-6467d6cfda94: {n}Without a sound, the dead man rushes to attack you.{/n}
114524ba-be34-4bf4-8daf-cc7f81616d3d: "You freed an innocent soul from eternal torment, {name}. Yours is truly a noble soul." {n}Tristian lowers his head and begins whispering a prayer.{/n}
fe816ea6-9323-42ff-bc91-2cb58a8cbf9e: "But why? We may have the power to help him!"
b03c090a-3ca1-4e0e-bfd5-f43e0a98a3ca: {n}A series of visions flash before your eyes — you see the Stag Lord dying in a variety of horrible ways: impaled, beheaded, drowned, immolated... The dead man lets out a moan full of rage and anguish.{/n}
c53b1b6c-890e-404a-8989-543acbb777c2: {n}The dead man bows his head. For a moment, a vision of a peaceful rural cemetery appears before your eyes.{/n}
d11bd660-f7ea-4f6e-a274-fb9d2d73e44d: "Right! Let's go make the goddess proud!"
e6fcada9-cc47-4e98-92ef-4ff09cb44451: "I certainly wouldn't call him beautiful, but you're right — there's a reason the goddess bestows her gifts, even on lowly peasants like him."
6671761f-7e7f-4bcf-8ab5-4d0b8564449b: "I feel nobleness in your words and deeds. I do not think you are from a common family."
ec56f13e-550b-4347-bf34-c113262e8cd0: "Does lineage mean anything? I'm the one who made myself."
956c6bab-9f50-422c-8dd7-840f29b869b7: "You are wrong. I am from a very common family, and even they rejected me."
0d996626-34e7-47d6-bf4b-3dc878ab12fb: "You are wrong, I'm from a very common family. I've worked hard and come a long way — from a wandering nomad to a ruler's respectable companion."
313f6c54-f532-43af-a850-c25f684fef97: "The smaller the party, the more vulnerable are the ones who remain…"
edd92c96-03fb-49b8-8499-6cbf6c9cec6a: "Your words are full of indifference to the deaths of others. We'll take care of ourselves — but let us show some compassion, and grieve our losses."

6dfc8134-1bb1-4f8a-b154-df9f92f17d1c:

Curses strike harder if you empower them with the piece of essence of the one being cursed. And I put my very self in my name — the name of a ruler and a vanquisher! The name I was cursed with…
I was blind back then, more blind than I am now. And I lost the greatest gift I ever received from my patrons — the daemons. Will I have to pay for such negligence?"
81028a7a-db8d-4d8d-ad01-98f1c1e545d2: {n}Freed from the prison, a soul flies up in a flash of light and rushes towards lifeless body of {d|Varn}Maegar Varn{/d}. 3538578c-12eb-47c6-9a5a-5ad4729d026f: "You look at me as if I committed some blasphemy. Hardly. They defiled my lands, so I defiled them in turn. Although, I didn't want to limit my revenge — their souls await fate inside the same jars, as does the soul of their arrogant leader."
f52e12fe-c813-4e48-923a-501cd115d09d: "He's kind of right... 82fd9009-10b9-4350-a84e-8adacb34122e: "Alas, Vordakai, this is the fate of every empire and every ruler... Your hubris helped you to persist much longer than you were supposed to — and yet, the time has come for you too to face oblivion."
16ad51dc-44f9-4af5-917f-f182840af4bf: "What a power... But what a stench!"
d969c45b-a429-437d-8fe9-991fcbdec7cc: "Indeed". {n}Vordakai stands up and lifts his hands.{/n} "Break the soul jar in your hands. Now."
d05cc43e-ef81-4e8b-9b33-1225e5565022: "Are you kidding me?! Good grief, we'd be better off putting you in a jar — and making sure to leave it here!"
62d8566d-0fbb-454b-a409-0d55f290f59b: "Are you out of your mind? He's a monster! An evil the likes of which the world hasn't seen in ages! He'll devour us in the night, and in the blink of an eye, the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g} won't be your realm, but his!"
f44cc24b-69d6-4a48-a16a-ca69214539a1: "That's right! You're just some garbage who somehow crawled out of the scrapyard of history, but we'll be sure to put you back!"
74094aa8-d4ab-4909-8d11-24919c0f7035: {n}Vordakai chuckles dryly, letting his teeth scrape together, bone on bone.{/n} "You expect gifts from gods, little {race}? You are but dust beneath my feet. Still... you may serve me yet."
d6e8c98b-8792-4d1e-b84c-eb030a2c004a: "An interruption?" {n}The creature's voice echoes, as though speaking across several chambers at once — or perhaps through many different selves. As the reverberations cease, the dead figure answers its own question — and the answer sounds like a death sentence.{/n} "So, what disturbs my meditations?"
4ef105e8-cfea-4065-9b8b-13a7b768f04b: "After all I've done... After all I've achieved..." {n}Vordakai's fingers claw at the floor, and he turns, as though searching for you.{/n} "After all the trials... still I fell... and to what?" {n}He bares his teeth, ichor and miasma running from his mouth.{/n} "To a pathetic thing like you!"
a2e933fc-d26f-44e7-af16-cfd81a48f2c4: "But..." {n}Vordakai's teeth click, like a death rattle, and the desiccated flesh around his empty eye socket constricts.{/n} "But this will take time. 829ecd73-849f-4438-a8da-d2004ae20610: "You didn't even realize what your sidekick stole... The Oculus of {g|Abaddon}Abaddon{/g} is not some eye. It's a dark creation having tremendous power. 68117977-4bfb-4a91-abbe-b30454bece42: "An excellent move, even if risky. We need to shake as much useful information from that dead chatterbox as possible. We can finish him off any time!"
a62786ab-9489-4bc0-9480-d011a7ea9aab: "So the little traitor has stolen an artifact of divine power? What a delightful end to our arduous expedition into this lair of dead monsters!"
9746fb5d-c9fe-4b3d-b1eb-322479301361: Why would he, supposedly a follower of virtuous Sarenrae, seek an artifact that's the center of all evil? His treason doesn't surprise me, but I don't understand what it could mean, or what he could hope to achieve."
2c9eabea-b166-4163-929d-d9100b1d2f0f: "Regongar, you stand as proof of all the worst rumors about your people."
8862d629-3e93-4319-bffc-bf4824c90adc: "And you'd rather I disprove them? Ha! I just give the people what they want."
1e433cd2-a44d-4243-b18b-734c73d3f489: "I've seen you before. Who are you?"
c4848f84-952a-40b7-bd20-ead30a4f562b: "What did you do to the Defaced Sister?"
a9e94791-45b1-4b19-9395-501bab683f95: "So, it was you who sent Tristian to me?"
03e56957-c35c-43a8-aba1-f6e1c4356ad4: "That's enough. I'll stop you — here and now."
a9787ae3-1931-4a5f-87bf-14492b0338ac: "Why are you telling me all this?"
92285c7c-f7d5-40d6-b2ce-827c916da3de: "I'm not your hound, watch your tongue!"
d8a82ea3-950c-4a57-9e78-b2f1de0f71de: "You know, I'm not one to be easily manipulated. Wasn't that the reason you were watching me so closely?"
5f26f00e-fa86-4d43-89ca-ba73495bd5e0: "Could this be the real you? I've seen another version of you. Proud, unbroken, and never so cruel."
92fd8cb9-4b68-4f12-a2d5-62459375739f: "I'm sick and tired of your empty talk. Enough!"
e06b229d-a84c-4623-94ae-9374ed6f8831: "Our paths have crossed again. Perhaps this time you'll finally tell me who you are…"
efdc03c5-2728-4ec5-9856-7090d70ab5b4: "What did the Defaced Sisters and the Numerian barbarians seek in Dunsward?"
44c1d3d7-95f7-4225-bacf-7a2cdc3882b3:
{n}It seems the air itself rings with a frenzied scream. It comes from a slim figure, kneeling on the stone floor — one of the Defaced Sisters — but this time, unmasked.
But above the Sister stands a nymph, the outline of her features shifting slightly, as if she stands beneath in a slow-moving waterfall. 0bbfa26c-38e2-44f5-b81e-19c2fe54fe3b: {n}Waves of anger stream from the nymph in the center of the room.{/n} "Pathetic creature! Tell me — is there any reason I should not torture you for your {d|c31 Oculus Destroyed}apostasy{/d}?" {n}The nymph raises her hand menacingly — whether to strike or cast a spell, you cannot tell.{/n}
74405661-af9c-4344-b04d-3b8175314e7d: {n}Tristian, despite the angry words of the nymph, seems oblivious to his surroundings. His face is pale and turned upwards, beads of sweat glint on his forehead. His lips move, as if reciting a prayer.{/n}
330e7fbc-413b-4cd6-ba67-78cae7faf430:
{n}The nymph leans over her kneeling victim.{/n} "Speak, defaced one. What do you see?" {n}The Sister, shuddering, chokes out an answer, her pained voice a whisper — you cannot make out her words, but the nymph listens eagerly, then gives a slight smile.
As the Sister on the floor utters a last, anguished moan, the nymph straightens, almost regally — and the Sister falls silent. The nymph regards the corpse before her and holds her breath for a minute — and the time within the room stops.{/n} "Finally..."
c60c9d4f-7e8b-409e-8846-a0b37b4e86e2: {n}The nymph stares at Tristian for a long moment. Then, instead of striking, her hand reaches out and clasps his face, turning it to meet her gaze.{/n} "What happened to you, my skylark?" {n}The nymph's voice is sharp and sickly sweet.{/n} "Your heart couldn't bear my anger? So be it. I was bored with your songs anyway — perhaps the snapping of your bones shall entertain me." {n}She raises her hand over the Tristian's head once again — then stops as she suddenly notices you.{/n}
64260b44-8ace-41f0-915a-b59acd2620c5: "We have guests." {n}The nymph turns to you with a slight smile, her eyes sparkling.{/n} "A hound, following my skylark's trail. You have done well, you've uncovered my old sanctuary — but it is one I shall never return to again. So now that you are here... what do you intend to do?"
b089312c-a710-48df-922f-61ca0484cd36: {n}Gravel crunches under your feet, but the nymph isn't startled at the sound, she merely turns her head slightly.{/n} "I can smell you, hound. Your kind always reeks of fear, subservience — it's unmistakable. Why are you here?"
1379e8f2-741a-43f9-9704-0806cce7e255: "Stop me?" {n}She laughs faintly, her eyes sharp.{/n} "A hound cannot best a dragon, nor bar its path. My goal is near — I can already hear its song, leading my heart to my final triumph. Nothing can stop me now."
0542ee76-621a-48d7-89c0-1714d3fe1168: "Your world is but a shadow of my home plane. I am the first and forever queen of these lands. And this sanctuary… is where whispers of the past live, and where I planted the seeds of the future. Here I raised a wolf cub, who eventually became the feared leader of {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g}. I watched him rise to power, butchering any who stood against him. And from this place I shall hear of his fall — the last howl of a dying animal."
23ebd628-1a1e-4045-91f2-dd74f83790be: "Now a hound comes to replace the wolf cub. Should I crush your skull and watch your life bleed from your body? Perhaps... but wouldn't it be more fun to observe whom you'd chase next? Whatever you choose, you'll be serving me. Like the skylark. Like the wolf cub. Like all who placed their trust in the illusion of freedom."
ec015438-142c-41f5-82af-6cab49ec113e: "Why, to watch the light of hope drain from your eyes and to see your dreams shatter into pieces. Loneliness has consumed me for too long — so now every upstart who dared to bring war to another's lands brings joy to my heart."
ff7ab97b-32dc-4428-9d15-d88a3202fabd: "Oh, and {g|Sarenrae}Sarenrae's{/g} messenger was a great servant, wasn't he?
