Do I really see surprised expression on your face?" {n}The nymph goes silent, then gives a faint laugh.{/n} "Can it be you still don't understand?"
6c8f5b35-6fdb-49ea-85ab-2be09537b708: "Now, we both know the skylark belongs to me — just as a butterfly belongs to the day it's born and the day it's destined to die."
c8b3bb75-31ef-42dd-b3bd-512e37304d9c: "One of the eye sockets of this creature was good enough to fit the Oculus of Abaddon — the one Tristian stole from under your nose. Sister used its power to reveal my path. That is all you need to know."
f766b82c-ce74-4bd4-b746-fc75aadb35c6: {n}The nymph throws back her head and utters a laugh that makes your skin crawl.{/n} "You seek to give a name to nature itself? Why should a servant seek to know the name of his mistress, when all you need do is play the role you have been given? Well..."
b81750da-487c-4c10-87d8-2b63d0d0763f: {n}The nymph straightens and her gaze locks with yours.{/n} "I am Nyrissa." {n}At the name, an echo rolls across the room, like a wave.{/n}
1d112a1f-ada8-4a91-b631-1b758fcb4954: {n}The nymph's lips curve in a charming and frightening smile.{/n} "You dare challenge your mistress? The one who has shown the way to hundreds... thousands of creatures such as you — filthy beasts who don't even know the face of their queen?"
51f56346-b527-4582-af94-001661df40a4: "You are my faithful hound, and Tristian is my silver-tongued skylark. Both of you serve my will, so how should I call you, if not by your true names?"
ed85b358-e87d-4238-9934-fe79b84c3d0d: "Tristian was the proud servant of {g|Sarenrae}Sarenrae{/g} herself, the personification of kindness and mercy. 7452374b-1aea-47a5-8c7c-a9b6ab1aa996: "Stop me? Do not think yourself my equal. Your interference has slowed me for a time, that is all — I shall find my heart's desire and find my purpose again. Even the loss of the Oculus can't stop me."
e130d3c6-771c-46c5-9257-00f74b45d9a9: {n}The nymph tilts her head.{/n} "In you I see my reflection. But no, that's utter nonsense! How can one such as I even for a single moment feel kinship with a creature born to become dust in my Apology cup? You are but a toy, a mere hound. A useful tool, no more!"
0ae97778-3baa-4222-9a49-dfea65a3b689: {n}Fire blazes in the nymph's eyes.{/n} "So bold, so self-confident... so familiar that it pains me to see. Yes, I've been watching you, and it seems that in doing so I've awakened the shadows of bitter memories from the faraway past, forever lost. So now it's time for me to recall how confidence is broken, and boldness is reduced to dust!"
d25f873b-144c-487c-880b-2ba007da8cc9: {n}Bitter anger flashes in the nymph's eyes.{/n} "You've seen nothing and you know nothing! My past is a fire that blinds those who stare. I've left it behind and accepted the fate that was designed for me. I..." {n}Her sudden outburst fades to nothing.{/n}
f5e3fe00-5e4e-43e3-8f8f-2f576659d6ce: {n}The nymph smiles — almost tenderly.{/n} "You can bark at your mistress however you want, hound. But you can't shed the collar and the leash."
777243c7-ac76-4143-877f-570844ffa5cf: "You're trying so hard to glimpse into my soul… are you not you afraid of what you might find? Very well, have it your way, hound. I'll share a little part of my darkness and my pain with you. I'll share with you my name."
09e2e1e3-67a6-4c14-ae38-8ffb0839a4b3: {n}Gravel crunches under your feet, but the nymph doesn't seem startled by your arrival. — She just turns her head slightly, as if she long expected you to come.{/n} "So, you're here, my hound. I'm not surprised."
17b67d6a-79fb-443a-8f84-ac0d4a004004: "An ancient power awakened in the mountains. A power capable of revealing that which was taken from me. By my order, the Sisters scoured the land for the Oculus. My wolf cub sent his barbarians to help them. But you outpaced all my servants. All but one."
748f1534-c1fc-4614-8182-7af48c141f7c: "When a seed falls upon fertile ground, it bears fruit for the landowner to harvest. The seed of betrayal grew strong, and I reaped its fruits."
30d80b55-513f-4de8-849c-3092cfd0583e: "When you do die – and it will happen sooner or later – I'll probably make a roast of your doggy. For aesthetic reasons."
930ac876-b4ea-47f4-a3a1-551fa05466bc: "Fine. When death does come, I'll save my last arrow for you."
4cd9af7e-9461-487f-bfe5-6f85095abe4f: "None of you will be governor. I will send my own viceroy."

72897b7d-d0de-4486-99da-c01c474b5307: "Guards! I sentence Stefano Moskoni to death. Take him!"

9fe767fe-7cc8-4ce6-be22-642395b54ba2: "Guards! I sentence Atalia Gitaren to be executed. Take her away!"

873962a6-ecac-471f-9b63-400ba6e0cd3e: "I accept your pledge. Serve the city as you have before."
7518e3a6-b961-42d8-bd03-0f0c628da7ae: "The city is now under new leadership. I will retire the city guard, and create a new one, personally loyal to me."

73bf5669-b28f-4493-a5cd-a3be0d4382f1: "I didn't ask for your advice. Have a good day, former captain Caelysse."
f9f5a747-1822-46a5-940e-8f33994851b1: "I've changed my mind, and I accept your pledge. Continue to serve the city as you always have."
f5ff8cf4-4071-4c0f-80de-e154f4be807a: "They are under my protection. Do not stand in the way of honest people doing fair business."
658fcdc0-a30d-4262-b3f8-db0031ea2fb6: "They have every right to do business unless they disturb the peace."
73bec803-9853-42a4-9807-26a33f2d1a76: "You can throw them out of the city. I won't lift a finger to protect that scum."
184357e9-f8a1-48e0-af86-d4a7233d0382: "You can continue in your usual work – just don't forget to share!"

1ad56887-ad6d-401b-bb96-9067ac5d9687: {n}{d|Stefano}Stefano Moskoni{/d} makes an formal low bow, hiding his mischievous smile.{/n} "Well, justice was served. f4df3d20-4582-419e-9a42-ac44e9ff4132: {n}The gnome smiles and rubs his hands together.{/n} "Sweet, sweet... You will see, Your Highness, you've made no mistake!"
ce3bface-2e49-486b-a35d-ccbae1ed7699: {n}A broad smile blooms on Stefano's face. He bows to the floor again.{/n} "Thank you from all my heart, Your Highness! I won't let you down."

b29c26bc-8028-4073-936b-e64c7d94d2d4: {n}The guards take away Gasperre, who is as pale as a sheet.{/n}
64f5c416-31e0-423c-8825-e27b0b9d9715: {n}Stefano is escorted away by the guards, his chin pointed proudly skyward.{/n}
af8be305-06fb-4325-8e38-5e362e29fe80: "Your Highness, {d|Atalia}I{/d} ask that you relieve me from my post as headmaster of the {g|Academy of Grand Arts}Academy{/g}. After all that has happened, I am hardly worthy of keeping it."

41faac0b-a2ed-4071-8450-eaba7fde5c69: "I know nothing of my true journey. Its end is lost in the darkness, and the beginning is so far away. But I know that you follow in his footsteps. As I once did, you fight to protect your lands from her... from Nyrissa."

e651615c-9c23-413f-b0ac-1a25e6e7128c: "I know I can have peace if I only learn the end of my story. There are three more mirrors somewhere in the house, which store its fragments. bbc590a7-325a-4290-adc2-a71b99dcb779: "I'm sorry, I'm not in the mood to talk."

f8f41460-ba3c-49f3-a700-4105e3483738: "Just because I'm cruel to enemies and strangers doesn't mean I treat my companions the same way."
bf1e03db-862a-4bc9-b28f-26bca025e34f: "You are useful to me, that's all. I look after you the way one looks after a useful tool."
b06a82d0-0ce3-4d68-8f16-bbdf9d99ccd7: "Kalikke, you are precious. I could never let anything bad happen to you. I'd face even the cruelest villain to protect you."
a9ca4d97-eff1-4e69-a110-e67c43a184a3: "Of course I look after you! We're friends."
34237f09-b397-4fc7-8b63-e398e3426183: "What if it's because you're special to me? I'd do almost anything for you, Kalikke."
126dcf4a-ce95-4be0-a6d1-8c3c18320f39: {n}Kalikke approaches you silently, raises her hand to capture your attention, but then stumbles in hesitation.{/n} "{name}! Not that it's important, but I'd like to ask you something…"

f46dbaee-49de-443e-ac30-a2aad21db8d5: "I know you're no stranger to kindness and honor. But still I'm amazed that you would show such kindness to me, a tiefling, a rootless outlander. And not only to me, but also to those who I hold dear. Even though we've brought you so much trouble!"
3e9ebcc5-da42-4c83-8a1c-2034d39cdeaa: "I'm amazed that neither darkness nor light prevails in you. – Perhaps that's just an illusion? You were so kind to me and my friends, though we brought you so much trouble…"
7f43e606-797b-49b8-9b7d-a2a8ecc7ca84: "I'm sorry if this offends you, but your soul seems dark to me, and your deeds seem cruel. But you're so caring towards me and those who are dear to me. Why is that?"

79d525bf-759b-46ce-b56b-96fc99e584d3: {n}Kalikke smiles a dreamy and sad smile.{/n} "You really are amazing, {name}. I owe you so much – and I've seen and learned so much, all thanks to you! b15c3820-cae1-47d2-b9e2-e70c414cbb4a: {n}A smile blossoms on Kalikke's face.{/n} "I'm so happy to hear that! Just to know that you have a friend – that's true happiness. Especially when it's someone like you. Thank you for your time. Sometimes I do like to chat!"

3bbe6a3e-30e8-4130-ae73-eb5b44454b56: "Thank you for your kindness." {n}Kalikke opens her mouth, as if meaning to say something else, but doesn't dare, and quietly walks away.{/n}
602e41cf-feb5-4f68-859a-9843bda40333: "You're always the first to get into fights – as if there are no fighters in the party except you."
78dd5ef5-7848-4ada-ad22-3e2724b28806: "Why not? I know there are others. But it's the custom – the best fighter is always in the front row!"
a83862eb-d1e9-4bd8-b585-12e1eb34729f: "Don't let it get you down. Life is short — tomorrow any of us might be joining them in the ground... Enjoy life while you can. If you're crying over someone's grave, it means that no one's dancing on yours."

5c227452-7fcb-4ded-a0bf-a74be9988991: "Ha, well said! Sadness can take a walk. Somebody hand me a bottle!"
f2b20f9f-a24b-49a3-ab35-ebb57764e20c: "Your words bring only more pain. And I see that was your intent."
2cd6e512-f87c-44b0-b0aa-d3ad719faa31: "Here's to death — our gracious lady! The one who will never deny you. In her house, everyone has a place."
67606339-5969-47e5-b9f4-9fbe933790e7: "Very true. It is well to hear a touch of reason from the mouths of the short-lived."
4b57c398-4977-44d8-aa44-dae7cd89feda: "You laugh at death, but you will face it someday..."
a0a2e0bd-c7b7-4f87-9e2d-7f96deff6f04: "No I won't! Think about it. So long as I'm alive, there's no death. And then when it comes, I'll already be gone, ha ha!"

4aa19e44-a926-41d2-96c7-1bec35a7ec7c: "Judging by your bags, you are not just traveling. You are on the run."
4f98973a-985c-4fbf-951f-374d2c4ccc35: [Attack] "Let's have a little fun. Why don't you try to run to Galt, and we'll see how many of you live to get there?"
c9b643da-b192-46ed-8289-4d2caf7ab279: "There's nothing you can do for Verdrin — his signs are like the others afflicted. Any moment, a monster might tear its way out of him. Keep your distance!"
e300c5f3-3dc5-45a9-9690-b68580a491d9: "Calm down. It wasn't me who killed your friend. What happened here was a tragedy, but it is not me you should blame."
4a484747-17d0-4d4d-9685-b1c76fa11e41: "I will not be able to protect you if you leave for Galt. Turn back, and inside the capital you will find protection from the beasts. You will at least save those who can still be saved."

683806be-2e9f-4190-bf01-ba231e07db2e: "Easy now! I'm doing everything I can! What, you think you'd do a better job if monsters started tearing out of your citizens all across the barony, huh? As a matter of fact, you — yes, you — are still alive, and I've yet to hear a word of gratitude."
327e8f7d-f063-4897-9359-f7103cf96c53: "I protect this realm for you, I fight monsters, and all I hear in return is cursing and the mewling of cowards! You ungrateful, narrow-minded fools!"

23d086f6-7bd1-4ebf-ba83-758081925445: [Attack] "Talking back to your {mf|baron|baroness} is akin to treason."
fe89a3cc-68e1-4365-acd1-df3546431bfa: "You cannot imagine the pain that fills my heart with each life lost. I am doing everything in my power to save those who still can be saved. Please, forgive me, for I cannot protect everyone."
4a049c36-e836-4bd1-aa28-4bb71cb7126b: [Attack] "Enough! I will make you shorter by the head."
7a7c67f0-685f-491c-800c-b7ff89b9d895: {n}A group of travelers carrying bags, satchels, and sacks full of all manner of goods and chattels are shuffling their feet on the road in front of you. d4c10b19-c30a-4476-854f-d0bd7925230f: {n}The man throws a glance at his small group.{/n} "Name's Uhrked. These here are my companions. We come from the village of Lervik, and we're traveling to {g|Galt}Galt{/g} in search for protection."
792145ee-629e-4374-ad8e-609a76bc3d94: "Oh, Verdrin, you mean? Must've eaten something. He was fine, see, then felt sick, fever and all, and in the morning he began to cough blood. {g|Erastil}Erastil{/g} willing, he'll make it to the border, and we'll find him a healer there."
ceda8da5-ab6d-496b-bb0a-ab580a8a3e8a: {n}You see a change in Uhrked's eyes, and he gives you a cold, even wicked, look.{/n} "And if it were so, Your Grace? 80f88581-2c00-40f9-8ba4-858445aed16f: {n}Uhrked pales and looks at the others.{/n} "Listen up!" {n}His voice is hoarse.{/n} "All back! Back, behind the {mf|baron|baroness}!"

0caf8e0b-f859-42d2-8e3b-0bc38a0bc040: "And whom should I blame? Or what?! Who is responsible for everything that happens here? Shouldn't it be the so-called 'ruler'?! Who is to answer for all these deaths, if not you?!"

95291498-fa1d-4b23-a663-fc7aea105ed6: "{g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}-loyal traitor! I hope you die in a ditch, 'baron{mf||ess}'!"
ac7ae113-c17c-468f-96c4-4f6c46f8d774: {n}Refugee clenches his teeth and shakes his fists in powerless rage.{/n}
042af565-d38d-4e71-b380-9eb607ffe329: {n}Tristian shakes his head slowly.{/n} "This is not food poisoning. The symptoms clearly indicate... I am sorry. I am so sorry..."
f0ed0a77-62ce-4a86-9d8e-71065f3fd611: "Die here, or in {g|Galt}Galt{/g}... From disease, or by the sword... A bit sooner, or a bit later... Our earthly lives are filled with choices, but what change truly comes of them?"
4e6c1d0f-14f6-43c7-8cb1-09053019e5bf: "Your ruler is trying to save you, fools."
f39e3e04-337a-4d36-be10-22841f235614: "Typical! 'I don't want to get to the bottom of things, though I know exactly who is to blame!'"
53d0d452-92f5-4cb6-a0d8-ebeff101b8f3: "Please, {name}, don't allow anger to guide your hand. This man has been crushed by loss and fear – and he will regret his rash words!"
933146f1-b8f7-4591-b86e-ab8029a606ea: "I do so love traveling! All the magnificent sights, our adventures, the people we meet... I just wish we didn't have to walk so much!"
f286dfc8-7ba0-4b24-99d0-6fd6251ecb4c: "Sometimes I regret that the gods didn't make my companions the same size as me — with the same stride, at least…"
706ffed0-30ac-402c-ba0d-681b6db53c1f: "Ha, we are not walking that far! Many of my fellow travelers come back taller — on account of the extra calluses on their feet."

df6de7df-6fad-41d8-aca0-e714de6eee3d: "Ahem. There is no request too small for a servant of Sarenrae. If you wish, I could take a look at your calluses..."
76b65012-10d2-49a4-b497-4138d8fba588: "Just five hundred gold coins a day — and I'll carry you myself. What, too stingy? Suit yourself, ha, ha!"

69d2b155-3454-45d7-a58a-1d02279510dd: "The goblins are behind this disaster, then?"
b9ab51e7-6dda-489e-b75f-fc73d4f0ffea: "So we need to find a goblin leader and press them for information. Any idea where to begin the search?"
756f21c7-b3a2-4f00-8abe-cac1952b14b9: "The epidemic continues. More and more people die — more and more monsters roam your lands. Some of your subjects have alread fled in search of safer havens. Your barony's very existence is in danger."
08638767-8495-42f9-853c-f4e4f188b778: "Whoever started this epidemic, there's no doubt their goal was to destroy your young barony. As the number of monsters increases, people panic and flee to other countries."
f930cb5d-d5e8-4630-bc4a-49f0b7f1b27e: "If we don't do something about this epidemic, and soon, you'll have only hydras and wyverns to rule over! The more folks get eaten, the more other folks panic, and the more they're tempted to flee to our neighbors."
aba26cc8-7109-4280-b136-1c5fdaada1bd: "We do have good news, too. I managed to gather some information that, I hope, will help you eliminate the threat before it's too late."
5b8df195-8798-466f-94ea-49e2c27c7a3e: "Shortly after the epidemic started, goblins began appearing everywhere. 98ff7077-e1db-4035-9005-f27f43662a2a: "Behind it? Doubtful. Benefiting from it? Quite likely. fac5732f-39fe-4ae5-bed0-21c6e6d5cccf: "She's called the Mother of Monsters. Her symbol is the three-eyed jackal head. d7bc2cdc-a51f-482b-83e7-62312efc4cfc: "Yes. You were wise to prevent widespread panic by keeping the epidemic secret. Due to that, my agents caught several goblins and learned the location of their village. I'll mark it on your map."
6b5afb44-0021-4beb-93ae-36be63afee06: "I hope it helps you to save the lives of your people."
2686e2fd-0b87-4969-a5f3-93ef37aba33f: "Happy to help. Take care, though — there's no doubt your enemies still have plenty of tricks up their sleeves. If you value your throne, take them down as soon as possible."
311af08d-3bc0-4fd9-80e1-afb4ce8316f2: "You're welcome! Be sure to make those goblins talk, though, or you may risk both your crown and your head!"
0726ef27-d4cf-4c16-884a-86ea2a74cdd4: "Alas, nothing more than vague speculations. Once you alerted your subjects to the danger, they began defending themselves as best they could — my agents couldn't catch even a single goblin alive. 4a6928f0-2129-478f-968b-449152989ba5: "I'm sorry, no. Panic spread everywhere — my agents had to run for their lives after villagers mistook them for spies and well poisoners. df63698d-ed86-4287-8914-3cbd2dcd25c6: "What were you saying about the city? What do you mean 'it's stuffy'?"
43d737f2-4d29-401c-a7f6-4346b6d8bd33: "Have any of the men come with you? We'll need help in the dungeon."
9995b37b-752a-4839-a3b7-e18f9a469055: "Good afternoon, Baron! Sir Cephal summoned me with a sending spell yesterday. – I suppose right at the moment you were setting camp. He asked that reinforcements and supplies be brought from Varnhold. I came as fast as I could."

329160ef-c53f-498d-9201-66a35e6ea4a6: "If I could explain better, I would. It's bad there, like something is going to happen. I talk to the people – many are having nightmares, always the same. Always about tearing their own eyes out. Fun, isn't it?"
511a88ea-144b-4eb2-a4af-33ca7621d56c: "He's hanging about at the tavern, writing and writing for days on end. He's been stranger than usual lately. Pale as a ghost, dark circles under his eyes, like he hasn't slept for a few nights."
e5633708-437d-4ddf-8a64-b4b0e62fbd10: "Go. And speed the Baron's steps. Let him be finished with this backwater quickly and get home."

493bc781-e09a-4249-92ab-273dfd7cd909: "Everything seems calm, Baron. The Host are standing guard. No one is making any trouble. No sign of cyclopes. Only it's... stuffy, you know. I wish I could explain it better. Like a storm is building over the city. You should return. They need you there."
a79dbcbf-261e-494f-836a-236985640640: "We are here with the express aim of protecting the city. It's all right, Kjerdi. Wait for us here. {name} and Cephal will go check the supplies you've brought. We might need something for the expedition into the tomb."

21e793d7-65c4-47d0-81d5-1532c4e265e2: {g|Military9_2}[Choice effects]{/g} "I want a mage to serve as general."
958f60df-d87c-4778-a8e0-401e0f5dfdf7: "Chief. We need to talk. There's a problem in your... in our army. The mages and warriors have been challenging one another to find out who's tougher. The competition is worse than it was when you came to power. Today I had to stop a knife fight."
70a75c98-4391-4599-9a13-41ca65f8e8cb: {n}Regongar looks a little banged up, and he smells like smoke.{/n} "{name}, you know me. I would never cause alarm for no good reason. 8eec78bc-0b87-40c3-92f3-8a0b0ae8d802: "Sooner or later, blood will spill and someone will die. I can always feel death in the air. If you don't want to watch your warriors kill one another, you should do something. Aside from appointing someone to beat the crap out of the idiots."
9a3f0ae3-c35f-41cc-883e-1f451161e376: "Two of our commanders are bursting with ambition. Both of them have outgrown their current positions. 61e141a4-fd4d-40f2-bb3f-04417c25aab9: "Chevold will make a good general. I'll train him myself. If he survives, he'll be strong as a bear and smart like me."
1c8e7f4c-070f-427a-88df-b12d91c0b994: "Good choice. A warrior needs a body that's tough enough to face the enemy on the front lines, and a head that's small enough to do it without fear. Mages are smarter and craftier. Zefa is your best option."

9ddd0692-e23b-4fff-8a1c-c400f09a1ee6: "It's time to show the mages that the soldiers are the real power in your army. Divide the army and appoint a second general. I vote for Chevold, the infantry officer. He was the very first {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g} swordmaster in our army. He proved himself in the war with {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g}. When the mage officer Zefa hears about this, she'll stop causing trouble."
c2ea642b-2c5d-493d-9b36-24e77c7b5e27: "Your Highness, there's unrest among the army's ranks. Your mages are turning up their noses at the warriors, claiming that they're the army's main assault force. There's little doubt that their power is great, but what would it be worth if they weren't shielded by the infantry?"
f14c04f3-1e33-41b9-b8b7-8aa943693c50: "There have already been a few fights. And sooner or later, there will be blood. We have to prevent this. And I've got a plan. You should appoint a second general to show them who is more important."
8b681488-af17-406b-a549-84243334fd52: "If you choose Chevold, the infantry officer, the warriors won't be so easily trifled with. He's a good fighter. He was among the first to join the army, and he's proven himself in battle. He will be assigned the officer mage Zefa. She's powerful but arrogant, and lacks experience."
17a4bbfd-9544-443e-9b36-c69b1a90d089: "A general must be able to stand in the front line and lead the troops, not to sit back in the rear where the mages stay. Chevold will make a worthy general!"
61876dae-5bf4-45f7-98b2-624fcce70056: "Are you seriously going to accompany my every phrase with a sad sigh and a glance of reproof?"
361f4f3d-4c63-4815-bdf4-00fe00b357e9: "I'm just trying to understand why you keep hurting people, yet harbor no evil in your heart."
6118b705-c386-4345-8727-e1595cedb0a0: "Bring it before us as an offering so that an Eldest may sip from it," the curse said. Having filled the cup, Nyrissa {d|c61 Nyrissa Left}appeared{/d} before the gods of the First World. That was when the Lantern King played another joke — he announced that the nymph, cursed for her attempt to become one of the Eldest, would now get to be one! The Eldest of dust and trampled hope, doomed to drink from her own cup and suffer terrible pain. Well, everyone got what they wanted: we got a peaceful kingdom, Nyrissa got her status as an Eldest, and the Lantern King got a finale to his horrific performance.
5db8ab23-b591-4194-97c3-de6c29c177d8: "Bring it before us as an offering so that an Eldest may sip from it," the {d|CURSE}curse{/d} said. Having filled the cup, Nyrissa {d|c61 Nyrissa Left}appeared{/d} before the gods of the First World. That was when the Lantern King played another joke — he announced that the nymph, cursed for her attempt to become one of the Eldest, would now get to be one! He commanded her to drink from the cup, and he was probably about to deliver some pompous speech, but...
9d2cc8e2-460e-4cc7-81c8-064b3e2e46d5:
Now that the Eldest and other spiteful beings wouldn't be bothering us, the {mf|king|queen} returned to {mf|his|her} subjects and celebrated the victory and the end of the kingdom's miseries with great fanfare!
Everything gradually returned to normal, including our exciting lives — not always peaceful, but also not troubled by invasions from another world. And little by little, our heroes and the common folk began to forget the sorrows of the past.
d5067494-3788-4d22-9bdd-8b7f75f81434: So the kingdom returned to Golarion, but not without taking a piece of the First World with it. Miracles and strange occurrences, both kind and cruel, became the norm — not that the citizens hadn't grown used to that! And the {mf|king|queen} became the Lantern King's herald. Who knows what mission was assigned to {mf|him|her}? Our scouts now sneak across Golarion with secret tasks, and our fighters and wizards spend plenty of time in the First World. But we became something straight out of legends — a country with a mysterious, immortal {mf|king|queen} whose existence spans two worlds!
0f05ecf9-e6a2-4e47-b4cc-6655e168daf6: So the kingdom returned to Golarion, but not without taking a piece of the First World with it. Miracles and strange occurrences, both kind and cruel, became the norm — not that the citizens hadn't grown used to that! Of course, the Lantern King wasn't thrilled with the way things worked out, but who cares? {Name} and {d|c61 Nyrissa Evil}Nyrissa{/d}, the {mf|cursed king and queen|cursed queens}, are ever ready to face the power of the Eldest. Until that time comes, our leader spends a lot of time in the First World, learning its secrets and testing {mf|his|her} new powers. The immortal {mf|king|queen} and {mf|his|her} kingdom became a legend come true in Golarion!
e5092785-649f-42ac-847a-fb86f69ce496: That's how the story ended. The Lantern King vanished without a trace, and we never heard from him again. {d|c61 Nyrissa TE}Nyrissa{/d} helped return the kingdom to Golarion and followed her beloved there. After celebrating the victory with great fanfare, everyone began work on restoration efforts. Nyrissa helped the {mf|king|queen} in every way possible, and she quickly came to be loved across the country. No one would have thought this kind nymph was a former villain, so recently guilty of causing all those afflictions!
d3f6f396-29e9-431b-a22c-40be06b7b084: The kingdom built by our hero{mf||ine} became an example for all its neighbors. What else would you expect? The Stolen Lands became the only place where the citizens sincerely toast the health of their ruler! The citizens lived trouble-free, and taxes made it to the treasury without losses. A powerful army guards the peace, exploration of magic is on par, the temples are flooded with their congregations, and — most importantly — our cultural contributions are at least the equal of Absalom!
7267c0e8-6745-4193-85bf-d6253ab7d02f: Under the wise leadership of the {mf|king|queen}, the Stolen Lands became a true country! There was still much to be done, of course, and some of it will need to be finished by our hero{mf||ine}'s descendants, but there are no longer cutpurses on every corner, and the peasants aren't afraid some new self-proclaimed chief will show up and strong-arm himself into power!
e0803b29-28c7-4388-892c-8745abfe761b: Sadly, the numerous misfortunes that befell the {mf|king|queen} took their toll on the Stolen Lands. Matters left to luck and state problems left unattended meant the Stolen Lands would remain a lawless realm. It turns out you can't be both a great hero{mf||ine} and a successful ruler at the same time — or the hero{mf||ine} of this story couldn't, at least.
5857c049-74d2-439d-b319-3fc617392c54: The Stolen Lands still remain a domain of bandits. However, every outlaw in the area {d|Kingdom Mafia}knows{/d} that if you don't bow to this new chief who wears a crown and calls {mf|him|her}self {mf|king|queen} — you're in trouble! The cutthroats know their place and unfailingly respect the hierarchy, but the kingdom's neighbors think it beneath their dignity to consider the {mf|king|queen} a true monarch.
3383dd63-8b1a-4022-985c-4f06e19292f5: The {mf|king|queen} firmly eliminated banditry in the Stolen Lands, to the delight of the long-suffering {d|Kingdom Citizens}locals{/d}, and brought peace and law to the area. That peace didn't last long, however — a "jolly gang" appeared in the Narlmarches, claiming to fight the "tyranny" of the {mf|king|queen} "for the good of the common people."
29458507-a7dd-4b46-bb1d-2f6d60eacbe3: The Stolen Lands are called the "land of popular rule," for in these lands, {d|Kingdom Folk}common people{/d} feel fully in control of their fates! Unfortunately, the total absence of authority allowed one of the richest regions of the kingdom to proclaim itself an independent republic, and retrieving those territories came at a rather high price for the {mf|king|queen}.
96b33970-34a1-4632-aa45-3adb22ef718d: The {mf|king|queen} did the right thing, leaning on {d|Kingdom Merchants}the richest{/d} citizens of the Stolen Lands in {mf|his|her} ruling. Thanks to their many trade relations, money floods into the kingdom, and the fact that the private mercenary armies bought with the merchants' money continue to gain power can still be overlooked.
2821415e-189b-4cbd-9fd7-583690b23639: Just half a year after the war with the First World, Galt moved its troops to the southern border of the kingdom. Their attack was rebuffed — the enemy state's infantry could do little against {d|Kingdom Might}soldiers{/d} who were skilled with their swords and knew the military arts better than the alphabet! Since then, Galt hasn't risked crossing any borders again, fearing cruel retaliation for further insolence.
28d0daca-7934-487b-802d-465aeca5aef8: Just half a year after the war with the First World, Galt moved its troops to the southern border of the kingdom. Their attack was rebuffed — the enemy state's infantry retreated when the army's {d|Kingdom Magic}wizards{/d} brought down rains of fire and magical arrows on the heads of the flabbergasted enemy soldiers! Since then, Galt hasn't risked crossing any borders again, fearing cruel retaliation for further insolence.
58961764-8555-4c40-b726-bb6a62c3f8af: The kingdom's treasury had been properly filled due to the efforts of the Treasurer and the {mf|king|queen}, until a scandal broke: for several years, the court's {d|Kingdom Official}advisors{/d} had been pocketing tax money! News of the noisy case echoed throughout the area, and for quite some time, neighboring states snickered at the {mf|king|queen}'s "incorruptible government."
88404ce0-c5eb-4ca2-bb61-8190fe6ba9b1: The {mf|king|queen}'s subjects praise {mf|his|her} {d|Kingdom People}generosity{/d} — while citizens of neighboring lands groan from crippling taxes, citizens of the Stolen Lands have it pretty good! Truth be told, the treasury isn't always capable of paying the royal bills, and the throne room's adornments are clearly decaying, but sometimes you have to buy the people's love — literally!
7cf5a726-06b9-4e97-88bc-a399f9f6f0ff: As the years went by, the Stolen Lands saw fewer small unknown cults and more temples devoted to {d|Kingdom Religion Control}famous{/d} and powerful gods. Followers of half-forgotten religions prefer to avoid the area, as the locals are a bit overzealous about the "religious purity" of their homeland.
bbc1239e-cfe3-4a85-8929-d22b0efa4cd9: The {mf|king|queen} decided to {d|Kingdom Religion Liberty}stay out{/d} of the religious lives of {mf|his|her} subjects — and so small cults and sects began to blossom in the Stolen Lands. More and more often, the theological arguments between feuding congregations would turn into full brawls — I could only hope the guards had enough power to keep the rage of the fanatics at bay...
432bb83b-be64-463b-959a-3910b1c1ba73: The tribulations suffered by the citizens of the Stolen Lands made them true patriots — intolerant to strangers, and ready to fight to the death for their homeland. Foreign ambassadors were reluctant to accept invitations to visit these lands, as they knew well that the kingdom's citizens prefer to solve their own problems and {d|Kingdom Isolation}stay out{/d} of external affairs.
8881e30b-a622-4279-852c-fde265cdf2c3: Who'd have thought that some tiny barony founded in the Stolen Lands by an adventurer would become a real kingdom, playing a prominent part in {d|Kingdom Open}world{/d} politics! Of course, not everyone likes the proactive stance of this young, bold state, but the fact of the matter is they can't afford to ignore the {mf|king|queen} and {mf|his|her} diplomats.
d56e5e3c-7098-499c-a31f-aaf87baebce3: The kingdom reached incredible {d|Kingdom Arcane Liberty}heights{/d} in the development of magical arts. Sorcerers, wizards, and other initiates feel like kids in a candy store in the Stolen Lands. Sadly, ordinary subjects aren't so thrilled — they have to deal with the consequences of careless experiments and failed magical tests!
f4d073d4-78c9-4516-a433-36dbd95b7a60: The {mf|king|queen} thought it best to {d|Kingdom Arcane Control}limit{/d} the use of magic by regular citizens. That decision, oft criticized by prominent minds in Brevoy, more than once proved to be the right one in the end — the kingdom is reliably protected from any magical "incidents" that might be caused by unskilled wizards or nefarious infiltrators.
c3322739-e11c-429c-991c-a9211a8fdb02: How do you turn the Stolen Lands, savage and unruly, into a stronghold of safety and stability? The {mf|king|queen} found an answer: by creating a police state! There are always some who are unhappy with the "excessive {d|Kingdom Source}interference{/d}" advisors have in the citizens' lives, of course, but their protests are easily overlooked.
33000ba9-80d7-4567-8252-e06d512c1c8f: How do you turn the Stolen Lands, savage and unruly, into a stronghold of safety and stability? The {mf|king|queen} found an answer: by tripling or even quadrupling the number of {d|Kingdom Defense}guards{/d}! These guards consider themselves something of a privileged class, of course, allowed much more leniency than anyone else, but the ordinary citizens, feeling safe and secure, prefer to just overlook the discrepancy.
5579e2cb-7d8a-4629-859e-25eebb0b6cf1: Generously {d|Kindom Culture Money}sponsored{/d} by the state, many bards, musicians, poets, and other servants of Shelyn create an abundance of artistic works praising the ruler and {mf|his|her} wisdom! Unfortunately, these creations are significantly less popular outside the kingdom.
b69a0ebe-3a5f-4960-bfca-ad4e224cb7e4: Although the state doesn't directly {d|Kingdom Culture Liberty}support{/d} creators, the kingdom's freedom of speech and self-expression became fruitful soil for dozens of talented people across the Stolen Lands. Many creators achieved recognition and fame due to their efforts, but the most talented soon left the "edge of the world" in search of a more worthwhile audience.
5ee71a45-142d-4029-9851-e223d9e58395: The mysterious "Minister," whose actual line of work is still an enigma to the {mf|king|queen}'s other advisors, took care of securing the state from the schemes of spies and other provocations. Their {d|Kingdom Plotting}stratagems{/d}, political intrigues, and diplomatic leverage bore interesting fruit, as other states decided they'd rather steer clear of a kingdom known for its ability to excel at shady games.
791c0134-03b5-4d42-95ac-618cfc9e27bd: The "Minister," whose responsibilities are hidden even to the {mf|king|queen}'s other advisors, did much to let the subjects sleep well at night. It didn't come without a cost, however — outside the Stolen Lands, the kingdom is known as home to the {d|Kingdom Violence}cruelest{/d} investigators and inquisitors, who zealously persecute any enemies of the state!
350e5590-d995-410b-8d50-925649c8470a: The {mf|king|queen} became a true patron of fine crafts. Over time, the castle treasury filled with wonderful gifts from the best masters in the area. Armor, weapons, even magical artifacts — and the collection is still growing!
ed67d7df-6532-4270-874e-5da6ddd6755b: No kingdom can function without its nobility, and the kingdom in the Stolen Lands is no exception. Landowners, ready to share the burden of ruling alongside the {mf|king|queen}, grew to be more and more influential over time — and the more pompous the court balls and receptions held by dukes and baronets became, the more eventful were the lives of the schemers and freeloaders who always live within the shadows of the powerful!
10fb8627-ebec-4a33-a96f-ac5a18f0aefe: Using necromancy in service to the state is a solution as bold as it is desperate! Pharasma's church still makes frequent — and frankly, reasonable — plans to send a massive crusade against the Stolen Lands to cleanse the nest of vice. The kingdom's citizens, however, not only yielded to the use of an undead workforce, they actually supported it! After all, someone has to do the most dangerous, most unpleasant work!
b538fcfa-f4db-4104-ae3d-46713ce097db: The feud between Brevoy's north and south, which had been smoldering for ages, finally sparked the fires of civil war. Our troops lent {d|c41 Choose Aldori}aid{/d} to the forces of Restov, led by Swordlord Jamandi Aldori. After several bloody battles, House Surtova was forced to recognize Restov's independence. The victory came at a high price, but we have no more loyal ally than once more free Rostland.
b439c16f-a057-410c-a658-e507b363e4da: The feud between Brevoy's north and south, which had been smoldering for ages, finally sparked the fires of civil war. Our troops lent {d|c41 Choose Surtova}aid{/d} to the forces of House Surtova, suffering terrible losses as they took the brunt of the damage from the Swordlords' forces. The rebellion was soon crushed, and Jamandi Aldori was beheaded in Restov's central square — and for a long time, any hope of an independent Rostland died with her.
d63bcb8f-54ee-4d19-8a30-effccfef9edf: The feud between Brevoy's north and south, which had been smoldering for ages, never sparked the fires of civil war. Through great effort, our {mf|king|queen} managed to bring both parties to the {d|c41 Brevoy Neutral}negotiating table{/d}. While Rostland didn't regain its independence, it did receive wide autonomy rights. Our relationships with both House Surtova and the Swordlords are respectful, but they've become lukewarm — because of us, neither side got everything they wanted!
22b93480-2d03-4217-9531-682edcef604c: The feud between Brevoy's north and south, which had been smoldering for ages, finally sparked the fires of civil war. We {d|c41 Independence}didn't interfere{/d}, watching as the forces of House Surtova and the Swordlords slaughtered each other. Alternating between brief truces and fresh fights, Brevoy was flooded with blood and grew weak. Its leaders could only watch helplessly as their border territories were slowly annexed by neighbors — until they fell to squabbling among themselves. The butchery in Brevoy jeopardized the peace of the entire region.
55843c36-0259-4d48-95b1-a322106cf664: Taking advantage of the tension in his homeland, the restless, {d|c41 Lander Lives}unlucky traitor{/d} Lander Lebeda abandoned his domain again and set off to attempt another scam! Our kingdom, along with Brevoy, actually proposed to celebrate the day he disappeared as a national holiday, but the initiative was shot down by the vigorous protests of House Lebeda!
38fcb659-6fe7-43b9-ae07-b2267a20844a: The Tiger Lords found it difficult to recuperate after what Armag did to them. The barbarians remaining in Numeria weren't very happy that we sheltered the deposed chief and his supporters, but they were too afraid of {d|c41 Chief Armag}him{/d} to attack us over it. That bomb has a long fuse, but it's definitely burning — I'm afraid that a few generations down the road, the grandchildren of the current Tiger Lords may want to retaliate against us for their grandfathers!
314bae19-37a9-4b3a-9ce9-f25bdbd5d107: Amiri didn't remain {d|c41 Chief Amiri}leader{/d} of the Tiger Lords for long — ruling was certainly not her calling! The years she spent with them were enough for them to regain their forces, though, and they recovered to be one of the best mercenary armies in the region again. They revere her as a great hero, even more than they once worshiped Armag. And they respect our {mf|king|queen}, of course — {mf||s}he was a comrade in arms of the great Amiri, after all! Their tribe came to be loyal allies.
5f3a8bbc-582f-41f9-81ec-df674292a9b9: {d|c41 Chief Ashman}Led{/d} by careful, level-headed Dugath, the Tiger Lords tribe reunited and started to lick the wounds left by the erratic Armag. Little by little, they once again became one of the strongest mercenary armies in the region. Dugath always assures our {mf|king|queen} of his friendship, but the {mf|king|queen} always stays on {mf|his|her} toes, understanding that anything could happen when that old fox is around!
88661525-ee29-44fc-850e-52d35f65721c: The Tiger Lords never fully recovered from the damage Armag did to the tribe. Lacking a strong leader and torn by infighting, the barbarians sank into a short but fierce internal war. Their lands were quickly appropriated by neighboring tribes, and the Tiger Lords were scattered across Numeria and the River Kingdoms, little more than pitiful remnants of a once great tribe.
2322ba1b-833c-4db1-86f5-5d5038730db6: Pitax almost returned to its former state — a joyful city filled with beer of dubious quality and deals of questionable legality. The old trade houses lost the crown, but they retrieved the property Irovetti had taken from them. Soon, Pitax became almost like a second capital in the kingdom, a thriving city through which rivers of money from across the region ran.
290a8b84-9e32-48c0-95d9-26ccb1640809: Having lost their {d|c51 No Guards}guard{/d}, Pitax was plunged into chaos. Soon another power was born from among the gangs fighting to redistribute the wealth, and a much more dangerous one — revolutionaries, dreaming of regaining Pitax's independence. Troops had to be stationed in the city, and the rebels responded with arson and political assassinations throughout the kingdom. Pitax was a headache to us for a long time.
9bf7ea43-4e90-4f7e-b496-b0e3b639d62c: Pitax had never been a paragon of law and order, but now it had become one giant bandit den. That has its benefits — a good share of the profits made their way to the treasury without fail, and the black markets held anything you could hope to find. But Pitax brought a lot of trouble, too, as thieves, extortionists, and drug dealers spread their tendrils throughout the entire kingdom.
2b93b640-1413-43ed-aa59-722c56305626: Pitax never regained its former stature. In their fight for power, both bandits and the relatively honest merchants lost all their strength, scaring away both customers and suppliers. Trade routes began moving through other cities. Pitax fell into decline, and the citizens quickly forgot all of Irovetti's atrocities, remembering his rule instead as a golden age for the region.
8e06ce27-5430-49ea-b919-b56047ebc226: Amid chaos and fighting, Headmistress {d|c51 Atalia Rules}Gitaren{/d} managed to preserve the Academy of the Arts, though not its reputation. Only sycophants willing to dash off odes to the highest bidder (primarily our {mf|king|queen}) stayed to work and study under her tutelage. One could say the academy still flourishes — though in the same way a pond covered with duckweed turns green on a sleepy summer day, slowly becoming a swamp. No one dreams of studying at the academy anymore — but for those more concerned with reality than dreams, it will always have a comfortable room.
359196f3-bd69-41b8-ac8c-c616dca9ca95: Maestro {d|c51 Annamede Rules}Belavarah{/d} gave the Academy of the Arts a second wind. Throwing out mediocre students and sycophants, she gathered within its walls talented visionaries, rebels, and freethinkers — those whose gifts felt cramped within the walls of more respectable institutions. She managed to do what Irovetti never could, namely make the academy truly famous, albeit scandalously so. And so what if, instead of odes to the {mf|king|queen}, the academy releases sneering pamphlets and revolutionary leaflets? It only helps {mf|his|her} reputation as a true patron of the arts.
66876dda-4bf4-4dcf-8991-3155e6173196: {d|c51 Academy Elections}Self-administration{/d} turned the Academy of the Arts into a strange place. The court sycophants were quickly ousted — it turned out they weren't welcome when there wasn't someone like Irovetti constantly ordering odes to themselves. In their place came a motley, unpredictable crowd: eccentrics, fashionable authors of popular prints and cheap novels, charlatans, scribblers with delusions of grandeur, as many as three feuding "experimental" theaters... and even a few truly unappreciated geniuses! The academy is not only highly esteemed — there's no place like it, even in Absalom!
6549af27-9348-46eb-9a61-f16196d1a607: There was no place for art in the new Pitax. Students and teachers from the academy were scattered to the winds. Some found a place in neighboring courts, while others set off to earn some coin in roadside taverns. A third group, harboring anger and resentment toward the {mf|king|queen}, began weaving revolutionary plots. The {d|c51 No Academy}ruins{/d} of the Academy of the Arts still stand in the middle of the city, overrun with ivy — empty and unwanted.
7364763b-89e3-4311-bf47-0ffbdf3d6226: Trolls and kobolds, two of the most savage native peoples living in the Narlmarches, were completely exterminated in the region. The forest paths became much safer, and the peasants' cattle have stopped going missing.
75afbed5-87d0-4ec5-b3df-6818a2dc77f4: The Stolen Lands managed to eliminate kobolds, but not quite all the trolls. Even nowadays, unlucky travelers and hunters sometimes stumble across one of these huge man-eaters in the depths of the swamps and forests. Do they have some {d|c21 Hargulka Exiled}leader{/d} hiding out there? No one knows for sure, and likely no one ever will.
d92e354b-6956-4a87-a5ee-e7e402373ed1: Hargulka, the troll king, still {d|c21 Hargulka Lives}lives{/d} in the Stolen Lands. Amazingly, he managed to bring his savage kin to heel, even organizing trade with nearby settlements of ordinary citizens! The common folk aren't exactly excited to have such neighbors, but they'll settle for trolls who've switched their menu to forest game and the cattle people sell them!
aca5f02c-d708-4a99-adc4-abe75b3e2626: The dangerous, man-eating trolls disappeared entirely from the forests and swamps of the Stolen Lands. Kobolds, though, being sneaky and clever, are still sometimes met by travelers and hunters who wander off the beaten track. Some even say the short reptiles still praise the "great king" {d|c21 Tartuk Exiled}Tartuk{/d}, but no one knows for certain — as soon as anyone approaches the kobolds, they forget their military honor and turn tail!
d7c50953-a218-4aef-86b7-a561ab100c18: Bartholomew Delgado still serves the {mf|king|queen} loyally. From time to time, he orders peculiar mechanisms and substances from all corners of the world. After receiving them, he spends a few days bragging about some great discovery he's about to make, then ends up gloomy for a few months. Then he receives another package, and the process repeats itself. At night, chilling screams are often heard from his laboratory.
db66f61c-e2c0-4b83-bd2f-97394fd28cca: After enduring so many storms and troubles, Varnhold eventually turned into a real city. Daring settlers decided to conquer the vast, wild expanses of Dunsward, and despite all odds, they succeeded! The modest colony that {d|c31 Maegar Saved}almost{/d} vanished at the hands of an ancient lich turned everything around to become a thriving city with lively river trading.
efd71eee-40d3-4ca8-8813-33edde4050e8: Unfortunately, without its founder, Varnhold never really recovered from the blow. Over time, the colony withered away — all the more so when its dwellers continued to disappear under mysterious circumstances! It took less than two years for Varnhold to permanently become a ghost town. The only person happy about the news was the {mf|king|queen}'s new advisor, a mysterious and powerful {d|c31 Vordakai Hired}wizard{/d}, who still serves the ruler loyally to this day.
ccdc68f8-c22c-436e-9179-6f3c424aa4da: {d|c31 Agai Lives}Agai{/d}, the spriggan leader, learned a valuable lesson after surviving his meeting with the {mf|king|queen} and even regaining his tribe's home — don't try to occupy seemingly empty settlements anymore! Instead, the spriggans settled across Dunsward's wild borderlands and proclaimed it as their domain! Keeping the peace in a situation like that seems like the stuff of dreams — as evidenced by the occasional lost patrols and stolen cattle!
c3bab0ce-bfb7-4d36-af04-9078251c43d6: {d|c11 Peacemaker}Peace{/d} reigns in the caves beneath the Old Sycamore. The kobolds and mites continue to explore the depths and learn simple crafts from each other. Rumor has it the first mite-kobold wedding even happened not long ago! That said, settlers still aren't rushing to build new homes in the area. Some kind souls even put up warning signs along the roads: "Beware, traveler! Steer clear of the Old Sycamore!" 46a26d81-bc91-4194-a84e-d3c7fb854c56: "I see many of you wearing Abadar's keys. Does the god of civilization approve of such uncivilized methods for solving problems?"
69a2ff26-7f08-4cef-a559-34638742e186: [Knock the wand out of her hands]
412df6b6-569d-4271-9ca0-88fdaae04956: [Signal to the guards not to attack]
543adc27-4c7a-41a0-bbbe-3153adef3327: "So are you here to complain about the sick cows, or to demand a people's republic? Make up your minds."
1b8f94ca-e7bd-454a-96a8-dd4e4a7ce609: {n}The situation is growing heated. Varn's guards, their weapons drawn, stand opposite a group of settlers who are yelling revolutionary slogans. You see some of the local fishermen among them. There's a half-orc woman in the front row, wearing a bright cape and shaking her weapon. She's obviously not from around here.{/n}
cf7316b4-d812-4b50-8da9-21a85746ae83: "Down with tyranny! We will not be treated like cattle! You can't enslave us!"
90e1d375-b27d-425b-b653-ea02ca0e08bf: "Calm down! Now..." {n}Noticing you, the guard sighs with relief.{/n} "Here's {Name}, the General of His Grace {d|Varn}Varn{/d}. I'm sure {mf|he|she} will deal with your problems, so we can all go home peacefully."
ccc54309-97d2-4db3-8376-214bab3c8314: "I am Leonta Misho of the revolutionary Crimson Swans of {g|Galt}Galt{/g}! We have freed our own home from tyranny, and I will not stand by as your new feudal lord tramples the freedom of these people under his boots!"
891f2a9c-f9f5-4068-a3f7-b25ab26722bd: "Kings, barons, earls... Ordinary people are like cattle to the nobility! We will not allow this new state to become yet another prison for the people, who groan under the yoke of tyranny! We demand that {d|Varn}Maegar Varn{/d} relinquish his power, proclaim these lands a people's republic, and gather a constituent assembly!"
0469230a-8cb7-4e04-b697-baa51ca07049: "Their problem is the autocracy of the tyrant!"
e410f3f7-8014-4d91-8d4d-348db8645db4: "Don't threaten us! We've seen worse than you!" {n}Settlers draw their weapons, ready to defend their leader.{/n}
5f9dd725-8062-4dde-a654-dccdf720587d: "Here's the whole story, General. We're from Brevoy. We were tired of working for the Surtova, so we decided to try our luck here in this new land. So we built a farm a couple of miles from Varnhold, and started settling in. And it was going pretty well, too! But then a pestilence struck the cows!"
eebec92b-22c9-4e6d-8518-0321585baa1a: "They can't even stand, the poor things. Their eyes are all dull and they're frothing at the lips... We sent word to His Grace – the Baron did promise to help us settlers! But we got no reply. He didn't even send a doctor – or even a bloody scroll!"
695ab241-d726-4a07-8931-be583e52ab89: "What's wrong with you? Are you prepared to live your entire lives as slaves to a feudal lord? Whoever still has a living, beating heart in their chest, and not a pile of dung – to arms! For freedom! Against tyranny!"
0ec0e49a-a271-4f1c-abfa-657268aa97e1: "Oh yes. The henchmen of dictators see evil everywhere, because evil is all they know! But we are not like them! Our hearts are pure, and our intentions are noble! To arms, my friends, to arms for our freedom!"
b33519b9-797a-4c31-a1f1-b8e362c0b420: "Forgive us. We didn't mean any harm. This damned troublemaker played us for fools! Throw the snake in prison! And we'll, you know.. We'll just go home."
6a76ad66-ddb2-4f04-b7d2-446b53dc1ef5: "Do you hear that? Violence is the argument of dictators! They think they can keep us forever enslaved, under threat of their swords! But they are wrong! We are invincible, because the truth is with us!"
f03c8246-78db-4f5b-a2e2-8f65ec9005ad: "A wand of invisibility? Old Ignash the sorcerer had one just like that... Now then, let me see it!"
cce385b6-4cee-4fce-9ff3-b6821e514482: "What wand? We're talking about the cows, and {mf|he|she}'s going on about a wand. {mf|He|She}'s just trying to distract us!"
03bf0012-a594-47fe-ba68-1f16abfcfb7d: "Right, who are we listening to? Those revolutionaries ruined everything in {g|Galt}Galt{/g}, and now they want to come here and tell us how to live?"
a8afd66d-78fa-4f73-9046-30eb37f6d022: "No, no, Leonta told us all about {g|Galt}Galt{/g}! The people rose to power there, but they couldn't save the country from traitors and saboteurs. That's not going to happen here. We've never have any traitors or saboteurs here!"
909530d4-266b-406a-a1c8-e38e5f9b1983: "Poison? Wait a minute, that does sound like poisoning! But who... Em... Leonta! Did you poison our cows just to stir up a riot?!"
760685df-e3c4-49d6-83e9-42a63b801327: "No, why would I? It's only an illness. Or maybe they ate some poisonous grass in the field. Either way, we need help, and the baron sends us nothing!"
9ed99a72-58c8-4d99-8029-f2b16126e791: "You're right! This doesn't seem right – drawing our weapons at the first sign of trouble. If we grabbed our knives every time there's a problem, what would happen? It wouldn't be a nice place to live, that's for sure!"
a64c6620-c3dc-4a35-9300-e6652bce7039: "Don't try smooth talking us! What Abadar thinks of me is my business. We came here to talk about our dealings with the baron!"
9c7749cd-571b-4594-997d-4ef6f182dbc3: {n}You notice the revolutionary take a magic wand from her belt. She's about to cast a spell!{/n}
85cb7502-3cc4-4b9a-9ba7-9929c8f65d88: {n}The revolutionary grabs a magical wand from her belt. Before you have a chance to react, she casts an invisibility spell and disappears.{/n}
4bec8b74-8793-4472-aa8e-9d2569d3e00f: {n}The settler looks more closely at the wand the half-orc is holding, and his faces grow dark with anger.{/n} "That's the wand of invisibility we took from old Ignash the sorcerer. So that's why you needed it!"
6b6963d9-7950-4668-9149-0b5bccf269bb: {n}The revolutionary ducks. Your fingers grab only air.{/n}
e3818085-eefd-4e84-8e12-231107f12292: {n}One settler picks up the wand from the ground, and his face grows dark with anger.{/n} "This is the wand of invisibility we took from old Ignash the sorcerer. So this is why you needed it!"
b9adb5d9-4c32-48f0-9c03-9c105f864a04: "Keep back, keep back... We can still avoid bloodshed!"
314914e7-eec8-4e7f-8cc1-ecb77f21274e: {n}The revolutionary casts an invisibility spell with the wand, and promptly disappears, but only you notice it happen. – Both the guards and the settlers are only concerned about the fight!{/n}
2aef1b14-1440-4083-9f7c-66e6dab196ec: {n}The guards loose a battle cry and attack the crowd. The first blood drops fall to the ground. Carnage is inevitable!{/n}
f0c717f9-98fd-4d44-be8d-0ce3f00d814f: "We wanted to forget it and seek our fortune elsewhere, but then this one came. Her name is Leonta Misho. She's from {g|Galt}Galt{/g}. She said the Baron didn't care about us, and wasn't going to help. That all he's good for is taking taxes. She said we should go make some noise, stomp our feet. Then maybe His Grace will pay heed to our troubles!"
a8473b6a-87b5-4e5a-8c69-da3e9a1b9fe5: {n}Baffled, the settlers stare into the empty space where she was just a moment ago. Rage fills their faces.{/n} "What is this? She brought us here, set the soldiers on us... And disappears? The Galtan snake!"
6e8e902f-173f-4911-a1ac-81f2076d7d40: "So that's your plan? Bring us here, set the soldiers on us... And disappear? You Galtan snake! Tie her up! Throw her in prison – or lead her to the chopping block. It's not our business any more."
53f8390d-1c17-4fad-93de-3ac01261cdc9: {n}The settlers exchange looks.{/n} "Yes, about the republic... We went a little overboard..."
dde91f29-8741-484b-a576-36ec829f22ad: "Citizens, don't listen to the tyrant's henchman! Don't give up! Fight for your rights! Don't you see? So long as a sovereign rules over you, no one will care about your suffering? Your cows, your fields, your homes – all of this is at risk, until you become your own masters! Down with the baron! The time of the people has come!"
0070b4c4-9314-44ff-a9db-a38697e24d7e: {n}Inspired by the revolutionary's speech, the settlers draw their weapons and move towards the guards. The latter raise their weapons and grit their teeth. A bloodbath seems inevitable!{/n}
96af22fa-f2c6-49fe-a438-aaa3a43d01e5: "But come to think of it... Please send us a doctor, or a healing scroll. Our cows keep getting ill, and the baron doesn't help, or even reply... If it weren't for the cows, we wouldn't have caused any trouble! All right, so long!"
3480d90f-c6a9-4379-8980-b4006ae0c9f9: "Let's go, everyone, before the baron's guards cut us to pieces! I guess there's no luck for us in Varnhold. We'll try to settle somewhere else. Maybe things will be better in Shrike Hills..."
33042b91-bc9f-47cc-87e4-1d956b77d4b7: "Keep quiet, you've had your say. Folks, tie her up!"
90071ab1-8c6b-4f4a-a93b-b79d01291222:
"You better surrender while you still can! Or we'll slaughter the lot of you!"
{n}The soldiers approach the crowd. They obviously don't want to fight the settlers, but they won't disobey your orders either.{/n}
6cb617ad-12bf-426f-a706-00404c044d4d: {n}The revolutionary casts an invisibility spell with her wand, and vanishes right in front of everyone.{/n}
3c5ca7ce-0986-40d9-8e6d-ea9efb52404f: {n}The fishermen exchange apprehensive looks.{/n} "We'll, you know... We'll go too, all right? We have some silly things written on our walls. We'll wash them off right away!"
f48dd091-24cc-47a1-bd39-d68b10b9cd52: "Yes! And there's holes in our boats. Can't catch any fish like that! But the Baron doesn't care! He loves to eat fish, I'm sure, but he's never held a fishing pole his whole life!"
03191e98-7197-49b5-b7e7-f69c06cf27c1: "Harrim, what do you mumble about? Want talk, talk loud!"
bd658f4b-59ce-47cc-b810-414d63d5f2ad: "My words are not for mortal ears, Nok-Nok. I send my prayers beyond this realm."
2bea3db7-43eb-47c4-b182-ed9951207ecd: "Why did you destroy this anvil? Does Groetus encourage destruction now? I've always believed that Groetus does not destroy, he just waits until the end comes to everything in this world?"
ba1f26c7-8efe-446d-80f3-d8ffde04f7b2: "Hey, don't touch the anvil! Step back!"
0e4e9291-d014-4d43-8594-9cc79ec4228e: "What's done is done. But in the future, I forbid you to touch anything that could be… Just don't touch anything at all."
3082d953-cddb-4ce2-9757-a95d343d5d8e: "You see, everything is not that bad after all! The anvil is still operational. What do you say now?"
3af0078e-7d38-47a6-a928-80fcdf62e884: "What have you done? We could use that anvil!"
a7b81870-ae0d-4d44-a7ee-fff612cfcd47: "What are you waiting for? Break it!"
a507f918-f2e4-46fc-a1dd-3f78bde47cff: "Perhaps Torag simply didn't want an apostate like yourself touching the anvil he had blessed."
41f2ce9f-60b7-4e8f-b92b-a5e589387bd4: {n}Octavia rolls her eyes and twirls her forefinger near her temple.{/n}
fdfb4489-1863-4bbe-84be-d093101a456f: "This shouldn't be like that! That is just wrong!" {n}Harrim turns around and glares at the anvil with hate in his eyes. His hands clench into fists.{/n} "{g|Groetus}Groetus{/g}, grant me strength! I'll restore righteousness!" {n}The dwarf deals a strong blow with his fist to the anvil base.{/n}
f7cc9d2a-c6ed-433c-bec8-dc3383a152f4: {n}The light grows dim for a moment. A dull rumble seems to start at the base of the anvil, the sound growing steadily louder, and finally filling the whole room with a deafening roar. You could swear you hear the mad laughter of Groetus in this roaring, or maybe it is Harrim's own laughter? The anvil trembles and suddenly falls apart, as if trying to catch up in time with the rest of the fortress in its state of ruin.{/n}
63b969d6-f405-49fa-b284-3db2a5daa300: "I've just made things right again," {n}Harrim sobs, a lonely tear runing down his cheek.{/n} "{g|Groetus}Groetus{/g} got what he wanted. Something that... That was rightfully his."
508954a5-b53e-436c-afac-290211958d1a: {n}Harrim doesn't seem to hear anything you've just said. He stands frozen in some kind of torpor over the destroyed anvil.{/n} "{g|Groetus}Groetus{/g}... has got what he wanted. My duty here is done." {n}His shoulders shake with suppressed sobs.{/n}
8fbe7c32-cd52-40c4-ab33-70e8ee12b078: "I've done what I had to do! This anvil should have been destroyed long ago! I've just restored righteousness!" {n}Harrim looks at you angrily, but his voice trembles with sorrow.{/n} "I had to do it. It was so hard for me, {name}. Almost as hard as living itself."
e12dd165-5254-47c0-a6f9-ef41dfce0d90: "For all the... How can you constantly doubt the overwhelming might of {g|Groetus}Groetus{/g}?" {n}his face grows red with anger, his eyes bulge and seem to almost fall from their sockets.{/n} "How can you denounce him every time you get a chance?! You're a blasphemer!" {n}Filled with rage he raises his hand to hit you, but at the last moment, he turns away and hits the base of the broken anvil instead.{/n}
3e3ace3b-d98e-4b0e-924e-7425992f44bb: {n}After several moments, Harrim comes to his senses.{/n} "Forgive me, {name}. Sometimes I still forget how difficult it is to follow the path of {g|Groetus}Groetus{/g}. I must not get angry at unbelievers. I must persuade them to make their own choice of following the one true God."
8de5d1f5-533e-4b19-ab70-484914a130d5: {n}Harrim's second blow shatters the remnants of the anvil. Among the shards, something catches your attention — an odd red stone, definitely of magical origins. It radiates heat and glitters with every shade of flame.{/n}
9db55839-3b92-4313-b92d-703444fec7e4: "I don't want to upset you, my friend, but you're such an idiot."
88167a64-e456-49ff-ac3c-299b5564539b: {n}He finally averts his gaze from the fire and turns to you.{/n} "The very existence of this anvil is miraculous and... unnatural. So much suffering and sorrow surrounds us, and yet here... hope?" {n}Harrim shakes his beard in negation.{/n}
0c2eae17-9b6b-4306-9cd7-ea27b88630d8: {n}The priest picks up the glimmering jewel from the floor and looks at it suspiciously. He nearly throws the gem against the wall, but something makes him hesitate. The red reflections dance on his face.{/n}
e98cccd3-f080-4218-a337-181ca34d47d9: "I don't know, but I feel Torag's touch upon it. Maybe those who created the anvil put it inside? Or... Hmm... No, no, nonsense, this cannot be. Jewels don't appear from out of nowhere... But then metal isn't usually broken with bare hands, right? I don't know, {Name}. I don't know."
c7923c6c-799a-4f62-b641-55e70345944e: {n}The dwarf hurls the shimmering jewel onto the floor. It shatters into splinters, which vanish into the air.{/n}
80231413-be62-47d8-8ec5-d21c695ef138: {n}Harrim hands you the jewel.{/n} "There. Do as you wish with it. You can sell it, throw it away, keep it as a memento... If it's {g|Torag}Torag's{/g} parting gift, I have no need of it."
1d687afc-a3ed-4d40-97a0-8b756a99a944: {n}Harrim wipes the tears from his eyes.{/n} "I shouldn't have come here. What did I expect to find besides decay, dust and ash? I... Forgive me, {Name}. Thank you for honoring my request and bringing me here. But now... now I wish to be alone."
c60fcc86-8f24-40ca-94a7-061a37d0e7e6: "Huh! That was awesome! When did you learn to break cast iron with your bare hands? You're strong!"
e9e0affb-8eb7-4999-b651-8053b22c4de0: {n}Harrim pets the anvil gently, without any fear of its heat.{/n} "Once… I dreamed of working with a furnace like that. I gave oaths to {g|Torag}Torag{/g} that I'd craft hundreds of suits of armor. That my hammer would be tireless... Oh, that was so long ago..."
5731d74f-7aed-4894-ab32-54854ec366c1: {n}Harrim seems not to hear you, totally entranced by the fire dancing before his eyes.{/n} "Once… I dreamed of working with a furnace like that. I gave oaths to {g|Torag}Torag{/g} that I'd craft hundreds of armor suits. That my hammer would be tireless... Oh, that was so long ago..."
cf88eb40-07a2-46e0-8661-f6587abb1d6d: "An ancient anvil... Can it… Can it still work? " {n}Harrim can't believe his own eyes, so he reaches to the anvil, touches it with care. Fiery sparks flit dangerously close to his beard.{/n} "It's just... beautiful..." {n}The dwarf smiles happily.{/n}
247a0f65-ce40-41b0-b9a3-4b95349ff4d7: "Jubi, what keeps you in our party, hunh? You just keep nagging and nagging, and you won't shut up. You don't like this, and you really hate that... So pick up your things and get out of here!"
f6b4cde0-2e18-46fc-ac68-b8e6628cf2fc: "I'm not nagging, I'm giving valuable recommendations. And luckily, unlike a hysterical vixen I could name, {Name} understands this!"
5c02be8e-997a-423a-8765-9785ef7ef0cd: "That's highway robbery! I'll be subject to Areena's whim without getting anything in return!"
d64d930d-ff40-40bc-a0f6-67f01da90547: "I'm not sitting around listening to insults. Throw this frosty worm into prison!"
ccc00850-ce81-4cb1-ab64-1d7f3d922549: "Have our special arrangements with Kaleena been included in the contract?"
5b4f5a50-0ee0-4886-98a6-74568e6c1579: "I'm not signing a trade agreement with Irrisen. Leave my lands."
49688d67-e6e2-4168-a378-8cc81df5e92e: "In that case, there won't be a deal."
39eca811-9b7d-49a9-b027-312eb13b357f: {n}A blond man dressed in furs and brocade bows ceremoniously.{/n} "{mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}, I am happy to greet you on behalf of her Excellency Duchess Korvosh."
b2153b30-901f-45ab-a772-fe4ecb870f7c: "I am honored to represent Areena Korvosh, the head of the noble house of Hoarwood. My mistress rose to power after her poor mother died and her ungrateful sister fell from grace – may her name be blotted from the history of the house."
b66b9278-0640-49d0-8c68-1d27c82ff551: "I am honored to represent the interests of Kaleena Korvosh, the head of the noble house of Hoarwood. My mistress courageously took the position left to her after the deaths of her mother and sister. You supported her Excellency in her hour of need, and now may enjoy a special honor."
652db449-2da6-4ee4-b465-98cbe5b36500: {n}The ambassador's clear dark eyes go to you.{/n} "I don't think you heard me correctly, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. My mistress grants you the honor of trading with her family, the noble house of {g|Irrisen}Irrisen{/g}. This privilege is offered to very, very few. I didn't come here to negotiate the terms. I'm merely informing you. If they're not good enough for you, it is none of my concern."
ca62dab7-69ed-4bfb-bdd3-822c6969f6b2: {n}The ambassador grins, rolls the scroll and makes a bow.{/n} "As you wish, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. Your rejection will hardly affect my mistress."
5d22d679-aed7-4a69-bba8-07313fffca01: "Where was I? Oh yes. Special privileges for the ambassadors of {g|Irrisen}Irrisen{/g} in your lands..."
b7b48347-088d-44ef-8d18-7cae8247abe8: {n}The ambassador utters an angry shriek.{/n} "You're going to be sorry! My mistress will learn of this, I swear it!"
9957d820-b53a-47b8-acb7-62043cc5ad80: {n}The ambassador's chilly smile barely conceals his discontent with being interrupted.{/n} "Of course. My mistress remembers perfectly well about your... merits, and your power to jeopardize her. Everything has been arranged."
630bfced-71c9-4284-8178-f0218f438a34: "Congratulations to you and to your {mf|barony|barony|kingdom|kingdom} on your new trade ally. May the relationship between our lands be eternal." {n}The ambassador bows deeply.{/n}
ff71cf30-e2de-41dd-b14a-1e258fdc1f0b: "According to the terms, you shall deliver a monthly load of vegetables and grain to {g|Irrisen}Irrisen{/g} in a timely fashion. Failing this, you will be penalized. Your merchants shall pay all fees associated with Hoarwood trading rights. Otherwise, a prison sentence is due. The cargo shall be paid for within an eighteen-month timeframe..."
f473a9c0-3e04-4f1a-b364-00fc985c45c1: "The noble house offers you special terms of trade, including tax exemption and assistance in delivery to the place of destination. According to the agreement..." {n}The ambassador dives into numerous clauses and items of the trade agreement. He doesn't seem to care if you're listening or not.{/n}
69c9a75e-2c09-45c1-bb19-e86c20385485: {g|Relations6_3}[Choice effects]{/g} [Gain 2 BP each week] "Bring in our troops to keep peace in Novoboro."
3ae27747-cc57-4cf6-a530-c6900e872520: {g|Relations6_4}[Choice effects]{/g} [Gain 2 BP each week] "We will buy wares from those who bring them. It's as simple as that."
9d0ad611-f4ba-48a1-96f8-f7a3d69222e3: "There's an issue that demands your attention. Sevenarches want to bring their fleet to Novoboro – allegedly to combat piracy. But in fact they simply can't accept that the elves of {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g} are trading dwarven wares with the {g|Five Kings Mountains}Five Kings Mountains{/g}. Control over Novoboro would allow Sevenarches to collect duties along this trade route."
0f896192-0a7c-429c-9bc4-7124b2ab66da: "One issue requires your attention. Sevenarches are bringing their fleet to Novoboro, an important point along the river trade, and create a 'customs' there to combat piracy. But don't be fooled, they're really just going there to level duties on wares brought in from the {g|Five Kings Mountains}Five Kings Mountains{/g} and heading towards {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g}."
3c366f0e-d90b-4730-85c2-275a725edfef: "An important issue requires your attention! Sevenarches wants to bring their ships into the harbor of Novoboro, a key point along {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g} river trade route. They claim that their only goal is fighting piracy, but in fact they'll be searching all ships for dwarven wares. The smart captains will pay duties to Sevenarches; the fools will be declared pirates."
af7daf2e-12d4-4cc1-b80f-e3bf66fb3adb: "As you say. I hope you have a good reason for getting us into this broil – and I hope you've chosen the right side."
994f84d7-f16e-49dd-bbba-58075b5dc0f3: "Great! It's time for {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g} to know their egoistic politics is over. There are several new, strong players in the {g|River Kingdoms}River Kingdoms{/g}. Like you, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}!"
f655bf5d-5182-4701-af12-79570f25b1f1: "Wonderful. We will let Sevenarches know that we won't tolerate their brazen efforts to seize an honest trade route."
86a3df10-bee3-40a8-949b-97d32fa19aef: "At least we'll be sure that no one is oppressing anyone. But will the others be sure that we're not oppressing them..."
7cd3cc50-ea7c-4882-92e1-59a43922ce25: "I will order our ships to reach Novoboro first. We seize control over trade, whatever our neighbors might think, and keep our eyes open for pirates and smugglers."
24aa27fe-0265-4805-aa6f-397e51ea3ce5: "That's a bold move, seizing their prize right out from under Sevenarches. But the fastest runner wins the race, right? I applaud your wisdom yet again."
15641bcb-9225-484c-981e-62904a2f8967: "Maybe it's better to keep out of the troubles of others. The elves aren't completely right to inflate the prices of dwarven wares and not share them with anyone!"
0075c3f7-b5f0-4d34-a669-890dfe1c76c1: "It is wise to keep your economy separate from the political broils of others. Let them fight over duties without us. Most reasonable, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}."
5405f0f2-5a20-400b-8766-f3b21d158f01: "At present, all the wares from the {g|Five Kings Mountains}Five Kings Mountains{/g} that we receive arrive here via the elves, at the prices they set. {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g} asks for our help in this trade war, and Sevenarches also offers its cooperation. e719d5aa-f24e-441b-ace7-2c6f660e24f6: "Both {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g} and Sevenarches are asking for support. I don't trust either of them, so I suggest we bring our own fleet to Novoboro. 8b969c1f-53b9-48e4-bba4-e8f9577a6cb4: "Choose something beautiful. A book you wouldn't be ashamed to have your teacher read."

c1f15a29-eaea-4bb8-9673-09dd6f9083cd: "Ha ha! Yes! Throwing truth in the faces of tyrants — that's a bard's highest calling! Though I'd certainly throw something heavier in Irovetti's face if I could... But let's start with the truth!"
b5b23ab4-15f9-4172-94f1-1be75e777b4c: "Well, that's not really what I had in mind, but... You're right. Art is art, but we can't forget the pelf it requires. It's a deal. I'll pay you back for the printing press, and then I'll work toward my higher calling as a bard — and as a book printer!"
2ffab20c-7143-4113-92f6-0c2d2656c66b: "Let's get to it! I'll send for horses to get this delivery the rest of the way to the capital."
dbfc16f3-bef1-4708-a9bd-5820f12c8eec: {n}Linzi smiles at you warmly.{/n} "It was Teacher who showed me the beauty hidden in books... I think the best way to repay that kindness would be to do the same for others. Maybe that's really the main calling of a bard."

e8f6b859-5584-4fd3-836d-1bfeb6778fee: "So, what brought you to these lands?"
3c424449-d3d5-46e3-aebb-420dbc3b0e9a: "I see you and Amiri are old friends."
dbe61c2d-ef72-4eaf-b871-6b13dd7a83ed: "Sounds like you're not too clever, so I'll speak in a language I'm sure you understand: one more rude word, and I'll punch your rotten teeth down your throat!"
804cc5ce-457b-4d40-981f-a06f083caee0: "Choose your words carefully, barbarian. You and your tribe are guests here."
9ad70160-09b8-4ed2-8832-36572bff3d09: "Amiri is no longer one of your tribe. She's with me now, so if you need something from her, you'll have to speak with me first."

eaea2d2b-0974-40ea-b476-be109092a253: "Don't say that! f1f8bc22-a591-4ee7-bc4a-861e84b49d84: "We were like sisters from childhood. She…"
590bf32d-b3ec-4bf3-baca-19137e569d2c: "It just didn't come up. In fact…"
c57c7f6c-2238-4a27-8f54-551c2bebbe23: "May both our tribes live in peace. We…"
87145d76-5139-4c19-aa9b-4554cc357172: {n}An old, grey-haired barbarian with a tattooed face interrupts her.{/n} "Nilak! Who are you chatting with? Who are you? Wait..."
07cf610f-0566-4203-b8e2-40fa08926606: {n}He looks closer at Amiri's face an suddenly starts to yell, pointing his crooked finger at her.{/n} "You! Pariah! Freak! After all you did, you still have the nerve to come and show your ugly face here!"
5e98d4ee-1405-401d-a542-b1ea2f1bba0c: "Chieftain Akaia, this is {mf|Baron|Baroness} {name}, we're in {mf|his|her} lands now. Please soften your heart. Maybe {mf|he|she} can help us."
d1d5946f-5174-47fa-8487-5c73a0eac1a7: "Hm! Hm. A baron? That's something like a chieftain, right? You don't look like one... Well, whatever. I am Akaia, chieftain of the Six Bears tribe, and I need you to give me this dirty scumbag!" {n}He points his finger at Amiri.{/n}
1b5b95e0-7feb-4be6-8536-b5c5fa53ae66: {n}The chieftain gives you a contemptuous look.{/n} "A baroness, huh? Yet another tribe ruled by tits? Ugh. Fine. I am Akaia, the chieftain of the Six Bears tribe, and I need you to give me this dirty scumbag!" {n}He points his finger at Amiri.{/n}
53a5e7c6-79c4-4737-bb1b-42b8ddf24684: "Guests?! We'd rather be guests in {g|Abyss}Abyss{/g} than this hole. But we had to come. I'll tell you why we're here!"
65672594-5531-4900-9589-27ce8d6511fe: "You threaten the Six Bears, you foolish {mf|pup|chick}?! Don't waste your breath. Thanks to her we've witnessed horrors you can't imagine! Just let me tell you what she's done to us!"
3308c034-0056-4e4f-b5f2-5927407e6979: "This criminal has the blood of her tribesmen on her hands! I'll tell you what she did to us — and then you can decide if you want scum like that in your tribe!"
47ad31bb-241c-4034-a38e-29ebbb2582cb: "You have no idea of what a venomous snake you've invited into your tent! Listen to me, and I will tell you!"
564e1ae9-df38-4667-bbd8-57c41864b021: "From the dawn of time, our tribe lived by the old ways: everyone had a place, a job to do. Men crafted and went hunting. And they were right: she brought disaster upon our whole tribe!"
e9c01edc-33c3-4bcf-9a82-d1a64aa7b265: "Once, a gang of giants came to our lands. They scared our prey, attacked our huntsmen... So we decided to deal with them. We sent a group — and she went along. For a long time we waited for this group to return, then we went searching for them even longer — but all we found were their dead bodies! Giants killed them all! Everyone... except for her!"
ab6841f4-16bf-4c02-aeca-cf4ceb1cd484: "And then things got even worse. Have you seen those monsters? An evil spirit sends them! The ghost of a giant! He's the one who chased us from our lands! He chased us through all of {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g}! Even now, he's somewhere nearby — maybe he's just over that hill! He chases us, kills our people... And always says the same: "Bring the thief to me! Find Amiri!"
c45c86b5-bfc6-4081-91c7-a089132c0d9a: {n}The chieftain turns to Amiri, his face red with anger. He shouts, slobbering in her face:{/n} "Now you understand?! That's what your dreams have cost us! We'll feed you to the ghost, and maybe then he'll leave us alone. And at least you'll atone for a tiny part of your guilt!"
94c359ca-df43-4975-9323-71177ba63eaf: {n}In reply, Amiri headbutts the chieftain's face, breaking his nose with a sickly crunch. 47e65f3f-d59e-4a31-bfab-5ba420c7b4df: {n}Amiri raises her sword. Akaia shuts his eyes, but the final blow never comes. Amiri sheathes her sword, pushes the chieftain onto the ground and spits on him.{/n} "Get lost of my sight, you scumbag! Next time I see you I won't stop at words!"
73ddd6e1-17a4-4db2-973c-7a616ec7bf15: {n}Amiri plunges her sword into the chieftain's chest. She breathes heavily, staring at the old man as he falls to his knees before her. fb659140-31f5-4f24-a335-f26c41fb4a3c: {n}Nilak helps the defeated chieftain stand up, and takes him into the nearest hut. The rest of barbarians hurry away, hiding themselves from Amiri's anger.{/n}

b4e5020d-93cb-4974-a0e1-942b0bf9772b: "So you're a bard? Great! Me too! We should share some songs when we have time. You can tell us what they sing in your tribe, and I'll tell you all about Amiri's feats!"
bf898e47-d84f-4638-890f-6f4fb53144da: "Watch your tongue, chief. You are a guest in these lands — uninvited, and not particularly welcome."
3238faa7-cef0-4757-94a3-5771f2fef996: "Quiet, woman! The chiefs are talking! You think you can talk back to a warrior just because you learned to put on armor?"
ceecd7e5-c59f-41eb-9035-7ee2b7d158d7: "Soft chief? They really couldn't find a better nickname for this brontosaurus than soft?" {n}Jubilost chuckles.{/n} "Or does this tribe consist only of giants?
