4314f7ab-2ba0-4bb1-be72-e533828abffc: "Do we?" {n}Jaethal idly brushes invisible dust from her sleeve.{/n} "He bothers me no more than any overzealous fool. He's tried so dearly to 'redeem' me with his faith. I know a few sweet ways to redeem him with mine."
1880e23a-5ddb-4697-9cea-94fb3948dae4: "Do you wish to know what it means to me personally? Or what powers and limitations it imposes?"
d7971e1c-e153-416a-99a3-52c3e62ae94f: {n}A shadow passes over Jaethal's face.{/n} "You surely know how to ask questions..." {n}She says nothing for a long time.{/n} "Two desires led me through life — to feel pleasure time and time again, and to achieve perfection. Un-life brought me closer to the second. I am changeless, torn from time. The chaos of the world, and even the soul circle, have no power over me. But everything comes with a price. Most things that brought me pleasure in life are meaningless to me now. How can I decide which is better?"
cd41054a-7ada-4c39-8f78-4737fd10ea66: "Long did I search for a way to avert this fate. Don't I, who has truly tasted life, deserve a better lot than those benumbed old elves who close themselves to the world? And I found a way in the ancient texts of {g|Urgathoa}Urgathoa{/g}. A ritual, involving the blood of my kin. A trifle, that would make each day feel as a holiday, created specially for me. The ritual gave strength not only to my body, but to my mind and my soul. And my mind whirled at every sensation, each sip of wine, or silken carress. Oh how I miss this..."
a2f2887c-bffe-4f8c-9b0f-8a0dcfc3afcf: "...My cousin was the first I used for the ritual. It was a simple matter to pass her death as an unfortunate accident. But the enchantment would not last. I had to find another, and again conceal my trail. With the third death, my family grew suspicious, and upon the fourth, my deeds were finally revealed. Such a pity. If not for this, my un-life even now would overflow with burning pleasure. For I have dozens of useless relatives."
b5ef99fd-ae44-4322-a6e2-db490f1f2d18: "I concur,"{n} the elf nods in content.{/n} "But not many possess the courage and honesty to admit it. The world is filled with cowards and fools."
928f68ea-5f33-44b8-80f4-cd7654b8e4c1: "Fair. Judge me for my present form. And better yet — for the benefits we can provide each other."
53490053-87cd-4ec8-a59f-0fb94fa2eefc: "Yes, I have." {n}Jaethal shrugs.{/n} "Use whatever high-sounding words you wish to describe my deeds. Say 'abominable' if it suits you. 'Reasonable' and 'honest' would fit just as well."
6b87b318-3a92-4730-9b00-9147a1bf8f30: "It might sound strange, but I know less than others about {g|Urgathoa}Urgathoa{/g} and her faith. My transformation into her inquisitor was... unexpected. But I will answer to the best of my knowledge."
5483ecb5-3a3f-4d6f-910c-0872854be365: "I hope you do not ask from idle curiosity. {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g} is the birthplace of the elves. The other races are allowed to visit, within reasonable limits. Usually, only as far as {g|Greengold}Greengold{/g}. That is the enclave for half-breeds and the short-lived, a whim of our queen. I enjoyed going there sometimes, as to a wild beast show. Beyond this caricature of a city, Kyonin is a mixture of grandeur and the sad remains of ancient glory."
efc4dc4b-2938-4b78-aead-51ba11ef896e: "Curiosity. The need for a reliable ally. You see, I must come to understand what my goddess seeks from me. {g|Urgathoa}Urgathoa{/g} gave me the powers of inquisitor without declaring her will to me. I await her reply, any hint or trace or clue. And I suppose our meeting was no mere accident. Besides..." {n}Jaethal cringes.{/n} "I imagine that several {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g} assassins still pursue me. They never risked attacking me while I was under the patronage of the Aldori. They are unlikely to attack while I have reliable allies like you."
3c42fa8f-470b-4405-8eee-9d9f5a461b26: "I don't know. They can't have been sent by the queen. I am branded outlaw, but my punishment was exile, and it is not custom for elves to contravene their own verdicts. My attackers shouted something about threat and blood. I suppose they are a splinter group of feeble-minded zealots. Or someone on a quest for personal revenge."
7f483049-c4e3-47f9-a74a-f0a1f07124a0: "I only offer information. Dispose of it as you see fit."
9c46982d-98de-47a6-b95c-daa3e731409a: "As you wish. Conversation is truly a waste of time."
20cf6968-35e1-42a0-8615-a611c32b7ee9: "Righteous anger? How tedious. But if it worries you so much, then yes, I appeared before the court. It deemed exile a fair penance."
2bfcc1d8-d4e5-4159-9230-e94c33c0ffd2: "It is much more difficult to accomplish this in {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g} than the {g|River Kingdoms}River Kingdoms{/g}." {n}Jaethal cringes.{/n} "But you are correct. I have learned a lesson from my past, and will be more careful in the future."
1f5b6fb2-096c-46d3-bc3d-8984d59c4d27: "For an elf", {n}Jaethal says pointedly,{/n} "...exile is a serious punishment. There is no other {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g} in this world. Even I, who despises its hypocrisy, must admit as much."
d386a340-57de-4073-9f87-68d39265dd10: "It's rather amusing. I belonged to a wealthy family, and held high position on the courts of Iadara, the capital of {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g}. When my little wrongdoings were revealed, the trial was held in the very same court where I tried cases and delivered sentences, over several hundred years. An awkward situation, don't you think?"
930e2195-576a-4117-9f90-5faa1cf643bd: {n}Jaethal frowns.{/n} "I... don't remember my death. I was stunned by the sentence of exile, and I admit, I showed weakness. I wandered aimless, absorbed in despair, without concern for my safety or sustenance. And then... then... I remember desolate rocks, a stone I lay upon, a convulsion, passing not only through my whole body, but through my soul. Then — I awakened. Cold, calm — my body overwhelmed with strength, but haunted by a strange internal silence."
53f68fce-1035-44e6-a981-fbec69354247: "There were bloody prints of bone feet on the stone next to me: the sign of the goddess. A battle scythe lay nearby. That was the first and last time I heard {g|Urgathoa}Urgathoa's{/g} voice. She spoke but three words: "Hail the inquisitor." That is all. She has neither addressed me nor answered my pleas ever since."
70dfc675-0ff6-45b8-a111-e0865487b563: "I will not bother you with the story of how I tried to comprehend my new... condition. Soon I had a chance to put my new powers to the test. A group of my kin had tracked me through the woods. They were insolent, and would pay dearly for this. But I had to reckon how I might free myself from their persistent chase. A powerful protector from among the short-lived could help me, and the {g|Swordlords}Swordlords{/g} seemed suitable. That is all."
9108eee9-efc6-4147-b99b-39ba6f939a87: "Next to today's graceful dwellings lie the ruins of ancient monuments and fountains. Elves prefer to live in small groups, in secluded settlements. The most outgoing and ambitious live in the capital, Iadara. Daily life is filled with the efforts of hundred-year-old infants seeking worthy goals, and thousand-year-old stony cynics entertaining themselves howsoever they can. That is all. It's scarcely worth mentioning that even this gloom is far more tempting than anything one finds in the lands of the short-lived."
e8eae955-ebe7-4c58-bb8a-db3a4698bf5b: "Dreadfully, of course. Your healers had better stay away from me in battle. The undead are 'healed' through interaction with negative energy. — And I can perfectly manage that on my own."
6cc73463-53ba-4e4a-bcf7-8b70aa5738f5: "I am spared from that bothersome need. But I hope you do not take this as a reason to invent additional responsibilities to entertain me during the night. I spend this time meditating and addressing the goddess."
0be4ad96-d4b9-4516-bd4b-58e5bf113180: "A tactless and facile question. That pleasure is now as senseless to me as food or wine. Action without feeling." {n}Jaethal cringes.{/n}
5229af68-405f-4bdb-bf5d-382b412d7439: "Perhaps. But the choice was made for me. I have nothing left but to follow the will of the goddess."
c19da6ce-5e32-446c-b93f-40d6bb3ee45f: "I would prefer to have both. But meanwhile I shall have to content myself with power."
7ffa8564-b3dd-4d2c-91a0-b7ea6cb81bae: "Not {g|Urgathoa}Urgathoa{/g}. But {g|Pharasma}Pharasma{/g} still tries to call her to order, and {g|Sarenrae}Sarenrae{/g}, to 'heal' her." {n}Jaethal laughs at the absurdity.{/n}
4206f858-f39b-41c3-b0c9-e9b8460c151b: "Oh, certainly. {g|Urgathoa}Urgathoa{/g} was once a mortal woman, basking in life and all the pleasures it had to offer. Her passion was so strong that Urgathoa rebelled against {g|Pharasma}Pharasma{/g}, against death itself and its laws. After her own death, she escaped the power of the Lady of Graves and returned to the world as a goddess — and the first undead. Since then she has protected all who submit their souls to pleasure and passion, paying no heed to worn-out morals and the dictates of law."
b3c164a6-0a52-4249-ac1e-16ee294388fc: "Because {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g} is plagued by narrow-minded cowards. Some tremble at the freedom granted by {g|Urgathoa}Urgathoa{/g}. Others fear the wrath of {g|Pharasma}Pharasma{/g} and her priests."
18e22cf4-88db-48c1-8eb7-a388bcdede9a: "To enjoy. To taste exquisite dishes, to feel the lover's caress, and drink the enemy's suffering. A wonderful religious obligation, isn't it?"
cfebe3df-93e4-4288-a96f-2785fffbd2c2: "How unwise. Is this your final decision?"
79bbb80f-6180-428e-b8d2-e1557f09419e: "Isn't that a shame?" {n}Jaethal smiles coldly.{/n} "I should say, it isn't."
e3fd2b6d-332c-43dc-a529-aa8050056745: "Entertained? You are welcome. What else is life for?"
48fdb85f-62e1-44d0-9b91-462696827262: "Do you mean someone I would hesitate to sacrifice? Perhaps my daughter. I would regret the wasted effort — the creature turned out quite well. Like a properly trained dog, or a well-managed horse."
d75f35fe-b820-4c78-8915-cd86f5caf9b9: "Yes, that's true. It's strange I do not think more about who might have killed me. I should crave revenge, but I do not. Time and again, I remember the moment when the power of my gift brought that young elf back from the dead. It was… exciting."
9cf448d1-ffb0-4d20-a6d6-9f5b4cef2a43: "For the second time in my life, I felt her divine presence, and the power of my gift — power itself! Isn't un-life a wonderful blessing? By my own will, I can wrest someone's beauty out of time and into eternity, to preserve them in this world forever."
3f7bb5ba-0e13-4c3e-8e7d-86fc6e23907f: "It intrigues me as well. Sometimes it feels like two forces are fighting inside of me. One is my logical side, which strives to understand my gift, to evaluate and calculate the consequences and limits of its potential. The other is deep and hidden... It laughs at the first, and urges me to simply enjoy the power I've been given, to breathe it in. Which side will win? Someday we may find out."
44badbab-3e41-415f-80ee-8ac20dec5b02: "Everyone has the right to their own prejudices." {n}Jaethal shrugs.{/n} "So long as they don't interfere with you ruling your {mf|barony|barony|kingdom|kingdom} as you see fit, then all is well."
bece4216-2fd3-4598-ad0d-c46c1582fed7: "I… I'm surprised at how deeply you can see. I shall ponder your words. Perhaps they will show me the way."
117550c1-d619-4cd1-8193-aefc899ffdd3: "She… she impressed me. What exactly would you like to discuss?"
4cdcebd7-2d57-478a-90b7-071dd0fad7a3: "You'll laugh to know what I learned... It offers great power, a chance for a new life... To put it simply, it's a way to transfer your soul into a blood relative's body. It's not so bad, if you think about it. You could choose that red-haired cousin or the niece with sweet dimples on her cheeks..." {n}Jaethal grins, making it clear that she was joking... probably.{/n} "But all my kin are in {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g}, and it's forbidden for me to go there. And even if I did... I don't know if {g|Urgathoa}Urgathoa{/g} would be angry with my decision to regain a living body. I suggest we stop talking about the ritual. It's pointless."
979e59dd-a8c9-443b-b9eb-2f0ed9b0e21c: "Of course. It was... An interesting experience."
4266aeee-83e4-46da-8f91-4a5c2e29a68e: "I must admit, the half-blood surprised me. I can say... he deserves respect. It's strange, isn't it? One might instead say that he lived in prison house built of dogma, and died serving it. But he was something I cannot yet fully be — an inquisitor with a purpose, someone who sees no barrier in the service of their faith. I'd come to think that the infinite search for new sensations and pleasures was the essence of life, but perhaps this is... not enough?"
357ffde7-607f-4061-8a48-f01097e68294: "Ah. That is my daughter. Did I mention her earlier? I should say the resemblance turned out to be superficial. Norte would not have reacted so cowardly if she rose as undead. I was a good enough teacher to raise her strong, restrained, sensible, and able to evaluate her situation before acting. She would have weighed everything thoughtfully, rather than immediately pleading for death."
d7b6daf8-b707-4262-8fdb-4b37ceb681c5: "Perhaps... Perhaps you're right. I don't know why exactly the half-blood's story moved me so. I should stop thinking about it and find something exciting to occupy myself with."
e0dd7cf8-43a3-4748-a17d-9e44d2eb5b27: "Can we really choose our own way? I don't know. I shall meditate upon this."
a145efc5-abaa-4fa9-9380-f7d86dd0e0d0: "I'm trying to imagine — what would my life be like, if I had a goal as decisive and inspiring as that? So many new thoughts, so many disturbing notions. At one time, my fear of losing my sense of novelty led me to kill. What will come next? It's impossible to predict."
de7412a0-c912-4f4f-80bf-6f795d66d2c8: "First of all, a new {d|Jaethal Reborn}body{/d} awaits me. It will take much time to prepare for the ritual, but then... three times a day I make a list of what I shall do, once I'm alive again. I'll not limit myself in any way — for at least ten years. It's sad, but after that, I shall have to turn my mind from the joys of life and give birth to a future vessel. Perhaps it is better to have several of them. It will be necessary to choose the father carefully, so that the vessel turns out to be beautiful. I've no wish to spend centuries in some ugly form."
746632dd-20d6-4798-919d-722eae64d870: "The Goddess has blessed me and made me stronger. That is why she requires {d|Jaethal Kills Daughter}sacrifices{/d}, right? She's waiting for me in her domain. Continuing my service, one day I may be awarded the title of Herald, the chosen one among chosen ones. But do not worry — I shall remain here until your affairs in the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g} are finished. I shall help you in everything. I can be grateful."
d8f3770b-10eb-4990-8718-45cc978c3654: "You must be wondering what the Goddess has awarded me with. It was promised to me that one day I shall go to the domain of {g|Urgathoa}Urgathoa{/g} to continue my service. If I continue to please my Goddess, someday I will be selected among the other chosen to be the Herald of her will. Until that time, I may live as I wish. Urgathoa bestowed a blessing upon me and breathed her power into me. Know this: until she calls me, I am at your disposal."
41b2cdba-0423-4a87-9f8d-0769380c7ae9: "This question is more complicated than it seems. An inquisitor is by nature the most zealous defender of their faith. — The hand of their Goddess in mundane affairs. When I received this title and power, I expected that {g|Urgathoa}Urgathoa{/g} would tell me my mission. But this never happened. The Goddess remains silent. There's only one reasonable explanation I can imagine: discovering what's expected of me is a part of my mission. So I reflect on this, make my prayers and wait for a sign."
8eee14bc-f7d4-4b9d-8b34-d23e229923b8: "Greetings!" {n}Something has subtly changed — either in Jaethal herself, or in her attitude towards you.{/n} "It's amazing how significantly our fates can change. Just yesterday I was lost, and hardly understood my own strength. I did not hear the voice the Goddess, and knew not the purpose of my un-life. Today I am triumphant. There is no longer any doubt, no burdensome connection with the past, and the road to a bright future lies before me. And it all happened thanks to you."
09d63da5-8e6d-4b85-83cc-cc7476280803: "From your question, I assume you're not from {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g}. Right?"
dc905a42-4156-4d63-bcfe-3cbee6dfcdcd: {n}Jaethal scoffs.{/n} "News! It's not about elves. Believe me, {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g} today is still the grim mix of ruin and splendor it has been for ages."
a4a88f32-905c-4f63-b9a8-e4d9a88a3655: "I'm afraid my story sounded too skeptical. You should definitely visit {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g}! Only there can you really understand what it means to be an elf — with all the benefits and vices that come with it."
6062b43e-caa1-4f32-9e0c-979d5f3ed305: "I hope I answered your question? I tried to tell you like I would tell an ordinary short-lived person who's never been to {g|Kyonin}Kyonin{/g}."
3c3a223a-c4d0-44be-b4d2-469b242d2d10: "Then you'll understand what I tell you next."
a99ef52e-d406-4b51-b2c0-f31311ea1736: "Truly. But what a paltry fate — to settle for what you have, not even trying to achieve more! That's exactly why I did what I did."
7139a6f5-d8e1-4939-aa46-13ee98e0fbc6: "Impossible is a word for those who are afraid of change," {n}Jaethal says firmly. Then she continues, softer,{/n} "But allow me to continue my story..."
e900a856-91bf-40fe-a34a-fc380c1dc4ec: "I like your optimism. But sadly, I look at things more pragmatically, and I'm not inclined to indulge in illusions about my kin or myself. We're all doomed to age mentally. But..."
6faed1ca-2c5d-4ea2-81bb-0aaef8ef9141: "Why do you ask? I know you pray to the Pallid Princess too... I must say, I'm glad. There aren't many countries whose leaders have the guts to accept her gifts!"
4ca58670-90d6-494e-87cf-9d5841f37b88: {g|Espionage6_4}[Choice effects]{/g} "Help Casal Tarne face his cousin."
a21efb31-c3c4-47f9-ae65-2f7203ac2eb9: {g|Espionage6_5}[Choice effects]{/g} "Dispatch soldiers to the Grey Gardeners."
e5ea73e6-5a76-4429-ae36-07ad8231bd0f: "We're fighting someone else's war. We aren't Gralton. We aren't Litran. We have no stake in this fight. Let us escape it before we're stabbed in the back. Petitioning for peace is an option, though unreliable. Let's distract them first."
30627b3e-f637-437d-9373-509139384037: "Look, {name}, we've suddenly stumbled into the middle of a fight between Litran and Gralton. I don't know who might benefit from this, but it's surely not us. It's time to figure out a way to extricate ourselves from the situation. I suggest we negotiate a peace treaty. However, if you're too proud for such a measure, I'll tell you a couple other options."
4b5ff133-0815-4d83-9ed2-ee8e26f4733d: "We are pulled deeper and deeper into Litran and Gralton's fight. This already drains our forces, and cannot end well. It's time we plan our escape from this situation – preferably something that casts us in a positive light. I can see two options."
4c8c4f7d-710e-4a7c-8fa2-ed50f3683716: {n}Ekun nods.{/n} "While the wolves fight in Gralton for dominance, we can disappear without a trace. And without any further losses."
6a771bb8-4979-449e-9a7c-a1a4c5c41b0d: "Hopefully, once this mob of aristocrats stops fighting, they won't remember what the whole thing started with..."
3233af64-a5ee-4123-9887-38f4ee2efdd9: "The short-lived are so easily manipulated. They're always seeking massacres, as if to make their lives even shorter. We'll just give them a little push, and they'll be trapped in bloody conflict!"
c135ee88-036a-4903-b522-569b1962ed67: "The Gardeners will strike Gralton with vicious force. The bloodshed will remind Gralton's people that there's a price for challenging us!"
87478d02-e71d-4590-913b-eee391ee0ca9: {n}Ekun nods.{/n} "A peaceful resolution is the best outcome."
9915c378-11b8-4058-91fb-9c0f8e59b081: "This is wise. I'll send ambassadors to Gralton. We must make peace – and then figure out how things could have gone so far! I suppose it would never have gone this far if I had a more flexible and less dignified ruler. But that's just an assumption."
33bcd6bc-854e-4563-a318-fd76ff9e4d0f: "Halidan Tarne is the commander of Gralton's army. He's the general that sending his raiders to {g|Galt}Galt{/g}. This commander is as bloodthirsty and narrow-minded as any other military man. His cousin, Casal, envies his relative but he's too cautious to disturb Gralton's fragile balance. But if you help Casal gain a piece of Halidan's power, they'll busy themselves with their own problems and leave us be."
b7eaea19-9da3-4e15-8239-2dfaa635c7a6: "On the other hand, we could involve Gralton in a fight with Litran. The Grey Gardeners' greatest strength is spywork and intelligence, and I respect their consistency and ferocity... But they need more soldiers. Real fighters. If we send them some experienced warriors, Gralton will focus all its time and energy on preventing Litran from crushing them. We ourselves cannot afford to make those arrogant fools from Gralton weep blood, but I'll enjoy watching the Grey Gardeners do it for us."
406ec3bd-fa35-4bc8-9047-3d11c71fcf56: "Officially, I must mention the third option. The Grey Gardeners. Good executioners, but poor soldiers. If we sent them more troops, Gralton would begin to smolder under the Gardeners' pressure. Although I don't think supporting these butchers is a good idea. So let's not discuss it further."
8b58f74e-692c-42fc-ba37-f3584e290a8b: "Gralton has many groups vying for power: the Wise, the Order of Vengeance, the Nameless, the Hand That Takes, the Directorate, and many other fancy names. There are also the people of Halidan Tarne, Casal Tarne... Speaking of which... they're cousins. The former is the army general, and the latter is the leader of the sentry guard. Halidan is a wild daredevil, while Casal is a careful fool. But Casal envies his cousin and his brave soldiers. If you help him take over something that belongs to Halidan, they'll busy themselves with their own problems and leave us be."
a55716dd-64ca-4334-997a-308ab0ca7a7d: "There's a good solution. Gralton is like a serpents' nest. Many squads, many commanders, all of them vying for power. If we aid the weak in taking something that belongs to a strong, the delicate balance will shift. They'll busy themselves with their own problems and leave us be. Casal Tarne, the head of the guards, is weaker than his cousin. Halidan Tarne, the army's commander, is the stronger of the two. Let us pit them against each other."
f4c39481-8608-4ad7-96c5-c62e1274af0c: "There's another solution, too, but it leads us down a dangerous path. We could aid the enemy of our enemy, the Grey Gardeners. They have punishers and spies, but few soldiers. If we send them more troops, the Gardeners will engage with Gralton. They'll keep themselves busy with their own problems and leave us be. But I would not advise interfering. They are cruel and know no mercy."
d21322bf-73b4-429a-a450-e093896a3e9d: "Hey, unknown voice — could you answer some questions?"
aa1ceb75-c6fb-4dbd-8e96-bf63af6e2cac: "Tell me, door, what's locked behind you?"
3967e3e2-5ddb-4d9e-aef6-1c819457980f: "Farnirras is imprisoned, Farnirras is the one who created you. Maybe you can explain what all this means?"
a86df8a4-ee56-4fa0-b219-e594036f4bc2: "It seems you're trying to hide something from me. This is no simple key, but a much more valuable artifact."
b99b2905-f3d2-4961-b649-797159462d0e: "Your 'key' is a lich's phylactery. What do you say to that?"
d4e9527b-f58e-4aff-a39d-8bf9cb301087: "The monsters and the key. The door will open to the strongest."
64b238e7-1813-4e96-a513-c88370d89522: {n}You plunge the key into the barrier and watch as waves of barely visible bluish light run up and down along it. It appears that a protective spell of some sort was hiding its true nature, but now it disappeared. An ethereal whisper comes from the door, and distinctly pronounces the word 'phylactery'. You barely have time consider its meaning when the key dissolves in the waves of blue light.{/n} "It's part of a plan. The imprisoned one can be free, but only by sacrificing the essence of his power."
a81abca2-6bda-48e1-afab-d502cd58a009: "The key is in your hands. Ages ago it was hidden in the dungeon, where two rivers flow into one lake. Ages later it was drawn into the light. Defeat the monsters, then give me the key — and the door will open to you."
4c245ad8-5f43-4687-af2d-5c0d0ae1b342: "The monsters are your trial. I will mark their lairs. Seek them out and defeat them. After all of them fall, the door will open to you."
c58ea025-3b73-4d3c-8fb5-cc75906ee023: {n}It seems that your attempt to plunge the key into the barrier is a waste of time. The shimmering surface is impenetrable.{/n} "The monsters are not defeated. Defeat the monsters and return with the key."
be66877f-4801-4d52-bae2-1a130bce6b99: "It is kept in the dungeon beneath the well. The city grows above it, the lake splashing its waves abreast. You came from the city. Bring the key from the dungeon. Defeat the monsters. The door will open to the strongest."
29c9fc50-392b-481d-b9c9-c1647020877e: {n}Silence falls for some time, and then the monotonous whispering resumes:{/n} "The door will open to the strongest. Defeat the monsters. The door will open to the strongest."
4007c2b4-0ae7-4f9b-873d-8f9501a8ee70: {n}As you approach, the barrier utters a deep sigh.{/n} "The monsters are defeated. The trial is passed. The door will open to the strongest. The door will open to you. Will open..."
4be5533f-b80d-4936-8cae-78f673b95ac8: {n}The barrier feels slightly warm and somehow alive to the touch. Odd patterns and magical symbols glimpse on its shimmering surface. Among them you notice numerous pictures of various animals, monsters, and unusual creatures.{/n}
3fe7d2eb-532c-4b6d-a233-e1e64997a0c4: "The key is delivered and destroyed. The monsters are defeated. The door opens to the strongest. Enter now!"
27d76992-9341-4b20-9f5c-406978279ab4: {n}The glow of the barrier is much more intense. Its surface is like a sun-warmed stone.{/n} "The blood of the monsters is on your hands. The door will open to the strongest."
8b4985d0-5bb0-412d-bbab-e59851aa5dfa: {n}It seems the barrier has changed since you were last here. Now it's enveloped in a barely visible glow, and the whispers have grown louder.{/n} "The door will open to the strongest. Defeat the monsters."
eadd44a3-b8cf-4b80-863e-518d474e9f5a: {n}The barrier glows, and radiates a strong heat.{/n} "You near your goal. The door will open to the strongest!"
d28405d1-ad9a-453b-a2cb-e2a28f8591f7: {n}The monotonous voice keeps repeating:{/n} "Will open to the strongest… Only to the strongest…"
db859924-7df0-48b5-979d-640b0e94a65e: {n}The whispering subsides for a moment, and then resumes with a different, intense intonation:{/n} "Yes. The key is more than just a key. It is a gage. It is part of a plan. The imprisoned one can only become free by sacrificing the essence of his power."
eb65c971-61b1-4a01-ab36-532d6569ad7d: "Your goal is near. The trial is coming to an end. Defeat your final enemies and the door will open to you."
7bdf5243-3504-44bb-a4c4-5129e558781d: "The monsters were the trial, and the trial has been passed. The door will open to you."
95900811-80b3-4d7f-8407-78d3f2986962: "You have vanquished many, but more yet must be defeated. The trial is not yet passed."
0e18c771-029a-495f-91ad-63081f2de8a0: "You have already met them. But more of them must be defeated, many more. The trial is not yet passed."
0c02ae02-9965-47b7-9755-80f6662f9c7b: {n}The closer you get to the magic barrier, the louder a whisper, just on the verge of hearing, becomes. It says over and over,{/n} "The door will open to the strongest. Defeat the monsters. Get the key from the dungeon. The key is hidden between two rivers falling into the same lake, on its shore. Find it and come. The door will open to the strongest..."
545106bf-1939-4952-8567-0196046b499c: "If this life troubles you, something should be changed. Your family and friends want you happy, not exhausted and hating your existence."
fcce1f9b-3062-4d2a-8c2d-3db2789e8cb0: [Offer 3000 gold coins to Luna] "Here, take it. You can spend it on traveling and seeing the world. – Together with your love if she agrees."
797c81c2-194f-4bbb-bc2b-7ef7ae3023dc: {n}A girl with unusual silver-gray hair is looking gloomily into her mug of ale. As she notices Jubilost clearing his throat, she raises her face and brightens.{/n} "Oh, they told me that the {mf|King|Queen} of {kingdomname} walks the streets, and feasts with everyone at the taverns – but I never believed it! Oh, forgive me, Your Highness. I am Luna Kettari."
eed950b0-9d5b-4fa8-a88e-1213d2a2fb41: "I am a messenger. I deliver correspondence from {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g} to {g|Mivon}Mivon{/g} and back, usually reports about a rich merchant's underlings and his orders for them. My parents live in Brevoy, and the girl I love, in Mivon…"
33f8e9ed-34c7-4e46-9979-35eaee6d57e3: "I've always dreamed of becoming a traveler, but that's not easy for the daughter of a weaver and a washerwoman. I was glad to find this messenger job, though. I thought that was pretty lucky. But now I'm traveling the same road over and over, every month. I even sit right here in your tavern on the twenty fourth of every month, right on schedule. The monotony is driving me to tears, but what can I do? I can't be everywhere at once, and I can't stand the thought of settling down..."
76529f62-64d6-4f36-bc20-f8aa5a4aa405: {n}Jubilost, who was listening surprisingly carefully, leans over to you and says quietly,{/n} "Do you see it now? 'When Moon leaves her path' – it's another part of the riddle! It looks we need to somehow convince our new friend to quit her well-trodden path and set off somewhere new. Plus, it would be good for her. The same road each month! If I were her, I'd have drowned myself a long time ago. If I didn't Bleach sooner."
c07a9f3c-ad5c-4bb5-91df-45bf4969f73a: "You speak with such confidence! Is it true you came to {g|Stolen Lands}the Stolen Lands{/g} as no one, and made yourself {mf|king|queen} by your own persistence and skill? I've heard so many stories! Your Highness, I wouldn't have taken this advice from anyone but you... but I've just decided – I'm going to travel! And I hope not alone... we'll surely be able to earn a piece of bread together."
d2f2cd20-8701-4240-abf2-679c7fa4a057: "I know. But it's easy to know. It's much harder to actually do something about it. Especially when you've got to think about how to earn a crust." {n}Luna grows sad.{/n}
5cc69eab-22ba-45ce-be6d-9ae2f45d38f8: {n}The girl looks at the coins in disbelief.{/n} "But this is... a very large sum! Of course, you're the {mf|King|Queen}, but you barely know me..."
4b4c2461-d7b0-44e4-bfdf-78b11176be1c: "Take it, take it," {n}says Jubilost protectively.{/n} "Believe me, traveling is contagious. You take one small step from your house, and you'll never be able to stop. The world is beautiful, especially when you're not discovering it alone... not that I myself ever... hmm, hmm..." {n}Jubilost stammers and pretends that he needs to wipe his glasses.{/n} "I'll leave you one of my latest almanacs – to help you find your way around at the start."
3900f9dc-babc-47d9-a766-7a213ed20d25: "You have my best! It was a pleasure talking to a real {mf|king|queen}!"
1aa05af2-27ad-4eb8-bf67-6b368773116f: "Thank you! Thank you, thank you! Oh, I don't even know how to repay you! But on the other hand... Maybe I do!" {n}Luna searches her bag quickly.{/n}
e34a981c-57ff-449c-86bc-4f71d2d97eb3: "Please, take this. It's a relic my family received from an elven ancestor. According to the family legend, the one who deciphers the map will find three things: an incredibly sad secret, a true treasure, and a door to another world which will never open again. The entrance to a certain dungeon is marked here, but there's nothing to say where to go looking. You're a {mf|king|queen}, with all the best scientists and travelers serving you. Surely they'll be able to read this map. Thank you again. Now I have to go!"
6d62eff5-a4a3-43e4-bc1c-faa3364fb3a7: "Ha! Moon has left her path! But now who can explain to me why the Host didn't simply tell us, 'go to the dungeon located here'? Why make us run around in circles? But let's have a look at this map... what do we have here... Why, I recognize the area around the {g|Candlemere}Candlemere{/g} at first glance! There are ancient ruins in this area. This dungeon must contain the traces of the very first gnomes to visit {g|Golarion}Golarion{/g}. Well, our goal is clear. Now we need only achieve it!"
cf438c85-3418-4277-bfb4-687609c343b1: "I was born with bright silver hair. The midwives never saw an aasimar before, they were frightened, but my mother – not a bit. She said her daughter's hair was silver like the moon, which meant I was blessed by {g|Desna}Desna{/g}. Hence the name. Actually I've always been drawn to faraway countries, like anyone touched by the Moon goddess, but I've never been beyond {g|River Kingdoms}the River Kingdoms{/g}..." {n}Luna sighs.{/n}
9c38f914-2cdb-4eb5-bcbd-c99cb4bb59e3: "Looks like that's our Moon. I'd like to know what 'leaving her path' means to her. And more importantly – how all this is related to the story of the gnomes! I hope we're about to find out..." {n}Jubilost clears his throat to attract her attention.{/n}
892052a8-25b1-4637-9b58-786d24d2c8dd: "Amiri, why don't you wear serious armor? Your entire body is covered in scars!"
214eaae4-8d10-4c4c-bb47-acd78863ec3d: "So what? I'm a barbarian, not some princess. It's like that with us: the more scars, the better!"
a37cdb1c-ac66-4060-8a77-190eb668bd1f: {g|Divine7_4}[Choice effects]{/g} "We shall allow the servants of Asmodeus to set up a temple, regardless of our neighbors' opinion."
664df44e-311a-4caa-a6aa-1b215082acfe: "Why don't you suggest a temple to your own god?"
84bd1463-3ac3-4c61-9dbd-7f707308226c: {g|Divine7_3}[Choice effects]{/g} "I will allow Abadar's followers to erect a temple in his honor."
8552b9bb-69b5-459a-84c6-f09b12f625a4: "Your Highness! The fame of our domain is increasing. Many priests look to erect their temples in the capital. The competition has stirred up no little tension, and even some arguments!"
805412c4-c92e-4cfc-a3b2-091055025d58: "{name}, the chronicles will remember you as a great {mf|king|queen}, not a mere {mf|baron|baroness}. But even if you were an {mf|Emperor|Empress}, you would still be wise to seek divine support. Four influential priests have arrived at your court to plead for a temple honoring their gods."
527dd69c-253a-42da-a7ec-9972e5af484b: "Your kingdom grows more famous by the hour, and many hope to take advantage of this. Four gods are keen to lay their hands upon your domain – or to grant you their patronage, to be precise. Priests of {g|Cayden Cailean}Cayden{/g}, {g|Abadar}Abadar{/g}, {g|Gorum}Gorum{/g}, and {g|Asmodeus}Asmodeus{/g} have each offered to build temples in the capital."
6c907604-4922-4e79-9cbd-ac3d21657a25: "A little feasting and fun won't hurt this kingdom and its citizens."
58cce624-2639-4f2a-855d-fc4079d25191: "The Drunken Hero? The one who hopes to drink himself into oblivion rather than face the inevitable end that comes even for him? I disapprove of your decision, but I will not oppose you on this."
98b84723-26f8-44bf-b9e4-9706d1cf9568: "{g|Cayden Cailean}Cayden{/g} may not be the worst option. Drunk people cast off the shackles of decency and turn into primal beasts."
d0507f97-22bc-493d-9843-ba4e55094b8d: "Are you certain that we need even more war and bloodshed? I'm afraid {g|Gorum}Gorum{/g} does not promise security to our kingdom. On the contrary, he will involve it in ever more battles."
f208e48c-abd9-46a4-be76-dbe6ed49e469: "I hope you will find satisfaction in his unforgiving patronage. He determines the end that comes for us all... and even for he himself."
4cdbabe6-418a-472e-96e7-5327afc94d51: "{g|Gorum}Gorum{/g} is ill-bred and cruel, but he's good in battle. At least our enemies' swords will drink the blood of his followers, and not my pack."
18ace146-14e8-4a6b-a282-5e931b09fc14: "Summoning the god of law and tyranny to lands that have hosted chaos for centuries... This is either very wise or very foolish."
65b53b73-bf41-4313-9dce-9211001b628b: "An ambitious decision. A deal with {g|Asmodeus}Asmodeus{/g} promises profit. But you must read the contract very carefully..."
2a818a42-6bf9-4cf8-a37d-594cf23e29a5: "Why would I? Take a look around. This land is covered in forests. There are plenty of deer in the thickets. Wildlife thrives in healthy lands, and its people are decent and honest. This land is already under {g|Erastil}Erastil's{/g} protection. Why would we need another temple?"
bf833214-2096-4580-a82e-efbf5d8b48d8: "But why would I? All temples will eventually be destroyed. All of {g|Groetus}Groetus'{/g} priests will turn to dust, like the priests of every other god. There are few who can hear his whispers, and we are satisfied with ruined temples to other gods..."
fa63fabb-6f1d-4066-82a9-63c06189496a: "So I could start looking for another refuge? As soon as {g|Lamashtu}Lamashtu{/g} became patron of these lands, some righteous paladin would be placed on your throne by common consent, while your head would be placed on the tip of his lance. No, the time has not come. Yet."
b6dac667-3c05-497a-b679-1cc30588507a: "It is no coincidence that {g|Cayden Cailean}Cayden's{/g} nickname is the Accidental God. He was a mortal, a deathly drunk mortal, when he became a god. He doesn't even remember how it happened. Under Cayden, your subjects will live happily but senselessly, spending their time in feasts and fairs."
e05c4fd8-9455-47b7-81dc-0dd780adf3f5: "{g|Cayden Cailean}Cayden{/g} loves freedom and the simple pleasures of life. People feel at ease with him. They drink, have fun, and live an easy life. He promotes feasts, fairs – and brewing!"
148e93f1-c7cf-4752-a996-f5f36b3908f1: "{g|Cayden Cailean}Cayden{/g} is the Accidental God. He loves everyone having fun, and no one troubling anyone else. It sounds nice, but would you really want your subjects always drunk, like their god?"
35551ebd-682b-4666-b5ea-efde9650f703: "Then let {g|Abadar}Abadar{/g} ensure your people are civilized and prosperous."
566e3974-7d44-437c-837e-abc04c4675aa: "Let {g|Gorum}Gorum{/g} carve his path of destruction through your city gates, {name}. Why postpone the inevitable?"
09a3442f-e6f3-44c9-a060-1ab245d3bd4f: "I will make arrangements with the priest of {g|Gorum}Gorum{/g}. Let your neighbors learn to accept that these are free lands, where we may worship any god we choose, even one known to be 'violent' and 'dark'."
5bf68c7f-861e-4229-bfad-b16f7440bcc5: "Each of them wants their god to win new followers in a young and strong kingdom. But they won't tolerate any rivals. Gods hate to share. Thus you must select only one god. I'd place my bet on {g|Gorum}Gorum{/g}. {g|Cayden Cailean}Cayden{/g} is an unreliable drunkard. {g|Abadar}Abadar{/g} and {g|Asmodeus}Asmodeus{/g} are alien to me by nature."
383bef44-82a0-46ad-95e8-c88addb1f3c9: "Each wishes your kingdom to prosper under the blessings of their god. We must choose between {g|Cayden Cailean}Cayden{/g}, {g|Abadar}Abadar{/g}, {g|Gorum}Gorum{/g}, and {g|Asmodeus}Asmodeus{/g}. I advise you to consider Gorum. His road to the end of things is at least simple and direct."
3755d7ab-df00-4215-9e14-0165f0476a0f: "We must opt for one of the great gods, thus winning the hearts of his many followers. The most influential priests are those of {g|Cayden Cailean}Cayden{/g}, {g|Gorum}Gorum{/g}, {g|Abadar}Abadar{/g}, and {g|Asmodeus}Asmodeus{/g}. My advice is that you take a closer look at Abadar."
84d5cf4c-95ea-4901-a3ca-6e039a692297: "{g|Gorum}Gorum{/g} is the dark patron of battle, the master of violence, bold and merciless. His followers believe only in power. They are soldiers, barbarians, mercenaries – and murderers."
a2391469-2f68-4040-b3aa-2be9e467b254: "{g|Asmodeus}Asmodeus{/g} is the strongest of the archdevils. {g|Cheliax}Cheliax{/g}, a powerful kingdom, has long prospered under his patronage. He believes in discipline and obedience, and the right of the strong to rule the weak. I wouldn't advise getting involved with him. Our neighbors will turn against us, and his patronage will bring down a curse on us."
aba8fdcd-c469-4989-bbc9-7ccc1ea6a3ed: "{g|Gorum}Gorum{/g} is a cruel and bloodthirsty warrior, as are his followers. He is the god of war. He is worshipped by orcs and barbarians, but he has quite a few followers among the civilized as well."
83efdb84-db40-4560-b39b-d49d54129bf6: "{g|Asmodeus}Asmodeus{/g} is the lord of {g|Hell}Hell{/g}. He's the archdevil worshipped by the powerful state of {g|Cheliax}Cheliax{/g}. Asmodeus believes in power, compacts, order, and the obedience of the inferior. He's crafty but not deceitful. You should read the contract very carefully, if you choose him."
17c73d62-7a74-46cc-824a-66e3272442a9: "{g|Asmodeus}Asmodeus{/g} is the archdevil, the lord of {g|Hell}Hell{/g}. {g|Cheliax}Cheliax{/g} made a deal with him – and benefitted greatly from it! It is now a great country which no one wants to fight with. For Asmodeus, order and discipline are absolute. He trusts in the right of the strong, the obedience of the weak, the power of compacts, and the impotence of reliance. It would be a profitable deal – which our neighbors would hate."
f7c23174-122b-4f7f-8f19-d2e1a2533d4d: "{g|Gorum}Gorum{/g} is the god of war, soldiers and assassins. He's arrogant and merciless. His followers are great warriors that would come in handy."
79e9c689-e224-42cc-8873-9dbe0e3215be: "{g|Abadar}Abadar{/g} is the god of cities and laws, merchants and trade. All he cares about is law and order. It wouldn't be an easy life for his followers in the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g}, but his patronage might make your citizens a bit more obedient!"
995baec0-b184-4a5f-9276-df3b6e3adb41: "{g|Abadar}Abadar{/g} is the patron of cities and trade. He is there, where civilization flourishes, and he detests chaos and destruction. I'm not sure if his followers will survive well here, in these wild and untamed lands."
960689de-3713-4c4a-a9f0-846c1a0e962b: "{g|Abadar}Abadar{/g} is the god of cities and civilization... which I hate by my nature. {g|Asmodeus}Asmodeus{/g} is the archdevil, the lord of {g|Hell}Hell{/g}. He trusts in the right of the strong, obedience of the weak, the power of agreement, and the impotence of reliance. If you decide to turn to one of these two gods, beware! They might strangle your {mf|barony|barony|kingdom|kingdom} and you with the infinite bonds of legislation.
e98d1976-5f58-4d57-8e70-50d37c67e089: "This is a wise decision, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. {g|Abadar}Abadar{/g} doesn't have too many enemies. No one will be sorely disappointed with your decision."
9a7e1f9e-372d-4044-8547-c3a1c974410f: "Once I return to Numeria... I don't know what I'll do there. Maybe I'll find my former owners and grind them to dust. Or maybe just walk the streets as a free person!"
2a669a0b-d1f6-4f9f-b750-e1f31e40f1ff: "I just need to get back and close that chapter of my life."
4e753319-4690-4bef-b8b9-36812e71d49b: [Attack] "You'll be dead before you know it."
d8ab72dc-1dc0-4fba-b8e0-16cb434d4082: [Leave] "Go on then, get out of my sight."
b9add543-0391-416c-8c62-b21de48e8ca9:
"Owwchh! Heh-heee... can't believe it, {mf|he|she} passed all the traps..." {n}The goblin taps his fingers together, as if it helps him think — beads of sweat are forming on his brow.{/n} "What I do now, do now, do... ahhh, I do know, I do!"
{n}The goblin raises his hands, as if welcoming you.{/n} "Gratulations, 'shanks! You passed my firstest test! And for that..." {n}He begins drumming his fingers again, and a bead of sweat builds, one becoming so large it begins to curl his ear down.{/n} "... for that you get a gift! Wait here, wait here, I bring it right away... I be back before you know it..." {n}The goblin begins backing away, wiping his shaky hands over his rags.{/n}
958ab068-1396-4701-9958-fe22b648e6ed: {n}Having backed away to what he deems far enough, the goblin raises four fingers defiantly and spits at you, then scampers off in a run, giggling to itself.{/n}
bc726f7a-db61-43af-8469-e8d622dd1d6d: "Little pest! I'll cut you in half!"
e3a7b5eb-dd27-4bcc-8cc5-0011f5ecc5f2: {n}Jaethal reaches for her weapon.{/n} "Had your fun yet? Because it's my turn now."
57bb8bd4-1bcf-457a-81df-86d6ce17209b: Frowned, bared {mf|his|her} weapons, and charged into battle.
d3968fa7-e339-42e8-beff-8554f03cebf5: Smiled, muttered "why not," and took a place near the fire.
7d2a3f59-1085-4114-87f6-8364ae6541cc: Spat on the ground and moved on.
e249f2fa-fe6a-47ab-8a1e-30f82966f203: Bravely filled the keg from the barrel.
0356b0a0-5134-4515-a23a-db93fd6daf1d: Drained the first keg to its dregs.
a0f2b756-6758-47ca-b5af-d124a5f33d31: Was already going to sip, but smelled the ale, shook {mf|his|her} head, and poured the beverage back in the barrel.
066a15e8-1b15-4716-9df6-e6809ddd4b7e: "I'm too tired to sing. You sing, I'll listen."
9ca7cf23-2f64-4779-b0cb-85e7cbfe4b54: And pass all your stupid tests.
1706da31-e482-400a-b653-0dc9320bb068: Get away from me, you pest!
8f196100-b641-462a-93b8-890af66423cd: Um, do I really have to rhyme here?
473c5ecb-44f3-4caf-8b38-d7b75189b557: Is to kill! And kill! And kill!
10d0b3d9-9e11-46ba-93f5-2b40f9217d3b: Is that his belly's hard to fill.
426390e5-115b-4896-a1e7-5c1c3482fcdc: Hey, you, I want my mug refill!
335b7a4a-82fc-42ad-bf11-66bf0ab19889: Scream like hell and run away!
37525d51-2867-41e7-b8f4-762e8d8899a0: Kiss your life farewell and pray.
c82dbf09-8c35-4108-b1f4-5cef8e0c95e2: Tell him you wants to parley!
12e0232f-bc5a-4947-80d1-7e147e99334f: So, a toast to Goblin King!
b1f46a8d-9042-4627-95ca-c39d141cffcb: We stay here till next spring!
49469b49-168a-4484-8eb9-7aa8b7906aec: By the way, your ale stinks.
cf0c20a0-68f1-42fc-9c38-4cc96fa98a24: And pull each other's nose rings, ha ha.
adb36e2c-fd2c-4967-b164-c99e74f24d23: And your belly will stay fulls.
f9813729-93ce-4c11-9b3c-399edacd61cb: To be smarts and no fools.
ec9def18-1aa1-4754-9ad7-3d7d235e488f: Also, learn to wipe your drools.
94de0461-8f47-415e-b04e-a62c451e3558: Pass me another keg, would you?
82104124-7799-49e9-ab70-6e77da5f62e3: Ugh. To annoy people, I guess?
843395ea-9170-4db0-bbdb-693c784a0a7a: Kicked the dog and took the plate.
d2e9a547-2cb1-46d4-9c89-4f7937a52c04: Answered that {mf|he|she} didn't feel like it.
cde1cacd-c134-466b-b9ed-d40c17e92f42: Snuck up to the plate to snatch it from under the hound's nose.
8d216bd3-12f3-4ffa-aefa-bd75af7e2cf4: Took the plate, ignoring the dog completely.

46391190-43f3-422f-9f59-6d5d8714851e: {n}The woman nods lifelessly.{/n} "I'm not surprised. The servants of {g|Pharasma}Pharasma{/g} have chased me for nearly forty years. My name is Taneka. What do you want to know?"
0a0b237a-8e79-4ce8-8723-049977125e3d: {n}The old woman shudders and stares at you.{/n}
7b8e61b8-8bf2-40f1-9125-7df1d7149512: "There can be no other time, my life is nearing its end..." {n}Taneka whispers and lowers her head.{/n}
e5a63618-3cb0-4c5b-b3b5-5dfe023ca3ff: "How could I not recognize the one chosen by the goddess? Her power in you shines like the full moon on a black velvet sky. I know that she can do many things – including sharing her gift with others."

532aec9e-a3e6-4fc9-94a6-9b81db0c3290: "This... this cannot be explained in one breath. Long ago, I was a powerful priestess of {g|Urgathoa}Urgathoa{/g}, the leader of a secret coven. f01a9c4f-a982-4195-9d12-97aa44be0a14: "But I was naive and overconfident of my power. I met an enemy who destroyed me and all my hopes of a second youth. 0e611ec7-cf7f-4948-846e-04097ee9e317: "Everyone died that evening – except the two of us. But no matter how self-confident the young inquisitor was, he could not defeat me. 9c0e4099-d555-49e2-89ca-73cb9d2c38cb: "Were his mocking words a curse or just a guess? I do not know, but they bore the fruit of truth. 'No way out'... My coven died, and my secrets were revealed. c1b308ff-0bf3-4636-b3eb-a5101f1e9e74: {n}Nok-Nok turns to you.{/n} "Big Hero Nok-Nok take care of them. All good."
2d63b823-264d-42fc-aff5-f830b7f82aeb: {n}Nok-Nok pauses, as if he's forgotten what happened a few moments ago – and you realize he has.{/n} "Capital big enough. Yes, Capital!" {n}Before you can stop him, he turns to the goblins.{/n} "All, you, go to capital, Nok-Nok command you, GO!"
fb1d6299-d961-40df-a15e-7c5f9adba9dc: {n}Nok-Nok pauses, then nods.{/n} "Capital not bad idea. All, you, go to capital, Nok-Nok command you, GO!"
5c555268-4499-4a23-9efb-732a4bff2eca: {n}To your horror, the goblins scamper away, running in all directions... but toward the direction of the your capital city.{/n}
5959ef99-d60f-402c-8a2b-7f1dd3c4bcee: "Oh my. Just..." {n}Jubilost stands with his mouth open for a few moments, obviously at a loss for words, then sighs with a defeated look on his face.{/n} "Oh my."
020cbbe6-e968-4d03-a99b-0ca810cdbea6: "The end of your {mf|barony|barony|kingdom|kingdom} just drew closer. Much closer."
db1b92a4-4961-493c-92ea-d8bd1a9c13ac: "Lại thêm mấy cục cưng xanh lè? Hay đấy! Và tất cả các người nên thôi quát mắng Nok-Nok đi! – Không thấy hắn cố gắng làm một cố vấn tốt đến thế nào sao?!"
374e7673-21cf-4ecf-923f-b25f47c9252c: {g|Divine2_1}[Choice effects]{/g} "Grind these strange idols to dust. I've no wish to see strange shrines in the area."
f16147e4-498c-42a9-9b87-5fe6cd7fcfe5: {g|Divine2_2}[Choice effects]{/g} "Leave the idols where they stand. Someone worships them, and we've no right to interfere."
45d92f22-35f6-4549-80ea-942fc2524cef: "I bear bad news, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. A number of foul idols have been seen around your new capital! They don't belong to any god known to me, and strange loners seem drawn to them – which only gives me greater concern."
52ecc344-b7f0-4903-b7ca-2aa681e2f790: "I suggest we tear them down and be done with it. Who know what evil still lingers in the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g} from the old times. In any case, they certainly don't belong here!"
1fc42a22-35e4-4853-bfb8-5420e17838f4: {n}Harrim mumbles to himself, pulling on his beard. Finally he notices you.{/n} "{name}! Allow me to speak for those who cannot protect themselves and their faith! The priests of {g|Erastil}Erastil{/g}, and the priests of the other gods – they've all turned against the ancient faiths that once flourished in the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g}, now long since passed into eternity. Their final traces are the ancient shrines and idols, which lay hid among the swamps and woods, symbols of transience and decay..."
1c6b564b-c58e-4cd8-8283-5c95660deabf: "{name}, your pack trembles in fear. Foul idols circle around your capital. Rumor has it they've been here forever, but the smell of blood upon them is still hot and sweet. Strange looking lights have been seen around one such idol. These remnants of ancient cults frighten your people, who clamor to demolish and burn them down."
a33d6303-6719-4f75-b022-f1bb7955f012: "But I would not, if I were you. Believe me, dead gods know how to leave nasty gifts for those who would destroying their last vestiges."
ff21c7e2-8ec5-468f-b432-36585adc4952: "Very well! I shall ensure that nothing remains of them, rest assured!"
2976b70f-addf-4e38-801c-1ad4323a4114: {n}Harrim sighs hopelessly.{/n} "Another shadow of the past, to dissolve before its proper time. It is a pity."
f08c0091-1fc1-4fef-a796-63f53b75bc11: "They do seem dangerous, yet my throat chokes when I hear you order them demolished. As does yours, I'm sure. Do you truly prefer to ignore their power, even as your every instinct cries out – 'Run!' Are you sure that this is wise?"
cf1f4143-8ee9-47a8-876a-cb91217faa42: {n}Jhod sniffs.{/n} "You're making a mistake! What if something hideous crawls out from under them? Some daemon or worse... You are simply too kind, {mf|Your Grace|Your Grace|Your Highness|Your Highness}. Too kind, and not firm enough!"
5e2d12ee-0bfa-42a5-85d8-70eaa5c6b362: {n}Harrim nods gravely.{/n} "That is the right decision, {name}."
249d9936-ecf9-4107-ad71-8e30a6b29cfb: "Most reasonable. You should not seek to awaken whatever lies there, sound asleep. It may have teeth sharper than yours."
a0981828-740d-4868-b421-df8533e85082: "Then it's time to send for our workers, and remove every trace of this heresy."
9ddea267-e8d5-4239-a920-16a13689a7ee: "I will preserve the shrines. May your subjects remember that this is the future of every faith."
b2af59c9-2c9e-41eb-9e69-fd0331fb4829: "I shall forbid anyone to engage with these idols. Who knows what strange darkness sleeps beneath them."
daacedca-3645-4a9b-8a13-6f99df7b5de7: "I've never understood what drives fools to collect ancient trinkets, things belonging to cyclopes and such. An entertainment to those whose hearts pump sweetened milk instead of blood."
4f68cb9c-4c7f-43e5-bf1c-0696d2da0b50: "I think it's exciting — the traces of creatures who roamed these same lands, under the same sun, thousands of years ago! How did they live? What became of them? How did their cities fall to ruin?"
cc1c1a5b-9e5d-454d-8d44-2a4b3cdf2071: "I have unraveled the secret of your magical powers! There are two stones in your head, constantly striking each other, trying to spawn a single thought. But instead they just make the sparks you emit from your fingers."
4aeb645e-498d-4d34-9b81-23d49749acd9: "The ruins of the ancients are pleasant to the eye, Regongar, for they remind us of the frailty of life. Those who left them are gone, and now we follow in their footsteps. Listen to the silence that remains — does it not fill your spirit with calm?"
7aab7050-a660-4106-850c-333e1c6ca90b: "What is it? I wasn't expecting guests..." {n}A woman comes out of the back rooms in a dress that was once expensive but is now moth-eaten and heavily mended. Her posture and gait give away a noble upbringing. She seems to be in her forties, though some pain or suffering must have worn her beyond her years, leaving wrinkles across her face and gray in her hair.{/n}
0d2eb422-cecf-41aa-ba42-5ecf13d94788: "I am Marchioness Clarida Della Fiorni. Welcome to my manor. I'm afraid I have nothing to offer you, nor do I have the honor of knowing you. To what do I owe the pleasure?"
059d07d8-b839-4cc0-852f-ae844b52ff64: "Oct... Octavia? Gods... My Octavia, is it really you? It's been so many years..." {n}The marchioness steps forward to hug her daughter, tears in her eyes, but she stops when she sees Octavia's stony gaze.{/n}
df62b4d7-8dc0-4d70-a6c8-0ca70ba8919f: "Your Octavia? Your?! My last memory of you is selling me to the slave traders! And you dare to call me yours?"
30ff9b5a-08fa-498a-88ae-bee56989bd5b: "Cruel words... but fair. Octavia, my child... let me tell you what happened. Afterward... you may decide on your own what to do — even if it means you never wish to see me again. All I need to be happy is to know you are safe and sound."
040d6d9a-a052-43cb-bd74-0607f18e4bb5: "A pathetic wretch, and nothing more. A visiting elf swept a silly young girl off her feet, then vanished as soon as he learned she was expecting. I care not to even say his name."
d6b6da48-6ac6-4325-a1a6-18ee2e1bf0e9: "Well, he at least made one good thing in his life, right?"
5e0956ec-0ed4-44f0-bf9d-a45be0bb58f7: "There are potions for those who don't wish to have children. They aren't expensive." {n}Octavia's voice is sharp and cold.{/n}
866311cd-9dda-474f-b36e-3160db0e11c3: "And what would I have done then? What would I do without you?"
0fa60ca9-3054-417f-93dc-bfeca72a7f4a: "My father, may his soul rest in peace, was a very stern man — some would say cruel. When he found out I was expecting the child of some adventurer, he expelled me from the house and cut me off from any inheritance. I scraped by on my own for three years — sewing, teaching, and the like... But then father discovered he was dying, and the Della Fiorni line would end. So he told me he would leave the full inheritance to me if I would only get rid of 'my disgrace' — get rid of you."
d3da2dee-5c80-4b92-9300-247c952fd528: "And so you did. Traded me for an inheritance. I see."
4259f8fd-35d8-4faf-b031-d23166d62655: "No, it wasn't like that at all! I... I had a plan... to deceive him, you know? I made arrangements with a man from the {g|Technic League}Technic League{/g}. He was supposed to take you to {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g}, keep you there until my father died, and then bring you back! I was trying to do what I thought was best for you, do you understand? I wanted you to grow up in your own manor, in luxury rather than poverty... But, once father was gone, the man from the Technic League said he didn't remember any such arrangements. He said he bought you, had already sold you, and had no idea where you were anymore."
a5bc6e2f-b092-496a-a6cd-e34633fbb213: "Nobility, to be sure..." {n}Regongar spits on the clean floor.{/n}
24cad268-f48b-4029-be72-0ffd56c6b439: "I had no idea where she was! Octavia, believe me, I continued to look for you all these years. I spent all of the inheritance hiring sleuths and investigators to scour {g|Numeria}Numeria{/g} and the {g|River Kingdoms}River Kingdoms{/g} for you! But you were nowhere to be found..."
66034585-7746-43ae-869a-f4d5afe758ce: {n}The marchioness wipes tears from her eyes.{/n} "I knew you were still alive. I could feel it. And I never stopped searching. I just wanted to see you again, just once... to at least beg your forgiveness."
8e34efe6-c778-40af-a844-dfaa6190c530: "What is there to say...? Mother, you're such a fool!"
6a611adc-eb8a-47a9-ba4a-93d621efd782: "I say I can't understand how this woman has the nerve to snivel and play the innocent victim. Quit the drama, mommy dear — you seem to have lived well enough all these years. You used me like a chip at the gambling house, and you lost! And once you changed your mind and tried to get me back, it was too late — well, too bad! Am I supposed to feel sorry for you?"
6eaf2c04-bcd0-467a-8098-c8574a18d1bc: "No, my child! I... I was young and stupid. I thought I could make a better life for you! I never needed the title, or even this town house..."
0d3d0998-8502-412e-9240-34d6442d4eac: "You didn't, did you? Is that so? Well, then, let me spare you of it!" {n}A smirk disfigures Octavia's face — or maybe rather a grimace of pain. She tears an oil lamp from the wall and hurls it to the floor.{/n}
62c62015-d5e0-4ecc-b82c-6897bb3beb80: {n}Octavia sobs.{/n} "You think we wouldn't have done fine without a title? I'd have grown up, learned some craft... We'd have been poor, probably, but at least we'd have been together..."
6209b726-db79-4a87-993f-25f3da594522: {n}The marchioness and Octavia hold each other tight.{/n} "Will you stay? At least for a little while? There's so much to talk about..."
8fc74576-54cf-4461-8162-6dd21420ff92: "Isn't it dangerous for you here, though, with just a couple of servants? There's a lot of disquiet in {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g} right now, and trouble all around. Magical beasts, barbarians... I live in {kingdomname} now — have you heard of it? It's recently established. Maybe you can move there. I'll be able to tell you what I've been doing all this time, and show you all that I've achieved!"
27c19421-ad88-4f94-93b8-ec38df7a58cc: "{kingdomname}? As you say, my child. I'll begin packing immediately."
d2cdb3ac-7e8c-456a-a540-65e4aaff38c3: {n}Octavia hugs her mother again.{/n} "I'll be waiting for you."
e3f769db-6b7d-42f1-9633-1a7f395ec529: "Those scouts must have had a great feast to your health, but without moving a finger! How naive to pay for such 'services' upfront!"
56f61eca-782f-477c-bf16-ce86b767c513: "Theo những gì ta thấy, không một ai trong gia đình này có khả năng suy nghĩ thấu đáo về hậu quả việc mình làm!"
0aae1535-91ff-4584-8462-826046b32b28: "I see. Let's discuss something other than your past."
c777ccba-219e-48c8-bcf9-32a0140c46ba: "Well, was the girl at least worth it?"
52adef44-355a-4de4-8e36-e28def1b8077: "Garess is the name of a noble house in Brevoy, is it not? You're a noble, then?"
63310c45-a94a-4b16-ba49-c8a0057e7b0a: "Care to tell me why you were exiled? You've asked me a favor. I'd say you owe me an explanation."
b59582d0-29a7-454d-b83a-28b62ffbf5e6: "I hope you regret the things you've done. Duty should stand above emotion."
6b661851-33c3-4eef-8255-9d1d6ce662fb: "Leave the past in the past and think of it no more."
e045ccd2-d8f4-40b4-86b4-1151b18733f9: "I would know more of House Garess and your homeland."
9f146448-8afe-4724-bf8c-94d780a134c0: "Tell me of the lands you grew up in."
6abaa078-d228-4622-9db4-6a02ac0a6e80: "Let's finish this conversation some other time."
42c2d3f5-67e4-44ba-b2ad-0be594064b0c: "Kesten, I failed to capture Tartuccio alive. He attacked me and was killed."
eb62fe18-7d57-4325-9cc1-2b3cbb426ccb: "What can Pitaxian spies hope to find in the Stolen Lands?"
73c083ce-9039-493f-9684-fa6e48f8ea4e: "What did you do to be exiled? I believe I have a right to know."
3834c3f0-a8d9-4948-afb7-c033287dacb7: "If I were to offer you a public position, what job would you like to do?"
6f714d9b-7768-4fc3-bdae-def1f4f7527e: "How are you managing the responsibilities of the main guard?"
ba434934-70b2-40d7-b90e-54fa88968c20: "How did Tartuccio manage to fool you?"
af891a03-7dc2-4fd3-a81e-c57a27b2d3dd: "I'd say you deserved a better fate, Kesten. True love should not be punished."
4a8588a2-af27-4153-96f7-9047269002f3: "How may I serve you, Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}?" {n}Kesten nods at you, pauses a moment, then bows awkwardly.{/n}
6e6e3a56-b423-4e1e-9a99-7231d556c7a8: "Used to be." {n}Kesten cringes, as if he'd bitten a sour fruit.{/n} "It's only a name now, nothing more. The {g|House Garess}Garesses{/g} are a noble family in {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}, they own several mines in the Golushkin Mountains. My father Evan is cousin to Lord Howlan Garess." {n}Kesten frowns.{/n} "But he's my father no longer."
e7713229-5bd0-479e-95e8-7eb04be4de36: {n}Before you stands a heavy-set man with grim, determined features. His weathered face is crossed by several scars — yet they do little to mar his appearance. His gaze is heavy, but he avoids eye contact, as if afraid of unwittingly sharing whatever burden weighs so heavily upon him.{/n}
83a3421c-b874-4ce6-8b09-a9aeb15fd799: "In any case, I brought shame upon my name, and was punished accordingly. The family disowned me. I fled to {g|Restov}Restov{/g} and took up the life of a simple mercenary — until I received an assignment here, in the {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g}."
cdce36fb-1a4e-4c5c-8501-2024b72e6cae: {n}An uneasy grin twists Kesten's lips.{/n} "Fair enough. For a {g|House Garess}Garess{/g}, the prosperity of the house and the honor of the name stands above all else. And I… I was betrothed to a widow from another noble house. This union was of great importance to the family. However, three months before the wedding I met a commoner girl, gentle and pure, and we fell in love. I would have rather died than leave my Tania, so I decided to break off the engagement with my noble bride. I could never have expected what would follow…"
3c6d55d0-02c2-448b-83c9-91ce395a8cf7: "My father was furious — I'd set a pointless love affair above the interests of the House. He expelled me from the family, and ordered to leave our lands under threat of death. And Tania..."{n} A shadow of a smile crosses Kesten's face, only to leave it even more grim than before.{/n} "Her mother was seriously ill, and she stayed behind to care for her, rather than follow me into exile. Thus, I was on my own: disgraced, without a name — and without love."
4602b603-65cc-403d-9628-d468d942ee13: "Don't imagine that I ask for pity,"{n} Kesten remarks in a somber tone.{/n} "Everyone gets what they deserve."
bcd3cbff-76aa-4628-8b23-0f0101c0b607: {n}Kesten sighs, then says abruptly:{/n} "I would never have left her of my own accord."
a01e3e3e-6f30-476f-8d5e-01f36f5e1675: "Fairness befits a ruler," {n}Kesten replies softly.{/n} "Be sure — I've learned my lesson well."
2a1de850-2e8f-4643-93c8-5b7d15a2b0f5: {n}Kesten frowns.{/n} "That's no simple task. It's not only the love of a woman and a family that I've lost. I had a place in life, a purpose. Once such things are lost, they're hard to find again."
9f039905-72da-49a8-8f70-f58421a8ce3c: "The sly bastard has caused us no little trouble, that's for sure." {n}Kesten frowns.{/n} "When he showed up in {g|Restov}Restov{/g} and announced he's going to join the expedition, nobody suspected a thing. Yes, a gnome. Yes, a sorcerer… But so what? Even after that terrible night some of my people were willing to bet money on you being the spy!"
6f7a4572-f4a7-45e0-b572-a98a4b13497d: "His overconfidence was his downfall. Tartuccio's henchmen, it seems, imagined they could safely meet with {g|Pitax}Pitaxian{/g} spies in the town's seedy underbelly. But {g|Restov}Restov{/g} is the ancestral home of the Aldori, and Lady Jamandi is respected not only by the aristocracy and the common folk, but also by those on the other side of the law."
ccf39807-b0a3-43ad-bd5b-3943008c3a8f: "We received a message from the slums. A good friend, who wished to remain anonymous, suggested the {g|Swordlords}Swordlords{/g} take a closer look at a certain guest from {g|Pitax}Pitax{/g}. Jamandi immediately sent for me, and ordered me to capture the spy — all very quietly, of course. He told us everything — and not only about Tartuccio. I doubt that Irovetti was pleased to hear of his agents' failure." {n}A nasty grin crosses Kesten's face.{/n}
315bbe32-dd79-412a-b68f-e7f2324b0b58: "{g|House Garess}House Garess{/g} owns a number of valleys and gorges in the Golushkin mountains. The landscape makes these places easily defensible, and they're rich in ores and everything else the depths of the earth have to offer. It is a place of rare beauty," {n}Kesten sighs.{/n} "When I moved to {g|Restov}Restov{/g}, I couldn't get used to it for a long time — there was nothing but sky between the rooves. No mountain peaks anywhere in sight."
4a18f950-f316-4306-b9b4-ff6dd8eb588c: "It is an old and renowned family, one of the most influential in {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g}. A long time ago, the {g|House Garess}Garess house{/g} entered a pact with the dwarven clan of Golka. This proved to be of great benefit to both parties, and they've supplied the ore for our forges ever since. Lord Howlan even took the son of the dwarven leader as his ward. Who would've known where this would lead!"
b15ff674-5f2a-413c-b0e9-c0a3f9df0488: "The same winter that {g|Brevoy}Brevoy{/g} lost the {g|House Rogarvia}Rogarvia{/g} dynasty, Howlan's only natural son, Bren, went missing in the mountains. Thus, Toval Golka, the lord's dwarven ward, became heir to {g|House Garess}house Garess{/g}. The lad has it tough though. Too many believed Howlan should have chosen someone of his own blood to be the heir. I would imagine my own father had similar plans for me... but we all know how that went."
5d8a87b2-084c-480c-8b45-4d2db7c05527: "Greetings!" {n}Kesten Garess, the former captain of Jamandi Aldori's personal guards, nods to you, as though you'd seen each other in Restov only yesterday. He limps noticeably, and his clothes are stained with blood — and looks every bit as grim and focused as when you first met. But this time you also sense a hint of excitement in his eyes.{/n}
e345d2cf-ca8c-472b-9c78-8c2a550574e9: "I have urgent news from {g|Restov}Restov{/g}. The investigation that I've conducted at lady Jamandi's orders have proved your innocence. Tartuccio was, and still is, the {g|Pitax}Pitaxian{/g} spy. That dreadful night, it was him who had opened the gate and let the assassins in. It appears that he planned to gain the barony and Aldori's support, only to later place these lands under the command of his true patron. King Irovetti is no stranger to intrigue, and likes to use others to do his dirty work." {n}Kesten winces.{/n} "Anyway, lady Jamandi sends her apologies."
18323852-e54d-4349-84e0-b004abd70179: "Lady Jamandi ordered me to capture Tartuccio. We were following his trail when that damned mist fell. First we entirely lost our way, and then stumbled right into a bandit ambush. Alas, nearly all my people were wounded, and can go no further. And so I am here, asking for your aid. I'll point out on the map where Tartuccio is supposed to be. Bring that scum to {g|Oleg's Trading Post}Oleg's Trading Post{/g}, dead or alive. {g|Restov}Restov{/g} will not forget this favor!"
1520ae62-1ccf-4db3-9c06-d8238b3f04e0: "We almost had Tartuccio cornered when this damned mist fell. First we entirely lost our way, and then stumbled right into a bandit ambush." {n}In an angry gesture, Kesten chops the air with his hand.{/n} "My people can barely stand, so I would be grateful if you help us to capture this Tartuccio. He must be somewhere nearby. Bring that scum to {g|Oleg's Trading Post}Oleg's Trading Post{/g}, dead or alive. The {g|Swordlords}Swordlords{/g} will remember this favor!"
2c336652-256c-46df-83ce-58204700f604: {n}Kesten sighs.{/n} "Well, this is not the best outcome, but I think it will be good enough for Jamandi. Take this as a reward for your help. I'll send word to {g|Restov}Restov{/g}, and let them consider how they might return the favor."
55eb8cbf-7509-411b-b4e2-3a17820fe8ad: "{g|Pitax}Pitaxian{/g} spies are much like magpies. They'll grab anything that catches their eye. Information, treasure, artifacts. This time King Irovetti had a chance to seize the entire {g|Stolen Lands}Stolen Lands{/g} region — and at the Aldori's expense. I'll give you some advice for the future — be wary of the Pitaxian king. He's truly a snake of a man."
c9b8b843-39d1-448d-a6a1-ba86d7ba9d80: "Once again, I thank you for your help. I'll remain here until my men recover from their wounds. Meanwhile, we'll help guard the {g|Oleg's Trading Post}trading post{/g} and fight off any bandits, should they return. Good luck in all your plans and endeavors!"
89c01372-5f21-4ce4-ae53-5be1d9c426f7: "I believe I can manage to uphold the law. Being a Warden would suit me well."
d47bb266-447c-4e0e-8533-e7e41bbb9089: {n}Kesten hesitates, carefully choosing his words.{/n} "As you know, this land is quite a troublesome place. But as long as its people trust their guards, at least a bit, and as long as those guards are loyal to their ruler, then we'll be able to deal with any trouble that comes."
8ea2b461-d069-4e15-b198-e1a9e6d67a79: "Your {mf|Grace|Grace|Highness|Highness}…" {n}Kesten falls silent, trying to choose the right words.{/n} "I have already failed at keeping this land secure. You'd better find someone who can succeed where I have failed."
3ab5e24d-f50b-44f0-bc47-1c544f5bd241: "What's done is done." {n}Kesten lowers his head.{/n}
efb892b6-deac-495c-85a6-cf0401224c45: "I saw a book here... It was quite interesting – with pictures! I think it was called 'Jade Wand Unlocks Jasper Gates'. Too bad I couldn't steal it. But I remember a few pictures!"
82ce108d-7c8a-45ac-ba93-450ab7c59544: "Hmm... I think I know which book you're talking about. Are you suggesting we try it?"
45199beb-ca4c-47b1-8854-b5d3fcf916f4: "Octavia's right, Reg. You didn't free yourselves on your own, remember? These people need our help."

7a602b88-daf1-4dec-a594-8b6d523736f0: "And one more thing… You remember that potion you helped me test?" {n}Bokken gives you a conspiratorial wink.{/n} "Well, it's almost ready!
